# Korg X5DR Editor — Decision Archive

*This is the append-only historical record: every decision made and every hardware discovery confirmed, with rationale. It is NOT read at the start of every session — only on demand, when a new session needs to understand why something is the way it is (debugging a regression, revisiting a past call, or onboarding a fresh thread on a specific topic). The always-read summary lives in `X5DR_Editor_Progress_Log.md`; the non-negotiable gotchas live in the "Landmines" section of `X5DR_Editor_Project_Context.md`.*

*Append new entries here at the end of a session. Do not edit or remove past entries — this is a historical record, not a living spec. The one recorded exception is the 2026-10-07 redaction-only pass (Archive #214).*

*Commit hashes before v1.0.0 refer to the private archive repository `x5dr-editor-private`. So do files cited here that are not in the public repo (for example `Setup Instructions/`, `docs/design spec docs/`, the Optimization Plan, `X5DR_Editor_Landmines_Full.md`).*

---

| June 2026 | EG Time Mod Parameter Change value encoding: `0`=off, `1`=+, `-1`=−                                                                                                      | Determined by monitoring outbound SysEx from X5DR front panel. The device transmits `01 00` for `+`, `00 00` for `0`, and `7F 7F` for `−`. `-1` encodes correctly via NOTE 12 signed encoding in `encodeParamValue`. Previous compact 2-bit approach (`sw \| (pol << 1)`) was wrong — value `2` for `−` was silently ignored by the device. Fix applied to `buildEgTimeMods` in `index.html`: `paramValue = newSel === 0 ? 0 : (newSel === 1 ? 1 : -1)`. All eight switch groups confirmed working on hardware.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| June 2026 | Parser multisound reconstruction: `((b[13] & 0x03) << 8) \| b[12]`                                                                                                       | Previous formula used `<< 7` and `& 0x7F` on LSB — both wrong. MSB contributes groups of 256 (not 128), and LSB is a full 8-bit value after unpacking. Fix applied to `parser.js` lines 170–171.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| June 2026 | **Design axiom:** The editor should always reflect the state of the device as closely as possible                                                                        | Drives decisions like resetting workingCopy on effect type change, eager Mode Change, NAK recovery, etc.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Per-type parameter slot order within each effect type must be verified by hardware capture — the reference doc is unreliable for this.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

Confirmed by hardware observation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

| June 2026 | BROWSER becomes a toggle button opening an overlay, not a peer tab                                                                                                       | §2.2b design session decision; BROWSER no longer switches `#content` panels — it opens a Patch Browser overlay scoped to the active editor type (PROG/COMBI), reusing/adapting the existing `buildPatchTable` rendering logic in a 5×20 grid layout                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| June 2026 | Patch Browser Cancel restores in-progress edits, not a full revert                                                                                                       | Distinct from existing "Discard Edits" — Cancel exits a *browsing/auditioning* session and must restore the device's edit buffer to the dirty working copy (preserving unsaved edits), not the clean last-saved snapshot. Achieved via a new `resyncDeviceProgramBuffer(progIndex, programData)` function, called with the dirty working copy and no `store.revertProgram()` call — distinct from "Discard Edits," which calls the same function with the clean snapshot and does revert the store                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

| June 2026 | `browserState` — single bundled object for all overlay-open transient state                                                                                              | Replaces what would otherwise be several loose module-level variables (one per overlay type) with one object (`{ kind, priorValue, priorParamPath, priorProgIndex, onConfirm, onCancel }`), reset to `null` on every overlay close. Chosen over separate variables because Brief #10/#11 introduce four new overlay types at once (Patch Browser, Write Browser, Multisound Browser, Drum Sound Browser), with Combi Timbre Slot and Multi Program Slot browsers expected to follow                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

The existing `MULTISOUND_NAMES`/`DRUM_SOUND_NAMES` arrays are also already inline; the new category tables are placed alongside them                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| June 2026 | Multisound/Drum Sound dropdown pickers replaced by a clickable "name + hover icon" field opening a dedicated browser modal                                               | Modeled directly on the Brief #9 program rename pattern (bounded box, name text, hover-revealed pencil icon) for visual/interaction consistency. | June 2026 | Drum Sound Browser single-click selection triggers an audible audition note (Note On at velocity 100, using the slot's already-assigned MIDI key) followed by a Note Off | Drum slot auditioning has no inherent audio feedback from a parameter change alone (unlike Program Edit, where a note may already be sustaining) — an explicit Note On is required to make selection audible. Sequencing: parameter change sent first (so the device is configured for the candidate sound), then Note On, then a delayed Note Off. The OFF row is treated identically to sound rows — auditioning OFF produces audible silence, which itself confirms correct behavior, so no special-casing is needed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| June 2026 | `sendProgramDumpAndAwaitAck` changed to resolve `'no-output'` instead of rejecting when no MIDI output is selected                                                       | Fixes a reproducible freeze (see Critical Discovery #26) where an uncaught promise rejection left the Abandoned Edits modal and Cancel button permanently disabled on machines with no MIDI output connected. | June 2026 | Write / Save / Cancel buttons replace `confirm()` as primary edit-action UI in PROG editor; Abandoned Edits modal handles nav-away-while-dirty                           | Three explicit buttons (Write to device, Save to file, Cancel/revert) give the user unambiguous control and remain in the editor after Write or Cancel. "Save to file" deliberately absent from the modal to keep escape paths simple; user can Stay in Editor and save explicitly.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

## Critical Discoveries — Full Write-Ups

*Short-form versions of the highest-impact items here live in the "Landmines" section of `X5DR_Editor_Project_Context.md` for always-read visibility. This section has the full narrative, root cause, and verification detail for each.*

### 1. Parameter Change requires a prior SysEx Mode Change

**The X5DR will NAK all Parameter Change messages (Func=`41`) unless the computer has first sent a SysEx Mode Change message putting the device into the correct edit mode.**

Pressing the Edit button on the front panel is NOT sufficient — it puts the X5DR into edit mode visually but does not satisfy the internal state required to accept incoming Parameter Changes via MIDI.

**The correct sequence for Program editing:**

```
Step 1 — Send Mode Change to Prog Edit:
F0 42 3g 36 4E 03 00 F7
(g = MIDI global channel, 0-indexed; channel 1 = g=0, so byte = 0x30)

Step 2 — Send Parameter Change(s) freely:
F0 42 3g 36 41 pp pp vv vv F7
(pp pp = parameter number, 7-bit packed LSB/MSB; vv vv = value, 7-bit packed)
```

The Mode Change only needs to be sent once per editing session — the X5DR stays in Prog Edit mode and accepts subsequent Parameter Changes without repeating the Mode Change.

**Architectural implication:** When the user selects a program to edit in the UI, the editor must automatically send the Mode Change as part of the program selection flow, before the user touches any control.

**Mode codes for Func=`4E`:**
- `00` = Combination
- `01` = Combi Edit
- `02` = Program
- `03` = Prog Edit ← use this for Program editing
- `04` = Multi
- `05` = Global

### 2. Web MIDI port selection

Select ports by name, not by numeric ID. IDs may not be stable across Chrome restarts or USB reconnections. Port names reported by Chrome on the hardware-test Mac:

| Direction | Port name | Physical connection |
|---|---|---|
| Output | `Korg X5DR <interface>` | the interface's port 2 → X5DR MIDI In |
| Input | `Korg X5DR <interface>` | X5DR MIDI Out → the interface's port 2 |

The "Korg X5DR" name comes from Audio MIDI Setup where the device connected to the interface's port 2 was named "Korg X5DR". This naming is not guaranteed on other machines — the port selector UI must allow the user to choose their own ports.

### 3. Multiple ACKs per message

Chrome reports multiple ACKs (`F0 42 30 36 23 F7`) per message sent — likely 3–4. This is a known behavior related to multiple MIDI input ports being enumerated for the same physical device. It is harmless — only one ACK represents the actual X5DR response. The ACK handler in the editor should de-duplicate or simply treat the first ACK as confirmation.

### 4. Active Sensing filtering

The X5DR transmits Active Sensing (`FE`) continuously. Filter it in the MIDI input handler:
```javascript
input.onmidimessage = (e) => {
  if (e.data[0] === 0xFE) return; // ignore Active Sensing
  // handle message
};
```

### 5. Reason drops SysEx

Reason DAW does not pass SysEx messages through its MIDI routing. The editor must address the interface directly — it cannot route SysEx through Reason. Note data from the MIDI keyboard can still flow through Reason to the X5DR independently, and the interface merges both streams in hardware.

### 6. Func=10 (Program Dump Request) has no padding byte

Most dump request messages include a `00` byte after the function code. Func=`10` (Program Parameter Dump Request) does **not** — it is simply `F0 42 3g 36 10 F7`. Sending the `00` byte causes the X5DR to silently ignore the request with no response.

`buildDumpRequest(funcCode, withPadding)` in `sysex.js` handles both cases:
- `buildDumpRequest(0x10, false)` — no padding (Program dump request)
- `buildDumpRequest(0x0F)` — with padding (All Data dump request, and most others)

### 7. X5DR ignores Program Change while in Prog Edit mode

Sending a MIDI Program Change (`0xC0 n`) while the X5DR is in Prog Edit mode (Func=`4E`, mode=`03`) has no effect — the device remains on the current patch. To change programs from the editor:

1. Send Mode Change to Program mode: `F0 42 3g 36 4E 02 00 F7`
2. Send Program Change: `[0xC0, programNumber]`
3. Send Mode Change to Prog Edit: `F0 42 3g 36 4E 03 00 F7`
4. Set `modeChangeSent = true`

This sequence is now handled automatically in the browser patch selection click handler.

### 8. Mode Change sent lazily causes device display to jump to OSC Mode

If `modeChangeSent = false` and the user immediately edits a parameter, `sendParamChange` sends the Mode Change first, which causes the X5DR to display the first edit parameter (OSC Mode) on its front panel — even if the user is editing a completely different parameter. The parameter change still goes through, but the display jump is confusing.

**Fix:** Send the Mode Change to Prog Edit eagerly when a patch is selected (in the browser click handler), not lazily on the first parameter edit. Set `modeChangeSent = true` immediately after.

### 9. Manual front-panel mode changes cause subsequent Parameter Changes to NAK

If the user presses a button on the X5DR front panel that exits Prog Edit mode, `modeChangeSent` remains `true` on the computer but the device is no longer in edit mode. The next Parameter Change will NAK.

**Fix:** Reset `modeChangeSent = false` in the NAK handler. This ensures the next edit automatically re-issues the Mode Change and re-establishes edit mode.

### 10. EG Time Mod polarity — encoding confirmed (resolved June 2026)

The correct Parameter Change value encoding for EG Time Mod per-stage parameters (TABLE 7 params 45–48, 53–56, 66–69, 74–77, and OSC-2 equivalents) is:

| UI state | Value to send | Encoded bytes |
|---|---|---|
| `0` (off) | `0` | `00 00` |
| `+` | `1` | `01 00` |
| `−` | `-1` | `7F 7F` |

**How it was determined:** A temporary SysEx logger was added to `onMidiMessage` to capture outbound messages from the X5DR when parameters were changed on the front panel. Stepping through VDF EG Time Vel Mod AT/DT/ST/RT on a patch showing `+`, `−`, `+`, `0` produced messages with value bytes `01 00`, `7F 7F`, `01 00`, `00 00` respectively — unambiguous.

**Fix applied:** `buildEgTimeMods` in `index.html` now uses `paramValue = newSel === 0 ? 0 : (newSel === 1 ? 1 : -1)`. The existing `encodeParamValue(-1)` correctly produces `7F 7F` via NOTE 12 signed arithmetic. All eight switch groups (VDF-1/2 × Vel/KBD Mod × OSC-1/2) confirmed working on hardware.

### 11. `05_effect_parameters.md` per-type parameter order is unreliable for Parameter Change offset assignment

Hardware testing (June 2026) confirmed that the parameter slot order documented in `05_effect_parameters.md` for most effect types does NOT match the device's actual Parameter Change parameter slot assignments. 21 of 25 unique parameter sets had incorrect offset assignments when transcribed from the reference doc.

**Root cause:** The reference doc describes the SysEx *dump data layout* (byte order within the packed parameter block), which does not match the *Parameter Change slot order* the device uses for real-time editing. These are independent orderings.

**Ground truth:** Hardware capture using Snoize MIDI monitor — navigate each parameter on the device front panel and capture the outbound Parameter Change message. The `pp pp` bytes decode to the parameter number; subtract the Effect 1 base (168) or Effect 2 base (179) to get the offset.

**What IS reliable in the reference doc:** parameter labels, value ranges (mostly), and initial values. The offset order is not reliable.

**Confirmed correct without hardware correction:** `rotary` (type 34) and `paramEQ` (type 37).

### 12. `(L)`/`(H)` byte-split entries are dump-layout artifacts — never independent Parameter Change parameters

Several effect types in `05_effect_parameters.md` show entries like `Delay Time L (L)` and `Delay Time L (H)` at consecutive offsets. These represent a single logical value (e.g. 0–500ms) stored across two bytes in the dump because the value exceeds 7 bits.

In the Parameter Change system, this is a **single parameter** at a single offset. The device accepts the full value as a standard 14-bit Parameter Change. The `(H)` entry does not exist as an independent Parameter Change target.

**Hardware confirmation:** Stereo Delay Delay Time L tested as Effect 1. Offset 0 (param 168) correctly changed D.Time L from 0–500. Offset 1 (param 169) correctly changed D.Time R from 0–500. There was no separate `(H)` control — each delay time occupies exactly one offset slot.

### 13. Dry:FX Balance — `balL` semantics differ by effect type group

The X5DR interprets the `balL` Parameter Change parameter differently depending on the effect type:

- **Types 1–39 and 44–45:** `balL` = **wet** amount (0–100). Sending `balL=39` gives the device a Dry:Wet display of 61:39.
- **Types 40–43 and 46–47:** `balL` = **dry** amount (0–100). Sending `balL=39` gives the device a Dry:Wet display of 39:61.

The UI `rebuildBalance` function accounts for this: for types 40–43/46–47, the slider position (0=dry, 100=wet) is converted before sending — `sendParamChange(balLPN, 100 - wet)`.

**Types 44–45 (Delay/Distortion, Delay/Overdrive):** `balR` (Parameter Change number 176/187) was confirmed to have no effect on the device. It has been removed from the UI. Only `balL` is written for these types (as the wet amount, same as types 1–39).

**UI display:** a `balanceSliderCtrl` renders a live `Dry:Wet` ratio label (e.g. `61:39`) next to the slider. The numeric field is replaced with this label. Slider fully left = 100:0 (fully dry), fully right = 0:100 (fully wet).

### 14. OUT3/OUT4 Pan dump encoding is inverted relative to Parameter Change encoding

The X5DR stores OUT3 and OUT4 pan position in the SysEx dump using an encoding that is directionally inverted relative to the Parameter Change encoding used for real-time editing.

| System | Value 0 | Value 1 | Value 101 (0x65) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dump** (bytes base+6, base+7) | OFF | R (hard right) | L (hard left) |
| **Parameter Change** (params 159, 160) | OFF | L (hard left) | R (hard right) |

**Conversion:** In `parser.js` `decodeEffects()`, raw dump bytes are converted to PC values on load:
```js
out3Pan = dump === 0 ? 0 : 102 - dump;
out4Pan = dump === 0 ? 0 : 102 - dump;
```

**Example (verified — A02 BigStrings):** Device has OUT3=L, OUT4=R. Raw dump bytes: out3Pan=101, out4Pan=1. After conversion: out3Pan=1 (L), out4Pan=101 (R). Displayed and sent correctly.

**The reference table `*11-1` in `05_effect_parameters.md`** correctly describes the dump encoding direction (01=R, 65=L). The value "65" in the table is **decimal 65**, which equals **hex 0x65 = decimal 101** as a raw byte. This is why the range was previously described as "extended from 0–65 to 0–101" — there was no extension, the range was always 0x00–0x65 (0–101 decimal). The reference table is accurate for dump interpretation; the panLabel function (1=L, 101=R) is accurate for Parameter Change.

**What the slider sends:** confirmed correct by hardware observation — moving the slider toward 1 pans the device LEFT; moving toward 101 pans the device RIGHT.

**Numbering note:** entries #15 and #16 below collide with Landmines entries #15–17 in `X5DR_Editor_Project_Context.md` (multisound parser formula, SVG className, continuous-block dump packing), which were added directly to Landmines without ever receiving full Archive write-ups — the two numbering sequences have drifted apart. Not resolved in this session; flagged here so a future cleanup pass knows about it.

### 15. OSC-1 Level and VDA-1 Level are the same device parameter

Discovered while mapping parameter numbers for the VDA copy-paste utility: VDA-1's `level` field sends Parameter Change number **25**, which is the identical param number used for OSC-1's `level` field (confirmed directly from `buildOscSection(n, 'osc1', 24, 25, 26, ...)` call-site arguments and `vda1P.level: 25` in `buildVdaContent`). This is not a bug — per the manual's TABLE 1, "Oscillator Level" exists once in the device's parameter space and this UI happens to surface it on two different tabs for convenience (OSC tab as "Level", VDA tab as "Level").

**Consequence:** the two controls are currently independent DOM elements with no synchronization. Editing Level on the OSC tab does not update the VDA tab's display (or vice versa) until a full panel re-render occurs (e.g. switching tabs and back). Both controls write to the same `workingCopy` path and the same device parameter, so the *underlying value* is always correct — only the *displayed* value can go stale within a single render pass.

**Not yet fixed.** Flagged as a Known Outlier and a queued Next Action (cross-tab sync architecture) rather than patched ad hoc, because the same class of problem will recur and multiply once Quick Edit is built — Quick Edit's whole premise is duplicating controls from other tabs. Recommended direction (not yet decided): a small pub/sub layer added to `setParam` in `store.js`, notifying any currently-rendered control of a path change, scoped as its own ADR-0002 amendment before Quick Edit work begins.

### 16. Patch audition vs. Edit mode entry — architecture and NAK recovery redesign

**Problem:** the original Patch Selection Flow (see entries #8/#9 above) sent Mode Change → Program Change → Mode Change to Prog Edit on every BROWSER row click, meaning simply browsing patches silently entered Prog Edit mode every time. This made patch *audition* (listening to a sound without intending to edit it) indistinguishable from patch *editing* at the protocol level, and meant the device was placed in Edit mode far more often than the user's intent actually called for.

**New architecture (Brief #1, not yet implemented):**
- BROWSER row clicks send **Program Change only**. No Mode Change.
- Mode Change to Program (`0x02`) is sent at two triggers instead: (a) once when a Snapshot is first loaded and BROWSER view is shown, and (b) whenever the user navigates back to BROWSER from an editor tab.
- A new persistent, context-aware **Edit button** (fixed screen position across all tabs) is the only thing that sends Mode Change to Prog Edit (`0x03`) and enters the editor UI. Button label/action depends on current top-level navigation context (Program/Combi/Multi — Combi/Multi stubbed as disabled for now, since those modules don't exist yet).
- The button carries a visible active/highlighted state reflecting whether Edit mode is currently entered on the device, and that highlight is now the user's primary signal of device state — replacing the old assumption that "being on the PROG tab" implied "device is in Prog Edit."

**NAK recovery redesign:** previously (entry #9), a NAK silently reset an internal flag and the *next* edit attempt would silently re-send the Mode Change before resending — invisible to the user. Now that Edit mode is a named, deliberate state with a visible button indicator, silent recovery was judged inconsistent with the Core Design Axiom (state should be visibly accurate, not just eventually-correct). New behavior: NAK immediately (a) reverts the failed param in `workingCopy` (unchanged), (b) clears the Edit button's highlight, (c) shows a dialog — *"Parameter change not received by device. Click OK to re-enter Edit mode and resend the change."* — with a single OK button (no Cancel; there is no safe alternative action once silent recovery is removed). OK resends Mode Change `0x03`, then resends **only the single failed parameter** (not the full dirty set, to avoid re-sending values the device may already hold correctly) using a new store slot `lastFailedParam` (`{ path, value }`) captured at NAK time.

**Known pre-existing tension not yet resolved by this brief:** `sendParamChange` (as implemented prior to this session) contains its own internal lazy Mode Change check (`if (!modeChangeSent) { ... }`), which is the exact pattern this redesign replaces. This function needs updating as part of Brief #1's implementation; it was flagged but intentionally left unmodified by the brief itself, since the brief is a planning document, not code.

**Open verification item:** how the new dialog-based recovery interacts with Brief #2's copy-paste utilities, which send multiple `sendParamChange` calls in a burst — if Edit mode drops mid-burst, does the dialog appear once (correct) or repeatedly per remaining field (incorrect)? Not yet tested; flagged as a Next Action.

### 17. NAK recovery: duplicate NAKs from multiple ports + Mode Change settling time on re-entry

Two related hardware issues surfaced during Brief #1 testing, both specific to the NAK recovery path.

**Issue 1 — Duplicate NAKs from multiple logical input ports**

The X5DR sends multiple NAKs per failed Parameter Change — the same multi-port behaviour as ACK deduplication (Discovery #3 / Landmine #7). When a NAK fired and the recovery `alert()` dialog blocked JavaScript, further copies of the same NAK queued up as macrotask callbacks. When the user clicked OK and JS resumed, the queued duplicate NAKs fired immediately after the recovery code ran, triggering a second dialog (and potentially a third, etc.).

**Fix:** an `ignoringNaks` boolean flag, set to `true` before the `alert()` call. The queued duplicate NAK callbacks execute before the `setTimeout(fn, 0)` scheduled inside the recovery path — both are macrotasks, but the NAKs were enqueued earlier — so they all return early and are silently suppressed. The `setTimeout(0)` then clears the flag. Any genuine NAK arriving *after* the flag clears (e.g. from the resend itself) is handled normally.

**Issue 2 — Mode Change settling time on re-entry from a non-edit state**

When recovering from a NAK, sending Mode Change `0x03` + Parameter Change back-to-back caused the Parameter Change to NAK even though the Mode Change was acknowledged. Hardware evidence: the X5DR's front panel displayed the OSC Type parameter (the default display on entering Prog Edit), confirming the Mode Change was processed, but the immediately-following Param Change was rejected.

The second recovery attempt (after dismissing the second dialog) always succeeded, because by then the device had been sitting in Prog Edit mode for 1–2 seconds (from the first recovery's Mode Change) and was fully settled when the second Param Change arrived.

**Root cause:** the device requires approximately 100ms to fully transition from a non-edit state into Prog Edit mode before it can accept Parameter Changes. This settling window does not affect normal editing — when the user clicks the Edit button and then moves a control, the natural human delay between button click and first control interaction easily exceeds 100ms. The recovery path exposes it because Mode Change and Parameter Change are sent programmatically with no gap.

**Fix:** `setTimeout(fn, 100)` in the recovery path. `ignoringNaks` is cleared and the Param Change resend fires after 100ms. This ensures the device has settled before the resend arrives, and ensures the `ignoringNaks` window also covers any stragglers from the original failure batch.

**Hardware verification:** single dialog, single OK click, parameter change takes effect on the device.

### 18. CSS `position: sticky; top: 0` measures from the content area, not the padding edge of the scroll container

When implementing the sticky prog-header (program name + inner tab bar), the initial approach used `top: 0` combined with a `margin-top: -1rem` trick to compensate for `#content`'s `padding: 1rem`. The intention was to make the sticky element sit flush with the visual top of `#content`. It did not work: after scrolling, a 1rem gap appeared between the main nav row and the sticky header, and content (e.g. "Mode... Double") scrolled visibly into that gap.

**Root cause:** For `position: sticky`, the `top` threshold is measured from the *content area* of the scroll container (inside its padding), not the padding edge. With `padding-top: 1rem` on `#content`, `top: 0` means "stick when my top edge would be 1rem below the visual top of `#content`." The `margin-top: -1rem` correctly repositioned the element's natural location to the visual top, but had no effect on where `top: 0` pins it when sticky activates — the pinned position was still 1rem below the visual top.

**What does NOT fix it:** negative `margin-top` on the sticky element. Margin affects the element's flow position, not the sticky threshold.

**Fix:** remove `padding-top` from `#content` entirely, changing `padding: 1rem` to `padding: 0 1rem 1rem 1rem`. With `padding-top: 0`, the content area starts at the visual top and `top: 0` correctly sticks the element flush against it. The `margin-top: -1rem` was also removed (no longer needed). The sticky element's side margins remain negative (`margin: 0 -1rem 0.75rem -1rem`) so its background extends to the edges of `#content`, covering content that scrolls behind it.

**Impact on other panels:** the `#content` `padding-top: 0` change removes the top breathing room from the BROWSER, COMBI, MULTI, and GLOBAL panels. Acceptable for Phase 2 (those panels start with their own sub-tab bars or placeholder content that sits naturally at the top edge).

### 19. Func=53 (Drum Kit Parameter Change) wire format — hardware-verified via Snoize

The original `buildDrumParamChange(paramNo, value)` was modeled identically to `buildParamChange` (Func=41): 10-byte message with 2-byte param number and 2-byte value after the header. This was wrong.

**Snoize capture (Kit 1, Slot #6):**
```
Inst No. (019: Soft Snare): F0 42 30 36 53 00 06 01 14 00 F7
Key (F2):                   F0 42 30 36 53 00 06 02 29 00 F7
Pan (CNT):                  F0 42 30 36 53 00 06 06 0F 00 F7
Pan (OFF):                  F0 42 30 36 53 00 06 06 7F 7F F7
```

**Snoize capture (Kit 2, Slot #10):**
```
Slot select (#10):          F0 42 30 36 53 00 46 00 0A 00 F7
Inst No (174: Pull 2):      F0 42 30 36 53 00 46 01 2F 01 F7
```

**Confirmed wire format:** `F0 42 3g 36 53 00 ss pp vv vv F7` (11 bytes)
- `00` = fixed padding byte (always zero)
- `ss` = slot index: 0–59 for Kit 1, 60–119 for Kit 2 (Kit 2 Slot 10 → `ss = 0x46 = 70 = 60+10`)
- `pp` = TABLE 10 parameter number (0–9), sent as a single byte — NOT the TABLE 6 byte offset formula
- `vv vv` = value in NOTE 12 signed encoding

**Key finding — Pan OFF encoding:** Pan OFF is `-1` in NOTE 12 encoding (`0x7F 0x7F`), not `0xFF`. This differs from the program-level Pan parameter which uses `0xFF` for OFF.

**Key finding — Inst No. encoding:** `instNo + 1` on the wire (1-indexed, 0 = OFF). Matches `parseDrums` which decodes `instRaw > 0 ? instRaw - 1 : 0`.

**Fix:** new signature `buildDrumParamChange(dumpIndex, paramNo, value)` producing the correct 11-byte message. Test suite includes exact byte-match against captured messages.

### 20. Drum kit parameters (Func=53) require Global mode, not Prog Edit

**Discovery:** during hardware testing of Brief #3, all drum slot parameter changes (Func=53) were NAK'd when the device was in Prog Edit mode (`0x03`). The NAK recovery dialog appeared on every control change in the drum editor.

**Root cause:** drum kits are global resources on the X5DR, not per-program. The device's own front-panel drum editing is accessed via the Global menu, not the Program Edit menu. The device requires Global mode (`0x05`) to accept Func=53 messages.

**Confirmed behavior:**
- Func=53 in Prog Edit → NAK
- Func=53 in Global mode → ACK, parameter takes effect
- Func=41 (program params) in Global mode → NAK
- Switching between Global and Prog Edit within a single editing session works correctly

**Solution:** the DRUM EDITOR inner tab (visible only when `osc.mode === 2`) sends Mode Change `0x05` on entry and Mode Change `0x03` on exit. Other Program Edit tabs (OSC, Pitch EG, VDF, VDA, EFFECT) remain in Prog Edit mode. The NAK handler is mode-aware: drum NAKs recover to Global (`0x05`), program NAKs recover to Prog Edit (`0x03`).

**Hardware verification:** drum parameter edits accepted after mode switch. Switching to EFFECT tab, changing an effect parameter, switching back to DRUM EDITOR, editing a drum slot — all confirmed working with correct mode transitions.

### 21. Effect type change off-by-one bug — `paramNos[7]` undefined → silent OSC Mode reset

**Symptom:** changing the Effect Type (for either Effect 1 or Effect 2) while in Double or Drums OSC mode silently reset the OSC mode to Single. The device display briefly showed the OSC mode screen.

**Root cause:** the effect type change handler reset per-type parameter slots to initial values in a loop:
```js
for (let off = 0; off < 8; off++) {
    sendParamChange(paramNos[off], initVal);
}
```
`paramNos` has 7 entries (indices 0–6, mapping to TABLE 7-1 offsets). On iteration `off = 7`, `paramNos[7]` is `undefined`. JavaScript's bitwise operators coerce `undefined` to `0` via `NaN → 0`, so `encodeParamValue(undefined)` returns `{ lsb: 0, msb: 0 }`. This silently sent Parameter Change for param number 0 — which is the OSC Mode parameter — with the effect's init value (typically 0 = Single).

**Why it wasn't caught earlier:** in Single mode (`osc.mode = 0`), sending param 0 with value 0 is a no-op (already Single). The bug only manifested when `osc.mode` was 1 (Double) or 2 (Drums).

**Fix:** changed loop bound from `off < 8` to `off < 7`.

## Critical Discovery #22 — X5DR "Received Data Format Error" (0x26) Is Distinct from NAK (0x24)

**Discovery:** during Easy tab hardware testing, all OSC-2, VDF-2, and VDA-2 parameter changes returned `F0 42 30 36 26 F7` — function code `0x26`, "Received Data Format Error" per `02_sysex_format.md` section (26). This is distinct from the NAK function code `0x24` ("Data Load Error"). The `isNak()` function only checked for `0x24`, so `0x26` responses fell through both `isAck` and `isNak` checks. The status bar continued to display the previous "ACK ✓" — the error was completely invisible to the user.

**Root cause:** the editor and device were out of sync on OSC mode. The editor (loaded from a device dump) showed the program in Double mode, but the device itself had the program in Single mode. In Single mode, OSC-2/VDF-2/VDA-2 parameter numbers (88–154) are out of range, and the device responds with `0x26` rather than `0x24`. OSC-1/VDF-1/VDA-1 parameters (0–87) continued to ACK normally because they are valid in Single mode.

**Why 0x26, not 0x24:** the `02_sysex_format.md` specification describes `0x26` as "When found an error in the received message (e.g. data length)." The device treats out-of-range parameter numbers as a message format error, not a data load error. This is a protocol-level distinction — `0x24` means "understood the message but couldn't apply it" (e.g., memory protection), while `0x26` means "the message itself is invalid."

**How the desync occurred:** uncertain. The dump was taken from the device, so the editor and device should have agreed on OSC mode. Treated as a one-off; not reproducible on demand. However, the missing error detection would hide any future occurrence.

**Fix:** added `isFormatError()` in `sysex.js` checking for `data[4] === 0x26`. Handler in `index.html` shows red status dot + `FORMAT ERR ✗ — param N` in the status bar + alert dialog with guidance: "The device rejected a parameter change as invalid. This usually means the editor and device are out of sync..."

**Landmine added:** #21 in Project Context.

## Critical Discovery #23 — Switching OSC Mode to Drums Leaves Stale Multisound Value

**Discovery:** when changing a Single or Double mode program to Drums mode via the OSC Mode selector, the Drum Editor tab rendered empty on first display. Changing the drum kit to Kit 2 then back to Kit 1 populated it correctly. The issue only affected the first render after the mode switch.

**Root cause:** `buildDrumEditorContent()` reads `store.getParam('programs.N.osc1.multisound')` to determine which kit to display. After changing OSC mode to Drums, this store value still held the previous Single/Double mode multisound index (e.g., 200 = "Grand Piano"). Since `200 >= 8`, the function took the `isRomKit` branch and called `renderRomKitList(200)` — but there is no ROM kit at index 200 (only indices 8–15 are valid ROM kits), producing an empty display.

When the user subsequently changed to Kit 2 via the kit selector dropdown, the store was updated to a valid kit index, and the Drum Editor rendered correctly. Changing back to Kit 1 also worked because the store now held index 0.

**Device behavior:** the X5DR itself resets the multisound to Drum Kit 1 (index 0) when entering Drums mode. The editor was not mirroring this reset, violating the Core Design Axiom ("the editor should always reflect the state of the device as closely as possible").

**Fix:** all three OSC mode change handlers now reset `osc1.multisound` to 0 in the store and send `sendParamChange(24, 0)` when the new mode is Drums (`v === 2`), before calling `renderProgPanel()`.

## Critical Discovery #24 — `Func=11` (Program Write Request) Requires `00` Padding Byte

**Symptom:** during Brief #8 hardware testing, clicking Write after editing a parameter produced a "rejected parameter change as invalid" alert. Cancel (which also uses `Func=40`) worked correctly, proving the program dump format was correct. The failure was in the subsequent `Func=11` write request.

**Root cause:** `buildProgramWriteRequest` was producing `F0 42 30 36 11 pp F7` (7 bytes). The correct format per `02_sysex_format.md` §11 is `F0 42 30 36 11 00 pp F7` (8 bytes) — a `00` padding byte between the function code and the slot index. Without the padding byte, the device interpreted `pp` as the padding and then hit `F7` before receiving the slot number, triggering `0x26` (Received Data Format Error).

**Why it wasn't caught earlier:** `Func=11` was a new message type introduced in Brief #8. The Brief's pseudocode specified only `11 pp F7` without the padding byte — the original spec was wrong.

**Verification:** the `0x26` from the write request fell through to the general `isFormatError` handler because the `awaitingWriteResponse` check only matched `isWriteError` (Func=22) and `isNak` (Func=24), not `isFormatError` (Func=26). This was also fixed — `isFormatError` now routes to the write error callback when `awaitingWriteResponse` is true.

**Fix:** added `0x00` padding byte to `buildProgramWriteRequest`. Updated test to expect 8-byte message. Added `isFormatError` to the `awaitingWriteResponse` routing.

**Landmine added:** #22 in Project Context.

## Critical Discovery #25 — `pack7bit` Trailing Zero-Padding Causes Device `0x26` Rejection

**Symptom:** during Brief #8 hardware testing, both Write and Cancel (which send `Func=40` single program dump) were rejected by the device with `F0 42 30 36 26 F7` (format error). The encoded program data was byte-for-byte correct in round-trip unit tests, but the device refused to accept it.

**Root cause:** `pack7bit` always produces output in multiples of 8 bytes, padding the last partial group with zeros. For 164 raw program bytes:
- 23 full groups of 7 → 184 packed bytes
- 3 remaining bytes → should produce 4 bytes (1 header + 3 data)
- Expected packed length: **188 bytes** (confirmed by `02_sysex_format.md` NOTE 2: "164Bytes = 7×23+3 → 8×23+(1+3) = 188Bytes")
- Actual `pack7bit` output: **192 bytes** (padded last group to full 8 bytes)

The device is strict about payload size and rejects the 4 extra zero bytes as a format error.

**Why unit tests passed:** `unpackPayload` in `parser.js` handles non-multiple-of-8 input by padding before unpacking, so both 188 and 192 packed bytes unpack to the same 164 meaningful bytes. The round-trip test was correct but not testing the device's stricter format requirements.

**Fix:** added `packedLength(rawLength)` helper to `sysex.js` that calculates the correct wire length without trailing padding. `buildSingleProgramDump` and `snapshotToSyx` both trim `pack7bit` output via `.slice(0, packedLength(raw.length))`. `pack7bit` itself is unchanged — it remains a general utility; trimming happens at the call site.

**Landmine added:** #23 in Project Context.

## Critical Discovery #26 — No-MIDI-Output Promise Rejection Freezes Abandoned Edits Modal and Cancel Button

**Symptom:** while visually testing the editor on a development machine with no MIDI interface attached, attempting to discard edits (via the Abandoned Edits modal's Discard button, or the standalone Cancel button) caused the UI to freeze: the modal's buttons remained disabled, with no error shown and no way to dismiss or retry.

**Root cause:** `sendProgramDumpAndAwaitAck(programData)` is implemented as:

```js
function sendProgramDumpAndAwaitAck(programData) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    if (!selectedOutput) { reject(new Error('No MIDI output')); return; }
    // ...
  });
}
```

Every caller — `doCancelFlow()`, the Abandoned modal's Write button handler, and the Abandoned modal's Discard button handler — calls this with `await` but with no surrounding `try/catch`:

```js
const ackResult = await sendProgramDumpAndAwaitAck(cleanProg);
if (ackResult === 'ack') { ... } else { ... }
```

`await` on a rejected promise throws. Since nothing catches the exception, it propagates out of the (async) event handler entirely, skipping both branches of the `if/else`. Each of these three handlers disables its modal/action buttons as its first statement, intending to re-enable them in whichever branch of the `if/else` is reached — but because the function exits via an uncaught exception instead, neither branch runs, and the buttons are never re-enabled. The user is left with a fully disabled, unresponsive modal.

**Why it wasn't caught earlier:** all hardware testing has been performed on the hardware-test Mac, which always has the owner's MIDI interface + X5DR attached. The bug is only reachable when `selectedOutput` is `null`, which only happens on a machine with no MIDI output selected — i.e., during visual/layout testing on the development Mac or any machine without the hardware connected. This is a legitimate and increasingly common workflow (UI/CSS iteration without the hardware on hand) that hadn't been exercised against this code path before.

**Why this matters for Brief #10:** the new Patch Browser Cancel flow (§4f of the Browser/Navigation/File I/O design spec) is built on a new shared function, `resyncDeviceProgramBuffer`, which itself calls `sendProgramDumpAndAwaitAck` internally. Without this fix, the new Cancel path would have inherited the identical freeze on any no-MIDI machine, immediately on first use.

**Fix:** changed `sendProgramDumpAndAwaitAck` to **resolve** `'no-output'` instead of rejecting:

```js
function sendProgramDumpAndAwaitAck(programData) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    if (!selectedOutput) { resolve('no-output'); return; }
    // ... unchanged ...
  });
}
```

All three existing callers (`doCancelFlow`, Abandoned modal Write handler, Abandoned modal Discard handler) updated to treat `'no-output'` identically to how they already treat `'nak'` — re-enable buttons, surface the existing error text/alert. The new Patch Browser Cancel path (and any future caller of `resyncDeviceProgramBuffer`) inherits the fix automatically, since it sits on the same underlying function.

**General principle for future code:** any function that can fail due to absent hardware/connection state should resolve a sentinel failure value rather than reject, unless the caller is guaranteed to wrap every call site in `try/catch`. Given this codebase's pattern of multiple independent call sites for shared async helpers (write/revert flows in particular), resolving a string status (`'ack'` / `'nak'` / `'no-output'` / `'error'`) and branching on it has proven more robust here than promise rejection.

**Landmine added:** #24 in Project Context.

## Critical Discovery #27 — Func=0x40 Single-Program Dump Response Must Use `replaceProgram`, Not `loadSnapshot`

**Discovery:** `scheduleDumpSettle` originally called `store.loadSnapshot(snap)` for all incoming dump responses. When the device responds to a Current Program Dump Request (Func=0x10) with a Func=0x40 single-program dump, `parseSnapshot([message])` produces a snapshot with `programs: [oneProgram]` — a 1-element array.

Passing this to `store.loadSnapshot(snap)` replaces `workingCopy.programs` with that 1-element array. All 99 other program slots become `undefined`. The Patch Browser silently renders 99 empty rows. Any subsequent FILE > Save > All Programs or Save > All Data would write 99 zeroed-out programs to disk.

**Why it wasn't caught earlier:** The previous "Request Dump" footer button sent a Func=0x0F (All Data) request, which returns a Func=0x50 response containing all 100 programs. `loadSnapshot` is correct for that path. The Func=0x10 (Current Program) request was new in Brief #10 and is the only source of single-program dump responses.

**Root cause:** `loadSnapshot` is a whole-snapshot replacement function — it has no concept of "merge one program into an existing bank." It was correct for the only pre-Brief-#10 use case (loading a full snapshot from file or All Data dump), and incorrect for the new single-program case.

**Detection:** `scheduleDumpSettle` inspects `dumpBuffer[0][4]` — the function code byte of the first received message — to distinguish response types:
- `0x50` (All Data) or `0x4C` (All Programs): `store.loadSnapshot(snap)` — replaces the entire working copy; opens Patch Browser
- `0x40` (Single Program): `store.replaceProgram(currentProgIndex, snap.programs[0])` — merges one program into the existing bank; refreshes the browser row and re-renders the editor panel

**Fix:** `isSingleProgramDump` boolean computed from `dumpBuffer[0][4] === 0x40`. If true: `store.replaceProgram(currentProgIndex, snap.programs[0])` + `refreshBrowserRow(currentProgIndex)` + `renderProgPanel()`. If false: `store.loadSnapshot(snap)` + `openPatchBrowser()` (existing path, unchanged).

**Landmine added:** #25 in Project Context.

## Critical Discovery #28 — Browser Overlay and Modal Overlay Both at z-index 100: DOM Order Determines Winner

**Discovery:** During Brief #10 hardware testing (July 2026, B03), the Abandoned Edits confirmation modal was not visible when the Patch Browser was open. Clicking the BROWSER tab while the editor was dirty would dismiss the browser (Cancel ran) and then show the modal — exactly the sequence that should not happen. The modal was in the DOM and structurally correct but invisible.

**Root cause:** `.modal-overlay` and `.browser-overlay` (the Patch Browser) were both set to `z-index: 100`. When two elements share a stacking context and equal z-index, the browser paints them in DOM order — later element wins. The browser overlay div appears later in the HTML than the modal overlay div, so the browser always painted on top. The modal existed in the DOM but was obscured. The user's Cancel click on the browser overlay triggered `cancelPatchBrowser()`, which then ran the navigation — the modal was never seen.

**Why it triggered multiple secondary bugs:** B04/B05/B06/B13 — all reported as "modal doesn't fire" or "modal fires in wrong sequence" — were downstream consequences of B03. With the browser always on top, any flow that depended on the modal appearing while the browser was open would instead see the Cancel/Close path run first. Once B03 was fixed (modal z-index raised to 200), those four bugs resolved without further code changes, consistent with the root cause analysis.

**Fix:** `.modal-overlay { z-index: 200; }` in the CSS. Browser overlay remains at `z-index: 100`. The modal is now always guaranteed to paint above the browser when both are open.

**Lesson:** When two overlays coexist in the same layout, assign distinct z-index values from the start. Shared stacking levels are fragile — a single DOM reorder silently inverts visibility. Always give modals a z-index tier clearly above any overlay they might need to appear over.

**Landmine added:** None — the fix is a single CSS line and the z-index tiers are now clearly separated.

## Critical Discovery #29 — `setParam` Wrapper Self-Recursion Silently Blocked All MIDI Parameter Change Output

**Symptom:** During a hardware test session immediately following the Brief #10 bug-fix pass, no parameter edits made in the editor reached the device at all — no MIDI LED flash on the X5DR, and Snoize MIDI Monitor recorded nothing outbound. The editor's own display still updated normally. Dump requests (Func=0x0F/0x10) and Program Change (browser audition single-click) continued to work correctly.

**Root cause:** the `setParam(path, value)` wrapper — introduced in the prior session specifically to fix B02/B07 by having every parameter write also call `updateProgActions()` (see the July 2026 "All parameter writes use the local `setParam` wrapper" decision above) — had its own body rewritten to call itself instead of `store.setParam`:

```js
function setParam(path, value) {
  setParam(path, value);   // should be store.setParam(path, value)
  updateProgActions();
}
```

Every control handler in the editor calls `setParam(path, v)` immediately followed by `sendParamChange(...)` (e.g. `setParam('programs.0.osc1.level', v); sendParamChange(25, v);`). The self-call recurses until the JS call stack is exhausted, throwing `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. Because nothing wraps these calls in `try/catch`, the exception propagates out of the event handler entirely — `sendParamChange` immediately after it in the same statement sequence never executes. This explains why the editor's own display could still update in some cases (any UI refresh not gated behind the throwing call) while literally zero MIDI bytes reached `selectedOutput.send()` for parameter edits.

**Why it wasn't caught by the 125 Vitest tests:** the test suite covers the pure communication/data layer (`sysex.js`, `parser.js`, `encoder.js`, `store.js`) per project convention — `index.html`'s inline event-handler wiring, including the `setParam` wrapper itself, is UI code and has no automated coverage. This class of bug (a wrapper function silently broken by an edit to itself) is exactly the kind of regression that only surfaces on hardware, since a broken `setParam` call still "succeeds" from the browser's perspective in the sense that the store technically never gets corrupted — it just never gets called, because the exception happens on the way in.

**Likely origin:** the `setParam` wrapper convention itself was rolled out via "a global `replace_all` that changed all 189 `store.setParam(` call sites in one pass" (see the July 2026 decision immediately above this one). It is likely that this same mechanical replace also matched and rewrote the wrapper's own internal reference to `store.setParam`, turning it into a self-call. A blanket text replacement targeting a function name has no way to distinguish "a caller of the function" from "the function's own definition, editing itself."

**Fix:** changed the wrapper's inner call to explicitly target the store: `store.setParam(path, value);`.

**Landmine added:** #26 already existed (documenting the wrapper convention itself); #27 was added this session documenting this specific regression. Landmine #27's citation updated to reference this entry.

**General principle for future code:** when using a mechanical `replace_all` to enforce a wrapper-function convention across many call sites, always check the wrapper's own definition afterward — it is often syntactically identical to a call site and can be caught by the same pattern.
