## Critical Discovery #109 — A Code Comment Mentioning Two Wildcard Selectors With a Slash Between Them Silently Truncated a CSS Comment, Which Silently Dropped the Next Rule

**Context:** part of the Design QA punchlist's Phase 1 (`X5DR_Editor_Phase3_Design_QA_Punchlist.md`) reported a missing gap between OSC's two-column row and its full-width Pitch EG panel below — the same shape of bug the user recalled from VDF. `.osc-content`'s CSS rule (`display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:0.9rem`) looked completely correct on inspection, and the raw file text was confirmed byte-for-byte well-formed (checked via `xxd`, brace-balance counting, and re-parsing the exact live `<style>` textContent in an isolated `<style>` element) — yet `document.styleSheets[...].cssRules` never contained a `.osc-content` entry at all, in a brand-new tab, with no cache involved.

**Finding:** the OSC CSS section's own header comment read `/* ... Duplicated from the .vda-*/.vdf-* pattern above rather than sharing selectors ... */`. `.vda-*` immediately followed by `/.vdf-*` forms the literal three-character substring `*/` — which the CSS parser reads as the comment's *actual* closing delimiter, long before the real, intended `*/` at the end of the comment block. Everything from that accidental early close through the next real rule boundary — the intended remainder of the comment, plus the entirety of `.osc-content { ... }` — gets parsed as garbage top-level CSS, fails, and is silently discarded by the parser's standard per-rule error recovery; parsing then resumes cleanly at the following rule (`.osc-panel`), which is why every *other* rule in the file was unaffected and this looked like an isolated, inexplicable single-rule disappearance rather than a comment bug. Confirmed via bisection: re-parsing the identical stylesheet text in a scratch `<style>` element reproduced the exact same 297-rule (missing one) count deterministically; truncating the text at any point strictly before the accidental `*/` restored `.osc-content` correctly.

**Fix:** reworded the comment to `.vda-* and .vdf-*` (no adjacent asterisk-then-slash), confirmed `.osc-content` and 5 more previously-invisible declarations reappear in the live CSSOM (297 → 303 total rules), and confirmed the gap now renders (measured via `getBoundingClientRect()`, 14.4px between rows, matching `gap: 0.9rem`). Grepped the entire file for the same `-*/ ` pattern — this was the only occurrence. VDF's own equivalent comment ("Duplicated from the .vda-* block above") never had this construction and was already rendering its gap correctly; the user's recollection of a "similar VDF issue" traces to an earlier, since-resolved state of that tab, not a currently-live duplicate of this bug.

**Lesson:** any code comment referencing two or more wildcard-style class prefixes (`.foo-*`, `.bar-*`) side by side must not place a bare `/` directly between an asterisk and the next token — write `.foo-* and .bar-*`, `.foo-*, .bar-*`, or similar, never `.foo-*/.bar-*`. This is invisible on casual reading (the comment reads correctly as prose) and produces no error of any kind — the browser silently drops exactly one rule with no console warning, no visual "obviously broken" signal beyond a missing gap that could easily be mistaken for a simple missing CSS property rather than an entire rule failing to parse. When a CSS rule that looks syntactically correct in the source doesn't seem to apply at all, check whether `document.styleSheets` actually contains it as a parsed rule before assuming the bug is elsewhere (a missing class, a specificity fight, an inline-style override) — "does this rule exist in the live CSSOM at all" is a cheap, decisive check that should come before deeper investigation.

## Critical Discovery #110 — The Browser's ES Module Cache Survives a Brand-New Tab, Not Just a Reload; Only a Different Origin Reliably Busts It

**Context:** verifying the Design QA Punchlist's readout value-color toggle (`src/state/theme.js` gaining `getStoredValueColorMode`/`setStoredValueColorMode`), the app's module script stopped initializing entirely after the edit — `window.store`/`window.renderProgPanel` and the temporary debug hook never became defined, with no error surfaced by `read_console_messages`.

**Finding:** dynamically `import()`-ing the app's own live module script (extracted from the page and written to a fresh file, so its relative imports would resolve against the real server) threw `SyntaxError: The requested module './state/theme.js' does not provide an export named 'getStoredValueColorMode'` — even though `curl`-ing the dev server directly, and reading the `<script>` tag's own live `textContent`, both confirmed the served file was correct and up to date. Landmine #69 (Archive #97) already documented that this project's dev server + Browser pane combination can serve stale JS across a forced reload, with "open a brand-new tab" given as the fix. That fix did **not** work here: a genuinely new tab (`tabs_create`, fresh `tabId`) still resolved the stale cached module. Only restarting the local Python dev server on a **different port** (a different origin entirely) produced a tab where `import` resolved the new export correctly.

**Verification:** confirmed the module graph (not just the top-level script) was the specific layer affected — `document.styleSheets`-style CSSOM inspection was irrelevant here; instead, dynamically writing the extracted module script to a temp file and `import()`-ing it with a cache-busting query string on its *own* URL still failed, because the failure was in resolving its *nested* `import './state/theme.js'` specifier, which carries no cache-busting query of its own and is cached by exact URL independent of the importing module's URL. A fresh tab within the same browser profile shares this cache; a fresh origin (new port) does not.

**Lesson:** for JS-level staleness, Landmine #69's "new tab" remedy is necessary but not sufficient once ES module imports are involved — the module specifier cache is keyed by URL and shared across tabs of the same profile, surviving both reloads and new-tab creation. When a newly-added named export genuinely isn't visible after both a fresh reload *and* a fresh tab, the next step is a fresh **origin** (restart the dev server on a different port), not further reloading. Amended into Landmine #69 in `X5DR_Editor_Project_Context.md`.

*Last updated: 2026-07-27 (Design QA Punchlist Phase 1, same session as Brief 5) — shell chrome fidelity (patch name font, nav/inner-tab pills, top app bar, header/sub-header backgrounds — several still pre-Phase-3 hardcoded hex), the readout value-color Theme-menu toggle, and the OSC Multisound field's label spacing all implemented and browser-verified across all three color schemes. Two genuine, non-obvious findings: a CSS comment (`.vda-*/.vdf-*`) formed an accidental `*/`, silently dropping OSC's entire `.osc-content` rule and explaining the "missing gap" report (Critical Discovery #109); a stale ES module import survived even a brand-new browser tab, requiring a fresh origin to bust (Critical Discovery #110, amends Landmine #69). Eight Decisions Made rows appended for the session's cross-tab consistency fixes and layout corrections. `npx vitest run`: 234/234 runnable tests pass. Next: OSC hardware smoke-test, then Design QA Punchlist Phase 2 (Pan/on-off split, fixed column width decisions).*

## Critical Discovery #111 — OSC Drums Mode's ROM Kit Selection Uses MIDI Manual Values That Are Wrong on Real Hardware

**Context:** hardware smoke-test of `phase3-osc-tab` (Brief 5) turned up a bug in Drums mode's Kit selector: User Kit 1/2 worked correctly, but selecting any ROM kit chose the wrong kit on the device. Selecting "ROM D.Kit 1" sent `F0 42 30 36 41 18 00 08 00 F7` (Parameter Change 24, value `0x08`) and the device selected **ROM Kit 7**. Selecting ROM kits 2–8 sent `0x09` through `0x0F` and the device selected **ROM Kit 8** every time. The device ACKed every message (code `23`) — no NAK, no communication-layer problem.

**Finding:** `03_program_parameters.md` (\*2, transcribed from the manual) states the OSC1/2 Multisound param's Drums-mode encoding is `00`/`01` = User Kit 1/2, then `08`–`0F` = ROM Kit 1–8 — an unexplained gap between `01` and `08`. `src/index.html`'s `DRUM_KIT_OPTS` implemented that literally. Hardware disagrees: the real encoding has no gap — `00`/`01` = User Kit 1/2, `02`–`09` = ROM Kit 1–8. Sending `0x08` under the real encoding lands on ROM Kit 7 (`02`=1, `03`=2, `04`=3, `05`=4, `06`=5, `07`=6, `08`=7), which is exactly what was observed; `0x09`+ mapping to ROM Kit 8 for every value above the valid range is ordinary out-of-range clamping, not a separate bug. This is the same category of unreliability already flagged for `05_effect_parameters.md`'s slot ordering (Critical Discovery #11) — a manual-transcription error, not a code logic error — just newly found in the OSC/Drums parameter table instead.

**Fix:** `DRUM_KIT_OPTS` (`src/index.html`) ROM kit values changed from `8`–`15` to `2`–`9`. Every other reference to the old `8`-based encoding updated to match: the `ROM_DRUM_KITS[kitValue - 8]` lookups (2 sites) → `- 2`, the `kitValue >= 8` branch deciding User-vs-ROM kit summary rendering → `>= 2`, and the explanatory `// device value 0x0N` comments on each `ROM_DRUM_KITS` block. No SysEx-layer change needed — `sendParamChange(24, v)` already passes the option's raw `value` straight through, so correcting the options array alone fixes the wire bytes.

**Lesson:** `03_program_parameters.md`'s Drums-mode Kit table (\*2) is now confirmed unreliable, alongside `05_effect_parameters.md`'s slot ordering — add it to the same "verify against hardware capture before trusting" list, rather than assuming only the effects table needed that caution. Not yet re-verified: whether other gapped/non-contiguous value ranges elsewhere in the manual's transcribed tables carry the same kind of silent off-by-N error; worth a skeptical read rather than assuming this was an isolated transcription slip.

*Last updated: 2026-07-28 — Hardware-verified bugfix on `phase3-osc-tab`: OSC Drums mode's ROM Kit selector was sending manual-documented values (`08`–`0F`) that don't match real device behavior (`02`–`09`); corrected in `DRUM_KIT_OPTS` and its two `ROM_DRUM_KITS` array-offset consumers (Critical Discovery #111). User Kit 1/2 selection was already correct and untouched. Awaiting a second hardware pass to confirm the fix before this branch can be considered fully hardware-verified.*

## Critical Discovery #112 — CSS Grid `auto` Columns Still Absorb a Container's Leftover Width Without `justify-content: start`

**Context:** implementing Design QA Punchlist Phase 3, `.osc-top-fields` (Multisound/Octave/Outputs A/B) was changed from `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) auto auto` to `auto auto auto`, on the assumption that `auto` tracks size purely to their content, leaving any leftover row width unused. The gap between Multisound and Octave stayed visibly larger than the gap between Octave and Outputs A/B even after this change — `.osc-sound-field` (Multisound) rendered at its correct explicit `width: 17.5rem` (280px, confirmed via `getBoundingClientRect()`), but the grid **column** it sat in measured `304.32px`, 24px wider than the field itself.

**Finding:** CSS Grid's `auto` track sizing is not "content-sized, full stop" — per spec, when a grid container has more available width than its tracks' combined max-content size and there is no `fr` track to absorb the difference, the browser's default `justify-content: normal` still distributes that leftover width across the `auto` tracks (they behave like implicit `fr` tracks in this situation), rather than leaving it as unused trailing space. This is easy to miss because most real-world `auto`-column grids either have a `fr` track present (which visibly "should" absorb slack) or happen to exactly fill their container, masking the behavior.

**Fix:** added `justify-content: start` to `.osc-top-fields`. This pins every column to its actual max-content size and leaves any leftover row width as genuine unused trailing space, matching the (correct) mental model the `auto auto auto` change was written under in the first place.

**Lesson:** `grid-template-columns: auto auto auto` (or any all-`auto` grid) is not implicitly content-sized-with-trailing-slack — verify with `getComputedStyle(el).gridTemplateColumns` (which reports resolved pixel values, not the source `auto` keyword) whenever a grid's row width might exceed its columns' natural content size, and add `justify-content: start` explicitly if trailing empty space (not redistributed growth) is the intended behavior. Also a reminder that a plausible-sounding fix (`min-width: 0` on the item, tried first here) can pass a "does the CSS apply" check via `getComputedStyle` while doing nothing for the actual symptom — the isolating measurement (comparing the *track's* resolved width to the *item's* rendered width) is what actually located the real cause. See Landmine #78.

## Critical Discovery #113 — A "Cancel This Ancestor's Padding" Negative-Margin Hack Silently Drifts Out of Sync When the Padding Changes Elsewhere

**Context:** `.prog-header`/`.combi-header` (the sub-header row containing the patch name and inner-tabs) used `margin: 0 -1rem 0.75rem -1rem` to cancel `#content`'s own side padding, so the row could span the full shell width rather than sitting inset inside `#content`'s padded box — a technique that worked correctly when `#content`'s side padding was `1rem` (16px). This session's Design QA Punchlist Phase 3 work changed `#content`'s side padding to `1.375rem` (22px) to match the Claude Design mockup, without updating this margin to match — silently reintroducing a ~12px (6px each side) width mismatch between `#header`/`#nav` (full shell width) and the sub-header row (now only partially compensated), reported by the user as "header/nav should be reduced to match the sub-nav width."

**Finding:** a negative-margin-cancels-ancestor-padding technique creates an implicit numeric coupling between two CSS rules that has no enforcement mechanism — nothing errors, warns, or visually breaks obviously when the two values drift apart; the symptom (a several-pixel width mismatch) reads as a plausible independent bug rather than an obviously-connected one, and was initially miscategorized as "which side is wrong" rather than "these two values must match."

**Fix:** `.prog-header`/`.combi-header`'s margin corrected from `-1rem` to `-1.375rem`, matching `#content`'s current side padding exactly. Comments on both rules now state explicitly that this value must track `#content`'s side padding.

**Lesson:** any negative-margin-cancels-padding pairing across two separate CSS rules is a latent landmine — search for all uses of a container's padding value before changing it, not just the container's own rule, and prefer a shared CSS custom property over duplicated literal values for exactly this kind of cross-rule numeric coupling if either value is likely to change again. See Landmine #79.

## Critical Discovery #114 — Pan's Position and Its Off State Are the Same Wire Value, Never Sendable Together — Confirms the Split Knob Must Fully Disable, Not Just Dim

**Context:** OSC's Pan was split (Design QA Punchlist Phase 2/3) into a plain bidirectional knob plus a separate Outputs A/B toggle. The knob dimmed correctly when Outputs A/B was Off, but the user asked whether it should also become fully non-interactive, suspecting Pan's position and its On/Off state might be coupled at the wire level such that there's no way to "stage" a position while Off.

**Finding:** confirmed via `NOTE 12` (`02_sysex_format.md`, Value Data Format used at Parameter Change) — Pan is a single signed value on a single Parameter Change (`panParam`), carrying either the real position (`0`–`30`) or the `-1` Off sentinel (Landmine #44). There is no second bit or separate message for on/off; the position and the Off state are mutually exclusive encodings of the exact same byte. Dragging the knob while Off could therefore never produce a meaningful wire message — at best a silent no-op (the existing `if (outputsOn)` guard), which reads as a broken control rather than an inert one.

**Fix:** `updatePanDim()` now sets `pointer-events: none` on the whole knob group (not just a CSS opacity dim on the ring) whenever Outputs A/B is Off, fully blocking both drag and click-to-edit. Verified against a real simulated mouse click at the control's actual screen coordinates and `document.elementFromPoint()` (both perform real hit-testing) — not a programmatic `.click()` call, which bypasses `pointer-events` entirely and gave a false pass on the first verification attempt.

**Lesson:** when a split UI control's two halves both write to the same underlying single-value wire parameter, check the actual protocol encoding (not just the current code's behavior) before deciding whether the "inactive" half should merely look dimmed or be fully non-interactive — and when testing `pointer-events: none`, use real hit-testing (`elementFromPoint`, a simulated `computer`-tool click) rather than a direct `.click()` call, which silently bypasses the CSS property being tested.

## Critical Discovery #115 — A Zero-Reference Knob Tick Needs a Size-Aware Treatment, Not One Constant Scaled by ViewBox

**Context:** user design review noted that every knob (unidirectional and bidirectional) reads as "inactive" at its zero/center value, since the accent fill arc has zero length there. A fixed reference tick was added to `buildKnobBase` (drawn in the shared `100`-unit SVG viewBox, scaling proportionally with the knob's physical container size like every other element in it) and validated first via a live interactive mockup at the small 38px size (used by 38 of ~41 knob instances) — approved as-is. The same tick, unchanged, read as visually heavy at the 82px hero size (only 3 instances: VDA/VDF's Level/Cutoff), and its own rounded end visually collided with the track's rounded start-cap once any small non-zero fill was present, producing an odd "hook" shape.

**Finding:** a tick sized purely as a proportion of the viewBox (thus proportional to physical knob size) does not read as proportionally-equivalent at every physical size — a treatment correct at 38px became too prominent at 82px, confirmed via true-to-size (not scaled-up) browser screenshots at both sizes before and after the fix. Separately, `stroke-linecap: round` adds a half-stroke-width semicircular overhang beyond a line's mathematical endpoints — even after clamping the hero tick's *length* to exactly the ring's own thickness (`8` units, matching the ring's `stroke-width`), the tick's rounded caps still visibly overshot both the ring's outer and inner edges by ~1.5 units each.

**Fix:** `buildKnobBase` now branches on `size >= LARGE_KNOB_SIZE`: small/default knobs keep the original 16-unit tick with `stroke-linecap: round` (unchanged, already approved); the large hero size uses an 8-unit tick (exactly the ring's thickness, so it's fully covered by the fill arc for any non-zero value — accepted, since the tick's only job was fixing *zero* looking inactive) with `stroke-linecap: butt` to eliminate the round-cap overhang. `knobOffDetent` (dormant, componentGallery-only) deliberately excluded — it already has its own floor marker (`offDot`) at the same position.

**Lesson:** a shared visual treatment expressed as "one constant in the same relative coordinate space as everything else" is not automatically size-invariant in how it *reads* — verify at each real physical size actually used in the app (not just a uniformly-scaled mockup) before generalizing a design decision approved at one size to every size. `stroke-linecap: round`'s overhang is easy to forget about when a tick/line's length is deliberately clamped to butt up against another element's edge; `butt` caps are the correct choice whenever a line's endpoint is meant to be visually flush with something else, not just aesthetically rounded.

## Critical Discovery #116 — `controls.test.js`'s Sandbox Timeout Had Been Silently Masking a Real, Pre-Existing Test Failure All Session

**Context:** every `npx vitest run` this session (and reportedly prior sessions) reported "234/234 runnable tests pass, `controls.test.js` unrunnable — worker-pool timeout, environment issue." Mid-session, one run of `controls.test.js` happened to actually complete (293 total tests, up from 234) and reported **one genuine failure**: `egCurveWidget`'s width-sizing test (`fills available width up to its natural size and scales as one unit via aspect-ratio... expected 'calc(var(--control-scale) * 243.6px)' to be '100%'`) — confirmed unrelated to this session's own knob/chrome work (no shared code path with `buildKnobBase`/`egCurveWidget`).

**Finding:** the "234/234 pass" framing used throughout this and prior sessions was true only for the 6 files that could actually run — `controls.test.js` timing out was silently treated as "234/234, environment issue, not a regression," which is accurate for *whether this session broke something* but not for *whether the suite as a whole is actually green*. A real failure sat undetected in the untested file for an unknown number of prior sessions, discovered only by chance when the timeout didn't occur.

**Fix:** none yet — logged as a Current Next Action, deliberately deferred since the next planned task (envelope curve widget redesign, per this session's user direction) will touch `egCurveWidget` directly anyway.

**Lesson:** "N/N tests pass" is only a meaningful claim if N is confirmed to include every test file that exists, not just every file that happened to finish running — when a suite has a flaky/timing-out file, explicitly note in the Progress Log which files were actually exercised, not just the pass count of whichever ones completed. See Landmine #80.
*Last updated: 2026-07-28 (Design QA Punchlist Phase 3/5 implementation, post-approval hardware-adjacent review session) — Phase 3 (fixed 1400px canvas, black backdrop, panel-width standard) and Phase 5 for OSC (Pan split, knob zero-tick) fully implemented on `phase3-punchlist-layout`, browser-verified. Five Critical Discoveries this session: #112 (CSS Grid `auto` columns absorb leftover container width without `justify-content:start`), #113 (a negative-margin-cancels-padding hack silently drifted out of sync when the padding it cancels changed elsewhere — Landmine #79), #114 (Pan's position and Off state are the same wire value per NOTE 12, confirming the split knob needed full `pointer-events:none` disable, not just dimming), #115 (the zero-reference knob tick needed a size-aware treatment — 16-unit round tick at small/default sizes, 8-unit butt-capped tick at the 82px hero size, after live comparison at true physical sizes), and #116 (`controls.test.js` finally completed mid-session after timing out all prior sessions, revealing one genuine pre-existing failure in `egCurveWidget`'s width-sizing test, unrelated to this session's work — Landmine #80, deliberately deferred to the upcoming envelope-widget redesign). User visually approved the final knob tick treatment ("Knobs look fantastic now"). Next: hardware smoke-test this branch (Pan control specifically), then the envelope curve widget redesign (which will also fix the newly-surfaced `egCurveWidget` test failure along the way).*

## Critical Discovery #117 — `egCurveWidget`'s Missing `preserveAspectRatio` Was Silently Distorting Every Cross-Tab Comparison, and Retroactively Explains the Prior Height-Retuning Saga

**Context:** starting the Design QA Punchlist's Phase 4 (envelope widget work), the user asked to slightly reduce the EG Time Mod reference line's visual weight, noting it read "slightly too much" on VDF but "way too much" on OSC's Pitch EG — the same nominal `stroke-width`/dash config in both places. Before touching any numbers, the actual rendered geometry was measured directly rather than trusted by eye.

**Finding:** `egCurveWidget`'s `<svg>` never set `preserveAspectRatio`, so it used the browser default `xMidYMid meet`. VDA/VDF pass an explicit `width` (`EG_FOUR_COL_WIDTH`, computed to match the 4 stage-field columns below, not the widget's own natural geometry); OSC's Pitch EG passes no `width` override at all, so its natural width matches its `viewBox` 1:1. Measured live via `svg.getScreenCTM()`: OSC's scale factor was `1.0` on both axes; VDF's was `0.596` on both axes (`a`/`d` on the CTM identical, confirming `meet`'s uniform-scale behavior). Since `meet` scales *both* axes by the same factor bound by whichever is more constrained, this single fact explained two previously-unconnected symptoms at once: (1) the *exact* stroke-width/reference-line config rendered at very different visual weights per tab (VDF's reference line at ~1.49px effective width vs. OSC's full 2.5px), and (2) the curve's vertical extent fell short of its own configured `height` on VDA/VDF specifically (only ~60% of it, in the case measured), which is very likely the real, previously-unidentified cause of Archive #103–#105's three separate rounds of ad hoc envelope-height retuning — each pass was chasing a moving target, because the configured height and the actually-rendered height were never the same number to begin with.

**Fix:** `preserveAspectRatio="none"` lets width and height scale independently, matching what the surrounding code's own comments already assumed was happening. This makes the y-axis always exactly 1:1 (viewBox height and configured `height` are the same number by construction) and leaves only the x-axis scalable, when a caller overrides `width` away from the geometry's own natural width. `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"` was added to the trace, ghost, and reference-line strokes so stroke width renders as constant on-screen pixels regardless of any remaining x-axis scale — meaning one shared stroke-width constant now looks identical on every tab, which was never true before. Point markers (fill shapes, not strokes, so `non-scaling-stroke` doesn't apply) were switched from `<circle>` to `<ellipse>` with an x-radius compensated by the measured x-scale factor (`rx = EG_MARKER_RADIUS / scaleX`, `ry` unscaled) so they stay visually round instead of squashing whenever `width` is overridden.

**Verification:** live-measured before/after on a controlled 4-stage config at VDF's real `width`/`height`: pre-fix, marker width/height differed between VDA/VDF and OSC test cases; post-fix, both report identical 8×8 (later 6×6 after the separate weight-reduction pass) regardless of which tab's `width` override is used. `controls.test.js`'s existing width-sizing test (Landmine #80/Archive #116, previously the one known pre-existing failure) started passing again as a side effect, since it was asserting the *old*, pre-Phase-4 responsive-sizing behavior against code that had since moved to fixed-pixel sizing — rewritten to assert the current fixed-size/no-shrink behavior instead.

**Lesson:** when the exact same component config renders at visibly different weights on different call sites, check the actual rendering transform (`getScreenCTM()`) before assuming the difference is data-dependent or needs per-instance tuning — a missing `preserveAspectRatio` on an SVG that mixes an externally-controlled `width` with an internally-computed `viewBox` is a classic, easy-to-miss source of exactly this symptom, and can silently invalidate any amount of "measure and re-tune" work done against the distorted rendering rather than the true one.

## Critical Discovery #118 — An SVG's Default Clip Cuts Off Strokes and Markers Exactly at Legitimate Data Extremes

**Context:** after Critical Discovery #117's fix let curves render at their true, undistorted scale for the first time, user visual review of a steep VDA attack (Attack Time near 0, Attack Level near 99) reported the curve's line and its top-left marker rendering thinner/partially missing right where the curve meets the window's top-left corner.

**Finding:** `egCurveWidget`'s trace legitimately starts at `x=0` (time 0) and can reach `y=0`/`y=height` (level 99/-99, or the floor). A point exactly on the SVG's own boundary has half its stroke width and half its marker radius clipped away, because an SVG root clips to its `viewBox` by default (UA stylesheet `overflow:hidden`) — this was invisible before Critical Discovery #117's fix specifically *because* the letterbox distortion described there was incidentally shrinking the rendered curve away from the true edges on VDA/VDF, and simply wasn't tested at a steep-enough angle on OSC (which had no letterbox but also hadn't been visually reviewed at this specific extreme case).

**Fix:** added `overflow="visible"` to the `<svg>` element. The existing 14px window inset (`EG_WINDOW_PAD_X`/`Y`, this session's Decisions Made) already provides ample room in the surrounding padded window for the overflow to render into — neither the `wrap` span nor the `windowEl` clip their own content, so this was the only change needed.

**Verification:** measured live against the exact steep-attack case from the report — the top-left marker's edge now sits a clean 10px inside the window's own border on both axes (well within the 14px padding), confirmed via `getBoundingClientRect()` comparison between the marker and the window, not just a visual screenshot check.

**Lesson:** any SVG whose content is deliberately drawn flush to its own `viewBox` boundary (as opposed to leaving natural margin) needs `overflow="visible"` plus external padding to avoid clipping strokes/markers exactly at the data points most likely to matter (extremes, not the average case) — and a distortion bug elsewhere in the same component (Critical Discovery #117) can mask this kind of edge-clipping bug by accident, so re-check edge cases specifically after fixing an unrelated scaling issue, rather than assuming a visually-clean regression pass covers it.

## Critical Discovery #119 — A Flex Column Double-Counts a Child's Own `margin-bottom` Plus the Parent's `gap`

**Context:** investigating why VDA's Level knob and VDF's Cutoff knob sat further below their own "LEVEL"/"CUTOFF" label than the sibling EG panel's own label-to-window gap, despite both using what looked like the same ~10px spacing convention.

**Finding:** `.vda-panel-label`/`.vdf-panel-label` (the shared label class used by every panel) carries its own `margin-bottom: 0.6rem`. `.vda-level-panel`/`.vdf-hero-panel` (the two 150px-wide hero panels specifically) are flex columns that *also* declare `gap: 0.6rem`/`0.625rem` between their children. Since the label is a flex child too, both the label's own bottom margin and the parent's `gap` applied between it and the next child (the knob), stacking to ~19.2px instead of the intended 9.6px — visually reading as the knob sitting noticeably lower than a sibling panel whose own label-to-content spacing comes from a normal-flow `margin-bottom` alone (no competing `gap`, since that panel isn't a flex container). Confirmed by direct measurement: label-bottom to knob-top gap measured exactly `19.188px` (≈ 2×9.6), not `9.6px`.

**Fix:** `.vda-level-panel .vda-panel-label`/`.vdf-hero-panel .vdf-panel-label` given `margin-bottom: 0`, scoped specifically to the label inside those two flex panels (the shared base label class is unchanged everywhere else). This shrank both panels' natural content height by ~9.6px, which had knock-on effects on every bottom-alignment value already tuned against them this session (VDA's `padding-bottom`, `VDF_EG_HEIGHT`) — each needed re-measuring and re-tuning afterward, not just the gap fix in isolation.

**Lesson:** a CSS `gap` on a flex/grid container and a `margin` on one of its own children are two independent spacing mechanisms that stack rather than one superseding the other — when a component's implicit spacing (a shared label class's own margin) is reused inside a container that *also* defines `gap` for the same axis, check for exactly this kind of doubling before assuming a value needs to be tuned upward. Also a reminder that fixing a spacing bug which shrinks/grows an element's natural size requires re-verifying every other measurement that was tuned against that element's *old* size, not just confirming the spacing itself now looks right.

## Critical Discovery #120 — `align-items: center` Only Translates a Flex Item's Visible Content by *Half* an Asymmetric Margin, Not the Full Amount

**Context:** the hero knob's value readout (`readoutMode:'below'`) reads as off-center under the ring, because its wrapping element (`.ctrl-readout-wrap`) also contains a permanently-reserved, hover-revealed stepper (Landmine #73) that the number itself doesn't visually occupy. A `margin-left` was added to shift the visible number back to center — the first attempt used the exact measured offset (7px) and only closed half the gap.

**Finding:** `align-items: center` on a flex container centers each item's full **margin box**, not its border-box position independently of margin. Adding `margin-left: 7px` to an item increases that item's total margin-box width by 7px on one side only (asymmetric); centering then splits that *extra* width evenly across both visual sides of the centered position, so only half of the added margin (3.5px) actually translates the item's visible content — confirmed by direct measurement: `margin-left: 7px` moved the number's rendered center by exactly `3.504px`, not `7px`.

**Fix:** doubled the margin to `14px`, which produced the intended `7px` visual shift (confirmed to `0.004px` via `getBoundingClientRect()` comparison against the knob's own true center) and, separately, confirmed with a forced-visibility test (`stepperEl.style.visibility = 'visible'` without triggering real `:hover`) that the number's position doesn't move at all when the reserved stepper becomes visible — the fix only had to compensate for `align-items: center`'s own math, not for anything about the stepper's reveal mechanism.

**Lesson:** when compensating for an off-center flex item by adding margin on one side only, the required margin is **double** the measured visual offset if the parent uses `align-items: center` (or any `justify-content`/`align-items: center` equivalent) — centering redistributes an asymmetric margin's extra space rather than simply preserving the item's shifted position. Verify the actual resulting shift with a live measurement rather than assuming the naive 1:1 margin-to-shift relationship that would hold under `flex-start`/`stretch` alignment.

## Critical Discovery #121 — `egCurveWidget`'s Omitted-`width` Fallback Is a Fixed Worst-Case Content Estimate, Not a Responsive Fill Value

**Context:** while comparing OSC's Pitch EG window against VDF's own envelope window ahead of a planned size-matching pass, the Pitch EG window measured 473.5px wide even though its wrapping column (`.osc-eg-window-col`) was `flex:1` inside a 652px-wide flex row — apparently coincidentally close to VDF's own deliberately-set 470px width, but with a visible ~190px gap of unused space between the window and the stage-fields column beside it, which a plain `flex:1` should not have left.

**Finding:** `egCurveWidget`'s `width` config, when omitted (as Pitch EG's original call did), falls back to `naturalWidth = geo.totalWidth + 2*EG_WINDOW_PAD_X`, where `geo.totalWidth` is computed by `egGeometry` as `stages.length * timeMax * pxPerTimeUnit` (adjusted for the sustain segment) — a fixed pixel value derived purely from stage count and the shared time-axis scaling constant, with no relationship whatsoever to the widget's actual container width or any `flex:1`/percentage sizing. It only *looked* like it might be responsive because the number happened to land close to VDF's own fixed 470px — Pitch EG has one fewer stage than VDF at the same `pxPerTimeUnit`, which is why the two fixed values were coincidentally similar rather than actually related.

**Fix:** not a bug fix (the fallback behaves exactly as its own code comment describes) — but this session's OSC tidy-up replaced the omitted `width` with an explicit `OSC_PITCH_EG_WINDOW_WIDTH = 470` matching VDF, and changed `.osc-eg-window-col`/`.osc-eg-fields-col` from `flex:1` to `flex:0 0 auto`, since `flex:1` was never doing anything useful once the widget's own rendered width is a fixed value independent of its container.

**Lesson:** a `flex:1` (or percentage-width) wrapper around a child does not guarantee the child itself is actually responsive to that wrapper — check whether the child's own rendered size is genuinely driven by the container (e.g. an explicit `width:100%`) versus carrying its own independent fixed value that merely happens to render inside a flexible box. Extends Landmine #74's fixed-vs-responsive precedent (Critical Discovery #103–#105) to the specific omitted-config-argument case, which hadn't previously been exercised in a `flex:1` context.

## Critical Discovery #122 — An Inset `box-shadow` Ring Follows the Element's Own `border-radius`, Not an Ancestor's Clip Path

**Context:** a user-directed toggle redesign replaced the fused segmented strip's (`buildFusedToggleGroup`, shared by `toggleButtonGroup`/`threeWayToggle`) solid active-segment fill with a transparent background plus an inset `box-shadow` ring. The strip's seamless, continuous-pill look has always come from a single shared outer border + `border-radius` + `overflow:hidden` on the wrapping `<span>`, with individual `<button>` segments carrying no `border-radius` of their own — correct for the original flat-fill design, since a middle segment's flat edges need no rounding and the wrap's own clip handles the strip's outer corners. Once the *active* segment's own inset ring could land at either end of the strip, it rendered as a hard-edged rectangle visibly poking past the wrap's rounded corner — reported by the user via screenshot, showing "Poly," "Off," and other edge-position toggles with square-cornered rings inside an otherwise rounded-pill control.

**Finding:** `box-shadow` (inset or otherwise) is computed relative to the element's own border edge and follows that same element's own `border-radius` — it has no awareness of an ancestor's `overflow:hidden`/`border-radius` clip. The wrap's rounded corners only clip the strip's outer silhouette; a descendant's own box-shadow is drawn using purely the descendant's own (default: `0`) border-radius, then merely clipped by the ancestor's box if it happens to overflow it — it is never itself rounded by the ancestor's radius.

**Fix:** the first and last button in each fused group now get a matching corner radius on their outer edge only (`{CHIP_RADIUS} 0 0 {CHIP_RADIUS}` for the first, `0 {CHIP_RADIUS} {CHIP_RADIUS} 0` for the last, computed from each button's index in `buildFusedToggleGroup`'s item loop); middle buttons correctly stay square-cornered, matching a flat segment boundary. The active ring now follows the strip's rounded ends correctly.

**Lesson:** any box-shadow or outline applied to an individual child inside a parent whose rounded corners come from `overflow:hidden` needs a matching `border-radius` on whichever children sit at the parent's rounded edges — the parent's clip affects only the parent's own rendered silhouette, never a child's own shadow geometry. This class of bug is invisible in a computed-style inspector (the box-shadow's color/inset values look completely correct) and only shows up in an actual rendered screenshot of the affected corner — verify visually, not just via `getComputedStyle`, whenever a shadow/outline is added to an element that sits at a clipped ancestor's rounded edge.

## Critical Discovery #123 — The Seven Browser-Like Modals' Shared Chrome Is Not Scoped the Way It First Appeared

**Context:** asked whether restyling the Multisound Browser (per a new Claude Design mockup) would also update the Drum Sound and Effect Type Browsers, since all three share the `.sound-browser-overlay` wrapper class. The initial answer — yes for those three, no for the Prog/Combi Patch Browser, which uses a separate `.browser-overlay` wrapper — was correct about the *outer* wrapper but incomplete.

**Finding:** the outer wrapper (`.browser-overlay` vs. `.sound-browser-overlay`) only controls positioning/backdrop/z-index (centered vs. top-anchored, z-index 100 vs. 150). The *inner* chrome — `.browser-overlay-panel`, `.browser-overlay-header`, `.browser-overlay-title`, `.browser-overlay-close`, `.browser-overlay-footer` — is a single shared class family used identically inside **both** wrapper types, across all seven browser-like modals in the app: Patch Browser, Write Browser (`.browser-overlay`), Multisound, Drum Sound, Effect Type, Program Browser, and Copy Effects Source Browser (`.sound-browser-overlay`). A grep for `browser-overlay-panel` across the markup was what surfaced this — the two wrapper families were never actually chrome-independent, only positioning-independent.

**Fix:** not a bug — the restyle (this session, Decisions Made table) was scoped correctly once this was found, deliberately touching the shared inner classes so all seven modals updated together, rather than restyling `.sound-browser-overlay`'s own three modals and leaving Patch/Write/Program/Copy Effects behind.

**Lesson:** when assessing a shared-styling question ("if I change X, what else changes"), check every class actually present in the target markup, not just the most visually obvious wrapper class — a component can have more than one shared-class family at different structural depths (outer positioning vs. inner content chrome), each with its own, independently-scoped blast radius.

## Critical Discovery #124 — A Child's Own Explicit CSS Rule Always Beats an Ancestor's Rule for Inherited Properties, Regardless of Specificity

**Context:** after restyling `.patch-table`'s selected-row highlight from a hardcoded blue to `var(--accent-fill)`/`var(--bg-page)` (Critical Discovery #123's session), the user reported the selected row's index number (`.num-col`) stayed dim and hard to read against the new bright accent background, while the row's name text was fully legible.

**Finding:** `.patch-table td.selected` sets `color: var(--bg-page)` on the `<td>`, intending it to apply to the whole cell including the `.num-col` `<span>` inside it via normal CSS inheritance. But `.patch-table .num-col` also has its own explicit `color: var(--text-secondary)` rule, declared separately, targeting the span directly. Because `.num-col`'s rule is an explicit match on the span itself — not an inherited value flowing down from the td — it wins unconditionally, regardless of specificity comparison against `td.selected` (which is actually higher-specificity than `.num-col` alone, `(0,2,1)` vs `(0,2,0)`, and would win if this were a same-element specificity contest). Specificity only resolves conflicts between rules matching the *same* element; it has no bearing on inherited-vs-explicit conflicts on a *descendant* element — an explicit rule on a child always overrides an inherited value from a parent, full stop.

**Fix:** added `.patch-table td.selected .num-col { color: var(--bg-page); opacity: 0.7; }` — an explicit rule on the span itself, which now wins on the same explicit-beats-inherited basis. `opacity: 0.7` keeps the number reading as secondary to the bold name (matching the reference mockup's own visual hierarchy) while now being fully legible.

**Lesson:** if a child element's color/property looks wrong despite an ancestor's rule that appears to target it correctly, check whether the child has *any* rule of its own for that property — including old rules from before the ancestor's rule existed — before assuming a specificity fight is the cause. Inheritance and specificity are resolved by entirely different mechanisms; conflating them (as the original "should be higher-specificity, so why isn't it winning" instinct did here) leads to the wrong fix.

## Critical Discovery #125 — Equal Character Count Does Not Mean Equal Rendered Width in a Proportional Font

**Context:** the Control tab rebuild (Brief 6) reused a mockup-specified flex/grid layout with fixed gaps, verified by rendering real field labels through a temporary debug hook (per ADR-0008 §4) rather than trusting the static mockup export. In Double OSC mode, "Pitch MG Frequency - OSC 2" wrapped onto a second line inside the AT + Mod Wheel panel, while the structurally identical "Pitch MG Intensity - OSC 1/2" pair one panel over (Mod Wheel) did not — despite "Frequency" and "Intensity" being the same character count (9 letters).

**Finding:** measured via `getBoundingClientRect()`/`scrollWidth` against the live-rendered DOM: "Pitch MG Frequency - OSC 1" needed ~180px, "- OSC 2" ~182px, against a per-item budget of exactly 180px at the original 16–24px gap values — a 2px overage was enough to trigger wrapping. The equivalent "Intensity" labels needed only ~172–175px, comfortably inside the same budget. In Inter (and most proportional fonts), "Frequency" renders measurably wider than "Intensity" despite equal letter count — different letterforms (e.g. 'q', 'F') simply occupy more horizontal space than others ('n', 't', 's'). The mockup's static HTML export never caught this because it used fixed-position absolute/inline-styled `<span>`s with illustrative sample text at a canvas snapshot in time, not a live flex/grid layout under real content — so its gap values were chosen without ever actually testing whether real label text fit inside them.

**Fix:** the AT + Mod Wheel panel's OSC pair was changed from a strict 2-column CSS grid (which forces both items into equal, non-negotiable track widths) to a flex `.control-pair-row` (which lets each item size to its own content, borrowing slack from whichever sibling needs less) — matching the pattern the Mod Wheel panel already used successfully. Combined with the later user-directed column-width increase (420px→460px, Decisions Made table), the wrap no longer occurs with ~18–20px of margin to spare.

**Lesson:** never assume two labels of equal character count need equal layout width — measure the actual rendered text, not the string length. This generalizes ADR-0008's existing "verify against real content, not synthetic/mockup data" rule (already established for VDF's alignment checks) to include *layout budget* calculations, not just visual alignment: a gap or column-width value copied from a mockup that never rendered real text through it should be treated as unverified until checked against actual `getBoundingClientRect()`/`scrollWidth` measurements.

## Critical Discovery #126 — Control Tab's "Mod Wheel" Panel Grouped a Field That Isn't Actually Mod-Wheel-Driven

**Context:** hardware verification of the newly-rebuilt Control tab (Brief 6, Critical Discovery #125) checked each panel's live behavior against its physical-controller source, panel by panel.

**Finding:** "VDF MG Intensity" (`modWheel.vdfMgInt`, Parameter Change 21) was grouped inside the Mod Wheel panel, alongside Pitch MG Intensity — both share the `modWheel.*` store-path prefix, which is presumably why the original Control tab inventory/brief assumed a common physical source. Hardware capture showed VDF MG Intensity is actually driven by Breath Controller (#2), not the Mod Wheel at all; only Pitch MG Intensity in that panel is genuinely Mod-Wheel-sourced. The `modWheel.` store-path prefix is a pre-existing internal naming artifact (likely inherited from the manual's own Parameter Change table grouping) and was never a reliable signal for the field's real controller source — the same category of trap as Landmine #40's `filter*` flat-key naming coincidence.

**Fix:** moved the VDF MG Intensity knob out of the Mod Wheel panel into its own new "Breath Controller (#2)" panel directly below it, same right column, matching `.control-column` spacing conventions. Mod Wheel panel resized down to its remaining single OSC pair; the `.control-stack` wrapper that stacked two panels-worth of content inside one panel is now unused and was removed. No Parameter Change number, `workingCopy` store path, or `data-sync` key changed — purely a layout/grouping correction, browser-verified only (297/297 tests, no console errors).

**Lesson:** a shared store-path prefix (`modWheel.*`, `filter*`, etc.) reflects how the manual's own reference tables grouped a field, not necessarily the field's true physical-controller source — do not assume two fields under the same prefix share a controller just because they share a name segment; verify each field's actual source via hardware capture, the same standing rule Landmine #9 already established for effect parameter ordering.

*Last updated: 2026-07-30 — Multisound Browser mockup (Claude Design option 6b) applied to all seven browser-like modals' shared chrome (Patch/Write/Multisound/Drum/Effect/Program/Copy Effects — a wider blast radius than initially assumed, Critical Discovery #123), plus three follow-up fixes: removed the redundant `×` close button app-wide, removed `.patch-table`'s keyboard-focus outline, and fixed a selection-highlight contrast bug on the index number (Critical Discovery #124). Control tab (Phase 3 Brief 6) fully rebuilt against the component library per its own inventory doc and design handoff — new `.control-*` CSS family, per-oscillator fields changed from a hidden-in-Single "1 / 2" pair to always-present/dimmed-in-Single knobs, a real label-wrapping bug caught and fixed via real-content verification (Critical Discovery #125), then widened 420px→460px per user follow-up for more breathing room between knob columns. Separately, added a File → Load → "Factory Sounds" menu item embedding the factory soundbank directly in `src/index.html` for one-click dev/demo loading straight into Prog Edit A00, keeping the existing destructive-write confirmation. All of the above browser-verified only (three themes, Single/Double OSC, no console errors) — hardware re-verification of this session's browser-chrome, Control tab, and Factory Sounds changes not yet done. `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass throughout.*

## Critical Discovery #127 — MG Status (`*11-3-3`) Is a Byte With Type-Hardwired Bits, and the Editor Sends Only the Free One

**Context:** pre-implementation investigation ahead of the Effect tab's Phase 3 retrofit (ADR-0008 Stage 1). While auditing `EFFECT_TYPES`' parameter formats for the Claude Design inventory doc, the `sinTri`/`mgStatus` format split raised a question about `buildMgStatusCtrl` — a 3-checkbox control that exists in code but is referenced by zero `EFFECT_TYPES` defs. The user supplied manual screenshots (`05_effect_parameters.md`'s underlying scans) for the four type-pairs that reference MG Status: 19/20 (Stereo Chorus 1/2), 32/33 (Phaser 1/2), 35/36 (Auto Pan/Tremolo), 42/43 (Delay/Chorus, Delay/Flanger).

**Finding:** MG Status is a single Parameter Change byte with 3 bits (`bit0`=Waveform Sin/Tri, `bit1`=Phase 0°/180°, `bit2`=Wave Shape Normal/for-Flanger), but **only one bit is ever genuinely user-adjustable for a given type** — the other one or two are hardwired constants specific to that exact type, denoted in the manual by a `←` assignment arrow, not a `=` range. Critically, *which* bit is free varies by type family: for 19/20/32/33/35/36 it's `bit0` (fixed `bit1`, sometimes `bit2`); for 42/43 it's `bit0` for 42 but **nothing at all** for 43 (`bit0` is also hardwired there — confirmed independently by the device's own front-panel LCD screens for type 43 showing no Sin/Tri field at all, per the manual's own screen-capture transcription). The two type-pairs' shared-table convention (`bit1 ← 1, (0)`) gives the first-listed type's value before the parenthesis, the second's inside it — and this exactly matches each pair's own prose description (Phaser 1 = out-of-phase L/R modulation, Phaser 2 = in-phase; Auto Pan = continuously panned, Tremolo = uniform volume) — i.e. bit1 (Phase) is literally *why* two effect types with different numbers exist for what is otherwise the same DSP engine, not a spare control bit.

`buildPerTypeParams`'s `sinTri` branch and the type-switch reset loop (duplicated between `buildEffectColumn` and the Easy tab's `buildEasyEffCol`) both send only the raw `0`/`1` toggle value as the *entire* byte, silently zeroing whichever hardwired bit(s) that specific type requires to be non-zero. `buildMgStatusCtrl` (the 3-checkbox control) turned out to be dead code from an earlier, incorrect reading of the same table — no `EFFECT_TYPES` def references it; the existing `phaser`/`rotary`/`autoPan` defs already correctly reduced to a single `sinTri`-format bit (correct instinct, incomplete fix — they dropped the two non-existent controls but never asserted the hardwired bit's actual value).

**Verification — two independent methods, both hardware-run by the user:**
1. **Byte-level audit** (`Effect_Tab_MGStatus_Hardware_Test_Plan.md`): captured the live outgoing Parameter Change for all 8 affected types, both at type-selection baseline and via the live Sin/Tri toggle. Result matched the bit-math model exactly on every row — types 19, 20, 32, 35 (all requiring `bit1=1`) sent `0`/`1` instead of `2`/`3`; types 33, 36, 42 (hardwired bits all `0`) were correct by coincidence; type 43 sent `0` instead of the required `4`.
2. **Device dump readback**: selected Phaser 1, wrote to device, then imported the program dump and decoded it (`unpack7bit` per `src/midi/parser.js`). `eff1Params` offset 4 (Sin/Tri/MG Status, per `phaser`'s hardware-verified offset order) read back as `0`, not `2` — proving the device stores exactly what's transmitted and does **not** self-correct or derive the phase bit internally from the type number. This directly answered an open question from earlier in the investigation (whether a wrong bit might be silently masked by the device) in the negative — the bug is real at the storage level, independent of any audible test.

An initial listening test (Phaser 1 sounding different via editor vs. front panel) was run and seemed to confirm audibility, but was **retracted by the user** — the actual cause was a Manual/Mod Depth/Mod Speed default-level mismatch, unrelated to MG Status. The dump-readback method (above) is what actually settled the "does it matter" question; the retraction is recorded here so a future session doesn't cite the original (incorrect) audible-difference claim as evidence.

A second, related finding from the same investigation: the type-switch reset loop unconditionally sends `0` for every offset `0`–`6`, regardless of whether the selected type's own `EFFECT_TYPES` entry defines that offset — confirmed via a targeted check on type 46 (Delay/Phaser, no MG Status documented at all), where the per-param-edit test showed no phantom traffic but the type-switch reset did. This is the same mechanism that causes type 43's bug and is broader than MG Status alone.

**Fix:** not yet implemented — specified in `Effect_Tab_MGStatus_Bugfix_Brief.md` for a dedicated `fix/effect-mg-status` branch (per-type hardwired-bit lookup table; generalized reset loop that only touches offsets a type actually defines; one explicit exception for type 43's undefined-but-required offset; shared extraction of the reset logic between `buildEffectColumn` and `buildEasyEffCol`). Must merge to `main` and hardware-verify before the Effect tab's own Phase 3 rendering-layer retrofit begins, per ADR-0008's data-layer/rendering-layer separation.

**Lesson:** a shared reference-table byte with multiple named bits does not mean all of them are user-facing controls — some can be per-type hardwired constants that are the entire reason two type numbers exist for what is otherwise one DSP engine. When a manual table uses assignment notation (`←`) rather than range notation (`=`/`~`) for a bit or field, treat it as a fixed constant to be asserted on every write for that type, not a value to read from a control the UI doesn't have. Also: a retracted piece of evidence (the audio test) is worth recording explicitly, not just quietly dropping — a future session re-deriving "was this audible" from a stale summary could otherwise cite the wrong conclusion.

*Last updated: 2026-07-31 — Effect tab pre-implementation investigation (ahead of the Phase 3 retrofit) found and hardware-confirmed the MG Status bug described in Critical Discovery #127 — affects 5 of 8 types (19, 20, 32, 35, 43), confirmed via both a byte-level audit and a device dump readback. Fix specified in a new `Effect_Tab_MGStatus_Bugfix_Brief.md` for a dedicated `fix/effect-mg-status` branch, to merge before Effect tab UI work begins. Effect tab's Claude Design inventory doc (`X5DR_Editor_Phase3_Effect_Inventory_For_Claude_Design.md`) written in parallel, scoped around a parameter-format taxonomy rather than per-type layouts. A scoped post-Phase-3 dead-code/duplication cleanup pass (motivated by this session's Easy-tab/Effect-tab duplication discussion, ADR-0002/ADR-0003) added to the Progress Log's Next Actions, timed to land after every Phase 3 tab is complete and before Phase 4 distribution. Also fixed a Landmine-numbering collision from the prior session (the Breath Controller entry was mis-numbered #76, duplicating a pre-existing entry — corrected to #88; the new MG Status entry is #89). No code changed this session — investigation, briefs, and documentation only.*

## Critical Discovery #128 — MG Status Bit-Packing Hypothesis (Critical Discovery #127) Hardware-Refuted; `fix/effect-mg-status` Reverted

**Context:** `fix/effect-mg-status` was implemented exactly per `Effect_Tab_MGStatus_Bugfix_Brief.md` — `encodeMgStatus`/`MG_STATUS_FIXED_BITS` added to `sysex.js` (unit-tested against the brief's reference table), `buildPerTypeParams`'s `sinTri` branch encoding through it, and a shared `applyEffectTypeReset` replacing the duplicated type-switch reset loops in `buildEffectColumn`/`buildEasyEffCol`. `npx vitest run` passed (303/303). Pushed to GitHub for hardware re-test on the test machine, per the plan.

**Finding:** hardware re-test refuted the fix's core premise, via two independent capture methods:
1. **Outgoing (editor → device), fix live:** Snoize confirmed the editor sent exactly the intended encoded values — `2`/`3` (not `0`/`1`) for types 19, 20, 32, 35; `4` for type 43. The code change executed correctly; this was not a deployment/caching artifact. But the device's response was wrong: any nonzero value displays as "Tri" on the front panel — `2` and `3` behave identically to `1`. Only `0` selects "Sin." The intended "Sin, phase bit set" state (`2`) is unreachable.
2. **Incoming (device → editor), operating the front panel directly:** with Snoize watching outbound SysEx from the device itself, changing the Sin/Tri parameter via the front panel showed the device *only ever transmits* `0` or `1` for this offset — never `2` or `3`.

Together, these show the device's live Parameter Change handling for this offset (Effect 1: param 172 for Phaser, 171 for Stereo Chorus, 168 for Auto Pan, 173/174 for Delay/Chorus/Flanger) is a plain binary Sin/Tri toggle. It does not decode or honor `05_effect_parameters.md`'s `*11-3-3` bit1 (Phase)/bit2 (Wave Shape) bits when written via Func=41 — whether because the manual's bit-packing model describes dump-only/internal state unreachable via live Parameter Change, or because the manual's bit table simply doesn't apply to this offset in practice, is unresolved and not investigated further this session.

**Re-reading Critical Discovery #127 in light of this:** the Section 4 device dump-readback test (Phaser 1, write then read back, stored value matched what was sent) is still accurate as far as it goes — the device does store whatever's sent, and doesn't silently correct it. But that test only proved *persistence*, not that the "corrected" value (`2`) was what the device actually wanted or would act on differently from `0`. The leap from "the device stores what we send" to "therefore the device needs `2`" was the actual point of failure — it was an assumption drawn from the manual's bit table, and #127 itself already flagged this exact gap in its Bug Log ("audibility of the specific bit not separately confirmed"). This hardware re-test is what finally closed that gap, in the negative.

**Action taken:** `fix/effect-mg-status` reverted via `git revert` (commit `60f153d` reverting `cefb32a`) and pushed to GitHub — branch now matches `main` exactly. Not merged; not deleted, kept for the record. `sinTri` is back to sending the raw `0`/`1` waveform value directly, matching behavior from before Critical Discovery #127 was ever investigated. The original "5 types silently zero a hardwired bit" framing from #127 no longer describes a fixable bug via this mechanism — there is currently no known path to setting the phase/wave-shape bit live, if the device supports it at all.

**Lesson:** a hardware test that confirms a fix's code executes correctly (the right bytes go out on the wire) is a distinct claim from the fix being correct (the device does what's intended in response). Don't conflate "test plan predicted X, we implemented X, X is what we now send" with "X is correct device behavior" — the persistence/dump-readback method used to justify the original bug (#127 Section 4) is good for confirming the device doesn't silently normalize a value, but it cannot substitute for observing the device's actual behavioral response (here: front-panel display state) to that value. When a fix is built entirely from a manual's documented bit semantics without a behavioral hardware check in the loop, treat the hypothesis as unconfirmed until that check happens — as very nearly did happen here, since the re-test was requested specifically because the user had hardware available for it, not because the original implementation was suspected of being wrong.

*Last updated: 2026-08-03 — `fix/effect-mg-status` implemented, pushed, hardware re-tested, and reverted after the MG Status bit-packing hypothesis (Critical Discovery #127) was hardware-refuted; see Critical Discovery #128 above, Landmine #90. Effect tab Phase 3 retrofit is no longer gated on a pending data-layer fix. Next: Effect tab Claude Design handoff.*

## Critical Discovery #129 — Effect Tab (Phase 3 Brief 7) Implemented End-to-End; One Dropped Legacy Behavior Flagged for Hardware Verification

**Context:** Claude Design returned the Effect tab handoff (`docs/design spec docs/Effects Tab/README.md` + `Effects_Tab_Design_Reference.html`), built against `X5DR_Editor_Effect_Parameter_Groups_And_Heroes.md`. `X5DR_Editor_Phase3_Brief7_Effect_Tab.md` was written from that handoff (per-group placement table extracted by parsing the reference HTML's actual grid DOM, not its prose), clarified once (OUT3/4 Pan's ON/OFF toggle turned out to be the same OSC Pan/"Outputs A/B" shape, not a speculative new control), then implemented in full this session.

**What changed:** `src/ui/controls.js` gained `HERO_KNOB_SIZE`/`HERO_VALUE_FONT_SIZE` and a `valueFontSize` override on `knobUnidirectional`/`knobBidirectional`'s `'beside'` readout mode (purely additive). `src/index.html`: `EFFECT_TYPES`' builder IIFE now also returns `EFFECT_GRID_LAYOUT` (a `Map` keyed by group-array identity, encoding Brief 7 §4's 26-group cell placement); `buildPerTypeParams` rewritten to render the shared `.effect-params-grid` template generically from that map, with typeNo 37 (Parametric EQ) redirected to a wholly new `buildParamEqPanel`; `buildEffectColumn`'s header rebuilt (hero Dry:FX Balance knob, themed `buildEffectTypeField`, `toggleButtonGroup` Switch, `knobBidirectional` Mod Intensity); `buildEffectContent`'s Routing section rebuilt (`toggleButtonGroup` Placement, theme-aware inline SVG Placement diagrams ported from the pre-existing `Effect_Placement_Diagrams_Reference.html` — which already used this app's own `var(--text-primary)`-style tokens, needing no conversion — a new `buildEffectPanControl` for OUT3/4 Pan+ON/OFF sharing one value, a 2×2 Level grid for Parallel 3, Copy Effects relocated into the Routing panel's left column). `buildSinTriCtrl`/`buildModShapeCtrl` restyled onto `toggleButtonGroup`/`knobBidirectional` (encode/decode math unchanged). Retrofit applies uniformly to Program/Combi/Multi (shared, mode-parameterized code, confirmed rendering correctly and independently for all three via DOM inspection — Combi's own Quadrature Chorus/Cross Delay default and Multi's own Hall/Stereo Chorus 1 default both rendered correctly alongside Program's untouched Phaser 1/Cross Delay in the still-mounted, hidden panel).

**Verification performed:** `npx vitest run` 297/297 throughout (no data-layer files touched). Browser-verified: no console errors across every interaction below; Placement toggle correctly swaps the diagram and Pan↔Level controls (confirmed Serial and Parallel 3); the diagram's `var(--accent-fill)`-colored boxes were confirmed to actually recolor under Cool Slate (`rgb(79,179,255)`) vs. Warm Graphite, proving the theme-aware-SVG decision holds, not just that it compiles; OUT4 Pan's ON/OFF toggle correctly dims the knob and shows "OFF" as the single shared value (not a second parameter); the PARAMETERS grid was spot-checked against Brief 7 §4's table by reading rendered cell labels back out of the DOM (not just screenshots) for `hallRoom`, `stereoChorus`, `stereoDly`, `quadChorus` (including its full-width Mod Shape row), `phaser`, and `paramEQ` — all six matched exactly. The Parametric EQ curve widget's mid handle was drag-tested via synthetic pointer events: Mid Freq/Mid Gain knobs updated to match the drag (63/7), and the polyline recomputed a correct Gaussian bump around the new mid frequency — confirming the 2D handle-drag → knob-sync → curve-recompute path all work together, not just render once.

**One legacy behavior deliberately not preserved:** the pre-existing `rebuildBalance`'s native-range-input `'change'` listener called `rerenderModePanel(mode)` (a full mode-panel rebuild) after every Dry:FX Balance commit. This has no clean equivalent on the new hero knob — `knobUnidirectional`'s `onChange` fires continuously during a live drag (same as every other Phase 3 knob), and calling a full DOM-destroying rerender on every drag tick would abort the drag gesture mid-motion. No comment or commit message explained why the original rerender existed, and Landmine #26's `setParam` wrapper already refreshes the dirty-button state on every commit independently — the balance rerender most plausibly predates both the component library and that wrapper. Dropped rather than reproduced; flagged here explicitly (not silently) in case a hardware pass surfaces a dependent behavior this session didn't anticipate.

**Two ambiguities resolved by inference, not confirmed against the live device:** (1) the mockup's Parallel 3 Level grid labels ("OUT1 Level"..."OUT4 Level") don't match TABLE 7-1 or the existing 4-field L/R-split data model (`out3LLevel`/`out3RLevel`/`out4LLevel`/`out4RLevel`) — kept the real 4 fields with corrected on-screen labels rather than inventing two new parameters with no known Parameter Change number. (2) Parametric EQ's curve x-axis has no documented Hz mapping (`05_effect_parameters.md` gives only raw index ranges for Low/Mid/High Freq) — split into three equal on-screen thirds proportional to each band's own raw range, explicitly not labeled with any Hz value, matching the design's own "axis deliberately unlabeled" note.

**Not yet done:** hardware re-verification (this entire tab is browser-verified only, same status as every other Phase 3 tab since the last hardware pass — Landmine/Known-Outlier already tracks this app-wide, not repeated per-tab here). `modSpeed`/`reverbTime`/`erTime` formats still render as plain raw index values, not Hz/seconds — carried forward unchanged from pre-Brief-7 behavior; the Inventory doc's original call for a value-formatter here was **not** implemented this session (out of Brief 7's stated scope, which was layout/placement, not new value-formatting logic) and remains open.

**Lesson:** when a legacy side-effect (here, a full-panel rerender-on-commit) has no accompanying comment explaining its purpose and no clean equivalent in the new component shape, the safest resolution is often to drop it and say so explicitly, rather than either (a) silently carrying it forward in a way that would actually break the new control (destroying a knob mid-drag), or (b) silently dropping it without a record — a future hardware pass that finds something subtly different post-retrofit has a specific, named suspect to check first instead of re-deriving the entire diff from scratch.

## Critical Discovery #130 — Effect Tab Visual Polish Pass (Same Evening as Brief 7): a Real Knob-Shrink Bug Found and Fixed Generally, Plus Four Layout/Consistency Fixes

**Context:** immediately after Critical Discovery #129's Effect tab implementation, the user reviewed the live result against the Claude Design reference HTML across several short follow-up rounds and flagged five things, in order: (1) the Routing panel's diagram/Copy-Effects position shifting when Placement changed, (2) a redundant border around the Placement diagrams, (3) header-row misalignment plus a missing "Mod Source" label and a stray leftover note, (4) a hero-knob-visibly-smaller-than-its-siblings bug on effect types 42/43/46 specifically, and (5) OUT3/4 Pan's label spacing, missing stepper/click-to-edit, toggle sizing, and toggle label order — the last of which was interrupted mid-session by an unrelated environment outage (see below) and finished after a reboot. A sixth, unrelated small request (a checkmark on the active Theme menu item) was folded into the same session.

**Finding/Fix, per item:**

1. **Routing-panel layout shift.** `.effect-routing-left` was width:auto, sized by its own content — the Pan-row (Serial/Parallel 1/2) and the Level-grid (Parallel 3) have genuinely different natural widths (measured ~385px vs ~293px), so switching Placement visibly moved the diagram (centered in the *remaining* flex space, which depended on how wide this column happened to be) and resized the Copy Effects select/divider (`width:100%` of the column) — two symptoms, one root cause. Fixed by giving the column a fixed width (24.125rem) matching the wider case.
2. **Double border on Placement diagrams.** All 4 diagrams were sourced (per Brief 7) from an older reference file (`Effect_Placement_Diagrams_Reference.html`) that draws its own inset border rect (`x=4,y=4,stroke=var(--border-subtle)`) inside each SVG — redundant, since `.effect-diagram-card` already provides a background block. Removed the rect from all four (a single `str.replace` across 4 identical occurrences).
3. **Header alignment.** Removed a stray "JS(+Y) = Mod Wheel..." note paragraph that had no counterpart in the reference HTML, and added the missing "Mod Source" field-label above its dropdown (present in the reference, absent in the first implementation). Both together — not either alone — fully resolved what the user initially reported as two separate alignment questions (Type/Mod Source vertical position relative to the hero knob, and ON/OFF+Mod Intensity's horizontal position): the note's extra height and the label's absence were both silently changing the `align-items:center` math the row's layout depends on. Verified by measuring the live DOM against the reference HTML's own box-model numbers (247px fixed columns, 22px gaps) rather than eyeballing a screenshot — they matched exactly once both were fixed.
4. **Knob-shrink bug (the most significant find of this session).** Effect types 42 (Delay/Chorus), 43 (Delay/Flanger), and 46 (Delay/Phaser) all have a hero-column second parameter with a long label ("Chorus Mod Depth", "Flanger Mod Depth", "Phaser Mod Speed"). Investigating showed the **knob ring itself** — not just the label — was rendering ~12px smaller than it should (measured 60-62px vs the configured 72px). Root cause: `controls.js`'s `readoutMode:'beside'` knob is nested flex (an outer group containing the knob ring + a label/value column), and every flex child defaults to `flex-shrink:1` — a label too long for its fixed-width grid cell (146px hero / 108px regular) caused the *knob*, not just the text, to absorb the overflow, since the knob is a fixed-px child with no shrink protection. Confirmed this wasn't scoped to just the 3 reported types — group 29 (Enhancer)'s "Harmonic Density" hero and even *regular* (38px) knobs like "Delay Feedback"/"Phaser Mod Depth" were independently found squished too, via the same mechanism. Fixed generally: `flex-shrink:0` on `.ctrl-knob` scoped to all three PARAMETERS-grid cell classes (hero/regular/col3), `min-width:0` on the label/value column so ellipsis can actually engage, and `overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;white-space:nowrap` on the label itself as the fallback — plus, per Brief 7 §4's already-documented abbreviation-fallback rule, shortened the four labels that were actually tightest ("Harmonic Density"→"Harmonic Dens.", "Chorus/Flanger Mod Depth"→"...Mod Dpt", "Phaser Mod Speed"→"Phaser Mod Spd") so they display in full on the happy path rather than relying on the ellipsis.
5. **OUT3/4 Pan spacing/stepper/toggle.** Traced to `buildEffectPanControl` hand-building its own label/value/toggle stack (`.effect-pan-text`) as a second, parallel implementation of the same visual shape every hero param control already gets from `knobBidirectional`'s `readoutMode:'beside'` — different DOM, different CSS, hence the spacing mismatch, and no `buildReadout` involved at all, hence no stepper/click-to-edit. Rebuilt to call `knobBidirectional` itself (with a `format` closure that reads a live `isOn` variable so toggling redisplays "OFF" without disturbing the knob's own internal value) and append the ON/OFF toggle into its `.ctrl-knob-beside-text` column as a third child — this got the identical spacing and the stepper/click-to-edit "for free," rather than needing two separate fixes. Toggle height was then confirmed against both the reference HTML (which uses a deliberately smaller `padding:4px 12px` for this specific control, vs. the shared default `6px/14px`) and OSC's own Off/On toggle (which renders at the shared default, 26px, vs. the new Pan toggle's 22px) — `toggleButtonGroup` extended with optional size overrides to make this possible without a second component. Label order swapped Off-first (`OFF`/`ON`, matching every other toggle in the app — confirmed by grep, not assumption) on both the Pan toggle and, for consistency, the Effect Switch toggle, which had the same On-first outlier order.
6. **Theme menu checkmark** (unrelated small request, same session): added a fixed-width reserved `✓` slot per menu item, updated from inside `applyTheme` itself so the displayed check can't drift from the actually-applied theme.

**Unrelated environment incident, same session:** mid-way through item 5, every file operation under `~/Desktop` (the entire project, since it lives there) started failing with `EPERM: operation not permitted` — not scoped to one file; `ls ~/Desktop` and reading unrelated files (`CLAUDE.md`, `controls.js`) failed identically. Simultaneously, `brctl status` (iCloud's own sync-daemon CLI, unrelated to this session) self-reported `"Access denied"`. A 5-minute background monitor polling for access to return timed out without success. The user recognized the pattern from a prior occurrence ("iCloud kept changing a file's status for a few minutes") and rebooted the Mac; access was restored immediately after. Writing to a path *outside* `~/Desktop` (this project's Claude Code memory files, under `~/.claude/`) continued to work throughout — confirming the outage was scoped to the Desktop location specifically, not a general tool/permission failure, which is what let the session hand off a written memory note rather than leave the state only in (possibly session-bound) conversation history. Not a code bug; recorded here since it cost real session time and matches a pattern the user says has happened before.

**Verification:** all six fixes browser-verified via live DOM measurement (not just screenshots) after each change — label→value gaps measured equal (0px offset in both hero and Pan cases), toggle heights measured (22px Pan vs. 26px OSC/Switch), knob widths measured at exactly 72px/38px across all previously-squished cases post-fix, toggle order/theme-checkmark confirmed via `textContent`/`classList` inspection. `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass throughout every step (no data-layer files touched by any of the six fixes).

**Lesson:** a single user-visible symptom ("this looks slightly off") can have a genuinely structural cause worth root-causing rather than patching cosmetically — the header alignment complaint (item 3) turned out to be two missing/extra elements changing a flex centering calculation, and the knob-shrink complaint (item 4) turned out to be a real component-library bug capable of silently affecting *any* sufficiently-long label anywhere in the app, not a one-off styling tweak scoped to the three types the user happened to notice it on. Checking neighboring cases (Harmonic Density, regular-cell knobs) the user didn't explicitly ask about — once the mechanism was understood — caught two more live instances of the same bug before they were separately reported.

*Last updated: 2026-08-11 (late session) — Effect tab visual polish pass (6 items) completed same evening as Brief 7's initial implementation; see Critical Discovery #130. Most significant finding: a real `flex-shrink` bug in the shared knob component was shrinking knob rings (not just label text) under long labels, fixed generally rather than per-instance. Browser-verified only throughout (297/297 tests, no data-layer files touched). A mid-session `~/Desktop` file-access outage (iCloud-related, resolved by reboot) is noted but was not a code issue. Next: hardware re-verification of the whole Effect tab (Brief 7 + this polish pass together), then the Landmine #72 dead-code/duplication cleanup pass now that all Phase 3 tabs are done.*
