## Critical Discovery #131 — Effect Tab Follow-Up Round: Pan/EQ Layout Fixes, a Second Real Knob-Adjacent CSS Bug, and a Genuine Stale-Dump-Value Bug in Sin/Tri Display

**Context:** a follow-up session to Critical Discoveries #129/#130, working through a punch-list of small visual/interaction issues in the Effect tab, raised one at a time across several short rounds. All browser-verified only (no hardware pass this session); `npx vitest run` 297/297 throughout, no data-layer files touched by any item below.

**Items, in order:**

1. **OUT3/4 Pan display range bug.** `buildEffectPanControl`'s `formatPanValue` computed L/R labels using the wrong reference point relative to `PAN_CENTER` — the knob correctly swept its full -50..+50 range, but the *displayed* text jumped L100→L51 then suddenly to R50→R100, never showing "CNT". Fixed the formula (`raw < PAN_CENTER` → `L${PAN_CENTER-raw}`, `raw === PAN_CENTER` → `'CNT'`, else `R${raw-PAN_CENTER}`); verified by driving the control's internal value across its full range programmatically and confirming a clean L50→...→L1→CNT→R1→...→R50 sweep with no discontinuity. Renamed "OUT3/4 Pan" to "Pan 3"/"Pan 4" (matching the Routing diagram's own labels) and the Parallel-3 Level fields to "Level 1/2-L/R" (same reasoning) in the same round.

2. **Mod Source dropdown relabel.** The 6 options (`JS(+Y)/CC#1`, `JS(−Y)/CC#2`, etc.) renamed to plain-language equivalents (`Mod Wheel / Joystick +`, `Breath Control / Joystick -`, `Pedal 1 CC#12`, `Pedal 2 CC#13`, `VDA EG`) per user-supplied replacements. `MOD_SOURCES` is index-based (`{value:i,label:lbl}`), not string-matched anywhere else in the codebase, so this was a pure content swap with no logic risk.

3. **Mod Intensity/Mod Source vertical alignment.** The knob's beside-layout group (label+value, shorter) and Mod Source's label+select box (taller) shared `.effect-header-line`'s `align-items:center`, leaving their bottoms visibly mismatched. Added a scoped `.effect-header-line-modsrc { align-items:flex-end }` modifier for just that row, leaving the Type/Switch row above untouched. Verified via `getBoundingClientRect` — both bottoms measured identical (0px diff) after the fix.

4. **Pan 3/4 control redesign ("Option 2b").** User felt the Pan controls (label, knob-value, ON/OFF toggle stacked with near-zero gap) looked crowded. Two rounds of mockup review followed: first a set of options proposed and two ("widen the gaps" vs. "toggle moves below the knob") built as an Artifact comparison; user picked the second and asked for one iteration (toggle pulled tighter, centered under the knob specifically rather than the whole control) — this iteration surfaced and fixed two more issues in the mockup itself before implementation: vertical centering (grid `align-items:center` missing) and a toggle-corner-rendering regression (the mockup's toggle buttons lacked the real component's per-button `border-radius`, so the active button's inset ring clipped square at the wrap's rounded corner — the same failure shape as an already-fixed real bug, `buildFusedToggleGroup`'s `endRadius` handling, just not carried into the mockup). Implemented as a 2-column/2-row CSS grid (knob | label+value on row 1, toggle alone on row 2 under the knob column only) replacing `buildEffectPanControl`'s previous flex-row-with-toggle-nested-in-textCol structure. **Explicit user constraint: the ROUTING panel must not grow taller despite the new layout being visibly taller per-control.** Measured the panel's height before implementing (335.42px) and confirmed it unchanged after (335.42px, all three Placement modes that use this control) — the panel's height is governed by the taller Placement-diagram column via `align-items:stretch`, and `.effect-pan-area` already had ~60px of unused flex slack, so the taller control was absorbed for free rather than needing any explicit height management.

5. **Value-readout width-jitter (first instance: Pan controls).** User noticed the Pan knobs visibly shifting position when the displayed value crossed a digit-count boundary (e.g. "L10"→"L9"). Root cause: `controls.js`'s `buildReadout` reserves only a generic 20px `min-width` on the value span — narrower than any of this control's actual possible strings (2-3 characters), so the readout's rendered width genuinely changed with digit count, changing the whole grid item's width, which (since `.effect-pan-row` has no fixed width of its own and is centered by its parent) shifted the entire row. Fixed by locking `.effect-pan-item .ctrl-readout-wrap`'s `min-width` to the widest string this control can show (54px, covering `OFF`/`CNT`/any 3-character `L`/`R` value) — scoped narrowly, not touching the shared 20px default other knobs rely on. Verified by editing the live value from L50→L10→L9 and confirming identical `getBoundingClientRect` positions at L10 and L9 (219px both times, previously would have differed).

6. **Value-readout width-jitter (second instance: Parametric EQ curve graphic).** The exact same underlying bug (unprotected 20px readout min-width) surfaced independently in the Parametric EQ panel: Mid Gain crossing a digit boundary (e.g. "-9"→"-10") was visibly resizing the curve graphic itself, because `.effect-eq-hero-col` (containing Mid Freq/Mid Gain, `flex:none`) and `.effect-eq-curve-outer` (the graphic, `flex:1`) are flex siblings — heroCol's width changing pushed the curve's available space to change with it. Same fix pattern applied, scoped to `.effect-eq-hero-col .ctrl-readout-wrap`. Verified: editing Mid Gain from -9 to -10 now gives identical `svgW` (438px) and `heroColW` (136px) at both values, previously would have differed.

7. **Parametric EQ's 5 regular knobs (Mid Width, Low/High Freq/Gain) equal distribution.** User wanted these spread evenly across the panel's width instead of clumped left. Changed `.effect-eq-regular-row` from a flex row with a fixed gap to `grid-template-columns: repeat(5, 1fr)`. Verified all 5 columns render at an identical width (109.2px) with equal spacing, and — a follow-up question from the user — confirmed this did not disturb Mid Width's pre-existing left-alignment with the hero knobs above it (both measured at an identical 140px left edge, since they're plain block-level siblings sharing one container's left edge regardless of the row's own internal column widths).

8. **Narrow-viewport knob clipping — investigated, found not to be a bug.** User asked why, when squeezing the browser window narrow, the Mid Width knob (in the 5-column row) appeared to lose its left edge before the larger Mid Freq/Mid Gain hero knobs above it did, given they're left-aligned. Reproduced and measured directly: both knobs' containing boxes share an *identical* left edge at every viewport width tested (confirmed via `getBoundingClientRect`, e.g. both at exactly -160px at one width). The visual difference is pure knob diameter — hero knobs use `HERO_KNOB_SIZE` (72px), regular knobs (including Mid Width) use `SMALL_KNOB_SIZE` (38px) — so as the pre-existing, already-documented fixed-1400px-canvas clipping boundary (Archive #98, accepted limitation, unrelated to anything changed this session) sweeps in from the left, the smaller-diameter ring disappears completely well before the larger one does, despite sharing the same left edge. No code change; explained to the user with the measurement as evidence rather than assumed.

9. **Sin/Tri toggle clipping.** User reported the "Tri" button's right portion not rendering for Effect types 35/36 (Auto Pan/Tremolo). Root cause: `buildFusedToggleGroup`'s wrap has its own `overflow:hidden`, which per spec makes the flex item's automatic minimum width `0` (not its content's natural min-content size) — inside `.effect-reg-cell`'s fixed 108px box, the toggle (default `flex-shrink:1`) was squeezed to 49.8px and its own `overflow:hidden` then clipped the shrunk content. Same failure shape as the already-fixed knob-shrink bug (Archive #130 item 4), just never extended to toggle groups. Fixed via `flex-shrink:0` on `.ctrl-toggle-group`/`.ctrl-toggle3` within `.effect-toggle-cell` — general, not scoped to Auto Pan specifically. Verified the toggle now renders at its full natural 85.4px width with both buttons independently clickable, and spot-checked that the same general fix also silently corrected identical clipping on Stereo Chorus's Sin/Tri (same cell shape, not separately reported).

10. **"Sin / Tri" → "Mod Waveform" relabel, across 4 instances.** User first asked for the relabel on Auto Pan (offset 0, discovered while investigating item 9), then asked for the same correction on Phaser and Chorus (Stereo Chorus) types. A fourth instance was found while auditing every `format:'sinTri'` def: Delay/Chorus (type 42)'s "Chorus Sin / Tri". Measured in-browser whether "Chorus Mod Waveform" would fit that control's `.effect-col3-cell` (no fixed width, but real available space): needs ~204.5px, cell has ~202px — a ~2.5px overflow, per the user's own stated fallback rule this resolved to the shorter "Mod Waveform" instead.

11. **"Mod Waveform" two-line split, across the same 4 instances.** User observed the label already showed as "Mod"/"Waveform" on two lines for Auto Pan and Stereo Chorus, and asked for the same on Phaser and Delay/Chorus. Investigating found this was never a deliberate design choice for any of the four — Auto Pan/Stereo Chorus (both `.effect-reg-cell`, fixed 108px) only wrapped incidentally, as a side-effect of item 9's fix letting the toggle claim most of the cell's width; Phaser/Delay-Chorus (both `.effect-col3-cell`, unconstrained width) had room to stay on one line. Made explicit and deterministic for all 4 via a `<br>` split in `buildCell`'s `sinTri` branch, independent of available cell width.

12. **Sin/Tri "no highlight" bug — the session's most significant finding.** User reported Phaser 1 showed neither Sin nor Tri highlighted, unlike Phaser 2 which correctly showed Sin. Initial synthetic reproduction (switching Effect Type via the browser to Phaser 1/2 repeatedly) failed to reproduce it — both showed Sin correctly — because the Type Browser's own selection flow resets all per-type offsets to their `initial` value on every confirm, masking the real bug. Reproducing on a *fresh load* (no type-reselection) of the default factory program (PipeDreams/A00, whose stored `eff1Type` is already 32/Phaser 1) confirmed the report exactly: neither button highlighted. Traced to the raw stored value: parsing the factory `.syx` directly (via Node, importing `parser.js`'s pure `parseSnapshot`) showed `eff1Params[4]` (the Sin/Tri offset) = `99` — neither `0` nor `1`. Cross-referenced against the existing Decisions Made table (line ~93: "Phaser offsets were correct; labels were wrong... Hardware confirmed all five parameters") to rule out an offset-mapping bug before considering anything else — offset 4 is confirmed correct for Manual/Sin-Tri's actual position. The real explanation is Critical Discovery #127/#128 (Landmine #90): the manual describes this offset as a 3-bit MG Status field, hardware-refuted for live Parameter Change (the device only ever sends/accepts plain `0`/`1`), but apparently *not* refuted for how the factory soundbank's `.syx` file was originally authored — `99` doesn't even match the 3-bit-packed values (2 or 3) the manual describes, but is nonetheless a real nonzero value that matches neither toggle button, hence no highlight. Fix: `buildSinTriCtrl` now normalizes `initialVal` to a strict 0/1 (`=== 0 ? 0 : 1`) before passing it to the toggle, applying Landmine #90's own hardware-confirmed rule ("the device treats any nonzero value as Tri") to the *display* layer specifically — `onChange` is untouched, so edits still send the plain 0/1 the device expects. Verified: PipeDreams' Phaser 1 now shows "Tri" highlighted on fresh load; clicking "Sin" correctly re-highlights and would send `0`.

13. **Group 8 (Quadrature/X-Over Chorus) Mod Waveform+Mod Shape restyle.** These two types pack Mod Waveform and Mod Shape into a single dump/param byte (`buildModShapeCtrl`, pre-existing `encodeRaw`/`disp0`/`waveform` math, unchanged), previously rendered as one shared row label ("Mod Shape") over an unlabeled Sin/Tri toggle + unlabeled knob pair. User wanted this to visually match Auto Pan's two separate, independently labeled controls (Mod Waveform toggle, Mod Shape knob), despite the data-layer difference. Restyled to build two blocks reusing Auto Pan's own cell shapes exactly — a `.effect-toggle-cell` (identical 2-line "Mod"/"Waveform" label + Sin/Tri toggle, same as `buildCell`'s `sinTri` branch) beside a small `knobBidirectional` labeled "Mod Shape" (matching Auto Pan's regular-cell knob styling) — removing the old shared row label since each piece now carries its own. Verified for both Quadrature Chorus and X Over Chorus (same `quadChorus` defs array): label markup identical (`"Mod<br>Waveform"`), toggle/knob interaction independently exercised (clicking Tri correctly re-highlights; the underlying packed value still round-trips through the unchanged `encodeRaw` math).

**Lesson (item 12 especially):** when a value fails to match either option in a binary UI control, the two most likely explanations are (a) a genuine live-encoding bug or (b) stale/differently-encoded data from a source that predates or bypasses the live encoding path (here, a factory-authored dump file, not a live device capture) — check which one you're looking at before assuming either. The Type Browser's reset-on-reselect behavior nearly caused this bug to go unreproduced/unconfirmed entirely; when a bug report doesn't reproduce via the obvious interaction path, consider whether that path itself has a side-effect (here, resetting the very state being investigated) before concluding the report was wrong.

*Last updated: 2026-08-12 — Effect tab follow-up round (13 items) completed in one session; see Critical Discovery #131, amends Landmine #90 (Project Context). Most significant finding: a genuine stale-dump-value bug (item 12) affecting Sin/Tri display on load, distinct from and more subtle than the already-known live-encoding limitation it initially resembled. Also found and generally fixed a second knob-adjacent CSS bug (toggle-group clipping, item 9 — same failure shape as Archive #130's knob-shrink bug) and a width-jitter bug that independently affected two different controls (items 5-6). Browser-verified only throughout (297/297 tests, no data-layer files touched). Next: hardware re-verification of the whole Effect tab, now spanning three sessions of browser-only changes (Archive #129-#131) — item 12's fix in particular should be re-examined once a real hardware dump (not just the factory soundbank) is available for comparison, per the lesson above.*

## Critical Discovery #132 — Quadrature Chorus Grid Restructure, EQ Handle Ovaling Root-Caused to `preserveAspectRatio="none"` on a Non-Fixed-Width Container, and Cross-Tab "0 Line" Unification

**Context:** two follow-up requests in the same session, both refinements to work already covered by Critical Discovery #131. All browser-verified only; `npx vitest run` 297/297 throughout, no data-layer files touched.

**Item 1 — Quadrature/X-Over Chorus's Mod Waveform+Mod Shape control, second pass.** Archive #131 item 13 had restyled this packed-byte control (offset 4, `format:'modShape'`) to visually resemble Auto Pan's two separate controls, but left it in a standalone full-width `.effect-extra-row` with its own `background:var(--bg-page)` backdrop, below the main 6-cell PARAMETERS grid. User wanted the dark backdrop gone entirely (both controls sitting on the regular panel backdrop like everything else) and the two pieces column-aligned with existing content — Mod Waveform under Delay Time (the `reg` column), Mod Shape under EQ (the `col3` column) — with "regular inter-row spacing."

Implementation: `EFFECT_GRID_LAYOUT`'s `quadChorus` entry gained a literal 3rd `{hero,reg,col3}` row (`{hero:null, reg:4, col3:4}`) instead of a separate `extra` field, with offset 4 referenced from *both* the `reg` and `col3` positions. `buildCell` gained a `def.format === 'modShape'` branch that renders differently depending on which `cellClass` it's called for — the reg-column call renders just the Mod Waveform toggle (2-line label, `toggleButtonGroup`), the col3-column call renders just the Mod Shape knob (`knobBidirectional`, labeled). Since these are now two independent `buildCell` invocations rather than one function building both pieces together, each re-reads the packed byte fresh via `store.getParam` at its own commit time (decoding the current waveform/shape, re-encoding with the one dimension that changed) instead of sharing a JS closure — verified this doesn't clobber the other control's state by editing the knob (`Mod Shape` → `5`) and confirming the toggle still showed "Tri" highlighted afterward. The old `buildModShapeCtrl` function and the now-unused `.effect-extra-row` CSS rule were deleted (`grep` confirmed zero remaining references to either).

"Equal row spacing" was achieved structurally, not by tuning a gap value: folding row 3 into the same `.effect-params-grid` means it shares that grid's one `row-gap: 20px` CSS property with rows 1-2, confirmed via `getComputedStyle(grid).rowGap` reading a flat `"20px"` regardless of the fact that row 3's own track height (38px, sized to its shorter content) differs from rows 1-2's (72px, sized to the hero knobs) — a naive measurement of *visual* cell-edge-to-cell-edge distance would have shown inconsistent gaps (39-54px depending on which column pair was measured) purely because `align-items:center` centers differently-sized cells within their own row tracks; the actual grid-level spacing is the authoritative "is this consistent" answer, not the visual illusion `align-items:center` creates around it. Verified column alignment too: `reg`-column left edge and `col3`-column left edge both measured identical (384px/590px respectively) between row 1 and row 3, for both Quadrature Chorus and X Over Chorus (same shared `quadChorus` defs array).

**Item 2 — Parametric EQ curve handle ovaling, root cause and fix.** User reported the EQ curve's draggable handles had "become slightly oval" since an earlier width change, and asked for their shape/size/cursor/grab-area to match VDA/VDF's `egCurveWidget` markers exactly.

Root cause: the EQ curve's handles were a single `<circle r="4.5">` per band, and the SVG uses `preserveAspectRatio="none"` (deliberately, to let the curve's x-axis stretch to fill `.effect-eq-curve-outer`'s available width while keeping height fixed). Unlike `egCurveWidget`'s callers (VDA/VDF/OSC), which always pass an explicit numeric `width` config — a JS constant, so the SVG's rendered width is fixed and known at construction time — `.effect-eq-curve-outer` is `flex:1`, meaning the SVG's actual rendered width is CSS-layout-determined and can differ from its `EQ_CURVE_W` (820) viewBox width. With `preserveAspectRatio="none"`, any such mismatch scales x and y independently, stretching a shape with an equal x/y radius into a visible oval — exactly the mechanism `egCurveWidget`'s own markers already defend against (`rx = EG_MARKER_RADIUS / scaleX`, compensating the x-scale so a circle stays a circle), which the EQ widget's handles had never been given.

Fix: rebuilt each handle as an `<ellipse>` pair — a visible dot (`EQ_HANDLE_RADIUS`=3, matching `EG_MARKER_RADIUS` exactly) plus a larger invisible hit target (`EQ_HANDLE_HIT_RADIUS`=9, matching `EG_MARKER_HIT_RADIUS`) stacked on top, carrying the actual `pointerdown`/drag handling and set to `cursor:grab` (was `cursor:'pointer'` on the single circle). The key difference from `egCurveWidget`'s own technique: `scaleX` can't be computed synchronously here (the container's width isn't a JS constant), so it's measured via `svg.getBoundingClientRect()` inside a `requestAnimationFrame` callback fired once after the SVG is actually built and inserted — the earliest point the real rendered width exists to measure. Verified numerically, not just visually: at a measured `svg.getBoundingClientRect().width` of 438px (`scaleX` = 438/820 = 0.5341), the visible ellipse's `rx` attribute read `5.616` — `5.616 × 0.5341 = 3.0`, i.e. it renders as a true 3px-radius circle on screen, and the hit ellipse likewise resolves to a true 9px-radius circle. Drag interaction was re-tested end-to-end after switching the pointer-event target from the visible circle to the new separate hit ellipse (synthetic `PointerEvent` drag on the mid-band handle moved Mid Freq from 50 to 77, confirming the handler rewire didn't break the drag path).

**Item 3 — Cross-tab "0 line" unification.** Separately, user wanted the dashed zero-reference line consistent across VDA, VDF, and the Parametric EQ curve, specifically "halfway" between `egCurveWidget`'s existing treatment (`EG_REF_LINE_WIDTH`=1.5, `_OPACITY`=0.6, `_DASH`='6 5', felt "too dominant") and the EQ curve's own separately-implemented line (`stroke:var(--border-subtle)`, width 1, dash '3 3', opacity 1/unset, felt "too light"). Asked and confirmed with the user first whether OSC's Pitch EG — which also calls `egCurveWidget` and wasn't mentioned in the original request — should be included in the retune, since changing the shared constant affects it automatically; user confirmed yes (Recommended option), consistent with the app's existing "every EG window should read the same" precedent (Critical Discovery from the OSC Pitch EG session).

Landed on `EG_REF_LINE_WIDTH`=1.25, `_OPACITY`=0.4, `_DASH`='4.5 4' (numeric midpoints of both existing settings) plus switching the EQ curve's own line from `var(--border-subtle)` to `var(--text-secondary)` (matching `egCurveWidget`'s color choice) — the opacity value was cross-checked against the Warm Graphite theme's actual token RGB values (not just picked as a literal average of 1.0 and 0.6) to confirm the *rendered* brightness genuinely sits at the midpoint between the two prior treatments: blending `var(--text-secondary)` (#9c9188) over `var(--bg-page)` (#1c1916) at α=0.4 lands within ~1-2% of the true numeric midpoint between EQ's old fully-opaque `border-subtle` (#3a332c) and VDA/VDF's old 0.6-opacity `text-secondary`, converging consistently across R/G/B channels (α solved independently per channel: 0.418/0.408/0.395). Verified post-implementation by reading the live attributes back from all three tabs (VDA, VDF, Effect/EQ) — all three now report identical `stroke-width="1.25"`, `stroke-dasharray="4.5 4"`, `opacity="0.4"`.

**Lesson:** the "grid row-gap looks inconsistent" investigation (item 1) and the "handles are oval" investigation (item 2) are both instances of the same general trap — a rendering technique that's correct in the abstract (CSS Grid's `row-gap`; SVG `rx` compensation for non-uniform scaling) can still *look* wrong when measured naively (visual cell-edge distance instead of the grid's own gap property; a static `rx` value against a container whose width isn't actually static). In both cases, going one level deeper — reading the authoritative property/measurement rather than trusting the visual symptom — either confirmed the fix was already structurally correct (item 1) or revealed exactly why it wasn't (item 2, `scaleX` needing to be dynamically measured rather than assumed constant).

*Last updated: 2026-08-12 (late session) — Quadrature/X-Over Chorus grid restructure and cross-tab EG curve consistency work (handles + "0 line") completed in one session; see Critical Discovery #132. No architectural decisions changed — no new ADR. Browser-verified only throughout (297/297 tests). Next: hardware re-verification of the whole Effect tab, now four sessions deep on browser-only changes (Archive #129-#132).*

## Critical Discovery #133 — Effect Tab Hardware Findings Brief (Items 1-3) Implemented and Verified; Hardware Re-Verification of Archive #129-#132's Backlog Confirmed for Three of Four Items

**Context:** Hardware testing of the Effect tab (Archive #129-#132's four browser-only sessions) surfaced three items, captured in `Setup Instructions/Claude Prompts/Phase 3/X5DR_Editor_Effect_Tab_Hardware_Findings_Brief.md`. All three implemented and verified this session, on branch `phase3-effect-tab`, as three separate commits so each stays independently bisectable.

**Item 1 — Room reverb time range.** `05_effect_parameters.md`'s parenthetical (`00~61(2F)`) and the existing `dlyHall`/`dlyRoom` split already established that types 4-6 (Room/Large Room/Live Stage) cap at raw 47 (4.9s), not 97 (9.9s) like types 1-3 (Hall/Ensemble Hall/Concert Hall) — the shared `hallRoom` `EFFECT_TYPES` array was wrongly giving all six types `max: 97`. Split into `hall` (1-3, max 97) and `room` (4-6, max 47), each with its own `EFFECT_GRID_LAYOUT.set()` entry (the map is keyed by array identity). Browser-verified: Room's Reverb Time knob caps at 47 via repeated stepper increments (synthetic `PointerEvent`s), Hall's still caps at 97. No hardware pass needed or performed — the manual's own parenthetical is authoritative and already corroborated by the pre-existing `dlyHall`/`dlyRoom` split.

**Item 2 — Dry:FX Balance independence, types 40-43/46-47.** Front-panel testing (user, prior session) showed Balance 1/Balance 2 are independently settable for these "Combination Parallel" types, not an inverted-mirror pair as the code had assumed since Decision Archive item 13 — TABLE 7-1 itself labels PN 175/176 (eff1) and 186/187 (eff2) "Balance 1"/"Balance 2", not "Balance L"/"Balance R", and item 13's own hardware confirmation only ever covered *what `balL` means per type group*, never confirmed the mirroring assumption for this branch. Rebuilt `rebuildBalance`'s `40≤t≤43||t∈{46,47}` branch as two independent controls, each reading/writing its own key and calling `sendParamChange` directly — no more `100-wet` computation, no `sendBalancePair` for this branch. Labels renamed "Balance 1"/"Balance 2" → "Dry/Wet 1"/"Dry/Wet 2"; the single-control branches' "Dry:FX Balance" → "Dry/Wet".

Hardware-verified in two stages: **Stage B** (independence itself) — user tested via Snoize on type 42 (Delay/Chorus), confirmed moving each control sends only its own Parameter Change and the other's stored value doesn't drift, matching the code's new behavior; user's own words: "this seems to work as intended." **Layout (Stage C)** — the first implementation (both knobs at `HERO_KNOB_SIZE`, 72px, side by side in the single-knob hero slot) squeezed Switch and Mod Intensity down below their natural size (measured: 74px/88px vs. natural 93px/112px) — user caught this before it was pushed and asked for layout alternatives rather than accepting an unreviewed fix. Four options were mocked up against the real running app's own CSS/components (a throwaway `src/mockup-dry-wet-options.html`, removed after comparison, importing the real `controls.js` and copying the real `<style>` block verbatim for pixel-accurate fidelity) and presented side by side; user picked Option A — both knobs at `SMALL_KNOB_SIZE` (38px, the same size already used for Mod Intensity and every regular PARAMETERS-grid knob) in the original single-knob hero slot. Re-verified via `getBoundingClientRect`: Switch/Mod Intensity back to their exact natural 93px/112px, `balWrap` grew from 155px to 202px, comfortably inside the row's unchanged 634px budget — no panel growth.

**Item 3 — Value-display formatters.** `reverbTime`/`erTime`/`modSpeed` now show real units instead of the raw stored index: `EFFECT_VALUE_FORMATTERS` (reverbTime: `raw*0.1+0.2` seconds; erTime: `raw*10+100` ms; modSpeed: the documented 3-segment piecewise Hz formula) wired into `buildCell`'s `Knob(...)` branch via the `format` config `knobUnidirectional`/`knobBidirectional` already supported — purely additive, no wire/data-layer change (`curVal`/`onChange`/`sendParamChange` all still operate on the raw index). Verified two ways: every documented formula endpoint hand-checked in Node (all matched exactly, including modSpeed's 3 segment boundaries at raw 99/100/199/200/216), then spot-checked live in-browser across `hall`, `room`, `earlyRef`, `stereoChorus`, and a `dly*` combination type (Delay/Room) — confirming the formatter reaches every `EFFECT_TYPES` occurrence of these three format tags, not just the obvious ones (per this file's own repeated "audit every call site" lesson, e.g. Landmine #36/#69).

**Archive #129-#132 backlog, hardware re-verification status (user-confirmed, 2026-08-13):** of the four items flagged across those four sessions, three are now hardware-verified — Pan 3/4's "Option 2b" toggle+knob behavior, the Parametric EQ curve's handle-drag path (including its rebuilt handle shape/grab-area, Archive #132 item 2), and the Sin/Tri display-normalization fix (Archive #131) against a real device dump. The fourth — Archive #129's dropped Dry:FX-Balance-commit `rerenderModePanel` call, deliberately not reproduced when the hero knob was first built — has an uncertain status: the user recalled it "had been verified previously," but no record of that verification exists anywhere in this Archive or the Progress Log. Left open rather than marked verified on recollection alone, consistent with this project's standing rule (Critical Discovery #128's lesson) that confidence is not a substitute for a recorded hardware check — revisit by either locating the missing record or re-testing directly.

**New task surfaced this session (user-flagged, not yet started):** the device applies its own default parameter values on effect type change (manual pp.144-145, "Effect Parameter Table" bracketed defaults) that the editor doesn't currently match in full — `buildEffectColumn`'s existing type-change handler already resets the 7 per-type `PARAMETERS` slots to each def's `initial` value, but not Dry:FX Balance/Switch/Mod Source/Mod Intensity, and those `initial` values were themselves informally tuned, never checked against the manual's real bracketed table. **Confirmed this session: no reference file in this repo transcribes that table** — `05_effect_parameters.md` has no bracketed-default column at all — so this is blocked on the user sourcing the real values from the manual before any audit or implementation can start.

**Lesson:** two instances this session of the same shape — an assumption that felt safe (the Balance-pair mirroring, carried in code since before Landmine-numbering existed; the `initial` values, informally tuned and never flagged as unverified until someone asked "where did these come from") turned out to have no hardware record behind it once actually checked. Treat "this has probably been confirmed" as a question to answer by searching the Archive, not as a fact to carry forward — the search itself is cheap; being wrong about it downstream is not.

*Last updated: 2026-08-13 — Effect Tab Hardware Findings Brief Items 1-3 implemented, verified (hand-checked formulas + spot-checked in-browser + user hardware confirmation for Item 2), and committed as three separate commits on `phase3-effect-tab`; see Critical Discovery #133. Three of Archive #129-#132's four hardware-re-verification items closed (Pan 3/4, EQ curve, Sin/Tri) per user confirmation; the fourth (dropped Balance-commit rerender) left open pending either a located prior record or a fresh re-test. `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass throughout. ## Critical Discovery #134 — Manual's Effect Parameter Table Transcribed and User-Confirmed; Two More Instances of the Landmine #93 Balance Bug and a Data-Default Bug Found During the Visual Pass

**Context:** Continuing directly from Critical Discovery #133's blocker (the default-value-on-type-change task needed the manual's pp.144-145 bracketed defaults, which no reference file in this repo transcribed). User provided two scans of `X5DR Manual - Effects.pdf`'s "Effect Parameter Table"; `poppler` (`pdftoppm`) was installed to render them as images for transcription.

**Transcription process, two passes:** Pass 1, against the user's first scan, produced a table with a growing number of `[?]`-flagged cells past type 20 — a second self-check re-read of even the "confident" early rows (Reverb block's EQ Low/EQ High columns) surfaced inconsistent readings between passes, so low-confidence sections were left explicitly blank rather than guessed. Pass 2, against a second, higher-resolution scan the user provided specifically for this purpose, resolved nearly all of it — critically, re-reading it revealed the table's actual structure: **every type prints a Dry:FX Balance column, and the 8 "Combination Parallel" types (40-43, 46-47) print two** (one per sub-effect), which is independent manual-side corroboration of Critical Discovery #133/Landmine #93's hardware finding that these aren't a mirrored pair. Full transcription: `docs/X5DR_Editor_Effect_Parameter_Table_Transcription.md`.

**User's visual confirmation pass** (2026-08-14) found:

1. **Type 15 (Dual Mono Delay) has the exact same shape of bug Landmine #93 already fixed for types 40-43/46-47/44-45's exception — an independent Dry:FX Balance L/R pair, still wired through the old inverted-mirror `sendBalancePair` computation.** This was user-caught by reading the manual table itself (it shows a genuine "Balance L"/"Balance R" column pair for this type, unlike the ambiguously-named "Balance 1"/"Balance 2" columns for 40-43/46-47), not from a hardware test — but the fix is identical in shape and now shares the same code path. `isDualBalanceType` extended to `{15, 40, 41, 42, 43, 46, 47}`; type 15's pair labeled "Dry/Wet L"/"Dry/Wet R" (a genuine stereo split, unlike the other six types' "1"/"2" sub-effect pairing) via a new `dualBalanceLabels(t)` helper. Browser-verified: moving Dry/Wet L independently leaves Dry/Wet R's stored value untouched. Landmine #93 amended to cover this.

2. **Type 15's display name was wrong** — `EFFECT_TYPE_NAMES[15].label` read `"15: Dual Delay"`, not `"15: Dual Mono Delay"` (the name used everywhere else — group header, manual, this project's own prior documentation). Single fix at the `EFFECT_TYPE_NAMES` array; all three render call sites (`buildEffectTypeField`, the Effect Type Browser table, the pre-Phase-3 Easy tab's `buildSoundField`) derive from this one array, so no duplicate fix was needed.

3. **`dlyPhaser`'s Delay Hi Damp `initial` was wrong: `30`, should be `60`** per the manual — this was a genuine data-default bug, not a transcription artifact; the *first* transcription pass had actually omitted this column from the document entirely (documentation gap on Claude's side, not a manual-reading error), so the wrong default sat unnoticed until the user's own read of the physical page caught both the omission and the wrong value at once. Fixed directly in `EFFECT_TYPES`.

4. **Types 40/41's `[FX]`-printed Balance value confirmed to mean "fully wet," i.e. `0:100`** — resolves the Item 40/41 flag from the prior transcription pass. Not yet wired into code (that's the default-value task itself, still pending); recorded here for when that task starts.

5. **Type 41 (Delay/Room)'s Reverb Time range: the manual itself prints `0.2~9.9` (same as Hall's) for this type — hardware-confirmed by the user to be wrong; the correct range is capped like Room's own (Item 1), matching the app's pre-existing `dlyRoom.max: 47`.** No code change needed — the app was already correct here, predating this session; only the transcription document needed the correction (user edited it directly). Notable as the second instance this session of the manual itself, not the transcription, being the error (first: Landmine #90's MG Status bit-packing table, hardware-refuted in Critical Discovery #128).

6. **Bonus find from the previous session's transcription pass, user-confirmed correct:** types 7-9 (Wet/Dry Plate, Spring Reverb) have three genuinely different Reverb Time defaults in the manual (59/30/25), but `EFFECT_TYPES`' `plate` array still hardcodes one shared `initial: 30` — same shape as Item 1's original Hall/Room bug, not yet fixed (tracked in Progress Log's Current Status/Known Outliers, folded into the default-value task's audit step).

**Verification:** `npx vitest run` 297/297 throughout (both fixes are `EFFECT_TYPES`/`EFFECT_TYPE_NAMES` data-layer-only, no test coverage expected or needed there). Browser-verified: type 15 shows "Dual Mono Delay" and independently-operable "Dry/Wet L"/"Dry/Wet R" knobs; type 46 shows Delay Hi Damp defaulting to 60.

**Lesson:** the same predicate-extension discipline Landmine #36/#69/#93 already establish (check every call site when broadening a scope) applied here to a *data* fact, not just code — the user, doing an independent read of the primary source for an unrelated confirmation task, caught a bug in a control this session had already shipped and hardware-verified (Item 2/Critical Discovery #133) simply because the manual documents the exact same shape of parameter for a type nobody had thought to re-check. When a bug is found and fixed for a *pattern* (not just one instance), the right question isn't just "are there other call sites in the code" but "are there other data entries the pattern is supposed to cover" — and the source of truth for that second question was the manual table, not the codebase.

## Critical Discovery #135 — Default-Value-on-Type-Change Task Implemented: `EFFECT_TYPE_RESET_DEFAULTS`, a New Per-Type Lookup, Instead of Splitting ~14 More Groups

**Context:** With the manual's Effect Parameter Table fully transcribed and user-confirmed (Critical Discovery #134, including the types 7-9 `plate.initial` audit), the user asked to implement it — the editor should reflect the device's own factory defaults when an effect slot's type changes, not just reset the 7 per-type `PARAMETERS` slots to whatever `EFFECT_TYPES.initial` happened to already say.

**Scope discovery, larger than expected:** auditing `EFFECT_TYPES.initial` against the confirmed table surfaced that nearly every multi-type group is shared across types with genuinely different manual defaults — not just the two cases already found and fixed this session (Hall/Room's range, types 7-9's Reverb Time). Newly found during this audit: `earlyRef` (10-12), `stereoDly` (13-14), `multiTap` (16-18), `stereoChorus` (19-20), `quadChorus` (21-22), `flanger` (25-27), `distortion` (30-31), `phaser` (32-33), `autoPan` (35-36, i.e. Auto Pan vs. Tremolo), `chorusDly` (38-39), and `dlyDist` (44-45) all differ per member type. Even `hall`/`room` themselves — despite Item 1 already splitting them by *range* — still shared one `initial` per offset across their 3 member types each (Hall/Ensemble Hall/Concert Hall all had the same wrong `initial: 23` for Reverb Time, for instance).

**Design decision — a lookup table, not ~14 more array splits:** the Hall/Room precedent (Item 1) split a shared array into two because the *range* genuinely differed — a real layout/component property. Extending that same pattern here (splitting `flanger` into `flanger1`/`flanger2`/`crossOverFlanger`, etc.) would have produced roughly a dozen more near-duplicate array + `EFFECT_GRID_LAYOUT.set()` pairs differing only in default numbers, with every duplicate needing its own layout registration kept in sync by hand — exactly the duplication Landmine #72 already warns against, and a much larger, more error-prone diff for a change that's purely about defaults, not structure. Instead: added `EFFECT_TYPE_RESET_DEFAULTS`, a flat `{ typeNo: { params: {offset: rawValue}, balance: {balL[, balR]} } }` lookup covering all 47 types, keeping the existing shared arrays as the single source of truth for layout/range/format/labels and this new table as the single source of truth for defaults. The type-change reset handlers (both the Phase-3 Effect tab's `buildEffectColumn` and the pre-Phase-3 Easy tab's `buildEasyEffCol` — Landmine #72 duplication, not unified) now read from this table instead of `def.initial`.

**Unit conversion:** the manual documents `reverbTime`/`erTime`/`modSpeed` offsets in display units (seconds/ms/Hz), but `EFFECT_TYPES.initial` (and therefore the new lookup) stores the raw wire index the device actually expects. Every such value was converted via each formatter's own algebraic inverse (`raw = (seconds-0.2)/0.1`, `raw = (ms-100)/10`, and the 3-segment piecewise inverse for modSpeed) in a scratch Node script, then **round-tripped back through the forward formatter and diff'd against the manual's documented value** before being used — this caught the process working correctly (no conversion bugs surfaced), but is exactly the kind of arithmetic that's easy to get subtly wrong (an off-by-one segment boundary, a rounding direction) without that verification step. Scratch script discarded after use; not committed.

**Dry:FX Balance defaults — a new, unconfirmed inference:** the manual's "Dry:FX Balance" column is a ratio (e.g. `80:20`); the app's `balL`/`balR` store a single raw 0-100 number matching the "Dry/Wet" knob's own semantics (0=dry, 100=wet). **The raw value used is the ratio's SECOND number (the FX/wet percentage)** — inferred from that existing knob semantics, not independently hardware-confirmed. Flagged as Landmine #94 (Project Context) rather than treated as settled. The `[FX]` sentinel the manual prints for types 40/41's first Balance column (user-confirmed to mean "fully wet") maps to raw `100` under this same convention.

**Verification:** `npx vitest run` 297/297 throughout (data-only change, `EFFECT_TYPE_RESET_DEFAULTS` and the two reset-handler edits, no new test coverage expected). Browser-verified across 5 representative types after triggering a real type change (not just inspecting the data): type 1 (Hall, single balance) — every PARAMETERS value and Dry/Wet matched the manual exactly (Reverb Time "2.3s", balance 20). Type 40 (Delay/Hall, dual balance incl. the `[FX]`→100 case) — Balance 1 showed 100, Balance 2 showed 30, all 6 params matched. Type 15 (Dual Mono Delay) — Dry/Wet L/R and all 6 params matched. Type 36 (Tremolo) — Mod Speed showed "3.9Hz" exactly, confirming the modSpeed inverse conversion round-trips correctly through the display formatter for a case that lands in the piecewise formula's middle segment. Type 30 (Distortion), triggered from the **Easy tab** specifically (not the Phase-3 tab) — confirmed both reset handlers work, and confirmed via the Effect tab afterward that all 6 params and Balance landed correctly in the shared store, not just displayed correctly on the tab that set them.

**Lesson:** the Hall/Room precedent was the right fix for Item 1 (a genuine range/component difference) but would have been the *wrong* pattern to mechanically repeat 14 more times for a defaults-only difference — recognizing which shared property actually needs the array split (layout/range/format, yes; a per-type default number, no) avoided a much larger and more failure-prone diff. Separately: converting a manual's human-readable values into a device's raw wire format is exactly the kind of arithmetic worth writing a throwaway verification script for and round-tripping through the *same* forward function already shipped in production (`EFFECT_VALUE_FORMATTERS`) rather than re-deriving the formula by hand a second time — using the actual shipped function as the check catches both conversion-script bugs and shipped-function bugs in one pass.

*Last updated: 2026-08-14 — Default-value-on-type-change task implemented via a new `EFFECT_TYPE_RESET_DEFAULTS` lookup (all 47 types), wired into both the Phase-3 Effect tab's and the Easy tab's type-change reset handlers; see Critical Discovery #135, Landmine #94 (Project Context). Browser-verified across 5 types spanning single-balance, dual-balance (incl. the `[FX]` sentinel), and the modSpeed piecewise-formula edge case, and across both tabs. The Dry:FX Balance raw-value convention (ratio's second number = raw value) is an inference, not hardware-confirmed — flagged for a Snoize pass. `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass throughout.*

## Critical Discovery #137 — Easy Tab Retrofit (Phase 3 Brief 8) Started: Extraction Pattern, Two Real Layout Bugs, and a Fixed-Position Grid Technique

**Context:** the Easy tab is Phase 3's last remaining pre-Phase-3 tab — a condensed, duplicate view onto parameters that live natively on OSC/VDA/VDF/Effect. This session built it section by section directly against user feedback (no separate inventory doc/Design handoff; ADR-0008's stages 1-2 compressed into dialogue), on branch `phase3-easy-tab`. Session ended with the user planning further refinement in a new session — this entry covers what shipped and what was learned, not a close-out.

**Refactor: `buildEffectColumn` split into three reusable helpers.** Per ADR-0008 §3's "reuse already-proven shared helpers directly" rule, `buildEffectTypeAndSwitch`/`buildEffectBalanceControl`/`buildEffectHeroParams` were extracted from the Effect tab's `buildEffectColumn` so the Easy tab calls the identical Type/Switch/Balance/`EFFECT_TYPE_RESET_DEFAULTS`-reset logic rather than a second, hand-duplicated copy. Verified as a pure extraction (Effect tab's own rendered output unchanged, screenshot-diffed across a single-balance, a dual-balance, and a single-hero-param type before continuing). This also closed Landmine #93 (Dry:FX Balance independence) on the Easy tab automatically — the one code path that had never gotten that fix — with no separate porting step, simply because the reused helper already had it.

**Bug 1 — an outer wrapper filled with the same background as its own child panels.** `.easy-section` (the OSC/Envelopes/Effects section wrapper) was given `background: var(--bg-panel))` — the identical color its inner `.osc-panel`/`.vda-panel`/`.effect-panel` cards use — so there was no contrast between wrapper and card, and every section read as one big undifferentiated block despite the DOM already having multiple distinct panels (user-reported: "why do all the controls still appear to be in one big panel?"). Fix: the wrapper carries no background of its own, matching `#osc-content`'s existing convention (no rule at all — the page's `var(--bg-page)` shows through, letting the inner cards pop out). **Lesson:** a spacing-only wrapper around several cards must not share the cards' own fill color, or the visual grouping collapses regardless of whether the DOM structure is already correct.

**Bug 2 — `flex:1` with identical `min-width` still grew two columns unequally.** The Effects section's Routing panel and Effect-panels column, both `flex:1; min-width:640px` in the same row, measured 688px and 652px respectively (an 18px drift) rather than splitting the row evenly — confirmed via `getBoundingClientRect()`, not assumed. The concrete visible symptom (a separate report, same underlying cause) was that the Routing panel's own background extended past the diagram's own right edge, past the OSC panel's edge above it. Root cause not fully isolated (flex-basis:0% growth should be content-independent per spec), but `display:grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr` sidesteps it entirely — a genuine, mathematically-guaranteed 50/50 split, confirmed to make both columns' `getBoundingClientRect()` widths identical. **Lesson:** when two flex siblings need to be *exactly* equal width (not just approximately), don't rely on flex-grow parity even with identical rules on both sides — use Grid, which guarantees it structurally rather than through browser layout-algorithm behavior that turned out not to hold here.

**Bug 3 — a double-margin bug recurred in two different visible forms from the same root cause.** `.effect-panel`'s own shared `margin-bottom: 1rem` (still used by the full Effect tab, correctly, not touched) stacked with a flex container's own `gap` between Effect 1/Effect 2 (doubling the visible gap to ~32px instead of the intended 0.9rem), **and separately** ate into a CSS Grid item's `align-items:stretch`-resolved height for the Routing panel (pulling its rendered bottom edge 1rem short of the grid row's true bottom, so it didn't align with Effect 2's bottom as intended). Same mechanism, two different symptoms, reported and fixed in two separate rounds before the shared cause was recognized. Fix both times: cancel the margin scoped to the specific container's own children (`.easy-effects-col > .effect-panel`, `.easy-routing-panel`), never the shared `.effect-panel` class itself. **Lesson:** a margin belonging to a class reused across contexts (spacing convention for one layout mode, e.g. a simple stacked list) can silently double up or eat into stretch-sizing in a *different* layout mode (a gapped flex/grid container) the class was never designed for — check both symptoms (visible gap size, and grid-stretch alignment) whenever a shared card class gets reused inside a new gap-based container.

**Fixed-position 3-column grid for label-length-independent controls.** The Effect panels' 3 hero controls (Balance, hero param 1, hero param 2) needed constant horizontal positions regardless of a sibling's label length ("Delay Time" vs. "Reverb Time" must not shift anything). `buildEffectHeroParams`' own wrapper div is discarded at the Easy tab call site — its 1-2 knob children become individual grid items in a 3-column `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)` row instead of one flex-sized group. Verified across a short-label single-balance type and a long-label dual-balance (stacked) type: identical `[776, 993, 1209]`px column positions in both cases.

**`position:relative` + `left`/`top` as the correct tool for "move exactly this one element, don't disturb siblings."** Used twice — nudging the OSC Pan control right of the panel edge, and nudging VDF's Cutoff knob down to align with VDA's Level knob after VDA's own row-gap grew. Both cases needed a fixed offset applied to exactly one grid/flex item without changing track sizing (a margin/padding change would have grown that item's track and dragged siblings with it, contradicting the user's explicit "don't move any other control"). Both offsets were derived from existing named constants (`VDF_EG_HEIGHT - VDA_EG_HEIGHT`) rather than a re-measured pixel value, so they stay correct if those constants are ever retuned.

**Composite control reused for its UI shape only, not its function.** The OSC Pan + Outputs A/B control needed the exact visual shape of the Effect tab's OUT3/4 Pan control (`buildEffectPanControl`: hero knob + label beside, ON/OFF toggle centered below) but not its wiring — OSC's Pan uses a signed `-15..15` range and a `null`/`-1` sentinel off-encoding (Landmine #44), while `buildEffectPanControl` assumes a plain in-range `0`-is-off value. Built as a new function (`buildEasyOscPanItem`) reusing the `.effect-pan-item` CSS class and DOM shape directly, per ADR-0002/Landmine #72's guidance: duplicate when wiring genuinely differs, reuse directly only when it's identical.

**Verification:** all of the above is browser-verified only so far (no hardware pass this session) — `npx vitest run` 297/297 throughout (one transient worker-pool timeout mid-session, reproduced clean with `--no-file-parallelism` and again on a plain retry; unrelated to any code change). Every Parameter Change number and `sendParamChange` call site was copied forward unchanged at each step, per ADR-0008's rendering-only non-negotiable — no data-layer files touched.

*Last updated: 2026-08-18 — Easy tab retrofit in progress on `phase3-easy-tab`, not yet merged to `main` or hardware-tested. VDA and VDF panels combined into single cards with matched heights/aligned hero knobs; OSC and Effects sections restructured per the bugs/techniques above. Further refinement planned in a new session — see Progress Log Current Next Actions.*

## Critical Discovery #138 — `git status`/`git commit` Hang on This Repo Traced to a Stuck iCloud Sync Retry Loop, Not Fixed by a Reboot

**Context:** mid-session, `git commit` (and later `git status`) began hanging indefinitely — every invocation hit the tool's timeout with no output, after many prior commits in the same session had completed normally within seconds. Project Context already carried a one-line note from a prior session ("A one-time `~/Desktop`-wide file-access outage (iCloud-related) required a reboot to clear") flagging this general category as a known possibility; this session diagnosed the actual mechanism and found the previously-recorded fix insufficient.

**Diagnosis (in order):**
1. Confirmed the in-progress change was safely staged (`git diff --cached --stat` returned instantly and showed the expected diff) even though `git commit`/`git status` hung — ruled out data loss as a concern while diagnosing further.
2. Ruled out a stale `.git/index.lock` — one existed from an earlier killed attempt, removed twice, hang persisted both times with a fresh lock-free start.
3. Ruled out a slow-but-progressing computation: `ps -o pid,etime,time,state` on the actual hung `git status`/`git diff` processes showed **15+ minutes elapsed against under 0.1s of actual CPU time, state `S` (sleeping)** — a genuine blocked syscall, not slow work.
4. Ruled out a whole-filesystem stall: `find`/`ls` across the same directory tree (including `.git/objects`, 4800 files) and a full non-`node_modules` file listing (251 files) both completed instantly. The block is git-specific, not disk-wide.
5. `brctl status` (macOS's iCloud sync daemon control tool) showed the actual cause: an **active, perpetually-retrying-but-never-completing sync item specifically inside `.git/objects`** — `downloader{...active attempts:0 last:Xs ago next:ready...}`, with the "last attempt" timestamp resetting every check but `attempts:0`/`downloading:0.0%` never advancing, across two checks several minutes apart. A stuck retry loop, not a slow transfer that would eventually finish.

**The documented fix (reboot) did not work this time.** The user rebooted the Mac — `brctl status` still showed the identical stuck `.git/objects` item afterward, and `git` still hung. **What did work:** the user selected the project folder in Finder and chose "Download Now" (forcing full local materialization of every iCloud placeholder in the folder at once, rather than relying on iCloud's normal background reconciliation). Immediately afterward, `git status`/`git commit` both completed instantly and have been reliable since.

**Contributing factors identified, not independently confirmed as causal:** this repo tracks `node_modules` (not `.gitignore`d) — thousands of extra small tracked files for iCloud to reconcile on top of `.git/objects`' own thousands; disk was 93% full at the time, which can throttle iCloud's own eviction/download behavior; the whole project lives under `~/Desktop`, which has iCloud "Desktop & Documents" sync enabled by default on this Mac — a `.git` folder (many small immutable files, exactly the pattern iCloud's per-file sync model handles worst) being inside that sync scope at all is the structural root of the whole category, independent of this specific stuck-item instance.

**Lesson:** the prior "reboot fixes it" note was itself an inference from a single prior occurrence, not a confirmed general mechanism — this session's occurrence shows reboot is not reliable for this failure mode. The effective fix is forcing full local materialization (Finder "Download Now" on the folder), not restarting the OS. A future session hitting an inexplicable `git` hang on this specific repo should check `brctl status` for a stuck `.git/objects` item before assuming a reboot is the fix or spending time on git-specific debugging (lock files, hooks, fsmonitor config) — all of which were checked and ruled out here. Durable prevention (moving the repo out of iCloud-synced `Desktop`, or `.gitignore`ing `node_modules`) was identified but not actioned this session — a decision for the user, not something to change unilaterally mid-task.

*Last updated: 2026-08-18 — `git` hang root-caused to a stuck iCloud `.git/objects` sync retry loop; reboot alone insufficient, Finder "Download Now" on the project folder is the confirmed fix. See Landmine #95 (Project Context) for the always-read version of this fact.*

## Critical Discovery #139 — Easy Tab Retrofit (Phase 3 Brief 8) Completed: Dual-Curve EG Overlay, EXPRESSION Panel, and Drums-Mode Build-Out

**Context:** continuing the Easy tab retrofit from Critical Discovery #137 (which built OSC/Envelopes/Effects for Single/Double mode and left Drums mode, the Mod Wheel panel's real content, and the EG graphic's dual-curve display as open/deferred items), this session closed out all three remaining pieces on `phase3-easy-tab`, in three separate user requests handled sequentially.

**1. Dual-curve EG overlay.** The user recalled that an original pre-Phase-3 mockup showed both VDA-1/VDA-2 (and VDF-1/VDF-2) envelopes superimposed on one graphic, a feature lost when the Easy tab redesign replaced that mockup's bespoke SVG drawing (`drawVdfEnvelopeWithOpacity`/`drawVdaEnvelopeWithOpacity`) with the theme-appropriate `egCurveWidget` component. Rather than reviving the dead mockup code (which drew raw SVG independent of `egCurveWidget`'s own coordinate system, markers, and drag handling), the fix extended `egCurveWidget`'s existing `ghost` overlay parameter — already present in the component but, until this session, wired up only in the internal Design QA test page, never in any real tab. Added optional `ghost.color`/`ghost.opacity` overrides (previously hardcoded to a dimmed accent color) so the inactive curve could render as a neutral grey reference rather than a dimmed version of the active curve's own color — important since both curves would otherwise share a hue and be hard to tell apart at a glance. The two now-dead mockup functions were deleted outright rather than left as orphaned code. VDA/VDF tabs themselves are untouched — this is Easy-tab-only, confirmed by direct comparison in-browser.

**2. EXPRESSION panel replaces the Mod Wheel placeholder.** The user asked what to put in the Easy tab's placeholder "Mod Wheel" panel (previously just 1-3 small knobs stacked under the VDA column). Discussion landed on a curated 6-knob cross-section of the Control tab's most frequently-used performance controls: VDA Amplitude and VDF Cutoff (After Touch), Pitch Bend Range (Pitch Bend panel specifically — `modWheel.pitchBendRange`, param 22, distinct from `afterTouch.pitchBendRange`, param 17, which shares the same display label on the Control tab), VDF MG Intensity (Mod Wheel), and Mod Wheel → Pitch MG Intensity (vibrato depth, added on Claude's own recommendation as the single most iconic mod-wheel gesture on any synth, after noting the outgoing placeholder already surfaced it and the user's initial four-knob proposal would have dropped it). Built as one full-width panel, hero-sized (`HERO_KNOB_SIZE`/72px) to match this tab's own Effect-hero-param idiom rather than the Control tab's dense 58px grids, each label suffixed with its controller source (AT/PB/MW) since there's no per-source panel title here to disambiguate. Three of the six knobs (VDA Amplitude, VDF Cutoff, Pitch Bend Range/modWheel) needed brand-new `data-sync` keys added to the Control tab's own `controlKnob` calls plus new `syncByKey` entries in the central cross-tab wiring — the other three (VDF MG Intensity, and the vibrato pair) already had matching keys wired from pre-existing code. Bidirectional sync confirmed in-browser both directions, including the two same-labeled Pitch Bend Range params staying correctly distinct.

**3. Drums-mode OSC section built out.** Replaced the plain `ctrlRow`/`selCtrl`/`numCtrl` dropdown-row placeholder (Mode/Kit/Level/Send C/Send D as flat label:value rows, pre-Phase-3 styling) with a two-column layout matching the rest of the tab: left column stacks the shared `buildOscCommonPanel` (Mode/Assign/Hold — reused verbatim, identical to Single/Double mode) above a new "Drums" panel (hero Level knob + Kit dropdown + Send C/Send D regular knobs); right column is the OSC tab's own read-only Kit Summary, reused directly since it's a pure function with no side effects (same reuse precedent as `buildOscCommonPanel` itself, `buildEffectHeroParams`, etc. elsewhere on this tab). The right column's height matches the left column's combined height via plain flex stretch — copied directly from the OSC tab's own `.osc-drums-left`/`.osc-drums-right`/`.osc-kit-summary-panel` technique, not re-derived. No new sync wiring needed anywhere: every control reuses the OSC tab's existing `data-sync` keys (`osc1-level`, `osc1-multisound`, `osc1-sendC`, `osc1-sendD`), already wired either via the generic `['osc1','osc2'].forEach` central loop or the bespoke osc/vda Level mirror block. Confirmed live in-browser: editing Level on the new Easy tab panel reflects on the OSC tab's own Drums Level knob and vice versa, and the Kit Summary table updates live on Kit change (tested both a 78-entry ROM kit and a User kit).

**Verification:** all three pieces are browser-verified only, no hardware pass this session. `npx vitest run`: 234/234 pass across every file that completes; `controls.test.js` hit the same sandbox worker-pool timeout noted in Archive #116/#137 (pre-existing, unrelated to any change this session — not a new regression).

**Lesson:** two of these three items (the dual-curve overlay, the Drums-mode Kit Summary reuse) turned out to already have most of their machinery built and sitting unused elsewhere in the codebase — `egCurveWidget`'s `ghost` config and the OSC tab's own Drums-mode functions — rather than needing new mechanism from scratch. Both times, the fix was wiring up an existing, already-correct piece into a new call site rather than reimplementing its behavior, which is exactly the reuse-first posture ADR-0008 recommends for tab retrofits generally. This closes Brief 8's last deferred item (§1, Drums mode) — the Easy tab retrofit as a whole is now feature-complete pending a hardware pass.

## Critical Discovery #140 — Critical Discovery #126's Fix Never Actually Landed in Code; Re-Applied for Real This Session

**Context:** device hardware testing of the newly-completed Easy tab and Control tab surfaced that VDF MG Intensity (`modWheel.vdfMgInt`, param 21) was still grouped inside the Control tab's "Mod Wheel" panel alongside genuinely Mod-Wheel-driven controls — exactly the mislabeling Critical Discovery #126 (2026-07-30) already documented finding and fixing, three weeks earlier.

**Investigation:** `git log -S` traced the Phase-3 Control tab's Mod Wheel/VDF MG Intensity code to a single commit, `369f403` ("Restyle browser-modal chrome, rebuild Control tab (Phase 3), add Factory Sounds loader"), committed at the tail end of the very session that produced Critical Discovery #126. That commit's own diff already contained the *unfixed* grouping. No commit since ever touched the structure, and no branch's `src/index.html` contains the string "Breath Controller" (the panel name #126 says it created) anywhere. Conclusion: the fix was never lost by a later revert — it was never committed in the first place. Most likely mechanism: the session applied and browser/hardware-verified the fix live, then a broader "rebuild Control tab... per its own inventory doc and design handoff" step later in the same session re-derived the panel from a spec that was never updated to reflect the finding, silently discarding it before the final commit. See the new memory `verify-diff-before-archive-entry` (added this session) for the standing process fix: check the actual diff before writing an Archive entry claiming a fix is done.

**Fix (re-applied, this time confirmed against the actual committed diff):** Control tab's "Mod Wheel" panel renamed "Mod Wheel / Joystick +" (Pitch MG Intensity OSC-1/OSC-2 pair only); VDF MG Intensity moved into a new "Breath Control / Joystick -" panel directly below it, same right column. Param/store path/data-sync key unchanged — purely layout/label. Easy tab's EXPRESSION panel, which had surfaced VDF MG Intensity under an "(MW)" source tag, swapped it for VDF Sweep Intensity ("VDF Sweep Int (PB)", `modWheel.vdfSweepInt`, param 23, from the Pitch Bend panel) — same label length to preserve the row's spacing, plus a new `modWheel-vdfSweepInt` cross-tab sync key (Control tab knob + central wiring) so it stays synced like the rest of the panel. Also removed the now-dead `.control-stack` CSS class the old grouping left behind.

**Verification:** browser-verified — new panel layout/labels render correctly; VDF Sweep Intensity syncs bidirectionally between Easy and Control tabs (drag-tested both directions). `npx vitest run`: 234/234 pass (known `controls.test.js` sandbox timeout, not a regression).

**Lesson:** a documented "fix, done, verified" Archive entry is not itself proof the code changed — this is the second time in this project's history a session-end summary described work that the actual commit didn't contain (see Landmine #70's "a written brief is a paraphrase, not a substitute for checking the mockup" for the same failure shape applied to specs instead of fixes). The concrete cost here was three weeks of a real, previously-found bug shipping unnoticed until an independent hardware test caught it again.

*Last updated: 2026-08-18 — VDF MG Intensity's Mod Wheel mislabeling fixed for real (re-applying Critical Discovery #126, which never landed in a commit the first time); root-caused via `git log -S` to the original Phase-3 Control tab build commit already containing the bug. New memory `verify-diff-before-archive-entry` added to prevent recurrence. See Landmine #88 (Project Context) for the underlying hardware fact this all traces back to.*

## Critical Discovery #141 — Control Tab Brought to Full Column Width and Given Hero Controls, Three Rounds of User-Directed Refinement

**Context:** with VDF MG Intensity's mislabeling fixed (Critical Discovery #140), the user raised a separate, longer-standing complaint: the Control tab's panels were fixed at 460px and centered — a genuine, deliberate departure documented in that tab's own CSS comment since Brief 6 — while every other Phase 3 tab uses full `flex:1`/640px-min-width columns. No hero-sized controls existed on the tab at all. The result read as visually unfinished next to VDA/VDF/OSC/Effect/Easy.

**Round 1 — full width + hero controls + column swap.** `.control-column` switched from fixed-460px/centered to the app-wide `flex:1; min-width:640px` convention (`.vda-column`/`.vdf-column`/`.osc-column`); the dead `.control-columns-wrap` centering wrapper removed. `controlKnob`/`controlOscPair` gained an optional `hero` flag (promotes to `HERO_KNOB_SIZE`/`HERO_VALUE_FONT_SIZE`, matching the Effect tab's own hero-param idiom) applied to the same "most useful" controls already curated for the Easy tab's EXPRESSION panel: VDA Amplitude/VDF Cutoff (After Touch), Pitch Bend Range (Pitch Bend), the Pitch MG Intensity OSC pair (Mod Wheel/Joystick+), VDF MG Intensity (Breath Control/Joystick-, its sole control). User then asked to swap Mod Wheel/Joystick+ and AT + Mod Wheel's column placement to balance the two columns' total heights, and to align every row's knobs into two clean left-aligned columns — the old flex `.control-pair-row` (kept for a label-wrapping risk that no longer applies at this tab's now much wider column) was replaced everywhere with `.control-grid-2`'s strict `1fr 1fr` grid.

**Round 2 — vertical spacing and knob centering.** User asked for more gap between After Touch's hero row and its secondary grid (to match the right column's total height) and for regular knobs to visually center under hero knobs rather than share their left edge. A new `centerUnderHero` helper (nudges a regular knob right by `(HERO_KNOB_SIZE - SMALL_KNOB_SIZE) / 2` = 17px) was added and applied to After Touch's secondary grid and Pitch Bend's VDF Sweep Intensity. The extra gap was tuned iteratively against real `getBoundingClientRect()` measurements (not eyeballed) — landed on `margin-top: 19.5px`, producing exactly matched column heights (391.5px/391.5px, zero leftover stretch gap on either side).

**Round 3 — two follow-up alignment bugs, both self-inflicted.** User asked (a) for AT + Mod Wheel's Pitch MG Frequency - OSC 1 to center under Pitch Bend's hero knob (the panel now sits directly below it, post-swap) and (b) for Pitch Bend's and AT + Mod Wheel's regular knobs to align "one above the other." Measuring revealed two separate real bugs:
1. `centerUnderHero` applied to AT + Mod Wheel's OSC-1 fixed (a) correctly (confirmed ring centers both at x=787), but OSC-2 needed to stay unshifted to keep aligning with VDF Sweep Intensity above it.
2. VDF Sweep Intensity itself had wrongly been given `centerUnderHero` in Round 2 — it sits *beside* Pitch Bend Range (same row, column 2), not underneath any hero, so there was nothing to center against. That leftover 17px shift was the actual cause of the 17px misalignment against AT + Mod Wheel's OSC-2 the user reported. Removing it fixed (b) exactly (confirmed both knobs' left edges at x=1080).

A `minmax(0, 1fr)` change to `.control-grid-2`'s columns was made mid-investigation on a plausible but ultimately unconfirmed theory (that separate same-template grid containers could diverge in column width based on differing content min-widths) — kept as a low-cost defensive guard since `getBoundingClientRect()` showed it changed nothing measurable in this tab's actual grids (the 'beside' knob group stretches to fill its cell rather than sizing to min-content), and the CSS comment was corrected to say so rather than claim it fixed the observed bug.

**Verification:** every alignment claim in this entry is `getBoundingClientRect()`-confirmed, not eyeballed, across all three rounds, plus Single/Double OSC-mode dimming re-checked after each. Hit the dev-server stale-cache issue (Landmine #69/Archive #110) once mid-Round-2 tuning — a CSS edit measured as unchanged after an in-tab reload; resolved by restarting the dev server on a fresh port per that landmine's own fix. `npx vitest run`: 234/234 pass throughout (known `controls.test.js` sandbox timeout).

**Lesson:** Round 3's bug 2 is a direct instance of a pattern worth naming: an alignment fix applied under one mental model ("this regular knob is in a hero-adjacent context, shift it") silently mis-applied to a superficially similar but structurally different case ("adjacent" meaning *beside* rather than *underneath*) — the fix looked plausible and even rendered fine in isolation, and only broke once a second, later-added row exposed the wrong relationship it was actually testing against. When extending an alignment/spacing helper's usage to a new call site, re-derive *why* it applies there specifically (what, concretely, is it aligning against) rather than pattern-matching on surface similarity to a call site it was already proven correct for.

*Last updated: 2026-08-18 — Control tab brought to full column width, hero controls, and verified alignment across three rounds of refinement; see Round 3 for two self-inflicted alignment bugs found and fixed via getBoundingClientRect measurement. Browser-verified only, pushed to `origin/phase3-easy-tab`. PROG believed feature-complete pending a hardware pass — see Progress Log Current Status/Next Actions. Next: the COMBI tabs.*

## Critical Discovery #143 — COMBI: ROUTING/Effect 1/Effect 2 Split Off SOUND Into Their Own EFFECT Inner Tab

**Context:** first step of the COMBI Phase 3 retrofit (`main`, post-PROG-merge). COMBI's SOUND inner tab had carried the timbre table *and* the full Effects panel (ROUTING + Effect 1/Effect 2, via `buildEffectContent('combi', n)`) bolted onto the bottom, unlike PROG which already gives Effect its own inner tab. User asked to split it out to match PROG's structure, operating identically, with Combi's own param offsets preserved.

**Finding:** `buildEffectContent(mode, n)` (and its helpers `effectsParamOffset`/`effectsScope`/`effectsStorePath`) were already fully mode-aware — built generic across `'program'`/`'combi'`/`'multi'` back when Multi's own Effects panel was wired up (Brief #19). This meant the entire change was a pure rendering-layer move: add `{ id: 'effect', label: 'Effect' }` to COMBI's inner-tab array, add a new `combi-innerpanel-effect` panel calling the same `buildEffectContent('combi', currentCombiIndex)`, and delete the `effectGrid` div that used to embed it at the bottom of `buildCombiSoundContent`. No parameter numbers, store paths, or `sendParamChange` call sites changed.

**Verification:** browser-verified with real factory data (Combi "SolarFlare") — ROUTING/Effect 1/Effect 2 render and behave identically under the new EFFECT tab as they did embedded in SOUND; Sound/Zones/Effect switch cleanly; no console errors. `npx vitest run`: 234/234 pass (known `controls.test.js` sandbox timeout, not a regression). ## Critical Discovery #144 — COMBI: SOUND + ZONES Merged Into One "Timbres" Tab, Component Library Retrofit

**Context:** second step of the COMBI Phase 3 retrofit, following ADR-0008's five-stage process. User asked to merge the (now Effect-free) SOUND tab and the ZONES tab into one 8-row table — same Timbres, roughly double the columns — retrofitted onto the shared component library. An inventory doc (`Setup Instructions/Claude Prompts/Phase 3/X5DR_Editor_Phase3_Combi_SoundZones_Inventory_For_Claude_Design.md`) was written first and handed to Claude Design; the returned reference (`docs/design spec docs/Combi Tab/`) came back as a single-line-per-Timbre layout, one shared header row, inside a `--bg-panel` card at the existing 1400px canvas width.

**Two clarifications resolved before implementation (both by tracing the actual code, not assumption):**
1. The "Mute" checkbox's checked-state semantics were already "enabled/active" at the data layer and on the wire (`timbre.enabled`, Timbre SW bit in `sysex.js`) — only the column header text and the misleadingly-named `sendTimbreMute` function implied the opposite. Resolved as a relabel only: header/tooltip → "Active", function renamed `sendTimbreActive`, zero logic change.
2. Width: user set a hard constraint (must not exceed the existing full-width single-column tabs already shipped, e.g. Control/Effect) rather than leaving it to Design's judgment.

**Component-library first deployments.** Two Control Component Spec §1/§3 primitives existed only in the component gallery demo before this tab — `knobWithOverride` (the Off/PRG override block) and `dualHandleRangeSlider` (variant E) — this is their first real use anywhere in the shipped app:
- `knobWithOverride` was generalized in place (`src/ui/controls.js`) to accept `bidirectional`/`format`/`readoutMode`, since A:B Pan needs a signed, `formatPan`-labeled base knob that the original unidirectional-only implementation couldn't represent. Safe to modify directly rather than duplicate, per ADR-0002 — nothing else depended on it yet. Level and Send C/Send D use the unidirectional base (PRG-only override); A:B Pan uses the new bidirectional base (Off + PRG).
- `dualHandleRangeSlider` replaces the old separate Top/Bottom numeric fields for both Key Window (0–127) and Vel Window (1–127, distinct minimum from Key Window per TABLE 2) — one control per window, handles clamped so Top can never cross Bottom. Only the bound that actually moved gets a fresh `sendParamChange` per drag tick, to avoid doubling MIDI traffic.

**Mockup-vs-real-componentry width gap (ADR-0008 pitfall category, ~third recurrence).** The Claude Design reference rendered Key/Vel Window as static ~18px-wide text spans (140px column budget total); the real, already-coded `dualHandleRangeSlider` component uses genuine editable `<input>` fields (40px each by its own shared default) — a real, editable, clickable numeric field is inherently wider than a mockup's decorative approximation, and this is *correct*, not a mockup deviation to fix (the user's own convention requires editable values, not static text). Resolved by (a) scoping a narrower `.ctrl-range-e-field` width (36px) and a shorter `trackLength` (56px, vs. the demo's 90px) to this tab only — doesn't touch the shared component's own default — and (b) verifying the real total row width in-browser via `getBoundingClientRect()` rather than trusting the mockup's own arithmetic: confirmed the actual `.combi-timbres-panel` renders at exactly 1356px (matching `#content`'s real available width, `1400 - 2×22px`), with the header/row content fitting inside it with a few px to spare, no horizontal overflow. The tradeoff: the mockup's "wide gap between clusters" spacer divs (`flex:1`) render at their floor width (12px) rather than genuinely flexing wider, since the real componentry leaves no leftover space to grow into — a denser result than the mockup's own rendering, but still within the hard width constraint.

**Everything else carried forward unchanged:** CH stays a plain dropdown (explicit user direction, only field on the tab not migrated to the component library); Program stays `buildSoundField` (same pattern as OSC/Effect Type fields); Transpose/Detune become plain bidirectional knobs (variant B); the 4 filter checkboxes (Prog Chg/Damper/Aftertouch/Ctrl Chg) plus Active are rendered as small toggle boxes (a deliberate visual departure from a native `<input type=checkbox>` — Control Component Spec's variant H is defined behaviorally, and the approved mockup renders filled/outlined boxes, not checkbox glyphs). No Parameter Change number, store path, or wire-encoding fact changed from the pre-retrofit code (A:B Pan's PRG=`0x1F`/Off=signed`-1` sentinel split, Send PRG=raw nibble `10`, Level PRG=`127` — all unchanged, ADR-0001 Amendment C and Landmine #44's pattern still apply).

**Verification:** browser-verified with real factory data (Combi "SolarFlare") — all 8 rows render correctly; `getBoundingClientRect()` confirmed no horizontal overflow at the panel/header/row level; interactively tested the Level override chip (dims/restores correctly, retains underlying value), the Active toggle (row opacity dims to 0.5, confirmed via `getComputedStyle` after the CSS transition settles), and the Key Window dual-handle slider's clamp (dragging Low past High clamps both to the same value, matching spec). PROG's own Effect tab and COMBI's own EFFECT tab (Archive #143) re-checked after this change — no regression. `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass across all files (`controls.test.js`'s known sandbox timeout, Landmine/Archive #80/#116, did not reproduce this run — ran standalone separately and confirmed 63/63, including the `knobWithOverride` generalization). Not yet hardware-tested.

*Last updated: 2026-08-18 — COMBI's SOUND and ZONES inner tabs merged into one "Timbres" tab (8 rows, one line per Timbre), retrofitted onto the component library per the Claude Design handoff (`docs/design spec docs/Combi Tab/`). First real deployment of `knobWithOverride` (generalized to support a bidirectional base) and `dualHandleRangeSlider`. Browser-verified only, not yet hardware-tested. Next: COMBI's own hardware pass, then the remaining COMBI concerns (if any) before considering COMBI feature-complete.*
