## Critical Discovery #145 — COMBI: A/B Experiment, `combi-timbres-split` Branch — Re-Splitting Timbres Into Timbres+Control Tabs

**Context:** with the merged SOUND tab (Archive #144) committed to `main` (`b1fb8bf`) and several rounds of polish applied on top (Program field font/theme/fixed-size matching Effect Type/OSC Multisound fields, CH dropdown theme match + centering, Level/Pan/Send C/Send D knob-overlap fix — all folded into that same `main` commit), the user wanted to try a "radical" alternative: recreate the original pre-merge SOUND/ZONES split as two tabs (**Timbres**: Active/Ch/Program/Level/A:B Pan/Send C/Send D/Transpose/Detune, full-size knobs; **Control**: Active/Ch/Program/Level/Key Window/Vel Window/PC-DM-AT-CC, larger Window sliders) to compare directly against the merged single-tab layout, while keeping `main` completely untouched as the safe fallback.

**Decisions (user-directed):** new branch (`combi-timbres-split`, off `main`'s `b1fb8bf`) rather than continuing on `main`; all three tabs — the original merged tab (renamed **SOUND**, its own pre-merge name) plus the two new **TIMBRES**/**CONTROL** tabs — coexist live in one running app for direct in-tab comparison, rather than only comparing via branch switching; SOUND is explicitly the tab slated for removal if the split wins, so its own code was deliberately left untouched (only its tab id/label renamed 'timbres'→'sound') rather than refactored to share code with the two new tabs.

**Implementation:**
- Active/Ch/Program/Level are genuinely shared fields — extracted into `buildCombiSharedActive`/`Ch`/`Program`/`Level` (index.html), used by both new tabs, live-synced across **all three** tabs (SOUND included) via the same `subscribeTo`/`data-sync` cross-tab-sync shape PROG's Easy tab already established — not a new pattern. SOUND's own pre-existing Active/CH/Level controls got minimal additive `data-sync` tags (no logic change) so they participate in the same sync web; without this, editing on SOUND wouldn't visibly update TIMBRES/CONTROL until a full re-render, which would have read as a real bug during the very A/B comparison this branch exists for.
- Level's sync needed a bespoke `subscribeTo` callback, not the generic `syncByKeyCombi` used for Active/CH — `knobWithOverride`'s `_setValue(v, ov)` needs the 127-PRG sentinel decomposed back into `{value, override}` explicitly, which a plain single-argument `_setValue(v)` can't express.
- Active's sync also needed to be bespoke — engaging/disengaging Active must re-dim/undim every cell in that Timbre's row on every tab, not just the toggle's own visual state. Solved via a new `data-timbre-row` tag on every cell (SOUND's whole `.combi-tmb-row`, and each individual TIMBRES/CONTROL grid cell), targeted by the sync callback alongside the toggle's own `data-sync` key.
- Both new tabs use **CSS Grid** (`grid-template-columns: repeat(N, max-content)`), not SOUND's fixed pixel column widths — deliberately, so a column can never spill into its neighbor's track by construction. This was a direct lesson from the knob-overlap bug already fixed once on SOUND this session (Archive #144's own polish round) — building the new tabs with fixed pixel widths risked re-deriving the identical failure mode.
- Follow-up polish, same session: CH/Program theme-matched (same token-based background/border/color/radius fix as SOUND's own) and Transp/Detune knobs explicitly sized to `DEFAULT_KNOB_SIZE` (58px) to match Level/Pan/Send (they'd defaulted to the smaller 38px "beside" size). Also a real Grid-specific bug: the Program field's `width: 100%` only reached its own grid-item box, not the shared column *track* — with the grid's default `justify-items: center`, each row's Program field kept sizing to its own shrink-to-fit content, centered within the (already correctly `max-content`-sized) wider track, rendering at inconsistent widths row to row (123–147px) with no truncation and no error, easy to miss without measuring. Fixed via a dedicated `justify-self: stretch` class on the Program cell specifically — now Landmine #98's general rule.

**Verification:** browser-verified — no overlap, no overflow on either new tab; Level's PRG-override sync, Active's row-dimming sync, and CH's value sync all confirmed working across all three tabs without a full re-render (toggling on one tab immediately reflects on the other two). VDF's existing 3-way toggle re-checked, unaffected. `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass. Not yet hardware-tested — this entire branch is exploratory.

*Last updated: 2026-08-19 — `combi-timbres-split` branch created off `main` (`b1fb8bf`); SOUND (renamed, untouched) / TIMBRES (new) / CONTROL (new) coexist for live A/B comparison.*

## Critical Discovery #146 — Off/PRG Override Redesign: Design Exploration → Fused Toggle Strip

**Context:** the user wasn't satisfied with the shipped Off/PRG override control's design (knob + a vertical stack of individually-bordered chip buttons beside it) and asked where prior alternate mockups for it lived. A thorough search (every doc/design file, the full `Reference Images/Claude Design/` tree, the `v2.zip` archive) turned up exactly **one** existing mockup — `X5DR Design Directions.dc.html` §5a, "KNOB W/ OFF · PRG OVERRIDE" — a pixel match for what's shipped; no alternates existed to recover. The user explicitly ruled out any design element sitting on the knob's own face (a drag target), and asked to see the "Off/PRG stacked with the numeric control" direction specifically, plus other options.

**Design exploration:** built and published a Claude Design canvas (`design` skill) comparing four directions at both the 58px full-size and 28px compact knob, each with a PRG-only (Level) and Off+PRG (A:B Pan) example: (1) **stacked with numeric** — value + override button(s) as one column beside the knob; (2) **mini-row below** — override button(s) on a second line under the unchanged knob+readout row; (3) **fused toggle strip** — override buttons become one bordered pill (shared outline, inset-ring active state) matching the app's existing `buildFusedToggleGroup` visual language (Sin/Tri, off/+/− toggles), rather than separate chip buttons; (4) current/baseline, included as the comparison anchor. User picked **option 3**, later clarifying the numeric readout and pill needed to be **vertically stacked** (direction 1's layout) rather than sitting beside each other on one line (an intermediate implementation mistake, since corrected — see below).

**Implementation (`knobWithOverride`, `src/ui/controls.js`):** new `overrideStyle` config — `'stack'` (default, unchanged everywhere else, including SOUND) or `'fused'`, which reuses `buildFusedToggleGroup` directly rather than a new hand-rolled pill. Toggle-off (return to knob-driven, no override) needed a same-tick correction through the group's own `setValue`, since `buildFusedToggleGroup` has no native toggle-off — it always just selects whatever was clicked. Applied to Level/Pan/Send C/Send D on **TIMBRES only** (user-directed scope) — Level is shared with CONTROL, so `buildCombiSharedLevel` takes an `overrideStyle` param (default `'stack'`) rather than silently changing CONTROL's look too.

**Real bug found and fixed along the way:** `buildFusedToggleGroup`'s first/last-button corner-radius logic (already patched once before, per its own code comment, for the multi-segment case) had never been exercised with a **single-item** group — Level/Send C/Send D's PRG-only case is the first caller ever to pass `items.length === 1`. The `i === 0` branch won the ternary and gave the lone segment only a left-rounded corner, so an active segment's inset ring would poke out the square right edge — exactly the failure shape the user's own "corner radius needs to match" instinct anticipated before implementation even started. Fixed for all group sizes; verified via `getComputedStyle` (8px on all four corners, matching the wrap and the inset ring exactly) and confirmed VDF's own unrelated 3-way toggle unaffected.

**Layout correction:** the first implementation pass left the knob's own built-in "beside" readout in place and just appended the fused pill as a third horizontal sibling (knob | readout | pill) — the same three-across shape as the old chip-stack design, just with a different pill widget, not what direction 3 (or the user's "vertically stacked" clarification) actually called for. Fixed by building the knob with `readout: false` in fused mode and constructing an external `buildReadout` instance stacked directly above the fused pill in its own column beside the knob — verified via `getBoundingClientRect` (readout sits directly above the pill, left-aligned, 0px horizontal offset).

**Stepper follow-up:** the external readout's `stepper: false` (carried over unreflectively from the earlier dense-table stepper removal, Archive #144's polish round) was flipped back to `true` once the layout was correct — TIMBRES' full-size knobs have real headroom for it, unlike SOUND's intentionally compact ones (`COMBI_KNOB_TIGHT`, still `stepper: false`, untouched). Verified functional (click-and-hold increments the value) on Level, Pan, and Send C/D.

**Verification (whole arc):** browser-verified throughout — dim/restore, toggle-off, cross-tab sync (mixed 'fused'/'stack' styles) all confirmed correct via `getComputedStyle`/`getBoundingClientRect`; `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass each round, `controls.test.js` standalone 63/63. Not yet hardware-tested.

*Last updated: 2026-08-19 — TIMBRES' Level/Pan/Send C/Send D now use a fused toggle-strip override (option 3 of a 4-direction design exploration), stacked under the readout, with a working stepper — plus a real dormant corner-radius bug in the shared `buildFusedToggleGroup` fixed for good.*

## Critical Discovery #147 — `knobWithOverride._setValue` Silently Clobbered the Real Value on Every Self-Referential Sync (Level's PRG Deselect Bug)

**Context:** hardware pass still pending, but the user caught this by eye first: engaging Level's PRG override and then disengaging it left the knob at 0, not the original value (e.g. 77) — contrasted directly against Pan/Send, which correctly dim-but-retain and restore. The user also noted this matches how equivalent PROG controls already behave, i.e. this was a real regression, not a design ambiguity.

**Root cause:** Level is the *only* Combi Timbres field wired into cross-tab `subscribeTo` sync (Archive #145) — Pan/Send C/D are standalone, wired into no sync at all. The store's pub-sub has no "skip the element that caused this notification" concept, so clicking Level's PRG button fired the sync callback back onto the **same knob that originated the click**. That callback (`renderCombiPanel`) passes `0` as a placeholder display value whenever the wire value is the 127-PRG sentinel — correct for a fresh page render, where the store genuinely holds no other number — but `knobWithOverride`'s own `_setValue(v, ov)` unconditionally adopted whatever `v` it was given, clobbering the knob's real last-known value down to 0 on every PRG toggle, self-inflicted by its own click handler's round trip through the store.

**Fix:** `_setValue` now only adopts the incoming value when `ov` (override) is falsy — while an override is engaged there's no real number to sync *from* anyway (the wire sentinel carries none), so the knob simply keeps whatever real value it already has. Root-caused and fixed inside the shared component itself, not patched around in the Level-specific sync callback — applies uniformly to both `overrideStyle` values and any future `knobWithOverride` caller, not just Level.

**Verification:** browser-verified — Level's PRG toggle now round-trips 77 → 77 (was 77 → 0) on both TIMBRES (fused) and SOUND (stack), value staying dimmed-but-visible throughout; all three tabs (SOUND/TIMBRES/CONTROL) stay correctly in sync. `controls.test.js` 63/63 standalone, full suite 297/297. **Hardware pass still pending** — user-flagged explicitly, not yet confirmed against the real device.

*Last updated: 2026-08-19 — Root-caused and fixed a self-referential sync bug in `knobWithOverride._setValue` that silently reset Level's value to 0 on every PRG deselect; Pan/Send were never affected (no sync wiring to trigger it). Browser-verified only.*

## Critical Discovery #148 — COMBI TIMBRES Tab: Full Panel Width via Three Equal Flex Gaps

**Context:** with the fused-pill redesign and value-revert fix landed, the user asked to make better use of the panel's full width — equal extra space specifically between Level↔Pan, Pan↔Send C, and Send D↔Transp, while keeping Send C/Send D and Transp/Detune visually paired, with Detune's right edge landing so the row's divider line sits equidistant from the panel's left and right edges.

**Implementation:** `.combi-full-grid-timbres`'s `grid-template-columns` gained three `minmax(0, 1fr)` spacer tracks at exactly those three positions, alongside the 9 real `max-content` field columns — CSS Grid distributes 100% of the panel's leftover width evenly across `fr` tracks once every other column sizes to its own content, so the row stretches to fill the panel edge-to-edge without disturbing the tight pairs (no spacer track between Send C/D or Transp/Detune, just the existing base `column-gap`). A new `fullSpacer()` helper appends an empty grid item at each spacer track's position — must appear in the header row and all 8 data rows, in the same relative position each time, for the shared grid columns to line up (same discipline as `fullHdr`/`fullCell`).

**Verification:** `getBoundingClientRect()` confirmed all three flex gaps measure exactly 86px (equal); the divider line sits at exactly 22px from both the left and right panel edges (matching the panel's own symmetric CSS padding, 1.375rem, with no extra math needed — `fr` tracks inherently fill to the container's true edge); headers remain perfectly centered above their data columns (0px offset). No overflow. `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass.

*Last updated: 2026-08-19 — TIMBRES tab now fills the full panel width via three equal flexible gaps (Level↔Pan, Pan↔Send C, Send D↔Transp); Send C/D and Transp/Detune stay tightly paired. Session close-out — moving to the CONTROL tab next session.*

## Critical Discovery #149 — CONTROL Tab Built Out: Shared Level Style Match + Key/Vel Window Redesign + Key Window Note Names

**Context:** first CONTROL-tab session after #148's close-out. CONTROL already had Active/Ch/Program/Level (shared with TIMBRES) and Key/Vel Window/PC-DM-AT-CC of its own from the original branch setup, but three things were asked in sequence: (1) make Active/Ch/Program/Level's placement, style, and operation pixel-identical to TIMBRES; (2) redesign Key/Vel Window — theme-colored numeric fields with a stepper (matching every knob's own readout), wide enough for 3-digit values, enough gap that the drag handle can't overlap the field, a wider track for the 0-127 range, and bigger group gaps (Levels↔Key Window, Key Window↔Vel Window, Vel Window↔PC/DM/AT/CC) so the last column reaches the same right edge TIMBRES' Detune does; (3) make Key Window display the actual note name (e.g. "C#3"), reverting to the raw number when clicked for direct editing.

**(1) Shared-column style match:** the only real gap was Level's override style — TIMBRES already used `overrideStyle: 'fused'` (Archive #146), CONTROL was still on the default `'stack'`. Fixed by passing `'fused'` through `buildCombiSharedLevel` on CONTROL's own call site too. Verified via `getBoundingClientRect()`: Active/Ch/Program/Level land at identical x/width on both tabs (x=64/146/255/421, matching widths, same 1356px panel) — switching tabs, the four columns visually don't move.

**(2) Key/Vel Window redesign — `dualHandleRangeSlider` (`src/ui/controls.js`) gained three new opt-in config params, defaults unchanged so every other caller (the component gallery's own demo) is unaffected:** `fieldStyle: 'plain' | 'readout'` (`'readout'` swaps the bare `numericField` `<input>` for the same `buildReadout(..., {stepper:true})` every knob's own value field uses — theme `--value-color` text, hover-revealed accent-colored stepper triangles, auto-width so a 3-digit value can never truncate); `gap` (default 6, unchanged) widening the space between each numeric field and the track (the handle overhangs the track by its own 6px radius at either extreme, so a tight gap risks visual overlap — CONTROL uses 14, giving an 8px worst-case clearance, confirmed via `getBoundingClientRect`); `format`, passed straight through to `buildReadout` for note-name display (see below). CONTROL's own `grid-template-columns` gained the same three-`minmax(0, 1fr)`-spacer-track pattern TIMBRES already used (Archive #148), pulling PC/DM/AT/CC flush against the panel's right edge instead of leaving dead space after it — confirmed pixel-identical to TIMBRES' own divider line (`sep` width 1312px, right edge 1376px, both tabs, both panels 1356px).

**(3) Key Window note names:** `format: midiNoteName` (the same helper VDA/VDF's KBD Track Key already uses) passed only to the Key Window slider, not Vel Window (velocity has no note-name meaning). No new code needed for the "revert to number when editing" requirement — `buildReadout`'s edit-mode `<input>` was already unconditionally seeded from the raw numeric value regardless of `format`; confirmed via a direct DOM test (click → input shows raw "60", not "C4"; blur → readout shows "C4" again).

**Verification:** all three items browser-verified via `getBoundingClientRect`/`getComputedStyle` plus direct interaction (stepper hover-reveal and click-to-increment both confirmed working via ref-precise clicks — a coordinate-based click risked mis-hitting the stepper's small hit target and holding long enough to trigger its auto-repeat, which is what happened on the first attempt and was not a real bug). `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass throughout (the slider's existing tests all use the default `fieldStyle`, unaffected). Not yet hardware-tested.

*Last updated: 2026-08-19 — CONTROL's Active/Ch/Program/Level now match TIMBRES exactly (Level's override style was the one gap); Key/Vel Window redesigned with theme-colored stepper readouts, wider gap/track, and bigger inter-group spacing; Key Window now displays note names (e.g. "C#3"), reverting to the raw number for direct editing. Browser-verified only.*

## Critical Discovery #152 — MULTI Retrofit: TRACKS/CONTROL/EFFECT Split, Bend Range, Dual-Tab Toolbar

**Context:** first MULTI-mode session after COMBI's close-out (#151). Confirmed design questions with the user before writing any code (per the user's own request): Pitch Bend Range placement (Control tab, between Level and Key Window — user's own instinct, confirmed correct: TABLE 9 param 112+n is genuinely per-Track and live, same shape as Key/Vel Window's own columns, so it drops cleanly into the existing grid); "Copy from Combination..." toolbar placement (kept on TRACKS, per Combi's own "Copy Effects From..." precedent of living on the tab it populates, rather than the header — but then extended to **both** TRACKS and CONTROL per user follow-up, since Program is editable on both and it keeps the toolbar in the same screen position across a tab switch); and the `#multi-title`/tab-pill overlap (root-caused to `#multi-title` having zero CSS of its own, unlike `#combi-name`'s `margin-right`/`flex-shrink`/`white-space`).

**Implementation:** `renderMultiPanel` rewritten to mirror `renderCombiPanel`'s three-tab shape exactly — SOUND→**TRACKS** (`buildMultiTracksContent`, was `buildMultiSoundContent`), CONFIG→**CONTROL** (`buildMultiControlContent`, was `buildMultiConfigContent`), EFFECT split into its own tab (was embedded under SOUND). TRACKS reuses Combi's exact `.combi-full-grid-timbres` column template (Active/Ch/Program/Level/A:B Pan/Send C/Send D/Transp/Detune) — a genuine **new** Ch column added here (didn't exist on the old flat table), wired to the same `midiChannel` field the old CONFIG tab already had. CONTROL gets a new `.multi-full-grid-control` template — Combi's own CONTROL grid plus one extra column pair for Bend Range. Both use new `buildMultiShared{Active,Ch,Program,Level}` field builders (mirroring `buildCombiShared*` but scoped to `multi.tracks`/`multiParamNo`/`'multi'`) — **not** a literal reuse of Combi's shared builders, since those hardcode Combi's store paths.

**Load-bearing fact surfaced, not previously written down this explicitly:** TABLE 9 has a live Parameter Change entry for Active (via the combined Program No. encoding)/Program/Level/Pan/Send C/Send D/Transpose/Detune/**Bend Range** — but genuinely none at all for MIDI Channel, Key Window, Vel Window, or the Damper/Aftertouch/Ctrl-Chg filters (only Prog Chg filter has one, 128+n b0, unused by this app). Those four write via the same debounced Expansion-dump sync (`scheduleConfigSync`) the old CONFIG tab always used — this was already correctly implemented and commented in the pre-retrofit code (`buildMultiConfigContent`'s own header comment: "No live Parameter Change path for any field here... confirmed via hardware capture"), just not previously connected to the fact that **Ch** (one of the four "shared" fields now duplicated across TRACKS and CONTROL) is one of them. So the two tabs' "shared" Active/Ch/Program/Level columns are not uniformly live the way Combi's are — Active/Program/Level are; Ch isn't. Cross-tab sync (`subscribeTo`, mirroring Combi's own block) covers all three regardless, since the sync itself just mirrors DOM state, independent of which write mechanism fired underneath.

**Dead code removed:** `buildTrackRow`/`buildTrackPanCtrl`/`buildTrackSendCtrl` (old pre-Phase-3 flat table), `buildMultiConfigContent`/`buildConfigRow`/`buildConfigFilterCell` (old CONFIG tab), and the now-fully-dead `.timbre-table`/`.send-cell` CSS (Combi had already stopped using it; Multi was the last caller).

**Verification:** browser-verified against the factory soundbank — all three tabs render correctly, no console errors; cross-tab sync confirmed live (toggling a Track's Active off on TRACKS correctly dims the same row on CONTROL without a full re-render). `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass throughout (no Parameter Change numbers or store paths changed — pure rendering-layer retrofit, per ADR-0008's standing non-negotiable). Not yet hardware-tested.

## Critical Discovery #153 — CONTROL Tab Grid Silently Overflowing; PC/DM/AT/CC Toggle Boxes Left-Packed Instead of Centered

**Context:** two follow-up user reports after #152 shipped, both caught by measurement rather than assumption, per this project's own established verification discipline (Landmine #78/Critical Discovery #112's precedent).

**Bug 1 — grid overflow.** User asked for PC/DM/AT/CC's right margin to mirror the left margin, with equal gaps between all the new CONTROL columns. `getBoundingClientRect()` on the live page showed something worse than a spacing tweak: `getComputedStyle(grid).gridTemplateColumns` had all four `1fr` spacer tracks resolved to **`0px`**, and the PC/DM/AT/CC cell's right edge sat **~19px past the panel's own right edge** — a genuine layout overflow, not a margin/centering issue. Root cause: adding Bend Range's column to a row that already only barely fit Combi's original 10-column CONTROL template pushed the row's total fixed-width content (dominated by the two 266px-wide Key/Vel Window sliders, `trackLength: 170` each) past what the panel could hold — CSS Grid can't shrink `max-content`-sized tracks below their content's own minimum, so once the fixed columns' sum + gaps exceeded the container, every flex track collapsed to zero and the row overflowed outright, at *any* window width (confirmed at both 1500px and 1300px — the app's own fixed ~1400px canvas, Archive #98, means there's no wider viewport to grow into). Fixed by shrinking Key/Vel Window's `trackLength` from 170 to 128 — Multi-only, since Combi's own CONTROL tab has no Bend Range column and isn't affected. Re-measured after the fix: all four flex tracks resolved equally (~10.7px each), and PC/DM/AT/CC's right margin exactly matched the panel's own 22px left padding.

**Generalizable lesson, promoted to a new Landmine (Project Context #99):** a CSS Grid row with several fixed-width (`max-content`) columns and evenly-distributing `1fr` spacer tracks between them can silently overflow the moment one more fixed-width column is added, with **zero visual warning that looks like an error** — the flex tracks just quietly collapse to 0px and the content spills past the container. `justify-content`/CSS-only tuning cannot fix this; the only fix is shrinking one of the fixed-width columns' own content. Always re-measure total row width via `getBoundingClientRect`/`getComputedStyle` after adding a column to any of this app's `.combi-full-grid`-family panels (TIMBRES/CONTROL on both Combi and Multi), not just visually.

**Bug 2 — PC/DM/AT/CC header looked offset right.** Same `getBoundingClientRect` approach: the header text centers correctly over its column's full 100px track width, but `.combi-tmb-col-filters` (the toggle-box container, shared by Combi's and Multi's CONTROL tabs) had no `justify-content`, so its 4 toggle boxes defaulted to flex-start, left-packing them and leaving ~8px empty on the right. The *visible* boxes' true center sat 4px left of where the header centered — read as the header being offset right. Fixed with `justify-content: center` on the shared class — benefits Combi's CONTROL tab identically (same bug, smaller/less-noticed offset there), confirmed via the same measurement on both tabs post-fix (header/visible-boxes center match to within 0.004px, float rounding, on both).

**Verification:** both fixes confirmed via `getBoundingClientRect`/`getComputedStyle`, not by eye, on both Multi's and Combi's CONTROL tabs. `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass (CSS-only changes). Not yet hardware-tested (not applicable — purely visual).

## Critical Discovery #154 — Copy from Combination Modal Rebuilt onto Browser-Overlay Chrome

**Context:** user asked for the "Copy from Combination..." modal (Brief #21 — 22A) to be redesigned to resemble the app's standard Browser modal — full Combination grid instead of a dropdown, Destination/Effects questions below it styled with the theme, Cancel/Copy as theme pills matching every other browser's Cancel/OK.

**Implementation:** `modal-copy-combi` (`.modal-overlay`/`.modal-box`) replaced with `copy-combi-browser-overlay` (`.sound-browser-overlay`/`.browser-overlay-panel`) — same chrome family as Patch/Multisound/Drum/Effect Type/Program/Copy Effects Browsers. Source Combination is now a `buildSoundGridTable` grid (all 100 shown at once, no PROG/COMBI toggle needed — Combinations only), same component every other picker already uses. Destination/Effects rendered as `toggleButtonGroup` pill rows (`.copy-combi-options`, new CSS) instead of hand-rolled radio buttons — reuses the same fused-pill component already used throughout the app (Placement, Mod Shape) rather than a bespoke radio treatment. Footer is the standard Cancel/`ok-btn` pair. Added into the Escape-key dismissal chain, which the old modal was never part of.

**Behavior change, not just visual:** the Source Combination selection is now itself a required, gating input (`copyCombiState.candidateIndex`) — the old `<select>` always defaulted to index 0, so Confirm was previously gated only on Destination/Effects; the browser grid has no default selection, so all three now gate Copy identically.

**Two real gaps found and fixed while verifying, not part of the original ask:**
1. `.browser-overlay-footer` had **no `:disabled` styling at all** — no prior caller (every other picker's OK only ever fires once a selection exists) needed its `ok-btn` to render disabled by default. Copy would have shown fully bright/active despite being unclickable. Added `.browser-overlay-footer button:disabled`/`.ok-btn:disabled:hover` rules, benefiting the whole shared family.
2. The pill toggles' unselected state (`var(--text-secondary)`, dim) is correct everywhere else in the app — dim means "not the current value." Here it's wrong: Destination/Effects are *unanswered required questions*, not alternatives to a current value, and read as muted/skippable (user-reported). Rather than a CSS override fighting `buildFusedToggleGroup`'s inline `btn.style.color`, added a proper opt-in `inactiveColor` config param to `buildFusedToggleGroup`/`toggleButtonGroup` (`controls.js`), default `var(--text-secondary)` unchanged for every existing caller. Copy from Combination is the first caller to pass `inactiveColor: 'var(--text-primary)'`, matching the Combination list's own brightness. Confirmed via direct DOM inspection that Placement's toggle (Effect tab) still renders with the original dim treatment — no regression.

**Verification:** full click-through with real data, not just visual inspection — selected a Combination, both questions, clicked Copy (with `window.confirm` monkey-patched to auto-accept for the automated check), confirmed the destination Tracks' Program/Level/Pan/Sends/Transpose actually updated to match the source Timbres and the modal closed cleanly, no console errors. `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass throughout (no data-layer changes — `performCopyFromCombi`'s own logic, including the Bend Range-from-source-Program resolution and Effects-copy paths from Brief #21, untouched by this session). Not yet hardware-tested (not applicable — the underlying copy operation is workingCopy-to-workingCopy only, no SysEx).

**Corrections from user review, folded in rather than re-litigated:** the fields duplicated across TRACKS and CONTROL (per #152) are Active/Ch/Program/Level, not Key/Vel Window/filters (those stay CONTROL-only, single mount point) — an earlier verbal recommendation misstated this. Separately, Combi's DM/AT/CC filter polarity is already hardware-confirmed clean (Archive #150) — not an open item, contrary to an earlier verbal recommendation that treated it as still-open.

*Last updated: 2026-08-19 — MULTI's TRACKS/CONTROL/EFFECT retrofit built out on new branch `multi-tracks-control-split` (~90% code-reuse from COMBI as expected), Bend Range added, Copy from Combination toolbar mounted on both TRACKS and CONTROL, `#multi-title` CSS fixed. Two real bugs found via `getBoundingClientRect` and fixed (CONTROL grid overflow, new Landmine #99; PC/DM/AT/CC centering, shared with Combi). Copy from Combination modal rebuilt onto the standard browser-overlay chrome, including a new `inactiveColor` opt-in on `toggleButtonGroup` and a first-ever `.browser-overlay-footer` disabled style. All browser-verified only, including a full click-through of the Copy flow with real data. `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass throughout. Pushed to `multi-tracks-control-split` for hardware testing — not yet merged to `main`.*

## Critical Discovery #156 — GLOBAL Tab Phase 3 Retrofit (Brief 9): Piano-Strip Fader, Five Rounds of Alignment Refinement

**Context:** GLOBAL's retrofit (Brief 9, `docs/../Phase 3/X5DR_Editor_Phase3_Brief9_Global_Tab.md`) compressed ADR-0008's stages 1–2 (inventory doc, Claude Design handoff) into direct discussion with the user, same shape as Easy tab's own Brief 8 — justified by GLOBAL's small control count (9 logical fields) and the user's own request to skip straight to a written brief. Two design decisions were made collaboratively before any code was written: Velocity/After Touch Curve as `toggleButtonGroup` pill rows rather than knobs (semantic honesty — 8 named curve *types*, not a continuous magnitude); and User Scale (the 12-note microtuning table) as a **new** component — a vertical, zero-centered, single-handle fader per key, piano-strip-arranged with sharp/flat tinting — rather than 12 stacked numeric rows.

**New component — `verticalFaderCentered` (`controls.js`, Variant I in the Control Component Spec taxonomy):** zero-centered fill (runs from the zero position to the handle, not from the track's bottom), a dashed reference line always marking zero regardless of handle position (same "deviation from center" visual language as `egCurveWidget`'s center-mode zero line, rendered as a filled bar instead of a curve since there's no curve to draw here), and an always-visible stepper readout beneath the track (user-directed — a 12-wide strip needs every value legible at rest, not one-at-a-time on hover, a deliberate departure from `dualHandleRangeSlider`'s own hover-reveal-by-default convention). Modeled structurally on `dualHandleRangeSlider`'s pointer-capture drag pattern but single-handle and vertical. First and only caller today, built as a real library primitive per the same precedent `dualHandleRangeSlider` itself set (single caller at first, second caller — Copy from Combination — added later).

**Real bug found during initial verification: sharp/flat tint couldn't apply via CSS class.** `.global-userscale-key--sharp .ctrl-vfader-track { background: ... }` silently did nothing — the component sets its own inline `style.background` on the track, and an inline style always wins over a class selector's rule regardless of specificity. Fixed by adding an opt-in `trackColor` config param to `verticalFaderCentered` itself (default `var(--track-empty)`), with the caller passing `trackColor: 'var(--bg-page)'` for the 5 sharp keys — the override has to come in through JS config for any component that already sets the same CSS property inline, not through an external stylesheet rule.

**Layout went through five user-directed rounds after the initial build**, each verified via `getBoundingClientRect`/`getComputedStyle` rather than by eye, several catching real bugs mid-fix rather than shipping them:

1. **Single-column-width panels, matching PROG Easy tab's own convention exactly** (`flex:1; min-width:640px` within a `flex-wrap` row, measured at 670px against Easy's own `.easy-osc-fields-panel`/`.vda-panel` — not a bespoke narrower cap, which an earlier pass had improvised at 380px before this round corrected it). Also: Tuning & Response's Velocity/After Touch Curve moved beside the knob pair instead of stacked beneath; Scale reverted from a fully-stacked pass back to Main | Sub side-by-side sub-columns within the single-column width (two requirements — panel *width* vs. internal *arrangement* — had been conflated in an earlier pass). Dropdown chrome (Main/Sub Scale Type/Key) rebuilt to match Combi/Multi's MIDI Channel selector token-for-token, replacing a stale pre-Phase-3 `.ctrl-row select` fallback (hardcoded hex colors, no border-radius token) that Global's selects had been falling through to since the very first pass. `#global-title` given the same font/size/weight as `#multi-title` (was completely unstyled).
   - **Bug caught, not shipped:** `.global-panel + .global-panel { margin-top: 1rem }` was written for vertically-stacked panels, but it's a sibling-selector — it also matched Tuning & Response/Scale once they became flex-row siblings within the same panel row, silently pushing the second one down 1rem and breaking the requested height match. Replaced with a `.global-tab-content` flex-column-plus-`gap` wrapper for the tab's top-level blocks, which can't leak into an unrelated row's own children the way a sibling selector can.
2. **Distribute Tuning row evenly; tighten Scale note spacing; right-align the sync-status pill.** `.global-tuning-row` switched from a fixed 2.5rem gap (which left a large unused gap on the right at full single-column width) to `justify-content: space-between`. The CC#4 note grouped tightly with Sub Scale Key specifically (`.global-scale-key-note`, 0.25rem internal gap) rather than sharing the column's uniform 0.75rem gap with Type→Key. `#global-sync-status` given `margin-left: auto` — Multi's own "Pending…" pill gets right-alignment for free from its `.inner-tabs` `flex:1` spacer sitting between title and status, but Global has no inner tabs to do that job, so the status was landing immediately after the title (left side) instead.
3. **Align Scale's Type row with Tuning & Response's curve pickers; reduce Scale's height to match.** Main/Sub Scale Type sat higher than Velocity Curve's pill row (curve fields have their own label above the pills; Scale's selects don't). Pushed down via `padding-top` on `.global-scale-cols`, funded by trimming the CC#4 note's own padding.
   - **Bug caught, not shipped:** the first attempt used `margin-top` for the push-down, which **collapsed with `.global-panel-label`'s own `margin-bottom`** (adjacent block margins collapse to the larger of the two, not their sum) — silently pushing content down by only ~12px instead of the intended 26px, and (since the panel's total height budget assumed the full 26px) shrinking the panel by 14px, which the user had explicitly asked not to happen. `padding-top` doesn't collapse; switching to it fixed both the alignment and the height in one move.
4. **Match GLOBAL's header height to every other tab; center Key Transpose between Master Tune and the curve controls.** Every other redesigned tab's `.combi-header` is 56.5px (14px padding top/bottom + a 28.5px content row contributed by the inner-tab pills' own line-height/padding) — Global has no inner tabs, so its content row was only the title's 22px line-height, landing the header at 50px and visibly misaligning "GLOBAL" against the other tabs' titles (user's own speculation, confirmed correct by measurement). Tuning & Response restructured from two grouped blocks (Master Tune+Key Transpose, then the curve stack) into three direct flex children under the existing `space-between`, so Key Transpose gets an equal gap on both sides (91.85px each, measured) — this is "centering" in the sense of equal flanking gaps, not necessarily the row's literal midpoint, given the three items' differing widths.
   - **Bug caught, not shipped:** the header-height fix's first attempt set `min-height: 28.5px` (the content-row figure alone) and did nothing — `.combi-header` is `box-sizing: border-box`, under which `min-height` caps the *whole* box including padding, and the header's already-larger natural height (title + padding = 50px) already exceeded 28.5px. Corrected to the full `min-height: 56.5px` (content row + both paddings).
5. **Title text to "GLOBAL SETUP"; align Scale's Key row with After Touch Curve.** `#global-title` renamed to match Multi's own "MULTI SETUP" full-name convention (nav pill stays short, "Global" — same short/full split Multi already established). Main/Sub Scale Key pushed down via `.global-scale-col`'s Type→Key gap (0.75rem/12px → 30px, applying uniformly to both columns' single gap), funded by trimming another 18px off the CC#4 note's padding (19px 0 → 10px 0) — continuing the same realign-without-changing-panel-height pattern as round 3.

**Two generalizable CSS gotchas surfaced this session, promoted to new Landmines (Project Context #100, #101)** — both hit while using small `margin`/`padding` nudges for precise cross-panel alignment, a technique this app increasingly relies on (Landmine #99's `getBoundingClientRect`-driven verification discipline extends to *making* these adjustments correctly, not just catching when they've gone wrong): adjacent block margins collapsing when `margin-top` is used for a push-down that's meant to *add to* an existing `margin-bottom` gap rather than tie with it: and `box-sizing: border-box`'s `min-height` capping the whole box (padding included) rather than just the content area, which silently no-ops if the box's already-existing content+padding total already exceeds the intended minimum.

**Verification, every round:** `npx vitest run` (297/297 throughout — every change in this whole retrofit was rendering-layer only; no `global.*` store path, `setParam` wrapper call, or `sendGlobalDumpAndAwaitAck`/`scheduleGlobalSync` sync mechanism was touched at any point). Browser-verified with real factory data (`.syx` load via the File menu) at 1100/1300/1500/1900px per round, via `getBoundingClientRect`/`getComputedStyle` comparisons, not visual inspection — this is what caught all three "shipped a bug, fixed before commit" instances above; a purely visual pass would very likely have missed at least the margin-collapse case (12px vs. 26px reads as "close enough" at a glance) and the border-box min-height no-op (no visible change to notice was missing). Not yet hardware-tested — Global has no live Parameter Change to spot-check against Snoize the way other tabs do (Landmine #55); verification there will be a write-then-read round-trip through the device instead, per the brief's own §4.

*Last updated: 2026-08-20 — GLOBAL tab retrofit (Brief 9) complete: Tuning & Response, Scale, and User Scale panels rebuilt against the component library, including a new `verticalFaderCentered` primitive (Variant I). Five rounds of user-directed layout refinement followed the initial build, three of which caught a real bug mid-fix (inline-style-vs-CSS-class specificity, margin collapse, border-box `min-height`) before it shipped. Two new Landmines (#100, #101) generalize the margin-collapse and border-box-min-height gotchas for future alignment work — directly relevant to the upcoming DRUMS retrofit. 297/297 tests pass throughout; browser-verified only, not yet hardware-tested.*

## Critical Discovery #157 — GLOBAL Hardware-Verified; Scale Dropdown Descender Clipping Fixed; Merged to `main`

**Context:** User hardware-tested `phase3-global-tab` — "all works great technically" — and flagged one cosmetic issue: in the Scale panel's Main/Sub Scale Type dropdowns, descenders (`q`, `p`, `g`) in labels like "Equal Temp" and "Pelog" were visibly clipped by the `<select>`'s bottom border, per a screenshot. Requirement: fix without changing the control's size or position.

**Two false starts before the real fix, both worth recording as they generalize:**
1. **First attempt** redistributed the existing `0.25rem`/`0.25rem` vertical padding to an asymmetric `0.15rem`/`0.35rem` split (same 0.5rem total, so box height provably unchanged). Technically applied — confirmed live via DevTools Styles panel, not overridden — but the shift was only ~1.6px (root font-size 16px), invisible in an ordinary screenshot. A 6x-scaled DOM-clone test made it look dramatic (1.6px × 6 ≈ 10px), which was misleading about the real, un-scaled effect. **Lesson: verify a sub-pixel-scale visual fix at the actual render scale the user will see, not a magnified proxy — a scaled clone can make a real-but-imperceptible change look sufficient when it isn't.**
2. **Second attempt** pushed the same padding budget to its max asymmetric split (`0` top / `0.5rem` bottom, a ~4px shift) and additionally tried `line-height: 1` to shrink the font's own line box, reasoning the content-box (~14px) was razor-tight against the font's natural ascent+descent (~15px, measured via `canvas.measureText().fontBoundingBoxAscent/Descent`). The padding shift measurably helped (confirmed via the same clone-at-scale technique, now showing a real, larger gap) but `line-height` turned out to be a dead end: **Chrome does not apply `line-height` to `<select>` elements at all** — confirmed by setting it via `el.style.setProperty('line-height', '1', 'important')` directly on the live element and observing `getComputedStyle` still report `normal`. This is a genuine platform limitation, not a specificity/cascade bug — no CSS lever exists for it on this element type.

**Real fix:** discovered the select's 24px box height was already fixed independently of this rule's own padding — by an older, unrelated rule (`.ctrl-row select { height: 1.5rem; box-sizing: border-box; }`, `src/index.html:1275`, still matching since the live element's direct parent carries `.ctrl-row`). Because `height` (not padding-driven auto-sizing) determines the box's final size under `box-sizing: border-box`, the *total* vertical padding could be cut dramatically (`0.25rem`/`0.25rem` → `0.05rem`/`0.05rem`, plain symmetric) without touching box height or position at all — verified via `getBoundingClientRect` before/after (24px both times). This freed far more accessible content-box room than any asymmetric redistribution of the old, larger padding sum ever could, and cleared the descenders decisively (confirmed at 6x clone-scale with a visibly larger gap than either prior attempt, this time for real).

**Generalizable lesson:** when a `<select>`/form-control's height is already pinned by an explicit `height` elsewhere in the cascade, padding is not a zero-sum budget for that element — shrinking total padding (not just redistributing it) is available and doesn't violate a "don't resize/reposition" constraint, because `height` (not the padding-driven box model) is what's actually setting the size. Check for an explicit ancestor-scoped `height` rule before assuming padding sum must stay constant to preserve box size.

**Merge:** `phase3-global-tab` merged into `main` via `git merge --no-ff` (`7952e43`), mirroring COMBI's (`combi-timbres-split`) and MULTI's (`multi-tracks-control-split`) own workflow exactly. `npx vitest run`: 297/297 pass, re-verified post-merge. This closes out GLOBAL — Tuning & Response, Scale, and User Scale are now hardware-verified and merged. Only DRUMS remains pre-Phase-3.

*Last updated: 2026-08-20 — GLOBAL hardware-tested (no functional issues), the Scale dropdown descender-clipping cosmetic fix applied and verified, and the branch merged to `main`. PROG, COMBI, MULTI, and GLOBAL are all now hardware-verified and merged. Next: DRUMS tab Phase 3 retrofit — the last remaining pre-Phase-3 top-level tab.*

## Critical Discovery #158 — DRUMS Tab Phase 3 Retrofit (Brief 10): Full Five-Stage Process, A:B Pan Target Correction, Real Out-of-Range Key Value Confirmed via Direct File Parsing

**Context:** DRUMS — the last remaining pre-Phase-3 top-level tab — went through ADR-0008's full five-stage process (unlike Brief 8/9, which compressed stages 1–2): inventory doc → Claude Design canvas mockup → written brief (Brief 10) → implementation → hardware-testing-round follow-up fixes, all on `phase3-drums-tab`. Structurally unlike every other retrofit — a list-select-detail workflow (dense slot grid → click → detail panel → cross-reference/exclusive-assign column), not a grid of fields or a per-row table — with no direct Phase-3 precedent to copy.

**Stage 1–2 (inventory + Claude Design canvas):** four user-directed decisions incorporated before handoff — Kit 1/Kit 2 moved into the title bar as `.inner-tabs` pills (not a fresh toggle), `#drums-title` styled to match `#multi-title`/`#global-title`, the slot list rebuilt as a dense multi-column grid (dropping the old redundant Slot#/raw-key columns), and a new live-updating Exclusive Assign Groups panel. The published mockup went through two rounds of user correction: (1) row spacing tightened + "Inst No." renamed "Drum Sound" + Key/Drum Sound combined onto one row + Excl. Asgn/Outputs A/B switched to the app's real fused-toggle shape (captured via live computed-style inspection, not guessed); (2) a genuine structural misunderstanding caught and fixed — the mockup had collapsed `#app-shell`'s full-bleed title-bar layer and `#content`'s inset-panel layer into one padded wrapper, making the title bar and content panels the same (both narrower) width, when the real app deliberately makes the title bar bleed to the full un-padded shell width via a `-1.375rem` negative margin while every other panel stays inset within `#content`'s own 22px padding. Confirmed by measuring `#header`/`#nav`/`.combi-header`/`#content` directly in the running app before re-fixing the mockup.

**Stage 3 (brief) → Stage 4 (implementation):** rendering-layer only, every store path/param number/wire encoding unchanged. One real target correction made mid-brief: A:B Pan was initially modeled on the Off/PRG override block (`knobWithOverride`, the shape Combi/Multi's own Pan uses) per the inventory doc's own inference — reading OSC's actual Pan code directly (`src/index.html` ~5040–5121) showed it's a different shape entirely: a plain bidirectional knob paired with an independently-placed "Outputs A/B" two-way toggle, with no PRG state at all (Drums has no Program level to defer to). Implemented to mirror OSC's exact closure-variable state model (`panPosition`/`outputsOn`, reset per-render) rather than the override block. One bug caught before commit via DOM inspection, not visual scan: the "Next →" button was missing its `.drum-nav-btn` class (unstyled, functionally fine, visually broken).

**Post-implementation user review round — five fixes, one of which was a real bug requiring primary-source verification, not just a formatting fix:**

1. **A:B Pan now dims when Outputs A/B is Off** (`updatePanDim`, opacity 0.4 + `pointer-events: none`) — copied verbatim from OSC's own function of the same name; the first implementation pass had wired the toggle's on/off state but never actually dimmed the knob.
2. **`.dirty-scope-banner` retokenized** to `--warning-tint`/`--warning-text` — these tokens have existed, fully defined per-theme (Warm Graphite/Cool Slate/Acid Archive), since the original Phase 3 color-token pass, but had **zero consumers** until now; the banner was hardcoded to Warm-Graphite-specific hex values the whole time, reading as visually broken under the other two themes (user-reported, screenshot showed it under a blue theme). Verified fixed by switching themes live and re-triggering the banner.
3. **Central detail panel auto-selects the first slot** (enabled slots by key, same order the grid itself uses) on tab open and on kit switch, instead of opening to an empty "Select a slot to edit" state every time.
4. **Detail header font switched from mono to the regular UI font** (`var(--font-ui)`), matching the "Used By" panel's own body text — color/size unchanged, user-directed.
5. **The Key dropdown showing "C0" while the slot grid showed "C-1" for the same slot was a real bug, not a data-corruption question** — user explicitly flagged it as a possible coding issue and offered to consult the manual. Manual check first (`04_combi_multi_global_drums.md` TABLE 6, line 175): documented valid Key range is `0C~73` (C0–G8), matching the dropdown's existing 12–115 loop bound exactly — so the loop bound itself wasn't wrong per the manual. The real discrepancy: **Kit 1's first slot ("Metal Kick") genuinely carries a raw key byte of `0` (C-1) in the actual factory soundbank**, confirmed by parsing `reference_sysex/X5dr Factory Sounds.syx` directly with the project's own `parser.js` in a throwaway Node script (not assumed, not eyeballed) — `parseDrums` decodes it correctly as `key: 0`; Kit 2's equivalent slot parses cleanly with an in-range value. This is a genuine out-of-manual-range value shipped in the real factory data (Korg-side quirk, not a transcription or parsing error), and the actual bug was in the DRUMS retrofit's own dropdown: populating its option list strictly from the documented 12–115 range meant a stored value outside it had no matching `<option>`, so the `<select>` silently fell back to displaying its first option ("C0") while the real value stayed correct underneath in the store/wire — a display-only lie, easy to mistake for the data itself being wrong. Fixed by always including the current value as its own option when it falls outside the normal range, while keeping newly-*selectable* options clamped to the manual's documented 12–115 — promoted to Landmine #102 (Project Context) as a generalizable pattern.

**Verification, both rounds:** `npx vitest run` — 297/297 throughout (rendering-layer only, no communication-layer file touched). ## Critical Discovery #159 — MIDI Port Selection Reviewed for Ungrouped-Port Systems: Kept As-Is, No Input Selector Added

**Context:** Exploratory discussion (no code touched), prompted by a question about how the editor should behave on systems where MIDI inputs and outputs are exposed as separate, ungrouped ports (e.g. Windows `loopMIDI`, some class-compliant interfaces) rather than name-paired by device the way they happened to be on the original hardware-test rig (Archive §2, above — both directions reported as `Korg X5DR <interface>`).

**What the current code actually does**, confirmed by reading `src/index.html` directly rather than from memory:
- **Output**: `#port-select` (`populatePortSelect`, `~index.html:15477`) is populated only from `midiAccess.outputs`, auto-selecting the first port whose name includes `"X5DR"`. This is the only device-selection UI in the app.
- **Input**: there is no input selector at all. `onPortSelected` (`~index.html:15504`) attaches `onmidimessage = onMidiMessage` to **every** enumerated `midiAccess.inputs` port unconditionally — not just the one matching the chosen output.
- **Why this has worked so far**: `handleSysexMessage` validates message *content* (Korg ID `42` + channel byte `3g` + family code `36` in the SysEx header, checked by `isAck`/`isNak`/etc.) rather than *source port*. On a typical rig — one X5DR connected, sysex enabled — "listen to every input" behaves identically to "listen to the X5DR's input" as a side effect of there being nothing else to hear from, not because the code enforces it.

**Risk analysis for the *ungrouped*-port case specifically (no code change resulted):**
1. **Cross-talk / false-positive ACK-NAK matching** — only possible if a *second* Korg X5D-family device is connected and transmitting SysEx on the *same* MIDI channel at the same time. Judged remote: the X5D/X5DR is an entry-level/legacy instrument, unlikely to be paired with a same-family sibling in a typical user's rig; and if it did happen, two devices answering to the same channel is itself a bigger, unrelated problem the user would need to resolve regardless of this app.
2. **User has no visibility into which input port is actually live** — true, but this is a diagnostics/UX gap, not a correctness risk, since content-level filtering already protects against wrong data being accepted. Judged low-value to fix given the device's typical setup: users of a device this old generally have few MIDI ports in play and can trace physical/virtual cabling by hand if something seems wrong.

**Decision:** leave the single-output-dropdown-plus-listen-to-all-inputs behavior as-is. If this is ever revisited, the fix would be a second `<select>` populated from `midiAccess.inputs` (mirroring `populatePortSelect`'s name-match auto-select), with `onPortSelected` wiring `onmidimessage` only to the chosen input instead of `midiAccess.inputs.forEach(...)` — a UI/wiring change only, since `handleSysexMessage`'s content-based validation already does the real correctness work and wouldn't need to change.

**Note for future user documentation:** worth a line explaining that the port dropdown selects *output* only, and that the editor listens to all connected MIDI inputs — relevant for a user setting up a system (e.g. Windows loopMIDI) where input/output ports aren't paired by device name the way they typically are in macOS Audio MIDI Setup.

*Last updated: 2026-09-01 — MIDI port selection (single output dropdown, unfiltered input listening) reviewed against the ungrouped-input/output-port scenario and deliberately kept as-is; no code changed. Recorded so a future session doesn't re-open the same question, and as a note for eventual user-facing setup documentation.*

## Critical Discovery #161 — Hardware-Test Mac's Chrome Stopped Delivering SysEx Input After macOS/Chrome Update: Isolated to a Browser-Side Regression, Not an Editor Bug

**Context:** Immediately after DRUMS' merge (Archive #160), the user rebooted the hardware-test Mac, which also updated macOS and Chrome. The editor then appeared to stop communicating with the X5DR entirely — a full-dump read left the UI empty, and a Factory Sounds write left "Writing All Data To Device…" stuck indefinitely.

**First data point — Snoize log of the dump request/response**, shared by the user: the outgoing Dump Request (`F0 42 30 36 0F 00 F7`) and a Func=`33` request both showed an odd three-line pattern per send (`SysEx 1 bytes F0`, then the full correct message, then `Invalid 1 bytes`) — but the **device fully responded**: a complete 35,318-byte All Data dump and a complete 244-byte Multi Expansion dump, both well-formed, arrived from the X5DR per Snoize. This ruled out cabling/port/channel/device-side problems outright — the wire-level exchange demonstrably worked.

**Diagnosis, via a throwaway console script** (not a code change — a temporary diagnostic run directly in Chrome DevTools against a fresh `requestMIDIAccess({sysex:true})`, mirroring the editor's own `onPortSelected` pattern of attaching `onmidimessage` to every enumerated input):
- `sysexEnabled: true` — the API-level permission grant is fine.
- 6 inputs enumerated (4× MIDI-keyboard ports, `<interface> Port A`, and one literally named "Korg X5DR" — note: not `Korg X5DR <interface>`, a naming discrepancy from Project Context's original port-name reference, itself possibly a side effect of the same update, not investigated further this session), all reporting `state: connected`.
- Triggering the dump: **Active Sensing (`fe`) bytes arrived continuously and correctly** on the "Korg X5DR" input — confirming that input is genuinely, physically live and that Chrome's Web MIDI *can* deliver at least some data to the page.
- **The actual SysEx dump response never arrived at the page at all** — zero `MIDI IN` log lines beyond the `fe` bytes, despite Snoize independently confirming the same data left the device on the wire at the same time.

**Conclusion:** this isolates cleanly to **Chrome delivering ordinary/realtime MIDI bytes to the page normally, while silently failing to deliver System Exclusive input specifically** — regardless of message size (the stuck "Writing All Data" spinner was waiting on a *small* Write Completed acknowledgment, not a large dump, and that never arrived either, so this isn't a large-message-only failure). `sysexEnabled` reporting `true` does not guarantee SysEx bytes actually reach `onmidimessage` — a real, apparently new gap between the permission flag and actual delivery. **Not a bug in this project's own code**: the editor's `onMidiMessage`/`handleSysexMessage` pipeline is architecturally sound and unchanged, and was confirmed working for whatever Chrome actually hands it (Active Sensing correctly filtered, per Landmine #6). Nothing here implicates `src/index.html`'s MIDI-handling code, and no code was changed this session as a result.

**Recommended next steps (not yet attempted — this session ended at diagnosis, not resolution):**
1. Note the exact Chrome version (`chrome://version`) for comparison/bug-report purposes.
2. Check for a persisted MIDI-related site permission (padlock icon → Site settings) separate from the JS-level prompt; reset and re-grant.
3. Test in a fresh Chrome profile/Guest mode — rules out a corrupted per-profile permission cache surviving the update.
4. **Test the same page in Microsoft Edge** (also permitted per CLAUDE.md's Chrome/Edge-only platform decision) — if SysEx input works there, this is conclusively Chrome-specific, and Edge becomes a working fallback on this machine while Chrome's own regression is tracked separately.

*Last updated: 2026-09-01 — Diagnosed (not yet resolved) a post-update Chrome regression on the hardware-test Mac: SysEx input delivery to the page appears broken while realtime/non-SysEx input (Active Sensing) still arrives normally, and `sysexEnabled: true` does not guarantee otherwise. Confirmed via a console diagnostic, not a code change — the editor's own MIDI-handling code is not implicated. Next session should pick up at the four untried remediation steps above before assuming any code-level fix is needed.*

## Critical Discovery #162 — Root Cause Confirmed: Chromium 152 Regression in MIDI-1.0-to-UMP/SysEx7 Conversion, Already Fixed in Chromium, Landing in Chrome 153

**Context:** Follow-up to Archive #161 the same evening. User tried Microsoft Edge (per that entry's remediation step 4) and hit the identical failure — which, since Edge and Chrome share the same underlying Chromium Web MIDI implementation, doesn't contradict the "Chrome-side regression" theory so much as sharpen it: this is a **Chromium-engine** bug, not a Chrome-brand-specific one, so switching between Chromium-based browsers was never going to route around it.

**Root cause found via web search**, not guessed: another company (Morningstar Engineering, makers of MIDI foot-controller hardware with their own browser-based device editor) posted a public incident notice two days prior (`forum.morningstar.io/t/important-notice-on-editor-connection-issues-after-chrome-update/12907`) describing the exact same symptom, independently diagnosed and confirmed by Chromium's own engineers:

- **Chrome 152 on macOS** (and, per a reply in the same thread, Windows too — this is not macOS-specific) shipped a regression in Chromium's internal **MIDI 1.0-to-UMP/SysEx7 conversion** layer — new internal plumbing Chromium added under the hood even for pages still using the classic Web MIDI API, unrelated to any page-visible API change.
- The bug **incorrectly frames SysEx messages**, producing spurious extra `F0`/`F7` bytes around the real message — this is a precise match for the stray `SysEx 1 bytes F0` / `Invalid 1 bytes` artifacts this session's own Snoize log showed around the outgoing Dump Request (Archive #161's first data point) — independent confirmation that this session's own symptom is the same bug, not a coincidentally-similar one.
- **Already fixed upstream in Chromium**, merged after the Chrome 152 branch point (too late to make that release) — the fix ships in **Chrome 153**, which began an Early Stable rollout within the last few days of this session (per the same forum thread's follow-up post).
- **No application-level workaround exists for a Web-MIDI-only app.** Morningstar's own mitigation was falling back to their Editor's Serial/Bluetooth connection modes, which this project's architecture doesn't have (Web MIDI only, by original platform decision) and has no reason to add for one transient upstream browser bug.

**Resolution:** update to Chrome 153 once available (`chrome://settings/help` triggers an update check) — no code change on this project's side, and none is warranted; the editor's own MIDI-handling code was never implicated at any point in this diagnosis (Archive #161's conclusion stands, now with a confirmed external root cause rather than an inferred one). If hardware testing needs to resume before Chrome Stable rolls 153 out to this machine, Chrome Beta already carries it.

*Last updated: 2026-09-01 — Root cause of the Archive #161 SysEx regression confirmed via public reports: a Chromium 152 bug in MIDI-1.0-to-UMP/SysEx7 framing, already fixed upstream and shipping in Chrome 153 (Early Stable as of this session). No project code change needed or made — purely a matter of the hardware-test Mac's Chrome updating past 152. Resume hardware testing once Chrome 153 (or later) is installed.*

## Critical Discovery #163 — Chrome App-Window Title Bar Color + Cross-Tab Phase 3 UI Polish Pass

**Context:** A run of small, user-directed fixes across a single session — most independent of each other, grouped here rather than given one entry each.

**UI polish, all browser-verified, all Prog/Combi/Multi/Global/Drums as noted:**
- Program Browser toggle (Timbre/Track Program No. picker): "BANK A" → "PROGRAM", "BANK G" unchanged.
- Main Browser modal toggle: "PROG"/"COMBI" → "PROGRAM"/"COMBINATION".
- Effect tab (Prog/Combi/Multi, shared `buildEffectColumn`): Mod Intensity knob's visible ring-bottom didn't align with Mod Source's box edge even though the two elements' outer flex boxes were correctly bottom-aligned (`align-items: flex-end`) — the ring's own value-arc sweep stops short of the bottom pole by design (same geometry `buildKnobContainer`'s `'below'` mode already documents), so bottom-aligning the *boxes* still left the *visible ring* sitting above the target. First attempt (`margin-top` on the knob) had no effect at all — under `align-items: flex-end`, an item's margin-box **bottom** edge is the alignment reference, so top margin only grows the box upward and never moves the bottom. Fixed with `position: relative; top: 0.5rem` instead (the knob's own inline style already sets `position: relative` for drag handling, so `top` just works). This first value was derived from this session's own `getBoundingClientRect` math in the Claude Browser preview pane and looked pixel-perfect there — but overshot visibly on the user's real Chrome/macOS, requiring a second round reduced to `0.25rem`, confirmed correct by the user. **Likely cause: this preview pane's native `<select>` doesn't render at exactly the same height as real Chrome's**, even from identical CSS — a real cross-environment discrepancy, not a math error; the pane's numbers should not be trusted alone for this class of alignment fix in the future. Separately, the Mod Source `<select>` was switched from `var(--text-primary)` to `var(--value-color)`, so it follows the Theme menu's value-color toggle like every other parameter value does — verified switching both directions.
- Prog > Easy > Expression panel: "MW Vibrato (OSC 1/2)" → "OSC 1/2 Vibrato (MW)", matching the panel's own controller-in-parentheses convention used by every other knob there (`(AT)`, `(PB)`).
- Prog > VDA > KBD/VEL panels: `.vda-subpanel-toggles-title`'s `margin-bottom` (0.1rem) brought in line with VDF's own `.vdf-subpanel-toggles-title` (0.5rem) — confirmed via `getBoundingClientRect` that both panels now measure an identical 8px gap.
- Global > User Scale: `verticalFaderCentered`'s readout looked centered under its slider only when the hover-revealed stepper arrows happened to be visible. Root cause: the stepper's reserved width is always laid out (`visibility: hidden`, not `display: none` — Landmine #73's own fix for a *different*, `display:none`-caused bug, correctly still in place here) so the wrap containing number+stepper is wider than just the number, and the *outer* fader's `align-items: center` centers that whole wrap — leaving the visible number off-center by half the reserved stepper's width+gap. This is the exact same shape `buildKnobContainer`'s `'below'` mode already solved once (`marginLeft: 14px`, doubled because `align-items: center` only ever translates half of an asymmetric margin) — reused verbatim rather than re-derived. Verified via `getBoundingClientRect`: readout center now matches the track's center exactly.
- Drums/Multi/Global panel titles (`#drums-title`/`#multi-title`/`#global-title`): switched `font-family` from `var(--font-mono)` to `var(--font-ui)` — user's stated intent is that monospace should read as "this text is itself editable" (matching Prog/Combi's own renamable patch-name titles), and these three titles never were. Then reworded for cross-tab consistency: "DRUMS"/"MULTI SETUP"/"GLOBAL SETUP" → "DRUM EDIT"/"MULTI EDIT"/"GLOBAL EDIT" (one shared word, "Edit", chosen from a short brainstormed list — "Editor" and "Config" were the other finalists; "Edit" won for echoing the device's own real front-panel mode names, Prog **Edit**/Combi **Edit**, even though Drums/Global don't have an identical device-side mode name). The **Drums nav-tab pill above the panel stays "Drums"**, deliberately unchanged — only the in-panel title text uses "Drum" (singular, matching "Multi"/"Global"). Row heights measured identical across all three (20.5px) before/after.

**Chrome app-window title bar color (new feature):** the user noticed their OS window title bar (macOS, in this case) doesn't match the app's own dark theme when Chrome renders it as a chrome-less "app window" (Page menu → *Open as window*, or an installed PWA — not a normal tabbed browser window, which owns its own chrome and ignores page content entirely for this purpose). Implemented via `<meta name="theme-color" id="theme-color-meta">`, updated inside the existing `applyTheme()` function by reading `--bg-panel` back from `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)` — deliberately *not* a hardcoded per-theme hex table, so it can't drift out of sync if the `[data-theme="…"]` palettes are retuned later. Confirmed live-updating on the user's real Chrome/macOS when switching the in-app Theme menu, with the window already open (not just at next launch). Alongside it, `src/manifest.json` + `<link rel="manifest">` were added, enabling Chrome's "Install X5DR Editor" address-bar affordance on an eligible `http(s)` origin — deliberately shipped with **no `icons` field yet** (Chrome won't offer to install without at least one; needs real artwork, not a placeholder — tracked in the owner's task list, PHASE 4 — Distribution & Release, alongside a "keep external vs. inline as a `data:` URI" decision for Phase 4's eventual single-file build).

*Last updated: 2026-09-02 — Both the UI polish pass and the title bar color feature merged to `main` (`29e2c24`, `--no-ff` from `feature/titlebar-theme-color`). 297/297 tests pass throughout (no wire-format/logic changes, UI-only). Browser-verified in the Claude Browser preview pane for every item; the title bar color specifically also confirmed on the user's real Chrome/macOS, including the live-update-without-reopening behavior.*

## Critical Discovery #164 — `file://` Likely Works for Web MIDI (Including SysEx) in Chrome, Contradicting an Unverified ADR-0002 Claim

**Context:** Discussing Phase 4 distribution options, the user recalled seeing another developer's browser-based editor for a different Roland synth (a single downloaded `.html` file) apparently working when opened directly via `file:///...` in Chrome — screenshotting a native "This file wants to: Control and reprogram your MIDI devices — Block/Allow" permission dialog as evidence. This directly contradicts ADR-0002 §6a and the Project Plan's Phase 4 section, both of which flatly state `file://` "will not work" for Web MIDI and require `https://`/`http://localhost`.

**Investigation:** This session's own tooling could not directly test `file://` behavior — the Claude Browser preview pane deliberately sandboxes local file access, loading `file://` navigations as inert `data:` URI snapshots (opaque origin, `isSecureContext: false`) rather than genuine `file://` navigations, so a first attempt at an isolated test page came back invalid/inconclusive by construction, not by finding an actual negative result.

The user's reference file (`S1 Editor/S1_MIDI_EDITOR.html`, 83,401 bytes, gitignored — reference material only, not project source) was inspected directly once moved somewhere this session could read it (macOS blocks Claude Code's default access to `~/Downloads`). Findings:
- **Structure confirms the theory needed for Phase 4 regardless of the MIDI question**: one `<!DOCTYPE html>` file, one classic `<script>` block (no `type="module"`, no `import`/`export`, no external `<link>`/CDN references of any kind) — fully self-contained, exactly the shape ES-module-based `file://` pages can't be (Chrome blocks cross-origin module fetches under `file://` outright, independent of the secure-context question).
- **Correction to an assumption stated earlier in this same conversation**: the permission dialog wording ("Control and reprogram your MIDI devices") was initially assumed to be SysEx-specific. It is not — this file calls `navigator.requestMIDIAccess()` with **no** `{sysex: true}` option at all (confirmed: zero case-insensitive matches for "sysex" anywhere in the file; it only sends/receives Control Change messages, `0xB0`-based, never a SysEx `F0...F7` message). That dialog is Chrome's **generic** MIDI-access permission prompt, not evidence of SysEx access specifically.
- **What the evidence does still support**: the `requestMIDIAccess()` promise visibly *resolved* (the user's second screenshot shows `scanPorts()` ran, populating "No MIDI hardware targets detected"), meaning `file://` passed Chrome's secure-context gate. Per the Web MIDI spec, that gate is a single check for the whole API, not applied separately per the `sysex` option — sysex is a *permission*, layered on top of an already-secure context, not a stricter context requirement of its own. There is no known mechanism by which passing the gate for plain access would fail for `sysex: true` specifically.

**Conclusion (not yet proven, but well-supported):** ADR-0002 §6a's claim was never hardware-verified in the first place — this session did not find it wrong so much as find that it was always speculative. `file://` likely works for this project's own SysEx traffic too, once Phase 4 removes the ES-module `import`s that independently block `file://` today for an unrelated reason.

**Not fixed/resolved this session** — deliberately deferred: testing requires the actual single-file Phase 4 build (or at minimum a from-scratch, no-import, `sysex:true`-requesting test page run in the user's own real Chrome, not this session's sandboxed preview pane). Tracked in the owner's task list (PHASE 4 — Distribution & Release: "Verify `file://` works for the single-file `dist/index.html` … Web MIDI + SysEx, not just plain MIDI") and flagged as Landmine #103 in Project Context so ADR-0002 §6a isn't restated as settled fact in the meantime.

*Last updated: 2026-09-02 — Investigated via a real reference file the user provided, not assumed or guessed; conclusion is well-supported but explicitly unconfirmed pending a direct test once Phase 4's single-file build exists. No code changed this session as a result — documentation/Landmine update only.*

## Critical Discovery #165 — DRUMS FILE/Device Menu Wiring (Load/Save/Import) Implemented; "Write to Device" Confirmed Correctly Absent

**Context:** The FILE and Device (DEVICE) header menus have had disabled "Drums" stub buttons since early in Phase 2 — Load, Save, Import from device, and Write to device all sat greyed-out, never implemented. The user noticed these and asked to confirm whether the disabled "Write to device → Drums" entry should be removed entirely (reasoning: Drums has no Edit Buffer, so there's nothing to "write" as a separate step) and to wire up the other three.

**Confirmed:** yes — Landmine #58 already establishes that both a live Drum Kit Parameter Change (Func=53) and a full Drums Data Dump (Func=52) write directly to the device's Internal Memory, with no Edit Buffer and no Write Request function code in between. This is architecturally identical to Multi and Global, neither of which has ever had a "Write to device" menu entry either — Import/Load/Save are each scope's *complete* device-facing surface. The disabled `write-drums` button was removed entirely (not just left disabled), matching that established precedent exactly, with an inline comment at the removal site explaining why no replacement entry belongs there.

**Implemented, mirroring the existing Global/Multi flows field-for-field:**
- `src/midi/sysex.js`: new `encodeDrumsToBytes`/`buildDrumsDump` — a standalone Func=52 message builder (header, `0x00` pad byte per `02_sysex_format.md` §20's own byte table — not assumed by analogy to Func=51, checked directly — 7-bit packing, `F7`). Deliberately duplicated from `encoder.js`'s existing local (unexported) `encodeDrumsToBytes`, which has a `kits == null` fallback specific to its own "All Data" assembly context that this new standalone version doesn't need (same reasoning `encodeGlobalToBytes`'s two versions already split on).
- `src/state/store.js`: new `store.replaceDrums(kits)` — always a full replace (both kits arrive together in one Func=52 dump), unlike `replaceMulti`'s per-key merge (which exists because Multi's two halves, Func=55/68, can arrive independently).
- `doRequestDrumsDumpFlow` (Import from device): sends Func=0D (Drums Data Dump Request, `00` pad byte, confirmed from the manual's own table) — a read-only query, no Mode Change needed first, same as every sibling Import flow. The Func=52 response merges via a new `isDrumsDump` branch in `scheduleDumpSettle`, via `store.replaceDrums` — never `store.loadSnapshot()` (Landmine #42/#56's scoped-merge rule).
- `doLoadDrumsFlow` (File → Load → Drums): parses a `.syx`, requires it actually contains Func=52 data, merges via `store.replaceDrums`, then auto-pushes to the device via a new `sendDrumsDumpAndAwaitAck` — which sends Mode Change `0x05` (Global mode) first, defensively, with the same 100ms settling delay `sendGlobalDumpAndAwaitAck` uses. **This Mode Change is not confirmed required by the manual for Func=52 specifically** — `02_sysex_format.md` §20's wording ("Receives this message & data, save to Internal Memory…") is silent on any prerequisite mode, identical to §19's wording for Global's own Func=51, which the existing `sendGlobalDumpAndAwaitAck` already sends a Mode Change ahead of anyway. Given drum kit *parameters* (Func=53) are hardware-confirmed to require Global mode (Landmine #19), sending it defensively for the full-dump write too was judged the safer default, matching Global's own established practice over trusting the manual's silence.
- `doSaveDrumsFlow` (File → Save → Drums): writes the current working copy as a Func=52 `.syx`, no destination picker (Drums is a fixed 2-kit singleton, same as Global/Multi have no picker for their own single-instance Save).
- `editMode` is set to `'drumsTab'`, not `'globalTab'`, inside `sendDrumsDumpAndAwaitAck` — same underlying device mode (`MODE_GLOBAL`) but a distinct UI-context value, per Landmine #60's existing rule (don't conflate GLOBAL's and DRUMS' own claims on the shared device mode).

**Tests:** `sysex.test.js` gained a round-trip suite for `encodeDrumsToBytes`/`buildDrumsDump`/`parseDrums` (an arbitrary in-range 2-kit fixture, a disabled-note-with-stale-`instNo` edge case confirming the byte-level `enabled ? instNo+1 : 0` encoding truly has no wire representation for a disabled note's `instNo`, and a full-wire-format round trip through `buildDrumsDump` → `unpack7bit` → `parseDrums`), plus `store.test.js` coverage for `replaceDrums` (basic replace, deep-clone-not-reference, throws-if-no-snapshot — mirroring the existing `replaceMulti` test shape).

**Not verified this session:** no real MIDI hardware is reachable from this session's tooling, and native file pickers (`showOpenFilePicker`/`showSaveFilePicker`) aren't scriptable here — so the Import flow was confirmed to correctly reach its `no-output` guard via a real click, and the underlying dump builder is unit-tested, but the actual device round-trip (ACK/NAK handling, a real file Save→Load cycle) is untested beyond code review. Also currently blocked on the Chrome 152 SysEx regression (Archive #161–#162) regardless. Tracked in the owner's task list as a reminder to hardware-test once Chrome 153 is installed on the hardware-test Mac.
