## Critical Discovery #166 — Native `window.confirm()`/`window.alert()` Replaced with a Themed Modal, App-Wide

**Context:** The user flagged that native browser dialogs (screenshot: `127.0.0.1:5500 says…`) were visually jarring against the app's own dark-panel design and confusing for a non-technical user, especially the most consequence-bearing one in the app (the post-Load "Write ALL DATA to the X5DR now?" prompt). Asked for an inventory of every such dialog, then a mockup, then implementation.

**Inventory (enumerated by grep, not assumption):** 7 `window.confirm()` call sites (Copy Effects, Copy from Combination's own confirm, both Load-flow write prompts, Write All Programs/Combinations/Data from the Device menu) and 2 `window.alert()`s (an informational "No Combinations Loaded" guard, and the NAK-recovery dialog). Two other native-dialog-shaped things were correctly identified as *not* replaceable: `showOpenFilePicker`/`showSaveFilePicker` (OS file chrome) and `navigator.requestMIDIAccess`'s one-time SysEx permission prompt — both are security-relevant browser/OS chrome, and a themed look-alike would be a phishing-adjacent anti-pattern.

**Design, established via mockup review before any code changed:** built entirely from CSS the app already shipped — the Abandoned Edits modal's `.modal-overlay`/`.modal-box` chrome, and the Cancel/`.ok-btn` button row already used on the Copy from Combination picker. Two new CSS rules only: icon+title alignment, and `.modal-warning-banner` (reuses `--warning-tint`/`--warning-text`, the same tokens `.dirty-scope-banner` already used elsewhere) for the "cannot be undone" line, applied to every confirm-before-write dialog. Buttons are action-labeled ("Write to Device"/"Not Now", "Copy Effects", etc.), not generic OK/Cancel.

**Implementation:** one shared `showConfirmModal({title, body, warning, okLabel, cancelLabel}) → Promise<boolean>` and `showAlertModal({title, body})` (single-button wrapper), `index.html`, backing a single `#modal-confirm` DOM instance reused across all 9 call sites. Keyboard parity with the dialogs it replaces: Tab/Shift+Tab cycle only between the dialog's own button(s) (a focus trap, since only 2 elements are focusable while open), Escape resolves as Cancel, Enter activates the focused button (implemented explicitly via a keydown handler rather than relied on via native button-activation, after the test harness's synthetic Enter key turned out not to trigger it — real keyboard input works either way, but explicit removed the doubt), and the affirmative button is focused on open, matching `window.confirm()`'s own default-to-OK (user-directed: keep muscle memory consistent across all dialogs rather than defaulting the destructive ones to Cancel).

**Follow-up fix — focus ring vs. fill ambiguity:** Tab-ing between the two buttons showed the browser's own system-colored focus ring *layered on top of* a static `.ok-btn` fill that never moved (user-reported: a ring around Cancel while "Write to Device" kept its unrelated fill color read as ambiguous). Fixed by moving the `.ok-btn` fill class to whichever button currently has focus (`setFilled()`, called on open and after every Tab/Shift+Tab) and suppressing the native outline on just these two buttons (`#modal-confirm-ok:focus, #modal-confirm-cancel:focus { outline: none; }`) — the fill swap alone is now the only visual signal, satisfying the same "one signal, not two" principle later reapplied to the browser-overlay pickers (Archive #167).

**NAK-recovery `alert()` conversion — deliberately deferred to its own pass, then done:** unlike the other 8, this dialog blocks the resend logic that follows it (native `alert()` is synchronous). Converting `handleSysexMessage` to `async` and `await`-ing `showAlertModal()` in the NAK branch preserved that same ordering (Mode Change + Landmine #18's 100ms settling delay + resend only run after the dialog closes) via an awaited promise instead of a blocking call. Hardware-tested successful.

**Stale-value resend bug, hardware-reported and fixed:** after acknowledging the NAK-recovery dialog, the device was correctly returned to edit mode, but the *value* resent didn't match what was currently shown in the editor if the user kept adjusting the same control while the dialog was open. Root cause: the handler snapshotted `pendingParam` into a `failedParam` variable at the moment the NAK arrived, then resent that frozen snapshot after the (now non-blocking) dialog closed — safe under the old blocking `alert()` (no further interaction was possible while it was up) but not under the new async one. Critically, `.modal-overlay` appearing on top does **not** stop an already-in-progress knob drag: pointer capture (set on `pointerdown`) keeps routing `pointermove` events to the original knob regardless of what's now visually on top, and each tick's `sendParamChange()` call unconditionally overwrites the shared `pendingParam` — so by the time the dialog closed, `pendingParam` already reflected the latest dragged value, but the handler was resending the earlier frozen one. Fixed by reading `pendingParam` fresh (as `resendParam`) immediately *after* `showAlertModal()` resolves, not before the `await` — always reflects whatever was most recently attempted, matching the Core Design Axiom (editor should track device state as closely as possible). Hardware-verified fixed.

**Tests:** `npx vitest run`: 304/304 pass throughout (no communication-layer module changed — all of this lives in `index.html`, untested by the Vitest suite per this project's own testing convention of not covering UI). Browser-verified extensively (all 3 themes, keyboard behavior via DOM/focus inspection) and hardware-verified for the confirm-dialog flow, the NAK-recovery dialog itself, and the stale-value fix.

## Critical Discovery #167 — Browser-Overlay Picker Tab Focus Trap + Theme-Colored Ring; Self-Introduced z-index Regression Found and Fixed

**Context:** Follow-up request after Archive #166: the user noticed Tab cycled through every focusable element on the whole page while a Browser overlay (Patch/Write/Multisound/Drum Sound/Effect Type/Program/Copy Effects/Copy from Combination) was open, not just that overlay's own elements, and asked whether the focus ring on Tab-reachable buttons inside them could be theme-colored instead of the browser's system color.

**Focus trap:** a single generic `keydown` listener (not a per-overlay-ID list, unlike the existing Escape-dismissal handler) finds whichever overlay is currently topmost/visible among `.modal-overlay.visible, .browser-overlay.visible, .sound-browser-overlay.visible` (by z-index, matching the app's existing tiering — Landmine #28/#29) and constrains Tab/Shift+Tab to cycling through its own focusable elements, wrapping at both ends. Covers every current and future overlay on this chrome automatically, plus the Abandoned Edits modal as a free side effect (it had no Tab-handling at all before). `#modal-confirm` is the one exception — it already had its own local Tab handling (Archive #166, since it also moves the `.ok-btn` fill along with focus) — that handler now calls `stopPropagation()` on Tab so the two mechanisms never double-handle the same keypress.

**Theme-colored ring:** a `:focus-visible` rule (keyboard-navigation only, not mouse clicks) recolors the ring to `var(--accent-line)` for every button these pickers can Tab to (type-toggle, category rows, every overlay's Cancel/OK footer, Abandoned Edits' buttons). `.patch-table` itself deliberately excluded — its own `.selected` cell fill is already the theme-colored "current position" indicator, so a ring around the whole table would be redundant.

**Follow-up finding, user-flagged and initially misdiagnosed as ambiguous, then correctly explained:** tabbing through the Patch Browser showed 5 focusable stops (PROGRAM/COMBINATION toggle, the grid, Cancel, OK) but only 3 were visually discernible. Verified via `getComputedStyle` that both toggle buttons *do* get the ring correctly — the issue is that whichever toggle is currently `.active` (persistently filled with `--accent-fill`) gets a ring in the *same* color as its own fill, making the extra 2px outline hard to distinguish from the button's existing bright state. **User confirmed this reads fine as-is** ("there is a gap between the pill and its ring") — no fix applied, correctly left alone rather than assumed broken.

**Real regression, found via user hardware/browser testing, not caught by this session's own screenshot-based verification:** on a short window, `.browser-overlay`'s (Patch/Write Browser) `align-items: center` clipped an overflowing panel symmetrically with no scroll mechanism to reach the clipped-off top (the PROGRAM/COMBINATION toggle row) — the classic "centered flexbox overflow" trap. First fix attempt copied `.sound-browser-overlay`'s already-shipped remedy verbatim (`align-items: flex-start; overflow: auto; padding-top: 6vh`) — this **made it worse**: the user reported the toggle row now never showed, even maximized and zoomed out. Root cause, found via `document.elementFromPoint()` (not `getBoundingClientRect()`, which had been showing seemingly-correct layout geometry the whole time and masked the real bug): `.browser-overlay` is deliberately `z-index: 100`, **below** `#header` (150) and `#nav` (120) — the Patch Browser was built not to dim/block the nav row, unlike `.sound-browser-overlay` (`z-index: 150`, same tier as header/nav, by design — see that class's own pre-existing comment). That was harmless under the old `align-items: center` (which usually placed the panel well clear of header+nav's ~113px combined footprint) but the flat `6vh` padding *always* started the panel around y=60–90px — squarely inside that footprint on every viewport size, so header/nav permanently painted over the toggle row regardless of window size. Fixed with `padding-top: max(6vh, 132px)` — 132px safely clears the measured ~113px footprint with headroom for `--control-scale`/font variation, and still grows via `6vh` once a viewport is tall enough that alone would clear it. `.sound-browser-overlay`/`.modal-overlay` were never at risk of this same collision (both sit at z-index ≥150). User-verified fixed on both the original short-window case and the maximized-window regression it caused.

**Verification technique used throughout, worth reusing:** `elementFromPoint()`/real hit-testing, not `getBoundingClientRect()` alone — the regression's entire failure mode was invisible to rect-based measurement (correct-looking layout coordinates, with something else painted on top), and this session's screenshot tool also had its own unresolved rendering quirk that made pixel-comparison screenshots unreliable for this specific vertical-overflow scenario throughout — causal DOM tests (revert old CSS on a forced-overflow panel, confirm the element sits at a negative/unreachable offset; apply new CSS, confirm positive/reachable; scroll down then back up, confirm re-reachability) were what actually caught and proved both the original bug and the regression.

**Tests:** `npx vitest run`: 304/304 pass (UI-only change, no module code touched). Extensively browser-verified (DOM hit-testing at multiple viewport sizes) and user-verified in a real browser for both the original short-window bug and the z-index regression.

## Critical Discovery #168 — Knob Zero-Tick Standardized App-Wide; Fused Override Readout Dimming; Key Window Layout Jump Fixed

**Context:** User wanted the small/default-size knobs' zero-tick (a line marking the zero/center position) to match the large hero knobs' (Level/Cutoff/Master Tune/Key Transpose) treatment — the small-knob tick extended past the ring's inner edge into the hollow center, while the hero knobs' was clamped to the ring's own stroke band. Discussed via mockups (design-only, no code) before implementing, including an alternative (tick tracks the current value instead of staying at zero) that was considered and not chosen.

**Fix:** `buildKnobBase` (`controls.js`) now always uses the hero-knob's ring-band-clamped tick treatment (8-unit length, stroke-width 3, butt cap) regardless of knob size, removing the size-based branch entirely. Confirmed legible down to the smallest deployed size (38px) via mockup review before implementing, and via live-app inspection after.

**Follow-up, user-reported:** activating a fused Off/PRG override correctly dimmed the knob ring but not its numeric readout (Combi/Multi Timbres' Level, A:B Pan, Send C/D — the only real users of `overrideStyle: 'fused'`). Root cause: `knobWithOverride`'s `updateDim()` only ever set `knob.style.opacity`; in fused mode the numeric readout is a separate sibling element (`readout: false` is passed to the underlying knob builder, since the fused pill+value column replaces the knob's own built-in readout), so it was never touched. Fixed by dimming that element too, tracked via a `fusedReadoutEl` reference — `'stack'`-mode callers (none currently live) are unaffected since their readout lives inside the same container as the ring already.

**Follow-up, user-reported:** Key Window's note-name readout (`dualHandleRangeSlider`, `fieldStyle: 'readout'`, `format: midiNoteName`) visibly jumped the Vel Window/Bend Range columns beside it on Combi/Multi's CONTROL tabs whenever a bound crossed into a sharp in octave −1 ("C#-1" is 4 characters vs. "C4"'s 2) — the readout's fixed 20px min-width was sized for a bare 0–127 number, not accounting for `format`'s variable-length output. Fixed with an opt-in `minWidthCh` param on `buildReadout` (default unchanged for every other caller) that `dualHandleRangeSlider` computes once, up front, by scanning `format()` across its own min–max range and reserving the widest result — Vel Window (no `format`) is unaffected.

**Tests:** `controls.test.js` unaffected structurally (no return-shape changes); `npx vitest run`: 304/304 pass throughout. Browser-verified (DOM attribute inspection confirming uniform tick geometry across 110+ knob instances; `getBoundingClientRect` confirming Key Window's slider width and neighboring-column position are pixel-identical before/after a sharp-note bound change) and merged to `main`.

## Critical Discovery #169 — Text-Casing Fixes; `buildFusedToggleGroup` Width-Jitter Bug Found and Fixed

**Context:** A batch of small, user-directed fixes: "Write in place" → "Write In Place" (Prog/Combi editors, all 14 occurrences including tooltips); "Copy from Combination..." → "Copy From Combination..." (Multi's toolbar button and modal title) and the same `from`→`From` capitalization on Prog's 6 "Copy from OSC/VDA/VDF-1/2" buttons; Global's Tuning & Response field captions (Master Tune, Key Transpose, Velocity Curve, After Touch Curve) changed from all-caps to sentence case by removing `text-transform: uppercase` from `.global-hero-field-label` — a class with exactly these 4 call sites, so the Scale panel's own "SCALE" header (different class) is unaffected.

**Real bug found while investigating a reported side effect:** the user noticed Copy From Combination's Effects question visibly resized every time an option was selected, and suggested the spacing needed adjusting. Root cause, in the shared `buildFusedToggleGroup` (`controls.js`, backing every `toggleButtonGroup`/`threeWayToggle` instance app-wide): the active/inactive distinction toggled `font-weight` between 400 and 600, and bold text is measurably wider than regular text for the same string — imperceptible for this app's typical short labels (Sin/Tri, off/+/−) but visible for this group's long sentence-length labels ("Include Combination's Effects" / "Leave Current Effects Unchanged"), resizing the whole fused strip on every click. Fixed with the standard "reserve max width" technique: an invisible ghost `<span>`, always rendered at the bold weight, sets the button's natural content width regardless of which state is currently showing; the real, visible label is absolutely positioned on top and is the only element whose weight actually toggles. The button's own click handler and the `buttons` array's external shape (raw `<button>` elements, consumed by 3 other call sites) were kept unchanged — the ghost/visible span pair and a `btn._fusedLabelEl` property are internal to the function.

**Verification:** `getBoundingClientRect()` confirmed the fused strip's total width and each button's own width are bit-for-bit identical across every selection state (previously: measurably different). Spot-checked VDF's OFF/LOW/HIGH/ALL and +/− toggles (short labels, the component's most common use) render correctly with no visual regression.

**Tests:** `npx vitest run`: 304/304 pass — `threeWayToggle`/`toggleButtonGroup`'s existing tests (classList checks, click dispatch, `border-style`) were unaffected by the internal span restructuring since none read `.textContent` directly on these buttons.

*Last updated: 2026-09-02 — Implemented and merged; 297→304 tests pass (7 new). Browser-verified (menu wiring, guard paths) only — hardware round-trip pending Chrome 152→153 update.*

## Critical Discovery #170 — Knobs "Grabbing Themselves" on Hover After a Missed Mouse Release: Six Drag Lifecycles That Only Ended on `pointerup`

**Symptom (user-reported):** from time to time, after editing a control (usually a knob), later moving the mouse over it with no button held changed its value, as if still being dragged. Not present in early iterations; had appeared "as the editor got more complex."

**Root cause:** every custom drag control attached a `pointermove` listener on `pointerdown` and removed it only on `pointerup`. If that `pointerup` never reached the element, the listener stayed attached indefinitely, and `onMove` never checked whether a button was actually held — so any later hover over the same element drove the value. Nothing handled `pointercancel` or `lostpointercapture`, and nothing filtered by button, so a right-click or macOS Ctrl-click also started a "drag" whose release the context menu then swallowed (the most likely everyday trigger). Other plausible release-swallowers: Cmd-Tab / focus loss mid-drag, trackpad gesture cancels. The pattern existed in six places: `attachKnobDrag`, `dualHandleRangeSlider`'s handles, `verticalFaderCentered`, `egCurveWidget`'s stage markers and Start Level handle (all `controls.js`), and the Effect tab's Parametric EQ curve handles (`index.html`).

**Why it appeared "gradually":** Phase 1/2 used native `<input type="range">` sliders, which the browser manages internally and are immune to this. The custom knob drag arrived with Phase 3 Brief 1 (`867c131`) and spread one tab retrofit at a time, so exposure grew with each tab — not a code-bloat effect, and a refactor/dead-code pass would not have fixed it on its own.

**Fix:** one shared, exported `beginPointerDrag(e, captureEl, onMove, listenEl = captureEl)` in `controls.js`, called from each control's own `pointerdown` handler. It returns without starting a drag unless `e.button === 0 && !e.ctrlKey`; otherwise it `preventDefault()`s, captures the pointer, and ends the drag (removing every listener and releasing capture) on `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, or `lostpointercapture`, and also on any `pointermove` whose `buttons` bitmask no longer has the primary bit set (treated as a missed release). `listenEl` exists for the EQ curve, which captures on a handle but listens on its parent SVG. All six sites now call it; no per-site drag logic changed beyond deleting the duplicated lifecycle code. Separately (same branch), the centered knob readout's manual double-click detection (Landmine #68) now ignores non-primary/Ctrl presses and resets its timer on them — a right-click followed by a left-click on the number had been counting as a double-click and opening the numeric editor.

**Verification:** `npx vitest run`: 304→313 pass across all 7 test files (9 new: 7 for `beginPointerDrag` — normal drag, `pointercancel`, `lostpointercapture`, buttonless-move-ends-drag, right-click, Ctrl-click, `listenEl`; 2 for the readout double-click, both confirmed failing without the fix). In the Claude Browser pane (component gallery): real drags still turn knobs; right-click + Escape + hover leaves the value unchanged; real double-click still opens the readout editor, right-click + left-click does not. The Browser pane shows no native context menu, so the release-swallow couldn't be reproduced there directly — instead a simulated missed release (`pointerdown`, no `pointerup`, then buttonless `pointermove`s) was run side-by-side against `main`'s original `controls.js` loaded as a separate module: old knob 30 → 62, new knob unchanged. User then tested in real Chrome, all good. Merged to `main` (`eb0cb97`; commits `2db8b29`, `5271af3`).

*Last updated: 2026-09-22 — Implemented, user-tested in Chrome, merged to `main`. 304→313 tests.*

## Critical Discovery #171 — Effect Params Weren't Translated Between Dump Layout and Parameter Change Order; Chorus/Flanger-Delay's Delay Time Also Wrong on the Live Wire

**Symptom (user-reported, then user hardware-confirmed via a scripted test):** an effect's parameters, as shown in the Effect tab after loading a program or device dump, didn't match the front panel — e.g. every Room/Hall program showed Pre Delay as 0. The user ran a two-part hardware test: (1) compared a Room/Hall program's Effect tab against the front panel on a freshly loaded factory bank; (2) edited Hi Damp on the Effect tab, pressed Write In Place, then checked whether the front panel showed the edited value in the right field.

**Root cause:** the X5DR's SysEx dump format stores each effect's 8 parameter bytes in a fixed, per-type order documented in `05_effect_parameters.md`'s `*11-3` tables — Reverb Time/NUL/Hi Damp/Pre Delay/E.R Level/NUL/EQ High/EQ Low for Hall/Room, for example. The Effect tab's own parameter order (`EFFECT_TYPES` in `index.html`) is a *different* order, hardware-captured via live Parameter Change edits during `effect_param_capture_sheet.md`'s session and confirmed correct for that purpose. `decodeEffects`/`encodeEffects` (`parser.js`/`sysex.js`) had always passed the 8 dump bytes straight through with no translation between the two orders — correct for nothing dump-based being exercised by prior hardware tests (which were live-edit-and-listen, per the capture sheet's own method), so the mismatch went undetected until a load-then-compare test was run.

**Verification the layout table is right:** rather than trust the manual's tables alone (several `05_effect_parameters.md` byte-order details have been wrong before, Landmine #9), every stored effect across three real banks (factory, an identified user's X5D bank, X5DR_SendCD — roughly 1,100 instances across 38 of 47 types) was decoded through the new table and checked against the editor's own value ranges; all passed. The same records were then re-encoded and checked byte-for-byte against the original dump bytes; all matched except 4 stored Balance R bytes (all Exciter, tolerated — see below). This caught two things the manual's tables don't fully describe:
- **MG Status** (`*11-3-3`) really does pack a hardwired 2-3 bit constant alongside the one user-adjustable Sin/Tri bit, confirmed per-type from real data (Landmine #89/#90's live-side finding, now also handled correctly on the dump side).
- **Dry:FX Balance for single-control types is stored differently between the two transports** — dumps hold the wet value in *both* bytes (1,025 of 1,029 stored instances), while live edits send wet/100-wet. The editor had been writing the live 100-wet form into dump data.

**Fix — `src/midi/effectLayout.js`:** a per-type table (`decodeEffectParams`/`encodeEffectParams`) is now the sole translation point between dump bytes and Parameter Change order, called from `decodeEffects`/`encodeEffects`. It also owns Dry:FX Balance's transport-specific encoding (`decodeEffectBalance`/`encodeEffectBalance`). Bytes the editor doesn't model (NUL/reserved bytes) are preserved from the originally-decoded block whenever the effect type hasn't changed, so untouched effects round-trip byte-for-byte — this is what the whole-bank re-encode test above actually checks. Applies to Program, Combi and Multi, since all three share `decodeEffects`/`encodeEffects`.

**Second bug found by the user's own hardware test, after the above was already merged locally:** setting Chorus-Delay/Flanger-Delay's own Delay Time (offset 4 of types 38-39) to 150 in the editor showed 300 on the front panel — live, before any Write. Pressing Write In Place then changed the front panel to 150, which looked like a fix but was really the dump-side code above (already correct) overwriting the wrong value the live edit had sent moments earlier. The device transmits/expects this one field in the same 2ms-step raw units on *both* the dump and the live Parameter Change wire (NOTE 12's `00~E1:00~450` range) — the editor was sending the full millisecond value live, unhalved. Odd editor values round the same way the device's own front-panel increment/decrement does: editor 151 showed 302 live, Write rounded it to 152.

**Fix:** `effectLayout.js` gained `liveEffectParamValue(type, offset, value)`, generalized from the same per-slot `scale` the dump codec already carries for this offset (same raw device register, same NOTE 12 conversion, just read through a different SysEx message type) rather than a separate hardcoded type/offset check. Every live-send call site for a per-type effect param now routes through it: `buildPerTypeParams`, `buildEffectHeroParams` (Easy tab), the type-change reset-to-defaults loop, and Copy Effects' live sends. Separately, `knobUnidirectional`/`buildReadout` (`controls.js`) gained an opt-in `step` config (default 1 — every other caller unaffected) so this one field's knob, typed-value edit, and spinner buttons all move in 2ms increments matching the front panel, with the same odd-value-rounds-up behavior confirmed on hardware.

**Verification:** `npx vitest run`: 313→330 pass across all 8 test files (17 new) — including a three-bank whole-effects-block round-trip test, and a test pinning the exact 150→75/300→150/odd-value-rounds-to-152 live-wire behavior. Browser-verified against real factory programs (A16 "Upright" Room, A33 "Lore" Stereo Delay, A04 "Rock On!!!" Flanger-Delay) before the user's own hardware pass, which confirmed both fixes directly: the original Hi Damp/Pre Delay test, a two-byte Delay Time R write, single-type Balance, EQ High/Low ordering on both a Room and a Distortion/Flanger, Chorus/Flanger-Delay's Delay Time live and after Write, Phaser 1's Sin/Tri, and the three layouts absent from all three banks (Wet Plate, Harmonic Chorus, Delay/Phaser) — all confirmed correct. Merged to `main` (`ee45687`; commits `cbc8e81`, `3995bdf`, `f340b18`).

*Last updated: 2026-09-24 — Implemented, user-tested in Chrome on real hardware (two rounds — the dump-layout fix, then the Delay Time live-wire fix it surfaced), merged to `main`. 313→330 tests.*

## Critical Discovery #172 — "Initialize Patch" Implemented: No Device-Native Init Function, Every Value Derived or User-Agreed

**Context:** synth editors conventionally offer an "Init Patch" action — a blank-slate starting point for sound design. The X5DR has no such function on its own front panel, and nothing in the manual (MIDI appendix or otherwise) documents an init/default value set for a Program. This is genuinely new editor-only behavior, not a device feature being surfaced.

**Design process:** rather than derive every one of a Program's ~150 individual fields unilaterally, each was proposed against what the field actually does (flat/off/0 for anything with no agreed role, matching the field's own manual-documented range) and reviewed field-group by field-group with the user before implementation — see the session's own back-and-forth for the full record. Four items were flagged explicitly as judgment calls rather than derivations: Poly assign, VDA velocity sensitivity (+40), VDA release time (15), and the effect Channel Enable bits (left on, since that field is untested/hidden — Landmine #16).

**A genuine correction mid-design:** the initial proposal set both oscillators' `level` to 99 (full). The user, looking at real factory patches, flagged this as implausibly high. Decoding `osc1.level` (and `osc2.level` when Double mode is used) across all three reference banks (550 samples) gave a median of 43, mean 46.0, with 30–49 the densest range (43% of all patches) — 99 sits in a small tail (6.4% of patches even reach 90–99). `INIT_PROGRAM` uses 43. This is the same "check the data before trusting a plausible-sounding number" discipline the effect-layout work (Critical Discovery #171) already established, applied here to a design decision rather than a hardware fact.

**A second correction, after initial implementation:** the user changed the two effects from Room + Stereo Delay to Stereo Chorus 1 + Room, keeping the same "each effect's own device defaults, fully dry, switched on" treatment. No design reasoning was given or needed — a straightforward preference swap, applied as a data-only change to `INIT_PROGRAM`.

**Implementation — `src/state/initProgram.js`:** `INIT_PROGRAM`, a plain object matching `parseProgram`'s exact output shape (`src/midi/parser.js`), so it drops directly into `store.getSnapshot().programs[i]` and round-trips through `encodeProgramToBytes` unchanged. Deliberately omits fields `encodeProgramToBytes` doesn't consume: `effects.io` (derived on encode from the individual bit fields, never read itself) and `effects.eff{1,2}DumpType`/`eff{1,2}DumpParams` (only meaningful for preserving an *already-decoded* effect's unmodeled dump bytes — correctly absent for a freshly-authored effect, which falls back to 0 for anything `effectLayout.js` doesn't model). A second export, `flattenObjectPaths(obj)`, is a small generic recursive flattener (objects and arrays, arrays indexed by position) producing the same dot-path shape every control's own `setParam` call already uses.

**Wiring — `index.html`:** a new "Initialize…" button in the PROG header's action row, styled plainly (no accent color, never disabled) and given extra left margin so reaching for Write/Discard doesn't risk it — a cheap second layer of misclick protection on top of the actual safety net, the confirm dialog. `doInitializeProgramFlow` (mirrors `doCancelFlow`'s own shape): shows the themed confirm *before* touching anything (per explicit user requirement — the app has no undo, so even a misclick mid-edit on an unsaved patch must cost nothing but a Cancel click); on confirm, applies `INIT_PROGRAM` field-by-field through the local `setParam` wrapper (Landmine #26) rather than a single `store.replaceProgram` — this dirties each field's own dot-path, the exact shape `doCancelFlow`/`revertProgram` already know how to find and clear, so Discard Edits works correctly on an Initialize the same as on any other edit; then pushes the result to the device's edit buffer via `resyncDeviceProgramBuffer` (a dump, never a permanent Write Request — nothing is stored until the user separately presses Write In Place). Effect On/Off (`eff1Switch`/`eff2Switch`) is sent as a separate live Parameter Change immediately after, since — being session-only (Archive #19) — it has no dump representation at all and the device's actual current Switch state (whatever it happened to be before Initialize) would otherwise silently disagree with what the editor now shows as On.

**Verification:** a dedicated round-trip unit test (`initProgram.test.js`) encodes `INIT_PROGRAM` and re-parses it, asserting every one of its own fields survives unchanged — with the two session-only exceptions (`eff1Switch`/`eff2Switch`, `out3/4LLevel`/`out3/4RLevel`) explicitly excluded and documented, not silently skipped. This test caught the session-only-field gap directly (both exclusions were confirmed, not assumed, by running the test without them first and seeing it fail with `undefined`). `npx vitest run`: 330→339 pass (9 new). Browser-verified end to end on a real factory bank (A00 PipeDreams): the confirm dialog blocks every change until OK is clicked; Cancel is a true no-op (name, dirty state, and device buffer all unchanged); OK sets every OSC/VDF/VDA/Effect field to the agreed values, with OSC-2/VDF-2/VDA-2 exactly mirroring OSC-1/VDF-1/VDA-1; Discard Edits immediately after an Initialize correctly reverts to the original patch. User then hardware-tested the full checklist (mid-edit misclick safety, front-panel edit-buffer contents, Write In Place persistence, Discard-after-Initialize, Double OSC mode mirroring) — all cases passed. Merged to `main` (`c5bf7aa`; commits `43a14b3`, `1400e09`).

*Last updated: 2026-09-25 — Implemented, user-tested on real hardware, merged to `main`. 330→339 tests.*

## Critical Discovery #173 — "Write to Device → All Data" Left the Device Stuck in Multi Mode, Corrupting Subsequent Edits

**Context:** hardware-reported: after Device menu → Write to Device → All Data completed, the editor visibly returned to whatever tab was active (e.g. PROG > Easy on patch A00). But the *device* was silently still in Multi mode, on Track 1. An immediate edit made from PROG > Easy — e.g. changing OSC to Drums — was then interpreted by the device as a Parameter Change against Multi Track 9's parameters instead, setting that track's Level to 0. No error surfaced anywhere; the mismatch was only caught because the resulting patch/track corruption was noticed on the device itself.

**Root cause:** `sendAllDataDumpAndAwaitAck` (the function behind this menu item) sends the main Func=50 All Data dump, then — because Func=50 structurally cannot carry Multi's 208-byte Track-assignment Expansion block (Archive #78) — separately calls `sendMultiExpansionDumpAndAwaitAck` to push it via Func=68. That second call unconditionally sends a Mode Change to Multi (`buildModeChange(MODE_MULTI)`) and sets `editMode = 'multi'` before sending, exactly as it should for its *original* caller (Multi CONFIG's own debounced live-edit sync, where Multi genuinely is the active tab and being left in Multi mode afterward is correct). But "Write to Device → All Data" is not scoped to Multi at all — it's a whole-device overwrite that can be triggered from any tab — and its own click handler did nothing afterward to put the device back in whatever mode the editor was actually showing. This is the same class of bug as Landmine #38 (a mode-entry point that claims the shared `editMode` on its way in must also handle restoring on its way out) — `sendMultiExpansionDumpAndAwaitAck` was a new, indirect entry point into that same shared state that hadn't been audited against that rule.

**Fix:** a new `resyncDeviceToActiveTab()` (`index.html`, placed beside `cancelPatchBrowser`), which mirrors that function's existing per-scope restore logic — Multi/Global/Drums: Mode Change alone is the entire fix (no per-slot edit buffer to resync, Archive #60/#86); Program/Combi: a full Edit Buffer resync via `resyncDeviceProgramBuffer`/`resyncDeviceCombiBuffer` — but keyed off the *live* active nav-tab (`.nav-tab.active:not(.nav-toggle)`) rather than a remembered `priorScopeType`. Called from the `write-all-data` click handler immediately after a successful (`'ack'`) write, before the freeze overlay (Critical Discovery — device freeze overlay, same session) releases, so no window exists where the UI is interactive but the device is still in the wrong mode. `sendAllProgramsDumpAndAwaitAck`/`sendAllCombisDumpAndAwaitAck` (the other two "Write to Device" bulk options) don't touch Multi mode at all and don't need this fix — confirmed by reading both; only Func=50's Multi Expansion side-effect does.

**Also considered and ruled out:** `doLoadFileFlow`'s own "Write to device?" confirmation (FILE → Load → All Data, from a picked file) calls the same `sendAllDataDumpAndAwaitAck` and has the identical theoretical exposure, but was confirmed *not* actually broken — it always follows the write with `openPatchBrowser()`, which is a full-screen overlay the user cannot get past without either picking a patch (which calls `switchToAndEditSlot`/`confirmPatchSelection`, itself a mode-correcting entry point) or Cancelling (which calls `cancelPatchBrowser`, the exact restore logic this fix generalizes). `doLoadFactorySoundsFlow` (the embedded-fixture load path) is likewise safe — it unconditionally calls `switchToAndEditSlot(0)` after its own write, by original design (jumping to Prog A00 is the intended end state of that flow, not incidental). Only the bare "Device menu → Write to Device → All Data" button, which does nothing at all after the write besides re-enabling itself, was actually exposed.

**Verification:** unit tests unaffected (this is pure device-mode control flow, nothing `parseProgram`/`encodeProgramToBytes`-adjacent); `npx vitest run` still 347/347. Syntax-checked; browser-verified the diff introduces no console errors. The actual MIDI mode-restore behavior could not be exercised in the dev sandbox (no Web MIDI/hardware reachable there) — verified by the user on real hardware: Write All Data from each of PROG/COMBI/MULTI/GLOBAL/DRUMS, followed immediately by an edit on that same tab, landed correctly in every case. Merged to `main`.

*Last updated: 2026-09-25 — Hardware-confirmed root cause and fix, merged to `main`. 347/347 tests (no change in count — this fix touches control flow only).*

## Critical Discovery #174 — Effect 1/2 On/Off Reverting on Write In Place; "Channel Enable" Was the Same Feature All Along, Not a Separate Unverified One

**Context:** hardware-reported: on Factory Sound Combi A02 StereoKeys (Effect 1 = Stereo Chorus 1, Off; Effect 2 = Hall, On), changing either Effect's On/Off state in the editor sent a live Parameter Change and the device reflected it — but hitting Write In Place reverted the device back to the original Off/On state, leaving the editor and device out of sync. Same result on A04 AnalogKing (both On, toggling either Off and writing reverted it back to On).

**Root cause:** `eff1Switch`/`eff2Switch` (the visible On/Off toggle, live PC 157/158 per `03_program_parameters.md`'s Table 7-1) and the dump's Effect I/O byte L/R channel-enable bits (`eff1IoL`/`eff1IoR`/`eff2IoL`/`eff2IoR`, `*11-2` in `05_effect_parameters.md`) were modeled in code as two unrelated features. `decodeEffects` never derived `eff1Switch`/`eff2Switch` at all (the UI just defaulted to On via `?? 1`, regardless of what a freshly-loaded combi/program actually had stored); `encodeEffects` reconstructed the dump's I/O byte purely from `eff1IoL`/`eff1IoR`/`eff2IoL`/`eff2IoR` — fields set only once, at parse time, and never touched by the visible toggle (which only set the session-only `eff{n}Switch` and sent a live Parameter Change). So Write In Place always re-sent whichever On/Off state was baked in at load time, silently discarding any live toggle made since. This also meant the editor showed the *wrong* On/Off state on every fresh load (always On), which the user was very likely correcting by hand before ever hitting Write In Place — making the eventual revert look even more like a genuine device-side bug.

This directly overturns Landmine #16 / Critical Discovery #71's premise that Channel Enable "has no live Parameter Change number at all." It has one — PC 157/158 — it just wasn't recognized as the same underlying state as the hidden, unwired Channel Enable checkboxes.

**Verification (before any code change, read-only investigation):** parsed all 100 combis and all 100 programs from three independent reference `.syx` files (`X5dr Factory Sounds.syx`, `X5DR_SendCD.syx`, `<identified user>_X5D.syx` — 400 combis + 400 programs total) directly through `parseSnapshot`. Zero cases anywhere of `eff1IoL !== eff1IoR` or `eff2IoL !== eff2IoR` — every real-world dump always sets both channel bits of a given effect together. Cross-referenced against the manual's own `*11-2 — Effect I/O` table, which documents bit0/1 as "Efct1 L-Ch/R-Ch Off/On" and bit2/3 as "Efct2 L-Ch/R-Ch Off/On" — i.e. the same conceptual On/Off state Table 7-1 lists separately as live PC 157/158, just packed as 2 bits per effect at the dump layer instead of 1 PC number. Directly confirmed against A02 StereoKeys (`io` byte `44` → `eff1IoL/R = 0,0`, `eff2IoL/R = 1,1`, exactly matching the user's hardware report) and A04 AnalogKing (`io` byte `15` → all four bits `1`).

**Fix:** `decodeEffects` (`src/midi/parser.js`) now derives `eff1Switch`/`eff2Switch` from the I/O byte's L bit for each effect (L and R are interchangeable given the L==R invariant above). `encodeEffects` (`src/midi/sysex.js`) now derives the I/O byte's four channel-enable bits from `eff1Switch`/`eff2Switch` instead of `eff{1,2}IoL/IoR` — both L and R bits of an effect are always set together from its single Switch value. The hidden, unwired Channel Enable checkbox UI (`src/index.html`'s `ioRow`, always `display:none`) was removed entirely, along with the now-dead `.io`-byte bookkeeping in the Placement toggle handler — `eff{1,2}IoL/IoR` remain on the decoded object (kept for diagnostic/back-compat shape parity) but are no longer read by `encodeEffects`. `copyEffectsFrom`'s comment corrected (Channel Enable no longer needs separate exclusion — copying Switch already covers it). `INIT_COMBI`/`INIT_PROGRAM` and their round-trip tests updated: `eff1Switch`/`eff2Switch` are no longer session-only exclusions in the round-trip check, since they now genuinely round-trip through `encode*ToBytes`/`parse*`.

**New tests** (`src/midi/sysex.test.js`): decodes A02 StereoKeys and A04 AnalogKing directly from the real factory `.syx` file, confirming the correct Switch values; asserts the zero-L/R-mismatch invariant across the factory bank; and — the test that would have failed before this fix — loads StereoKeys, flips both switches, re-encodes, and confirms the change survives instead of reverting to the original Off/On state.

**Verification:** `npx vitest run`: 347→352 pass (5 new). User hardware-tested both original repro cases (A02 StereoKeys, A04 AnalogKing) after merging: toggling Effect 1/2 On/Off in the editor and hitting Write In Place now correctly persists the new state on the device. Merged to `main` (`bdac2a5`).

**Lesson:** a field with no known live wire path and a field with an unverified/unwired UI control looked like two separate unresolved questions (Landmine #16's "no confirmed live Parameter Change path for Channel Enable" and Archive #19's "Effect On/Off is session-only") — but both were symptoms of the same unexamined assumption, and neither had actually been checked against the other. Scanning real captured data directly (rather than reasoning from the manual's table structure alone, which lists them as separate parameter numbers) surfaced the connection immediately.

*Last updated: 2026-09-26 — Hardware-confirmed root cause and fix, merged to `main`. Landmine #16 (Project Context) corrected in the same session. 347→352 tests (5 new).*

## Critical Discovery #175 — "Write To A New Slot" Split Button; Cross-Slot Write Left Both Slots Showing Edited Data; Three Related Browser-Sync Gaps

**Feature:** PROG/COMBI's "Write In Place" button is now a split button — a caret on the right edge (visually joined to the main pill: background/border/radius live on the `.write-split` wrapper only, both buttons reset to `border:none`/`background:transparent` so the wrapper shows through) opens a one-item dropdown, "Write To A New Slot…". It hands off to the exact same destination-slot picker `openWriteBrowser` already provided for Device → Write to Device → Single Program/Combination — `doWriteProgramToNewSlotFlow`/`doWriteCombiToNewSlotFlow` were factored out of those menu handlers so both entry points share one implementation. No confirm dialog: picking a slot in the picker is itself the confirmation, matching how that menu item always worked. Went through several visual-design rounds (mockup iterations, a caret-hover regression that briefly created a two-tone look, then a full rebuild once the approved mockup's actual CSS structure — background/border on the wrapper, not each button — was read directly rather than re-guessed from screenshots) before landing on today's version.

**Bug found in hardware testing #1 — cross-slot write duplicated edited data:** after editing a parameter/name and choosing "Write To A New Slot" (or the pre-existing Device menu equivalent — same underlying function), *both* the original (source) slot and the newly-written (destination) slot showed the edited data in the editor and the Browser tab, even though the device itself was correct (only the destination was actually written). Root cause: the success handler called `store.replaceProgram`/`replaceCombi` (correctly deep-cloning into the destination slot) followed by `store.clearDirty()` — but never reverted the *source* slot's working copy. Since the source slot was never actually written to the device, it should have rolled back to its last-known-clean state; instead it kept the edited values while dirty-tracking was wiped, so both the editor and the Browser displayed it as if it had been saved.

**Underlying design gap this exposed:** neither `doWriteFlow`/`doCombiWriteFlow` (Write In Place) nor the Unsaved Edits modal's "Write to Device and Continue" button ever updated `cleanSnapshot` after a confirmed successful write — only `dirtyParams` was cleared. So a later edit-then-Discard on a slot that had *just* been successfully written would revert past that write, back to whatever was clean before it. This is very likely the actual mechanism behind a second symptom reported at the same time ("patch name in editor and Browser get out of sync after renaming and discarding") — most reproducible on a slot just landed on via a new-slot write.

**Fix:** new `store.commitProgram`/`commitCombi` (`src/state/store.js`) — like `replaceProgram`/`replaceCombi` (deep clone into `workingCopy`), but also updates `cleanSnapshot` for that index and clears only that index's dirty paths. Deliberately a *separate* method, not a behavior change to `replaceProgram`/`replaceCombi`: those are also used for file/dump imports that are not yet written to the device and must stay dirty-eligible/discardable (confirmed by checking every call site — Load → All Programs/Combinations, Load → 1 Program's destination picker, and the Func=0x40/0x49/"All Programs"/"All Combinations" device-dump-response handlers all still use plain `replaceProgram`/`replaceCombi` correctly). `commitProgram`/`commitCombi` are now used at every *confirmed-successful-device-write* call site: `doWriteFlow`, `doCombiWriteFlow`, `doWriteProgramToNewSlotFlow`, `doWriteCombiToNewSlotFlow`, and the Unsaved Edits modal's `modal-btn-write` handler. The new-slot flows additionally call `store.revertProgram`/`revertCombi` on the *source* slot whenever the destination differs from it (guarded — picking the source as its own destination is a same-slot write, already fully handled by `commitProgram`/`commitCombi` alone).

**Bug found in hardware testing #2 — Unsaved Edits modal's Discard didn't refresh the Browser row:** switching patches via the Browser tab while dirty (not via the header's own Discard Edits button) correctly reverted the device and the editor's working copy, but the Browser tab's row for that slot kept showing the discarded name until something unrelated forced a full rebuild. `doCancelFlow`/`doCombiCancelFlow` (the header button) already called `refreshBrowserRow`/`refreshCombiBrowserRow` right after reverting; the modal's own `modal-btn-discard` handler never did. Fixed by adding the same calls there.

**Bug found in hardware testing #3 — Browser highlight stale or entirely absent after a slot switch:** `openPatchBrowser`'s highlight logic only ever touched `#programs-table-container`, keyed to `currentProgIndex` — after a new-slot write switched the editor to a different Program slot, reopening the Browser could show the original source slot still highlighted (this logic hadn't been re-verified against a mid-session slot change before); for Combi it was worse — `#combis-table-container` was never touched by this code at all, so no row was ever highlighted there, regardless of what `currentCombiIndex` was. Fixed by looping over both sub-panels and highlighting each against its own current index — the in-browser PROGRAM/COMBINATION toggle only shows/hides whichever table already exists, without re-running any highlight logic, so both need to already be correct going in.

**Inconsistency found in hardware testing #4 — Factory Sounds didn't open the Browser after writing:** `doLoadFactorySoundsFlow` ended with `switchToAndEditSlot(0)`; the equivalent disk-file path, `doLoadFileFlow`, ends with `openPatchBrowser()` after its own "Write to Device?" modal resolves (Write or Not Now, unconditionally). Made Factory Sounds match exactly.

**New tests** (`src/state/store.test.js`): 15 new cases for `commitProgram`/`commitCombi` — bulk-replace, clean-baseline update (the behavior that distinguishes them from `replaceProgram`/`replaceCombi`), scoped dirty-clearing, no cross-slot interference, a later edit+revert correctly reverting to the just-committed data rather than the pre-commit baseline, and deep-clone independence between `workingCopy` and `cleanSnapshot`.

**Verification:** `npx vitest run`: 352→367 pass. The cross-slot-write fix was additionally verified via a standalone Node script replaying the exact store-call sequence (both the different-destination and same-destination-as-source cases) before it was ever wired into `index.html`. Several of the later fixes (the Browser-highlight and Factory-Sounds-Load fixes, and re-confirming the write-flow fixes) were verified end-to-end in-browser using a temporary, uncommitted diagnostic hook — a fake `selectedOutput.send` that self-replies with ACK/Write-Completed bytes through the real `handleSysexMessage`, letting the actual success-path code run without hardware in a sandbox with no MIDI device. All four fixes hardware-tested and confirmed by the user; merged to `main` (`035d4ff`).

**Lesson:** `store.clearDirty()` clears the *symptom* (dirty tracking) but was never the same thing as "this data is now confirmed on the device" — three different call sites (Write In Place, Write To A New Slot, the modal's Write button) had each independently reached for it as if it were, because until a cross-slot write made the gap between "same slot" and "different slot" observable, the two things had never actually diverged. Any future write-success handler should reach for `commitProgram`/`commitCombi`, not `clearDirty()` + a manual `replaceProgram`/`replaceCombi`.

*Last updated: 2026-09-27 — All four fixes hardware-confirmed by the user across several test rounds; merged to `main` (`035d4ff`). 352→367 tests (15 new).*

## Critical Discovery #176 — Bundled Factory Soundbank Fixture Had Drifted From Real Hardware; Replaced With a Genuine Hardware Capture; Landmine #102's Evidence Invalidated

**Context:** While planning hardware A/B tests for Progress Log Next Action 1 (non-effect round-trip normalizations), the user performed a front-panel factory-preset restore on the X5DR (Bank A) followed by Device > Import > All Data from the editor, capturing the resulting SysEx traffic directly in Snoize — independent of the editor's own encode/decode path. This gave, for the first time, a hardware-captured factory soundbank not sourced from `reference_sysex/X5dr Factory Sounds.syx` (which had been downloaded from the internet at project start and never independently verified against real hardware).

**Finding:** Parsing both files with the project's own `parser.js` and diffing every Program/Combi field found:
- **Combinations: 100/100 identical. Multi Setup: identical. Global: identical.**
- **Programs: 98/100 identical — 2 differ.** #82 "VeloFlugel" differs in one field (`osc1.pitchMG.intModByMW`: 35 vs 3). #97 "SopranoVox" differs in 18 fields scattered across `osc1.pan`, most of `osc2.pitchMG`, `osc2.pitchEGInt`, most of `vda1.eg`, and `vdf1.colorIntensity` — not a byte-alignment shift (surrounding fields line up correctly), genuinely different stored values.
- **Drums:** Kit 1 note 0 differs substantially between the two files (old file: mostly-zeroed/silent slot; hardware capture: fully populated). Investigated separately below.

The downloaded file's corruption is real, not a parsing artifact, and was isolated enough (2/100 programs) that it had gone unnoticed through months of use as the project's primary reference fixture for round-trip and effect-encoding tests.

**Action taken:** The hardware-captured files (`Factory A Bank Pt 1 dump.syx` = Func=0x50 All Data, `Factory A Bank Pt 2 dump.syx` = Func=0x68 Multi Expansion — the same two-message shape the app's own Factory Sounds load produces) were added to `reference_sysex/` as `X5dr Factory Sounds - Hardware Capture 2026-09-29 (All Data).syx` / `(Multi Expansion).syx`. The original downloaded file was kept on disk, untouched, for historical comparison — not deleted. `src/index.html`'s embedded `FACTORY_SOUNDS_SYX_BASE64` (used by FILE → Load → Factory Sounds) was replaced with the hardware-captured bytes, verified byte-for-byte via a round-trip decode check. All four test files that referenced the old file (`encoder.test.js`, `parser.test.js`, `sysex.test.js`, `effectLayout.test.js`) were repointed at the hardware capture, adding the Multi Expansion file alongside it wherever a test needed `snap.multi.tracks` (only reachable via the standalone Func=0x68 dump, never the All Data dump — Landmine #53). `npx vitest run`: 367/367 pass throughout.

**Landmine #102 invalidated by this finding:** that landmine's motivating example — Drums Kit 1 slot 0 ("Metal Kick") carrying a real out-of-manual-range key byte (`0`/C-1) — was sourced from the same corrupted downloaded file. The hardware capture shows **no out-of-range Key value anywhere in either drum kit.** The underlying code fix (always include the current value as a dropdown option even if out of the documented range) is still good defensive practice on its own merits, but the specific "confirmed real Korg quirk" framing no longer holds. Amended in place (Project Context, Landmine #102) rather than restated here as a new landmine, since the defensive behavior itself didn't change.

**Progress Log Next Action 1 re-verified, not invalidated:** re-ran the exact byte-level round-trip diff (Program byte 134, Program byte 29's Cutoff MG bit, Combi byte 10, Timbre Control Filter bits 4-5) against the hardware-captured canonical data. **Every count reproduced identically** — same 15 programs at byte 134, same 1 program (#88 "Syn Brass") at byte 29, same 59 combis at byte 10 (always exactly `4`, never another value), same 631/800 timbre records with Control Filter bits 4-5 ≠ `11`. This rules out file corruption as the explanation for any of those four findings — they are present in genuine, hardware-verified factory data, which raises their priority from "probably harmless, low priority" toward "worth resolving before publishing," particularly Combi byte 10 (a consistent nonzero value on 59/100 real combis looks like an undocumented real flag, not padding) and the Timbre Control Filter bits (79% of real timbre records don't match the encoder's forced "per-manual" value).

**Open question the user raised, not yet resolved:** whether byte 134's "(RESERVE)" designation (03_program_parameters.md, TABLE 1, transcribed from the X5DR Owner's Manual pp.180-181/183) might carry over unused-on-X5DR data from a sibling instrument in the X5 family (the X5DR shares MIDI implementation lineage with the X5/X5D). Plausible but unconfirmed — nothing in this project's reference material speaks to the X5's own TABLE 1.

**Lesson:** A bundled reference fixture sourced from an uncontrolled third party (an internet download, never hardware-verified) can silently drift from ground truth for a long time without any test catching it, if the drift is small enough (2/100 programs) and no test happens to touch the specific affected fields. Any fixture serving as the project's "ground truth" for round-trip/encoding tests should eventually get at least one direct hardware-captured cross-check, even if it was "probably fine" for months.

*Last updated: 2026-09-29 — Hardware-verified canonical factory soundbank added and wired into the embedded app data and test suite; Landmine #102 amended; Next Action 1's findings re-confirmed against real data. `npx vitest run`: 367/367 pass.*

## Critical Discovery #177 — Program Byte 29's Unmodeled Cutoff MG Bit (Program #88 "Syn Brass") Confirmed Harmless on Hardware

**Context:** One of Progress Log Next Action 1's four non-effect round-trip normalizations — `encodeProgramToBytes` only models bits 0-2 (waveForm), 5-6 (oscSelect), and 7 (keySync) of Program byte 29 (`cutoffMg`), leaving bits 3-4 an unmodeled gap always written as 0. Program #88 "Syn Brass" is the only program (of 100, confirmed against both the downloaded reference file and the 2026-09-29 hardware capture — Archive #176) where the real factory data has bit 4 set, so a round trip through the editor silently drops it (orig `0b11110010` → re-encoded `0b11100010`).

**Test performed:** User front-panel-auditioned the hardware factory-reset "Syn Brass" patch, then compared it against the same patch after an Import All Data → Write All Data round trip through the editor.

**Result: no front-panel difference and no audible sonic difference found.** Whatever bit 4 of byte 29 does (if anything, on this specific offset), losing it on a round trip has no observable effect on this program's Cutoff MG behavior.

**Disposition:** Closed — no code change needed. This does not resolve the analogous open questions for Program byte 134, Combi byte 10, or Timbre Control Filter bits 4-5 (still open, Progress Log Next Action 1), which involve different bytes/fields with much larger real-data footprints (15 programs, 59 combis, and 631/800 timbre records respectively, vs. this bit's single affected program) and were not covered by this test.

*Last updated: 2026-09-29 — Cutoff MG bit (Program byte 29) hardware-confirmed harmless; closed. Remaining Next Action 1 sub-items (byte 134, Combi byte 10, Timbre Control Filter bits 4-5) still open.*

---

## Critical Discovery #178 — Program Byte 134 and Combi Byte 10 Dismissed: Both Manual-Documented "Reserved," No Front-Panel Difference Found

**Context:** Two more of Progress Log Next Action 1's four non-effect round-trip normalizations. `encodeProgramToBytes` always writes Program byte 134 as `0`, though 15 of 100 real factory programs carry a nonzero value there (clustered around `0x0A`/`0x0F`/`0x13`/`0x3C`/`0x3E`). `encodeCombiToBytes` always writes Combi byte 10 as `0`, though 59 of 100 real factory combis carry the identical value `4` (0x04) there. Both counts were re-verified against a genuine hardware capture, ruling out file corruption as the explanation (Archive #176).

**Resolution:** the user confirmed both offsets are independently documented as "(RESERVE)" in **both the X5D(R) and X5 manuals** — not just the X5DR's own TABLE 1 (`03_program_parameters.md` line 119 for byte 134; the equivalent Combi table for byte 10). No front-panel difference was observed. Given dual-manual confirmation that these bytes are formally reserved, plus no observable device-behavior difference, both are dismissed as inconsequential — most plausibly leftover/carried-over data from the X5 family's shared internal dump structure (per the user's own hypothesis raised this session) rather than anything the X5DR itself reads.

**Disposition:** Closed — no code change needed; the encoder's existing "always write 0" behavior for both bytes is fine to keep as-is. This does not resolve Timbre Control Filter bits 4-5, the one remaining open sub-item of Next Action 1 — that field has no equivalent "documented reserved" cover (the manual instead describes it as fixed at 1,1 "per the manual," which real data contradicts 79% of the time) and has not yet been hardware A/B tested.

*Last updated: 2026-09-29 — Program byte 134 and Combi byte 10 dismissed (manual-documented Reserved, no front-panel difference). Only Timbre Control Filter bits 4-5 remains open in Next Action 1.*

## Critical Discovery #179 — Timbre Control Filter Bits 4-5 Dismissed: No Front-Panel Difference on Hardware; Progress Log Next Action 1 Fully Closed

**Context:** The last of Progress Log Next Action 1's four non-effect round-trip normalizations. `encodeTimbre` always writes bits 4-5 of the Control Filter byte (`ctrlFilter`, dump offset `t+10`) as `11` ("per manual," per the manual's own description), but 631 of 800 real factory timbre records (79%, across both the downloaded reference file and the 2026-09-29 hardware capture, Archive #176) carry `00` instead — the largest-footprint and least-covered of the four sub-items, since unlike Program byte 134/Combi byte 10 there was no independent "documented Reserved" citation to fall back on.

**Test performed:** User compared front-panel settings for Combi #2 "X Strings" between the hardware factory-reset version and the Import All → Write All round-tripped version through the editor. This combi was specifically chosen because its own 8 timbres are a real mix — timbres 0-3 already match "per-manual" (`11`) in factory data, timbres 4-7 don't (`00`) — making it a genuine within-combi A/B case, not just a whole-file comparison.

**Result: no front-panel difference found.** Whatever bits 4-5 of the Control Filter byte represent (if anything), forcing them to `11` on every write has no observable effect on any of Combi #2's 8 timbres, despite 4 of them having a different raw value in the real factory data.

**Disposition:** Closed — no code change needed; `encodeTimbre`'s existing `| 0x30` (bits 4,5 fixed at 1,1) is fine to keep as-is. **This closes Progress Log Next Action 1 in full** — all four non-effect round-trip normalizations (Program byte 134, Program byte 29's Cutoff MG bit, Combi byte 10, Timbre Control Filter bits 4-5) are now confirmed cosmetic/inert via a combination of hardware A/B testing (Cutoff MG bit, Archive #177; Control Filter bits, this entry) and dual-manual "Reserved" documentation (byte 134/Combi byte 10, Archive #178). Next Action 1 removed from the Progress Log's active list.

*Last updated: 2026-09-29 — Timbre Control Filter bits 4-5 hardware-confirmed harmless (Combi #2 "X Strings"). Progress Log Next Action 1 fully closed — all four sub-items resolved.*

## Critical Discovery #180 — MIDI Output Port Auto-Select Broadened to Any Case-Insensitive "X5" Match

`populatePortSelect` (`src/index.html`) previously pre-selected an output only if `port.name.includes('X5DR')`. Changed to `port.name.toLowerCase().includes('x5')` so X5, X5D and X5DR devices are all picked up by default. Still output-only (the app listens on all inputs, Archive #159); manual selection is unchanged.

## Critical Discovery #183 — Discard Edits and Continue Blocked the User When No Device Answered; Both Discard Paths Now Share One Best-Effort Implementation

**Symptom:** the Abandoned Edits modal's "Discard Edits and Continue" showed "Discard failed — could not restore device state." and left the user stuck whenever no MIDI output was selected, while the header's "Discard Edits" worked fine in the same situation.

**Cause:** the two paths were written at different times. The header button (`doCancelFlow`/`doCombiCancelFlow`) got the July 2026 B16 fix (local revert unconditional, device resync best-effort). The modal handler never did: it resynced the device first and reverted the store only on an ACK, so `'no-output'` and `'nak'` both blocked. Worse, the ACK wait had no timeout, so a port that was selected but had no responding device (powered off, wrong channel, SysEx disabled — the status pill only reflects that an output is selected) left the modal permanently disabled, Stay button included.

**Fix (branch `fix/discard-edits-consistency`):**
- New shared `discardEditsAndResync(scope, {render})`: revert the store and refresh the Browser row unconditionally and first; resync the device only if an output is selected; a NAK/timeout/no-output produces a status-bar message and never blocks. Used by the header button (`render: true`) and the modal (which still `await`s it before `navigateAway()`, so the resync's Mode Change + dump can't collide with the destination tab's Mode Change — Landmine #18/#41).
- `sendProgramDumpAndAwaitAck`/`sendCombiDumpAndAwaitAck` gained an optional `timeoutMs` (default none — Write flows must still wait for a real confirmation); `resyncDeviceProgramBuffer`/`resyncDeviceCombiBuffer` pass `RESYNC_TIMEOUT_MS` (3000). On timeout the call's own callbacks are cleared (only if still current) and it resolves `'timeout'`. This also bounds Initialize and Patch Browser Cancel resyncs, whose callers already treat any non-ACK as "may be out of sync"; the Patch Browser/`resyncDeviceToActiveTab` messages now cover timeouts too.
- Decision (owner-confirmed): on NAK/timeout the modal proceeds silently with a status message rather than asking a second question.

**Verification:** browser-verified with a mock MIDI output (no output / silent / ACK / NAK, header and modal paths, message order PC → Mode Change → dump → destination Mode Change). Not yet hardware-tested — see the hardware test plan handed over with the branch.

**Addendum (hardware test #4, 2026-09-30):** with no MIDI output, "Discard Edits and Continue" then switching back to PROG showed the discarded values with Write In Place/Discard Edits still lit but inert. The modal path reverted the store but didn't redraw the panel, and re-entering PROG/COMBI only redraws via `switchToAndEditSlot`/`-CombiSlot` when a device is connected (the old ACK-gated code never reached this state without a device, so the gap was latent). The modal now calls `discardEditsAndResync(..., {render: true})`, same as the header button. Browser-verified with no output (panel values restored, both buttons disabled). Hardware tests #1–3 and #5–10 passed.

## Critical Discovery #185 — Every Send Path Now Times Out; A "No Response from Device" Modal Points to Disabled SysEx

**Symptom (hardware-reported):** with SysEx reception disabled on the device, any write from the editor hung — the freeze overlay never lifted. The device doesn't answer at all in that state (no ACK, no NAK). The earlier timeouts only covered *import* (`beginDumpRequest`'s 12s watchdog) and the best-effort resync (Archive #183); all ~10 send-and-await-ACK helpers still waited forever.

**Fix (branch `fix/sysex-send-timeout`):**
- New `armAckReply(resolve, byteCount, opts)` / `armWriteReply(resolve, opts)` replace the hand-rolled callback blocks in every helper: single Program/Combi dumps, All Data, All Programs, All Combinations, Multi Expansion/Effects, Global, Drums, and both Write Requests. They resolve `'timeout'` when nothing arrives, clearing shared state only if it is still theirs.
- The window **scales with message size**: 5s + 0.4ms/byte. MIDI's wire speed needs ~0.32ms/byte just to transmit, and the device ACKs only after receiving everything — an All Data dump (~35 KB) takes ~11s to send alone, so a flat timeout would have failed healthy writes. Result: ~5s for a single Program, ~19s for All Data.
- New `showNoResponseModal()` explains the likely cause (SysEx reception disabled: X5D/X5DR Global page 02E, EX: → ENA), plus channel/port/cable/cheap-interface checks. Rate-limited to once per 30s, since debounced Multi/Global syncs can time out repeatedly during editing. The resync path (`RESYNC_OPTS`) opts out of the modal and keeps its status message. The import watchdog's modal text now carries the same hint.
- Callers: status messages added for `'timeout'` where the fall-through would have been misleading; Multi/Global sync status treats `'timeout'` as error, not idle.
- Also fixed: Device → Write → All Data overwrote its own success status with "No data loaded — nothing to write." (a trailing `else` fired on `'ack'`).

**Not covered:** live single Parameter Changes (Func=41) are fire-and-forget with NAK detection only; a silent device is not detected there. **Verification:** browser-verified with a mock MIDI port (silent device: single write → modal at ~5s and buttons re-enabled; All Data → overlay lifts and modal at ~19s; normal ACKs still succeed). Not hardware-tested.

**Addendum (Retry, owner-requested):** the "No response from device" modal now has **Retry** and **OK** buttons (Escape = OK). Retry re-runs the same send with the same size-scaled timeout and shows the modal again if it fails again, so the user can troubleshoot the device between attempts; OK gives up and returns to the editor with all edits intact. Implemented as `withTimeoutRetry(attempt, args)` wrapping each single-attempt `send…Once` helper (and All Data's main dump), so a multi-step flow resumes at the step that failed (e.g. only the Write Request is retried, not the dump). The modal moved out of `armAckReply`/`armWriteReply` into `promptNoResponseRetry`. While it is up the "Writing…" freeze overlay (z-index 300, above every modal) is hidden and restored on Retry, or the modal would be unclickable. The 30s rate limit now applies only to *background* sends (`{background: true}`: the debounced Multi CONFIG and Global syncs); a send the user started always gets the modal. Resyncs still use `{alertOnTimeout: false}` (no modal, no retry). Browser-verified with a mock port: Retry with a still-silent device re-prompts; Retry after the device responds completes the write; OK during an All Data write clears the overlay.

## Critical Discovery #186 — MIDI Channel Selector: The Editor No Longer Assumes the Device Is on Channel 1

**Why:** since Phase 1 every message assumed the X5DR's Global MIDI Channel was 1 (the device default). The device silently ignores SysEx whose `3g` header byte doesn't match its own Global MIDI Channel (Landmine #57), so users with a non-default channel (multi-module or daisy-chained rigs) could not use the editor at all, with no indication why. The device's own Global MIDI Channel still cannot be read or set over SysEx (Landmines #56, #57) — only the front panel changes it — so the editor needs to be *told* the channel.

**Change (branch `feature/midi-channel-selector`):**
- A **Ch 1–16 dropdown** beside the port selector in the header (`#channel-select`, `initChannelSelect`/`onChannelSelected`); default Ch 1; persisted in `localStorage` (`x5dr-midi-channel`, try/catch). Changing it resets `editMode`/`pendingParam` (as a port change does) so the next edit re-sends Mode Change on the new channel.
- **Option A (module-level channel):** `sysex.js` now holds the channel (`setSysexChannel`/`getSysexChannel`) and every builder, plus `encoder.js`'s `assembleSyx`, takes its header from `sysexHeader()` (`F0 42 3g 36`). `SYSEX_HEADER` is kept only as the channel-1 constant for reference/tests — builders must not use it. Option A was chosen over passing the channel into every builder (~55 call sites, and a silently-missed site would keep sending on channel 1).
- **Response checkers accept any channel** (`isAck`/`isNak`/`isFormatError`/`isWriteCompleted`/`isWriteError` via `hasX5Header`); they used to require `0x30`, so on any other channel every ACK would have been ignored and every write would have timed out. Incoming routing and the parsers already ignored the channel byte.
- **Plain MIDI sends follow the channel too:** the 6 Program Change sends (`0xC0 | channel`) and the Drum Sound Browser's audition Note On/Off (`0x90`/`0x80 | channel`). The encoder serves both device sends and file saves, so saved `.syx` files carry the selected channel byte; loading ignores it.
- Help text (Getting Started, Troubleshooting), the "No response from device" modal and Copy Diagnostics (`MIDI channel: N`) now refer to the selector.
- **Tests:** new `channel.test.js` — every builder and encoder addresses the chosen channel, only the channel byte differs from channel-1 output, a dump built on another channel still parses, response checkers accept any channel and still reject other manufacturers/families/functions, and the default is unchanged (the 374 pre-existing tests pass unmodified). `npx vitest run`: 385/385 (12 files).

**Verification:** browser-verified with a mock device that listens on channel 5 and ignores others: with the selector on Ch 5 every SysEx byte is `0x34`, Program Change is `0xC4`, and a write completes from a channel-5 ACK; on Ch 1 the same write times out and the modal points at the selector; the choice persists across a reload. A syntax slip (an unescaped apostrophe in a modal string) that broke the whole page was caught in this check — `node --check` on the extracted module script is a cheap guard. **Not yet hardware-tested:** needs the device set to a non-default Global MIDI Channel (front panel) and the write/import/browse/audition checklist run on it.

**Addendum (2026-09-30):** hardware-tested by the owner on a non-default Global MIDI Channel — all checks passed (import, write, browse/Program Change, drum audition, wrong-channel modal and Retry, channel-1 default). Replaces the "not yet hardware-tested" note above. Getting Started's "Auditioning sounds" now notes the one exception: a short audition note in the Drum Sound Browser.
