## Critical Discovery #190 — Audit T2 B1: A Manually Chosen MIDI Port Was Lost After the First Send

**Context:** Optimization Plan Workstream C, tier T2, branch `refactor/audit-t2-port-select`, finding B1. First of seven T2 branches (order agreed with the owner: B1 → X7 → B3/B8/B11+X12 → B9 → X6+B6 → B4 → B5).

**The bug (reproduced on a fake Web MIDI port against `main`):** `midiAccess.onstatechange` re-ran `populatePortSelect()`, which re-selected only a port whose name contains "x5". The Web MIDI spec fires `statechange` when an output is implicitly opened by its first `send()`, as well as on hot-plug. With a hand-picked "Roland UM-ONE", the first Mode Change (nav to MULTI) went out and the list immediately fell back to "— select a port —": `selectedOutput` was `null` and every later send was silently dropped. The pill even read "Connected" for a moment, because the first ACK arrived after the reset. Every rebuild also cleared `editMode`/`pendingParam`, even when the port was unchanged.

**Fix (`f1d1c13`):**
- The user's choice is kept by name in `preferredPortName` and saved in localStorage (`x5dr-midi-port`). Port ids aren't stable across restarts; names are what the project already matches on.
- A rebuild selects, in order: the current port, if it is still listed and matches the saved choice; the saved choice by name (so it comes back after an unplug/replug or on the next launch); the current port; and only then, if the user hasn't explicitly chosen "— select a port —" this session, the last "x5" match, as before.
- Ports with `state === 'disconnected'` are no longer listed. Chrome keeps unplugged ports in the map, and sending to one throws. With no outputs left, `selectedOutput` is now cleared too; before, the "no outputs" path only set the pill.
- A new `setSelectedOutput(port)` resets `editMode`/`pendingParam` only when the output actually changes, so an unrelated hot-plug no longer forgets the device mode.
- A saved choice that isn't connected at launch falls back to "x5" auto-select, without overwriting the saved name.

**Verification:**
- `npx vitest run`: 382/382 across all 12 files (channel, effectLayout, encoder, factoryBanks, parser, sysex, controls, drumCrossReference, initCombi, initProgram, store, theme). No module changed.
- `node --check` on the extracted module script: passes.
- **Fake Web MIDI comparison** (untracked `src/__h_main.html`/`__h_branch.html`, with a classic-script stub that records sends, replies ACK and simulates implicit-open `statechange`, hot-plug and unplug):
  - `main`: pick "Roland UM-ONE" → nav to MULTI (1 send) → selection lost; nothing sent afterwards.
  - Branch: the selection survives the implicit open and a hot-plug, and MULTI → PROG after the hot-plug sends Program, `C0 00`, Prog Edit (the mode was kept). Unplug → "— select a port —"; replug → re-selected. Reload → the saved port wins over an "x5" port. An explicit clear → a later "x5"-named hot-plug is not auto-selected. All ports unplugged → "— no MIDI outputs found —", and a nav sends nothing and doesn't throw.
  - Default path (no saved choice, "FAKE X5DR"): an identical 18-message stream on `main` and the branch, over 8 nav-tab switches, a Patch Browser open/cancel and a hot-plug.
- Smoke test: every tab and sub-tab renders (PROG ×6, COMBI ×3, DRUMS kits, MULTI ×3, GLOBAL) with Factory Bank A loaded; File/Device/Help menus and the four Help modals open and close; Patch Browser opens and cancels; no console errors. The real `index.html` loads cleanly.

**Hardware checklist (owner, 2026-10-02, on a second computer via the pushed branch):**
- **Pass:** "x5" auto-select on reload with a live PROG edit; a hand-picked port renamed without "x5" stays selected through MULTI → PROG and edits land (the B1 case); the choice survives a reload; unplug → selection cleared at once, replug → re-selected, and MULTI → PROG → edit lands; after an explicit "— select a port —", unplug/replug auto-selects nothing.
- **Not tested:** hot-plugging an unrelated device (no second USB-MIDI device available). Covered on the fake port only.
- **Observed, Chrome behaviour, not the editor:** a port renamed in Audio MIDI Setup keeps its old name in the list until Chrome is quit and restarted, while an unplug shows immediately. Chrome caches port names and fires no `statechange` for a rename, so there is nothing for the editor to rebuild from.

New Landmine #118.

## Critical Discovery #191 — Audit T2 X7: One Helper for the Mode-Switching Dump Pushes

**Context:** Optimization Plan Workstream C, tier T2, branch `refactor/audit-t2-dump-send`, finding X7 (⚑ Landmines #112, #115). Second of the seven T2 branches. Scope as agreed with the owner: the four functions the finding names only. `sendProgramDumpAndAwaitAckOnce`/`sendCombiDumpAndAwaitAckOnce` have the same shape but sit on the #114 resync path, so they stay as they are.

**Change (`f76910f`):** `sendDumpAndAwaitAckOnce(buildMsg, {mode, editModeAs})` sends the Mode Change, sets `editMode`, waits 100ms (Landmine #41), builds the dump, arms `armAckReply` and sends it. `sendMultiExpansionDumpAndAwaitAckOnce`, `sendMultiEffectsDumpAndAwaitAckOnce`, `sendGlobalDumpAndAwaitAckOnce` and `sendDrumsDumpAndAwaitAckOnce` are one-line wrappers over it (Multi/`'multi'`, Multi/`'multi'`, Global/`'globalTab'`, Global/`'drumsTab'`). Their `withTimeoutRetry` wrappers and every caller are unchanged. Net −26 lines.

**One deliberate behaviour change:** the helper re-checks `selectedOutput` after the 100ms delay and resolves `'no-output'`. Since B1 (#190) clears `selectedOutput` on unplug, a port lost mid-push used to throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'send')` in the timer. The already-armed reply then timed out after 5s and showed a misleading "No response" modal. Now the caller reports "no MIDI output selected, not written to device".

**Verification:**
- `npx vitest run`: 382/382 across all 12 files (channel, effectLayout, encoder, factoryBanks, parser, sysex, controls, drumCrossReference, initCombi, initProgram, store, theme).
- `node --check` on the extracted module script: passes.
- **Fake Web MIDI comparison** (untracked harness copies, as in #189/#190), after loading Factory Bank A, in 10 steps: Write All Data (incl. the Multi Expansion push and the #112 resync); FILE → Load Multi, Global, Drums (files captured from the app's own Save); a debounced Global edit; Load Global with a silent device → "No response" (freeze overlay hidden while it's up) → OK; Load Drums silent → Retry → ACK; Load Multi with NAK. Every step was identical on `main` and the branch: all 25 sends byte for byte (dumps compared by hash, incl. the 35,318-byte All Data), status text and modal/overlay state.
- **Port lost during the 100ms delay** (unplugged right after the Mode Change): `main` throws the TypeError and shows "No response" ~5s later; the branch sends nothing more, shows the no-output status and logs no error.
- **Smoke test:** every tab and sub-tab renders with Factory Bank A loaded. Per-sub-tab visible element counts are identical to `main`. Menus, the four Help modals and the Patch Browser open and close. No console errors from the branch.
- A harness note, not an app bug: the fake port's NAK-everything mode also NAKs the unarmed Mode Change before a dump, which reaches the Parameter Change NAK recovery. The dump's own NAK is routed correctly through `writeCallbacks`.

**Hardware checklist (owner, 2026-10-02, via the pushed branch):**
- **Pass:** FILE → Load Multi, Global and Drums each write to the device; Write All Data, then a PROG edit lands on the Program (#112); the debounced GLOBAL and MULTI Control syncs reach the device; with SysEx disabled, Load Global → "No response" → OK gives the GLOBAL-tab Retry status, and Load Drums → re-enable → Retry completes.
- **Skipped:** the port unplugged during the 100ms delay (too short a window by hand). Covered on the fake port only.

## Critical Discovery #192 — Audit T2 B3/B8/B11/X12: One Mode-Restore Routine, and Two More Mode Bugs

**Context:** Optimization Plan Workstream C, tier T2, branch `refactor/audit-t2-mode-restore`, findings B3, B8, B11 and X12 (⚑ Landmines #38, #54, #62, #112, #114). Third of the seven T2 branches. The design was approved by the owner before coding, including the two extra fixes below.

**Two more problems found while reading the code (both fixed here, owner's choice):**
1. **A Program Change sent in the wrong mode.** `resyncDeviceProgramBuffer`/`resyncDeviceCombiBuffer` sent `Cn pp` in whatever mode the device was in, then let the dump re-enter edit mode. After Write All Data's Multi push the device is in Multi mode; X7's test log shows `4E 04`, Func=68, **`C0 00`**, `4E 03`, Func=40. In Multi mode a Program Change on the channel most likely retunes the Multi Track on it — Multi data is stored directly, so Write All Data from PROG may have silently changed that Track's program (unconfirmed — the hardware checklist tests it on `main`). From Prog Edit the Program Change is ignored (Landmine #2). After a Patch Browser sub-panel switch to Combinations, Cancel's Program Change selected a Combi.
2. **The nav flush race.** Leaving MULTI/GLOBAL flushed the pending debounced sync (Mode Change, then the dump 100ms later) and immediately sent the destination's Mode Change, so the Func=68/51 dump landed in the destination's mode. Harness stream on `main`, MULTI edit → PROG: `4E 04`, `4E 02`, `C0 00`, then 100ms later Func=68 **and** `4E 03`. A NAK there only shows as "Sync failed" on the tab just left.

**Changes:**
- **`1b7c097` — resync sequence.** Both resync helpers send Program (Combi) mode → Program Change → 100ms (Landmine #41) → the dump, which sends its own edit-mode Mode Change and waits 100ms. Callers: Patch Browser Cancel, the post-push restore, Discard (#114) and Initialize Patch/Combi. `sendProgramDumpAndAwaitAckOnce`/`sendCombiDumpAndAwaitAckOnce` get X7's port-lost guard.
- **`8a83217` — `restoreDeviceModeForTab(tab, {resync, progIndex, combiIndex})`** (X12). MULTI → `4E 04`/`'multi'`; GLOBAL → `4E 05`/`'globalTab'`; DRUMS → `4E 05`/`'drumsTab'` (#60). PROG/COMBI in *select* mode re-select the slot via the new `selectSlotOnDevice` (shared with `switchToAndEditSlot`/`switchToAndEditCombiSlot`), except that a dirty PROG gets a bare `4E 03` (#62); in *resync* mode they reload the editor's copy through the resync helpers. With no output, resync sets one "could not restore the device to <mode> mode" status; nav stays silent, as before. `cancelPatchBrowser` maps its `priorScopeType` to a tab and calls it; `resyncDeviceToActiveTab` is gone.
  - **B3/B8:** Write All Data and FILE → Load Multi/Global/Drums record `editMode` before the push and call `restoreActiveTabModeIfChanged` afterwards. It resyncs the active tab only if the push moved `editMode` — after a failed Multi push too (B3), never after a main-dump failure that sent no Mode Change. The freeze overlay stays up until the restore finishes. The caller's status is put back 100ms after the restore (its ACK and Chrome's repeats would show "ACK ✓"), unless the restore itself failed after a successful push. Side effect: Write All Data now ends on "All Data written to device." instead of "ACK ✓".
- **`c18d565` — nav (B11 + flush race).** Every nav-tab switch calls `restoreDeviceModeForTab(dest)` (select), whatever `editMode` says. Clicking PROG while on PROG still does nothing (#39). DRUMS → PROG with PROG clean now uses the full select sequence instead of a bare `4E 03` (owner's choice). Leaving MULTI/GLOBAL awaits the flushed sync (the debouncer's `flush()` now returns its promise) under the freeze overlay, then restores.

**Verification:**
- `npx vitest run`: 382/382 across all 12 files (channel, effectLayout, encoder, factoryBanks, parser, sysex, controls, drumCrossReference, initCombi, initProgram, store, theme).
- `node --check` passes on the extracted module script of each of the three commits.
- **Fake Web MIDI comparison** (untracked harness copies, timestamps rounded to 10ms), 21 steps on `main` and the branch:
  - **Identical streams:** PROG→MULTI→GLOBAL→DRUMS, PROG→COMBI, COMBI→PROG, PROG→PROG (nothing sent), Load Global on GLOBAL (no restore), Patch Browser from MULTI → Cancel.
  - **Intended differences only:** DRUMS→PROG clean (`4E 02`, `C0 00`, +100ms `4E 03`); B11: MULTI → channel change → PROG (`main` sends nothing; branch sends the select); B11/#62: dirty PROG → DRUMS → channel change → PROG (`main` nothing; branch a bare `4E 03`); Discard (`4E 02` before `C0`, +100ms); B8: Load Multi/Global on PROG and Load Drums on COMBI (`main` leaves the device in Multi/Global; branch resyncs PROG/COMBI afterwards with correct statuses); Load Drums on GLOBAL (one extra `4E 05`, `'drumsTab'` → `'globalTab'`); Write All Data (`4E 02` before `C0`); B3: Write All Data with the Multi push NAKed (`main` stops in Multi; branch restores, NAK status kept); Browser from PROG → Combinations → Cancel (`4E 02` before `C0`); flush race MULTI → PROG and GLOBAL → COMBI (the dump now goes out before the destination's Mode Change).
  - **Edge cases (branch):** flush with a silent device holds nav on MULTI under the overlay, the overlay hides for "No response", and the PROG select follows the OK. Dirty PROG → MULTI → Abandoned Edits → Discard sends the #114 resync and then `4E 04`. With no port, nav sends nothing and stays silent; Patch Browser Cancel shows the no-output status.
- **Smoke test:** every tab and sub-tab renders with Factory Bank A loaded, with per-sub-tab visible element counts identical to `main`. Menus, the four Help modals and the Patch Browser open and close. No console errors from the branch.

**Hardware checklist (owner, 2026-10-02, via the pushed branch):**
- **Problem 1 confirmed on `main`:** after Write All Data from PROG, the Multi Track on the editor's channel was retuned by the resync's Program Change. The Track was on Bank G, so `C0 00` selected G01 (Piano): Bank G is shown one-indexed, so G01 is raw 0 (Landmine #33). On the branch the Track keeps the file's program, and the next PROG edit lands.
- **Pass:** Load Multi/Global on PROG and Load Drums on COMBI (statuses correct, edits land afterwards); MULTI → channel change → PROG; a PROG → COMBI → MULTI → GLOBAL → DRUMS → PROG round with edits; DRUMS → PROG clean; Patch Browser from PROG → Combinations → audition → Cancel, and from MULTI; Discard and Initialize Patch.
- **B11 dirty-PROG case:** pass on retest. Edit PROG → DRUMS → change the editor's header Ch selector → PROG: the PROG edits are intact and the next edit lands. The first attempt changed a MULTI Track's MIDI channel by mistake, which has no DRUMS equivalent.
- **Flush race, untestable by hand:** the sync completes faster than a second click. Covered on the fake port only.
- **B3 failure path:** with SysEx disabled, Write All Data → "No response" → OK; after re-enabling SysEx, the first PROG edit showed "Parameter Change Not Received", and after OK editing worked. This is the expected recovery: the restore after the failure couldn't reach the device (its Mode Changes were dropped, but the Program Change, a channel message, got through), so the first Parameter Change NAKed, and the NAK handler re-entered Prog Edit and resent it (Landmine #4).

Landmines #38, #54, #62 and #112 updated; new #119 (`HW` after this check), #120.

## Critical Discovery #193 — Audit T2 B9: Imports and Bank Writes Now Advance the Clean Baseline

**Context:** Optimization Plan Workstream C, tier T2, branch `refactor/audit-t2-clean-baseline`, finding B9 (⚑ Landmine #113). Fourth of the seven T2 branches.

**The bug (reproduced on the fake port against `main`; all 9 cases failed):** paths whose data then matches the device used `store.replaceProgram`/`replaceCombi`, which leave the clean baseline (`cleanSnapshot`) at the old data. An edit followed by Discard then reverted the editor, and resynced the device's edit buffer, to stale pre-import data.

**Fix:**
- **`91bce66` — imports and confirmed loads.** Import From Device: Current Program/Combination (`commitProgram`/`commitCombi` on the current slot) and All Programs/Combinations (new `commitAllPrograms`/`commitAllCombis`). FILE → Load 1 Program/1 Combination: commit after the Write Request completes. FILE → Load All Programs/All Combinations: commit after a confirmed "Write to Device". "Not Now" and failed writes still use `replace*`, so those merges stay discardable. All Data's `loadSnapshot` already sets the baseline. Load 1 Program/1 Combination with no bank loaded now stops before the file picker with a status message; previously `replaceProgram` threw uncaught inside the destination picker's callback.
- **`6477406` — Device → Write All Data / All Programs / All Combinations** (the same failure, found while fixing B9 and included). These write the editor's copy, *including unsaved edits*, but left those edits dirty with the baseline behind. A Discard after a successful bank write reverted past what was now stored on the device. A confirmed write now commits the written programs/combis. `commitAllPrograms`/`commitAllCombis` refresh the Write/Discard buttons (`updateActionButtons`) and skip a bank that isn't loaded (e.g. a programs-only file loaded cold).
- Note on Current Program/Combination: Func=10/19 return the device's current edit buffer, so the imported data is what the device is playing. That is the right baseline after an explicit import.

**Verification:**
- `npx vitest run`: 382/382 across all 12 files (channel, effectLayout, encoder, factoryBanks, parser, sysex, controls, drumCrossReference, initCombi, initProgram, store, theme). `store.js` is unchanged; `commitProgram`/`commitCombi` are already covered.
- `node --check` on the extracted module script of each commit: passes.
- **Fake Web MIDI test**, with Factory Bank B as the "device" and Bank A in the editor. The fake answers the four dump requests with Bank B dumps saved by the app itself. Each case: load Bank A → import/load+write Bank B → toggle a control → Discard → compare the Func=40/49 dump that Discard sends with Bank B's. On the branch, all 8 import/load cases resend Bank B's data, and after Write All Data with an unsaved edit Discard is disabled (nothing dirty). On `main`, all 8 resend Bank A's and Discard stays enabled. With no bank loaded, Load 1 Program/Combination shows the new status and opens no picker. No uncaught errors.
- MIDI streams: no send changed (store and button state only).
- **Smoke test:** every tab and sub-tab renders, with visible element counts identical to `main`. Menus, the four Help modals and the Patch Browser work. No console errors from the branch.

**Hardware checklist (owner, 2026-10-05, via the pushed branch):** all 7 checks pass: Import Current/All Programs and Combinations, Load 1 Program, Load All Programs → Write to Device, Write All Data with an unsaved edit, and Load 1 Program with no bank loaded.
- **Expected, documented, not a bug:** Load All Programs → "Not Now" → edit → Discard reverted to the editor's earlier data and resynced the device's *edit buffer* with it. That data differed from the device's stored programs, because the editor's bank had itself been loaded without writing. Switching patches on the device then reloaded the device's own stored data. "Not Now" deliberately leaves the editor and the device different; Discard reverts to the editor's baseline and only ever touches the edit buffer, never device memory (Landmine #114). Accepted by the owner as an anomaly the user creates on purpose.

Landmine #113 updated.

## Critical Discovery #194 — Audit T2 X6 + B6: One Dump-Request Helper; the Watchdog Sized to the Reply

**Context:** Optimization Plan Workstream C, tier T2, branch `refactor/audit-t2-dump-request`, findings X6 and B6. Fifth of the seven T2 branches. The design was approved by the owner before coding. B6 was changed from "re-arm on each received chunk" because Chrome delivers a SysEx message only once it is complete, so the ~35 KB All Data reply produces no event to re-arm on until it has fully arrived.

**Changes:**
- **`43e37eb` — `DUMP_REPLY_BYTES`** (`sysex.js`): the byte size of each dump the device sends in reply: program 194, allPrograms 18750, combi 162, allCombis 15550, multiEffects 41, multiTracks 244, drums 967, global 39, allData 35318. `factoryBanks.test.js` checks all nine against the encoder and the two hardware-captured replies in Bank A (All Data, Multi Expansion). A mutation check (global 39 → 40) fails the test. 384 tests.
- **`1034159` — X6:** a `DUMP_REQUESTS` table (`[func, pad]` requests, label, reply bytes) and `requestDumpFlow(kind)` replace the eight `doRequest…DumpFlow` functions. The dirty gate, sends and status/overlay text are unchanged. Net −101 lines. **B6:** `beginDumpRequest(message, replyBytes)` arms `armDumpRequestWatchdog()` with `ACK_TIMEOUT_BASE_MS + bytes × ACK_TIMEOUT_PER_BYTE_MS`. Each reply message re-arms it for the bytes still expected. The modal states the actual window instead of "12 seconds". The 500ms settle is unchanged.

**Verification:**
- `npx vitest run`: 384/384 across all 12 files (channel, effectLayout, encoder, factoryBanks, parser, sysex, controls, drumCrossReference, initCombi, initProgram, store, theme).
- `node --check` on the extracted module script: passes.
- **Fake Web MIDI, parity:** the fake port answered each request with Factory Bank A dumps saved by the app itself. Their sizes equal `DUMP_REPLY_BYTES`. For all 8 Import From Device items, `main` and the branch were identical: request bytes, overlay text, final status and every follow-on send (All Data's Patch Browser Mode Changes).
- **Timing, silent device:** single program `main` 12.0s → branch 5.1s ("within 5 seconds"); All Data `main` 12.0s → branch 19.2s ("within 19 seconds").
- **Slow interface** (All Data reply delivered 13s after the request): `main` shows "No response" at 12s and discards the late data. The branch completes ("Dump received — 100 programs, 100 combis").
- **Smoke test:** every tab and sub-tab renders, with visible element counts identical to `main`. Menus, the four Help modals and the Patch Browser work. No console errors from the branch.

**Observation, not fixed:** the 500ms settle doesn't check that both replies of a two-reply request (Multi; All Data + Func=68) arrived. A Func=50 without its Func=68 would be processed without Multi's Tracks. Not seen in practice.

**Hardware checklist (owner, 2026-10-05, via the pushed branch):** all pass. All 8 Import From Device items complete with their usual status, and All Data opens the Patch Browser. With SysEx disabled, Single Program shows "No response" after ~5s ("within 5 seconds") and All Data after ~19s ("within 19 seconds").

## Critical Discovery #195 — Audit T2 B4: Both "No response" Modals Name Both Channels; Retry on Dump Requests

**Context:** Optimization Plan Workstream C, tier T2, branch `refactor/audit-t2-no-response-modals`, finding B4 (owner's expanded spec). Sixth of the seven T2 branches. The design was approved by the owner, with two corrections to the front-panel pages.

**Correction (owner, 2026-10-05):** on the X5D/X5DR, SysEx reception is **[GLOBAL] page 02D**, EX: ENA, not "02E (MIDI FILTER)" as Getting Started, Troubleshooting and both modals said since Archive #181/#185 (taken then from the owner's notes and never checked against the device). The Global MIDI Channel is **[GLOBAL] page 02A, CH**. The page name "MIDI FILTER" was dropped because it hasn't been confirmed for 02D.

**Changes:**
- **`e0dccc8` — modals.** Both "No response from device" modals (the send timeout `promptNoResponseRetry` and the dump-request watchdog) share `NO_RESPONSE_SYSEX_TEXT` (page 02D) and `noResponseChannelText()`: the X5DR's Global MIDI Channel ([GLOBAL] 02A, CH) must match the editor's Ch menu, top right, "currently Ch N" from the live selector, and the device silently ignores other channels. The dump modal used to say "Global MIDI Channel (1)", which could mean either the device's or the editor's. The dump-request modal is now **Retry / OK**: Retry re-runs the same Import From Device item via `requestDumpFlow(kind)` (`beginDumpRequest` records the kind and start time). It reports the time actually waited since the request. OK leaves the status as before.
- **`1cc9475` — Help.** Getting Started and Troubleshooting: 02E (MIDI FILTER) → 02D; every mention of the device's Global MIDI Channel gives Global page 02A, CH.

**Verification:**
- `npx vitest run`: 384/384 across all 12 files (channel, effectLayout, encoder, factoryBanks, parser, sysex, controls, drumCrossReference, initCombi, initProgram, store, theme). No module changed.
- `node --check` on the extracted module script of each commit: passes.
- **Fake Web MIDI, editor on Ch 3:**
  - Import Single Program with a silent device → OK/Retry modal, "currently Ch 3", 02D and 02A present, no 02E, "within 5 seconds", overlay gone.
  - Retry while still silent → the request is resent (on channel 3, `F0 42 32 36 10 F7`) under the overlay, and the modal returns.
  - Device answering → Retry → "Current program dump received — A00 refreshed."
  - OK → status stays "No response…", nothing more sent.
  - The send-timeout modal (Load Global, silent) shows the same channel and page text with the overlay hidden, and Retry → "Global settings loaded and written to device." The Retry/OK flow is unchanged.
- **Smoke test:** every tab and sub-tab renders, with element counts identical to `main`. Menus and all four Help modals open (Getting Started/Troubleshooting contain 02D and 02A, not 02E). The Patch Browser works. No console errors from the branch.

**Hardware checklist (owner, 2026-10-05, via the pushed branch):** pass: the channel wording ("currently Ch N", 02A, 02D), OK, Retry after re-enabling SysEx with the modal up, the send-timeout modal, and the 02D/02A steps in Help, checked against the device.
- **Finding:** with an *editor-side* channel mismatch, Retry is no use. The modal blocks the header, so the Ch menu can't be changed while it's open; the user has to choose OK, fix the Ch menu and start the import again. Retry still helps when the fix is on the device (its channel, SysEx, a cable).
- **Follow-up (`07773ca`, owner chose rewording over a Ch menu inside the modal):** both modals now end with `NO_RESPONSE_NEXT_STEPS_TEXT`: "If the editor's Ch setting is wrong, choose OK, change the Ch menu, then try again. Choose Retry after fixing the device (its channel, SysEx setting or cable)." Text only; the B4 harness run was repeated with identical results (384/384, `node --check` passes). Merged on the owner's approval without a further hardware pass.

## Critical Discovery #196 — Audit T2 B5: The Status Pill Shows Device Health

**Context:** Optimization Plan Workstream C, tier T2, branch `refactor/audit-t2-status-pill`, finding B5 (owner's expanded spec). Last of the seven T2 branches.

**Before:** `setDot(state)` accepted `'green'/'yellow'/'red'` but only distinguished grey (Disconnected) from everything else, so after a NAK or timeout the pill still read "Connected". The `'yellow'` set at the start of every Import was a no-op, and it also cleared any earlier state to "Connected".

**Change (`cf3e255`):** `setDeviceHealth(state)` with a `DEVICE_HEALTH` table (class, label, tooltip). It forces Disconnected whenever there is no output.
- **Disconnected / Connected** as before.
- **Amber "No response"** (`.no-response`, `--status-no-response: #e0a03c`): set by a timeout in `armAckReply`/`armWriteReply` (every send-and-await helper, including background syncs and best-effort resyncs) and by the dump-request watchdog.
- **Amber "Rejected"** (same colour): set by a NAK (Parameter Change NAK recovery, a NAKed dump via `armAckReply`, a NAK to a Write Request) and by the OSC-mode format error (Landmine #21).
- **Cleared to Connected by** the next ACK (generic or awaited), Write Completed, Write Error (the device answered; the status says Memory Protect), any received dump (including a parse error or "no snapshot to merge"), a port change and a channel change. `setSelectedOutput` resets it only when the port actually changes, so a hot-plug or the implicit-open `statechange` (Landmine #118) leaves it alone. The Import start no longer touches it.
- Live Parameter Changes are fire-and-forget, so silence after a live edit leaves the pill as it is (Landmine #115).
- Colour is a fixed amber, unthemed like `--status-connected`/`--status-disconnected`: the themes' `--warning-text` is blue in Cool Slate and lime in Acid. Markup tooltip: "No MIDI output selected". Troubleshooting's heading now names the new states.

**Verification:**
- `npx vitest run`: 384/384 across all 12 files (channel, effectLayout, encoder, factoryBanks, parser, sysex, controls, drumCrossReference, initCombi, initProgram, store, theme). No module changed.
- `node --check` on the extracted module script: passes.
- **Fake Web MIDI**, step by step:
  - startup → Connected;
  - Import Single Program, device silent → No response (modal up and after OK);
  - unrelated hot-plug → still No response;
  - next ACK (nav to MULTI) → Connected;
  - live edit into silence → still Connected;
  - Write In Place timeout → No response; channel change → Connected;
  - live-edit NAK → Rejected; the recovery resend's ACK → Connected;
  - Write Error (Memory Protect) → Connected, with the Memory Protect status;
  - Write All Data NAK → Rejected;
  - unplug → Disconnected; replug → Connected.
- Computed colour `rgb(224,160,60)` with dark text in Warm, Cool and Acid; screenshot checked at 1440px.
- **Smoke test:** every tab and sub-tab renders, with element counts identical to `main`. Menus, the four Help modals and the Patch Browser work. No console errors from the branch.

**Note for the owner:** in Warm Graphite the amber sits close to the orange accent (`#ffab4a`). The pill's position and label set it apart, but the colour can be changed if it reads as an accent button.

## Critical Discovery #197 — FILE → Load All Data/Programs/Combinations Accept Any File (Audit B12)

**Context:** after T2 was complete (Archive #196), the owner asked what happens when the file picked doesn't match the Load item chosen (e.g. FILE → Load → All Programs, then a Drums file). No code changed in this investigation; the fix is finding B12.

**Method:** the fake Web MIDI harness on `main` at `fbeb833`. For each of the 8 FILE → Load items, Factory Bank A was loaded, then each of 9 files was fed to the file picker: All Data (Func=50 + 68), All Programs (4C), All Combinations (4D), 1 Program (40), 1 Combination (49), Multi (55 + 68), Drums (52), Global (51), all saved by the app from Bank A, plus a non-Korg SysEx message (`F0 41 …`). Every write prompt was answered "Not Now" and every picker cancelled. Afterwards the editor's programs, combinations, drums and global were saved and compared with Bank A's.

**Results:**
- **Load 1 Program, 1 Combination, Multi, Drums, Global:** wrong files are refused and the editor is unchanged, but the refusal is only a status-bar line ("Load error: file does not contain Drums Data (Func=52)."). Files that contain the needed data are accepted silently: All Data → Drums/Global/Multi, and All Programs/All Data → the 1 Program source picker.
- **Load All Data, All Programs, All Combinations:** no check. A file lacking the expected data falls through to `store.loadSnapshot(snap)`, which replaces the editor's entire contents. Status reads "Loaded: x.syx (0 programs, 0 combis)", PROG shows "Load a .syx file or use Import From Device to begin.", and the prompt "Write ALL PROGRAMS/COMBINATIONS/DATA to the X5DR?" follows. With the editor emptied, Save All Programs still produced a full 18,750-byte (blank) bank, so "Write to Device" would most likely overwrite every program on the device (not attempted). Saving Drums/Global failed ("Cannot read properties of null (reading 'masterTune')"). Seen for every mismatched file, including the non-Korg one.
- **Load All Programs ← 1 Program file (and Combinations ← 1 Combination):** `replaceProgram` runs for slot 0, then throws on slot 1: "Load error: \"undefined\" is not valid JSON".
- `parseSnapshot` ignores messages it doesn't recognise and never checks the `F0 42 3g 36` header, so a non-X5DR file parses to an empty snapshot.

**Owner's decision (2026-10-05):** B12, spec in the findings doc. A warning box appears *every* time the file doesn't match the operation, including when the operation is possible (Cancel / Continue). Refusals are also warning boxes, not status-bar text, so the user can't believe an operation completed when it didn't. To be done on `refactor/audit-t2-load-file-check` in a new session, with the owner's hardware checklist before merge.

## Critical Discovery #198 — Audit B12: FILE → Load Checks the File Before Touching the Editor

**Context:** Optimization Plan Workstream C, branch `refactor/audit-t2-load-file-check`, finding B12 (owner's spec in the findings doc; the bug is Archive #197).

**Owner's decisions before coding (2026-10-05):** the box wording was approved with one change: say "compatible", not "X5DR", since the editor also serves the X5, X5D and 05R/W (refusal title "Not a compatible file", body "This file can't be loaded as All Programs: it isn't a compatible SysEx file."). The file is picked and checked first, then the unsaved-edits check. The other status-bar-only failures in these flows become warning boxes too. Box text uses the menu's own labels, "Single Program"/"Single Combination".

**Change:**
- `1573932` — new `src/midi/loadFileCheck.js`:
  - `classifySyxFile(messages)` keeps only messages with an `F0 42 3g 36` header (any channel). It returns `compatibleMessages`, the set of dump `funcs` (40 49 4C 4D 50 51 52 55 68), a `kind` (one Load item's type, `mixed`, `no-dumps` or `not-compatible`) and `contents` labels.
  - `checkLoadFile(item, messages)` returns `outcome` (`match`/`possible`/`refuse`), the box text, the refusal's status line and `loadMessages`, which are the only dumps the item uses. Parsing only those means a stray dump elsewhere in the file can't override the one being loaded (`parseSnapshot` lets a later dump win).
  - "Possible" follows the spec table, and also covers a mixed file that holds the needed dump (e.g. All Programs from a 4C + 4D file).
  - Multi: 55 + 68 matches; 50 + 68 is possible; 50, 55 or 68 alone is refused.
  - `loadFileCheck.test.js`: 111 tests. They cover every cell of the spec table (8 items × 10 test files), the exact wording, every channel, other manufacturers and Korg families, mixed files, files with no dumps, and the hardware-captured factory dumps parsed through `loadMessages`.
- `f3c2f2b` — `src/index.html`:
  - `pickAndParseSyxFile` became `pickAndCheckSyxFile(item)`. It picks the file, runs the check, then:
    - on a refusal, sets the status line and shows `showAlertModal`;
    - on a possible file, shows `showConfirmModal`, Cancel → "Load cancelled — editor unchanged.";
    - otherwise parses only `loadMessages`.
  - Each of the 8 Load flows now picks and checks the file first and then calls `afterDirtyCheck(proceed)`.
  - `refuseWithoutLoadedData` gives a "No data loaded" box *before* the picker for Single Program/Combination, Multi, Drums and Global. Multi/Drums/Global used to fail with "Load error: No snapshot loaded".
  - `reportLoadError` turns any other load error into a "Load failed" box, and the status bar repeats it.
  - The status-only refusals and the `snap.programs`/`combis` guards are gone, because the check guarantees the data is there.
  - A cold Load All Programs/Combinations still calls `loadSnapshot`, after the check, with `onlyCategory(snap, …)`, so an All Data file loaded that way gives the same result as a real All Programs/Combinations file.
  - Factory Sounds A/B are untouched.

**Verification:**
- `npx vitest run`: 495/495 across 13 files (channel, effectLayout, encoder, factoryBanks, loadFileCheck, parser, sysex, controls, drumCrossReference, initCombi, initProgram, store, theme).
- `node --check` on the extracted module script: passes.
- **Fake Web MIDI load matrix**, run on `main` and on the branch. The test-only harness was injected into untracked copies, which were deleted afterwards.
  - Setup: Factory Bank A was loaded, and the app's own saves were captured: All Data 50+68 (35,562 bytes), All Programs 4C, All Combinations 4D, Single Program 40, Single Combination 49, Multi 55+68, Drums 52, Global 51. A non-Korg file (`F0 41 10 42 12 40 00 7F 00 41 F7`) was added.
  - Each of the 72 cells (8 items × 9 files) started from Factory Bank B, so a real load shows up as a change.
  - For each cell the run recorded the boxes, the status history and the MIDI sent. It also hashed programs, combinations, drums, global and multi after the load, each from its own save. Bank A and Bank B have the same Global and Multi, so loads of those were confirmed by the MIDI sent (F51, F55 + F68).
- **`main`:** reproduces #197 exactly:
  - All Data/Programs/Combinations ← any wrong file: "(0 programs, 0 combis)", every category changed, saves failed, and a write prompt followed.
  - All Programs/Combinations ← a single program/combination file: "\"undefined\" is not valid JSON".
  - The other items: status-bar-only refusals.
- **Branch:**
  - All 55 refuse cells show the right box: "Can't load this file as …" naming the contents and the right menu item, or "Not a compatible file". The editor is byte-identical, nothing is sent and no write prompt follows.
  - All 9 possible cells show the Cancel/Continue box. Cancel → byte-identical, nothing sent.
  - Continue → All Programs/Combinations replace only that category; Single Program/Combination open the source picker; Multi/Drums/Global send F55 + F68 / F52 / F51.
  - The 15 load paths compared (the 8 matches, plus 7 possible cells with Continue) have the same hashes, MIDI and status as `main`; the only difference is the box on the possible cells.
- **Cold start:** the "No data loaded" boxes appear for Single Program/Combination, Multi, Drums and Global. All Programs ← All Data, Continue → "(100 programs, 0 combis)", the same as a real All Programs file loaded cold.
- **Unsaved edits:**
  - A refused file, or Cancel, leaves the edit dirty, and no Unsaved Edits modal appears.
  - Continue brings up the Unsaved Edits modal afterwards; Stay loads nothing.
- **Unexpected error:** shows the "Load failed" box.
- **Smoke test:** every tab and sub-tab (PROG ×6, COMBI ×3, DRUMS ×2, MULTI ×3, GLOBAL) renders with element counts and text identical to `main`. No console errors.

**Not changed (noted):** the check reads only the header and Func byte. A truncated or corrupt dump of the right type still parses (as before). After a Multi/Drums/Global load, a NAKed device push is still reported only in the status bar (timeouts already get the Retry modal, Landmine #115).

New Landmine #122; Landmine #42's "Open (B12)" note removed.

**Hardware checklist (owner, 2026-10-05, via the pushed branch):** all 7 pass: each correct file type loads through its own item with no extra box and writes; a Drums file via Load → All Programs is refused with the editor unchanged and no write prompt; an All Data file via Load → All Programs warns, Cancel leaves the editor unchanged, Continue loads only the programs and writes; Load → Multi from an All Data file warns and writes; a refused file keeps unsaved edits with no Unsaved Edits prompt, Continue brings it up; a non-Korg file gives "Not a compatible file"; a fresh page gives "No data loaded" before the picker. Merged on the owner's approval. **Audit T2, including B12, is complete.**

- The "`file://` will not work" claim is in the **Project Plan's Phase 4 text**, not ADR-0002 §6a. §6a assumes `file://` works and asks for verification. Landmine #103's wording ("ADR-0002 §6a's claim") is to be corrected when the test is run (Release Plan A2).
- The Project Plan's Phase 4 build bullet is out of date: it says inline `sysex.js`/`store.js`, and there are now 11 modules. Its "Windows setup notes (loopMIDI)" item and the task list's README note (IAC/loopMIDI/MIDIflow) are obsolete, because the editor talks to the interface directly.
- Personal/machine references in docs to be published: the task-list app, the two Macs' model names, the MIDI interface's brand and model, iCloud and the notes app appear in the Archive, Progress Log, Project Plan, Landmines (#95) and `00_INDEX.md`. No personal email address, `/Users/` path or username was found in docs or `src/`.

**Owner's decisions (2026-10-05):**
1. **Repo:** rename the current repo to `x5dr-editor-private` (private, archive) and create a new public `x5dr-editor` from a single initial commit under the noreply address. Development continues in the public repo.
   - *Why not the 2026-09-30 filter-repo plan:* the cleaned history would carry different hashes from those cited in the docs anyway, so it adds steps without benefit.
   - *Why not an in-place rewrite plus force-push:* GitHub keeps replaced commits viewable by hash, and the docs cite about 31 hashes.

The scrub is a one-time, recorded exception to this Archive's append-only rule, with substitutions only and owner diff review. Everything else stays in the private archive (list in Release Plan §10).
3. **Korg material:** ship the transcription `.md` files with a © Korg notice. Ship Factory Banks A/B, marked as Korg's data (not MIT) and removable on request. Add "not affiliated with Korg" to README and About. The PDFs stay private.
4. **Third-party `.syx`:** private. Tests are retargeted to the hardware captures before the cut. `<identified user>_X5D.syx` may return with permission and credit.
5. **Deploy:** `dist/` stays gitignored. CI runs tests and the build on every push and PR. Deploy to Pages runs on a published Release, which also gets `dist/index.html` attached.
6. **Address:** `https://baylo1.github.io/x5dr-editor/`, no custom domain. This is final, because a later origin change loses users' installs, MIDI permission and settings.
7. **Versioning:** SemVer and CHANGELOG; `APP_VERSION` = `package.json` version, enforced by the build test. Launch with an unannounced `v1.0.0-rc.1` beta, then `v1.0.0`.
8. **Offline:** no service worker in v1.0.
9. **Fonts:** embedded in the build (base64 WOFF2, SIL OFL); `src/` keeps the CDN link.

## Critical Discovery #200 — Release Plan A1: The Single-File Build

**Context:** Release Plan step A1 (Optimization Plan Workstream D), branch `build/single-file`.

**Change (`e0ce670`):**
- `scripts/build.mjs` (Node built-ins only) reads `src/index.html` and parses the named imports of its one module script, recursively. It orders the 11 modules topologically: effectLayout, sysex, parser, loadFileCheck, initProgram, initCombi, encoder, drumCrossReference, store, theme, controls.
- Each module becomes `const __m_<path> = (() => { …; return { exports }; })();`, and every `import { a, b as c } from './x.js'` becomes `const { a, b: c } = __m_x;`. Everything goes into the one inline `<script type="module">`.
- The build refuses anything it can't inline (Landmine #123): it checks every imported name is exported, detects cycles, and fails if `APP_VERSION` ≠ `package.json` version.
- **Fonts (Release Plan D9):** the Google Fonts comment, preconnect and stylesheet lines are replaced with three base64 `@font-face` rules (Latin `unicode-range`) from `src/fonts/`. Inter is the variable file covering 400–700; IBM Plex Mono is 400 and 500. The OFL texts are copied to `dist/fonts/`; the WOFF2 files are not, since they're embedded. The SVG effect diagrams ask for Plex Mono 600, which was never loaded from Google either, so it is synthesized in both builds.
- The build copies `manifest.json` (and `icons/` once B1 adds them) and stamps `<!-- Built by scripts/build.mjs from <hash>, version <v>. Edit src/, not this file. -->`.
- `npm run build`; `dist/` added to `.gitignore`; `.claude/launch.json` gets `x5dr-dist` (`npx serve dist`, port 5520).
- About's font line no longer says "loaded from Google Fonts".
- **One false positive fixed during the work:** the dynamic-`import()` check first matched the words "import (Landmine #42)" in a `store.js` comment. It now requires `import(` followed by a string.
- Output: `dist/index.html` 934 KB (src 729 KB, plus about 105 KB of fonts and the inlined modules).

**Verification:**
- `npx vitest run`: 517/517 across 14 files (channel, effectLayout, encoder, factoryBanks, loadFileCheck, parser, sysex, drumCrossReference, initCombi, initProgram, store, theme, controls, and the new `scripts/build.test.js` with 22 tests). The new tests check:
  - one module script, no import/export statements or module paths, and `node --check` passes;
  - the inlined IIFEs, evaluated, export exactly the real modules' names and equal constants, plus a `buildModeChange` spot check;
  - both factory-bank base64 constants are identical to `src/`, and each font is embedded byte-for-byte with no Google Fonts reference;
  - `APP_VERSION` matches, the manifest ships, and the SPDX line and stamp are present;
  - 12 refusal cases: default and namespace import, dynamic import, `export default`/list/`*`, `fetch`, a missing export, a missing module, a bare specifier, a version mismatch and a cycle. A comment containing "import (" is accepted.
- `node --check` passes on both the src and dist module scripts.
- **Browser, `dist/` on port 5520 vs `src/` on 5510, Browser pane at 1440×900:**
  - No console errors on load. Getting Started auto-opens. The only resource requests are data URIs (no Google). All three faces show `loaded`. With MIDI permission unavailable in the pane, the status bar reads "Web MIDI access denied …" and the port list "— Web MIDI unavailable —".
  - Factory Bank A loads (100 programs, 100 combis) with the Write All Data prompt (Not Now).
  - Every tab and inner tab renders with no errors: PROG ×6, COMBI ×3, DRUMS kits, MULTI ×3, GLOBAL.
  - With the file picker stubbed in the page, all 8 FILE → Save items produce **byte-identical output on `dist` and `src`** (same length and hash), e.g. All Data 50+68 = 35,562 bytes, matching Archive #198.
  - All 5 Help items open their dialogs. About and Copy Diagnostics show version 1.0.0. The clipboard fallback ("copy this manually") appears because the pane page isn't focused.
  - PROG › VDA screenshots of the two builds are indistinguishable.
- **Owner hardware smoke test on the built file:** pending. The branch is pushed; see the Progress Log.

**Not done here (later steps):** the `file://` test (A2), the CI/deploy workflows (A3), and an optional ADR-0009 "Distribution build and hosting", best written after A2's result.

## Critical Discovery #201 — Placement Diagrams Lose Their Arrows on COMBI/MULTI (Duplicate SVG Marker IDs)

**Reported by the owner (2026-10-06)** while hardware-testing A1: the Serial Placement diagram on the COMBI and MULTI Effect tabs had no arrows, while PROG's did. The owner wants exactly four diagrams (Serial, Parallel 1–3), all with arrows, shared by every Effect tab.

**Cause:** there already *was* only one set of four diagrams. `EFFECT_PLACEMENT_DIAGRAM_SVG` is rendered by the shared `buildPlacementDiagram`, and every SVG has arrowhead `<marker>`s. But each template used a fixed marker id (`arrow-eff-serial`, `arrow-eff-p1`…`-p3`). When two tabs showed the same placement, the page held two elements with that id. `url(#arrow-eff-serial)` resolves to the first one in the document, which was inside the hidden PROG panel, and markers inside a `display: none` subtree don't render. Confirmed in the Browser pane on `src` with Factory Bank A: COMBI's visible Serial diagram referenced PROG's marker (`resolvesToOwnSvg=false`, 2 elements with the id). MULTI's Parallel 3 looked fine only because no other tab showed Parallel 3. Any placement on any tab could break the same way; which one depended on what the other tabs were showing.

**Fix (`b05655a`, branch `fix/effect-placement-arrows`):** `buildPlacementDiagram` appends a per-call counter to every `arrow-eff-*` id in the template (`arrow-eff-serial-3`), so each copy references its own markers. These diagrams are the only SVGs in the app that use `url(#…)`. New Landmine #124.

**Verification (Browser pane, `src`, Factory Bank A):**
- `node --check` on the module script passes.
- On PROG, COMBI and MULTI › Effect, each of Serial, Parallel 1, 2 and 3 was selected in turn. Every visible diagram's `marker-end` references resolved to a marker inside its own SVG (9 / 11 / 9 / 13 arrows), and all marker ids in the page were unique.
- Screenshot: COMBI › Effect › Serial shows its arrows.
- Owner visual check before merge.

## Critical Discovery #204 — FILE → Load/Save Become One "Data File…" Checkbox Dialog (Decision)

**Context (2026-10-06):** loading `<identified user>_X5D.syx` (Func 4C + 4D + 52 + 51, no Multi) through FILE → Load → All Data was refused under B12's rule (Archive #198, Landmine #122). I first proposed letting Load → All Data accept any bank-level file, with a box listing the contents, per-type merge, and a write prompt limited to what was loaded. The owner extended it: replace the per-type Load and Save items with one dialog listing every type, with a checkbox each, and grey out the types that aren't available.

**Owner's decisions:**
- Adopt it as Release Plan step **C1c** (branch `feature/file-data-dialog`), before C2.
- Menu label **"Data File…"** for both Load and Save.
- Factory Sounds A/B and Single Program/Combination stay as they are.
- Keep the agreed rules: merge per type; write only what was loaded; bank-level types only.
- The Device menu's per-type items stay for v1.0; the same dialog for the Device menu is a v1.1 item.

**Design points agreed with the proposal (detail in Release Plan C1c):**
- Multi, Drums and Global are written to the device on load, as today; they have no separate editor copy (Landmine #58). The dialog says so next to those checkboxes.
- The post-load Write / Not Now prompt covers only the Programs/Combinations that were loaded, sent as separate All Programs/All Combinations dumps. It never builds an All Data dump from a mix of file and editor contents, which could push stale or blank Multi settings to the device.
- Save with all five ticked keeps today's Func 50 + 68 file. A partial selection saves one dump per type.
- Multi is unavailable from an All Data file with no Multi expansion (Func 50 without 68), as under B12.
- `loadFileCheck.js` becomes a per-type availability check, and Landmine #122 will be rewritten.

  - `encoder.test.js`: the `buildSingleProgramDump`, `snapshotToSyx`, `combisToSyx` and `programsToSyx` round trips → Bank B.
  - `sysex.test.js`: the `encodeCombiToBytes`/`buildSingleCombiDump` round-trip block (6 tests) → Bank B.
  - `parser.test.js`: `parseProgram`/`parseCombi`/`parseGlobal`/`parseDrums` → Bank B.
  - `effectLayout.test.js`: the real-bank round trip runs over Banks A and B (was A + the identified user's file + SendCD).
- Comments naming the three third-party files (tests and `effectLayout.js`, comments only) now say "private archive". No other mention remains in `src/` or `scripts/`.

**Needs approval (materially changed tests; nothing skipped or removed):**
1. The parser "Black Duck" check (the identified user's A00) now checks Bank B 00 "Sunrise". It is still OSC mode 1 (Double), so the mode check keeps its meaning.
2. The separate-message file test (was `parseSnapshot — <identified user>_X5D.syx`, the only file made of 52 + 51 + 4D + 4C dumps) now builds those four messages from the Bank A capture with the app's own builders. Their lengths (967 / 39 / 15,550 / 18,750 bytes) equal the identified user's file's. All original assertions are kept, plus one new test: each section parses back to the same data as the All Data capture. A device-made separate-message file is no longer tested.
3. `effectLayout`'s real-bank round trip:
   - The tolerance "≤4 normalized bytes per file" is now an exact count per bank (A = 2, B = 1), and each tolerated byte must equal Balance L.
   - One named exception: Bank B Combi 4 "Mr. Tone" (below).
   - A new synthetic test (a Bank A program with Eff1 = Dual Mono Delay (15), Eff2 = No Effect (0)) covers the types only the identified user's file stored.

**Effect coverage (Landmine #108):**
- Before: 1,200 stored effects over 39 types. SendCD has exactly Bank A's type set and the same two Exciter mismatches, so it looks like a variant of the factory bank, and the independent coverage was nearer 800.
- After: 800 stored effects over 41 types, plus the synthetic 15 and 0.
  - Lost: types 0, 11, 15 and 30. Types 11 and 30 share layouts that are still covered (10/12 and 31). Type 15 now has only the synthetic test.
  - Gained: types 7, 8, 12, 16, 25 and 46.
  - Never stored in any bank: 9, 23 and 44.

**Found:** Bank B Combi 4 "Mr. Tone", Eff1 type 31 (a single-control Balance type), stores Balance L = 50 and R = 100. It is the first non-Exciter case of L ≠ R: Bank A has 2, all Exciter; the identified user's file had 0. The editor saves single-control Balance as wet in both bytes (Landmine #108), so Write In Place of that combi changes the stored R byte from 100 to 50. Whether that is audible is untested (hardware check, not blocking).

**Verification:**
- `npx vitest run` before: 517/517 across 14 files.
- After: 518/518 across the same 14 files (parser 52 → 53).
- With the three third-party files moved out of `reference_sysex/`: 518/518, 0 skipped. The files were then restored; they stay tracked in this private repo and are excluded at the public cut (Release Plan §10).

## Critical Discovery #206 — Release Plan C1b: A Box When MIDI Permission Is Refused

**Context:** Release Plan step C1b (Archive #203, A2 check 4), branch `fix/midi-permission-denied`, commit `845648b`.

**Change (`src/index.html`, `initMidi`):**
- When `requestMIDIAccess({sysex: true})` rejects, a warning box appears; the status bar keeps its line.
  - `NotAllowedError`/`SecurityError`: the box is titled "MIDI access is blocked" and says how to allow MIDI from the address bar.
  - Any other error: "MIDI is unavailable", giving the browser's message.
  - Buttons: **Reload** / **Close**.
- `watchMidiPermission()` subscribes to `navigator.permissions.query({ name: 'midi', sysex: true })`. When the state leaves `denied` (`granted`, or `prompt` after a reset), it calls `initMidi()` again. If that succeeds while the box is still up, the box closes itself.
- Where the permission can't be watched, the box text says "Then click Reload" instead of "The MIDI ports appear as soon as you allow it".

**Verification:**
- `node --check` on the module script passes. Vitest 517/517 across 14 files (no tests touch this code).
- **Browser pane** (where MIDI is denied; `permissions.query` reports `denied`): the box appears above Getting Started with the watching wording, Close dismisses it, and there are no console errors.
- **Owner checklist** (sent with the built file), Chrome and Edge, over `file://` and `http://localhost`:
  - Block → the box appears.
  - Allow from the address bar → do the ports appear and the box close by itself, or is Reload needed? This is the unknown for `file://`.
  - Reload works.
  - Allow normally → no box.

## Critical Discovery #207 — Release Plan A3: CI and Deploy Workflows

**Context:** Release Plan step A3 (D5), branch `ci/workflows`. The workflows were written by a subagent in its own worktree (`1247f7b`); the main session bumped the action versions (`317fab2`) and pushed.

**Change:**
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
  - Runs on a push to **any branch** (not only `main`, as the plan first said), on PRs to `main`, and by hand.
  - Steps: `npm ci`, `npx vitest run`, `npm run build`, then uploads `dist/` as the artifact `x5dr-editor-<branch>-<sha7>`, kept 30 days. `/` in branch names becomes `-`.
  - Writes a job summary saying how to download and open the build.
  - Why every branch: the owner's test computer has no npm, so every pushed branch needs a downloadable build. A push to a PR branch runs twice (push and PR), which is harmless.
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, on `release: published` (pre-releases included):
  - build: fails unless the tag minus `v` equals the `package.json` version, then runs tests and the build, and uploads the Pages artifact plus a copy of `index.html`.
  - deploy: `actions/deploy-pages`.
  - attach: `gh release upload --clobber`, which runs **only after a successful deploy**, so a Release never carries a file the site lacks.
  - Each job has only the permissions it needs; release and PR values reach scripts through `env:`.
- Action versions: `checkout@v7`, `setup-node@v7`, `upload-artifact@v7`, `download-artifact@v8`, `configure-pages@v6`, `upload-pages-artifact@v5`, `deploy-pages@v5`. The first run on `@v4` warned that those actions target the deprecated Node 20.
- `scripts/build.mjs` only needs `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, so a shallow checkout is enough.

**Verification:**
- Locally, from a clean `npm ci`: 517/517 across 14 files, and the build succeeds.
- GitHub Actions:
  - Run `37483107721` (`@v4`) passed in 20s with artifact `x5dr-editor-ci-workflows-1247f7b` (293 KB zipped).
  - Run `37483351085` (bumped actions) passed in 17s with no deprecation warning.
- `deploy.yml` can only be proven at E6. Before that: set Pages source = GitHub Actions (E5); add a `v*` tag rule to the `github-pages` environment if it rejects tag deploys; and don't publish a Release before E5, or the deploy fails.

**Note:** `ci.yml` only runs on branches that contain it. Until A3 is merged, other branches get no CI build.

## Critical Discovery #208 — Release Plan C1c: FILE → Load/Save → "Data File…"

**Context:** Release Plan step C1c (decision Archive #204), branch `feature/file-data-dialog`, commit `bd1af9f`. Branched from `fix/midi-permission-denied`, because both change `src/index.html`; the branch includes C1b. The dialog and box wording were sent to the owner for approval before merge.

**Change:**
- **Menu:**
  - Load: Factory Sounds Bank A, Factory Sounds Bank B, **Data File…**, Single Program, Single Combination.
  - Save: **Data File…**, Single Program, Single Combination.
  - The six bank-level items on each side are gone.
- **`loadFileCheck.js`:**
  - `checkDataFile(messages)` returns, for each of `DATA_TYPES` (programs, combis, multi, drums, global): whether it's available, the reason if not (the tooltip), and the messages to parse.
  - A type's own dump wins over the All Data dump: 4C, 4D, 52 and 51 before 50.
  - Multi needs 68 plus 55 or 50.
  - `isCompleteDump` checks the payload unpacks to the dump's size. Func 68 has no `00` byte after the Func: its payload starts at byte 5. A cut-short dump greys out its type ("This file's Programs data is incomplete.").
  - A file with no available type is refused with a box: not compatible; a single program/combination (pointing to its own menu item); no dumps; or only partial or incomplete data.
  - `checkLoadFile` now serves only Single Program/Combination. Its refusals point bank-level files to "Data File…".
  - `dataFileSaveName`/`dataFileSaveKind`.
- **Dialog** (`#modal-data-file`, `showDataFileDialog`):
  - One checkbox per type. Every available type starts ticked; an unavailable one is greyed out with its reason as the tooltip.
  - On Load, Multi, Drums and Global carry "— written to the X5DR on load".
  - OK is disabled when nothing is ticked, and Escape cancels (an `ESCAPE_ACTIONS` entry, Landmine #117).
- **Load → Data File…** (`doLoadDataFileFlow`):
  - Pick → check → dialog → (Programs or Combinations ticked: `afterDirtyCheck`).
  - Programs/Combinations merge per slot (Landmine #42). Multi/Drums/Global go through `replaceMulti`/`replaceDrums`/`replaceGlobal`.
  - When nothing is loaded yet, or the editor lacks a ticked bank type (e.g. Combinations after a Programs-only load), the flow does a `loadSnapshot` of what's there plus the ticked types. This also fixes a latent crash: the old cold Load All Programs followed by Load All Combinations called `replaceCombi` on `null`.
  - Then Multi/Drums/Global are pushed (`pushDataFileDeviceTypes`), with one `restoreActiveTabModeIfChanged` (Landmine #112). Any push without an ACK gets a "Not written to the X5DR" box.
  - Then the Write / Not Now prompt, covering only the loaded Programs/Combinations, sent as 4C then 4D (`promptWriteDataFileBanks`; a confirmed write commits, Landmine #113). A failed write gets a box naming the Device → Write to Device items to retry with; a failed 4C skips 4D.
  - The Patch Browser opens when Programs or Combinations were loaded.
  - `sendAllDataDumpAndAwaitAck` is no longer used by FILE → Load. Factory Sounds and Device → Write to Device → All Data still use it.
- **Save → Data File…** (`doSaveDataFileFlow`):
  - A type is available when the editor holds it: Programs/Combinations need 100 slots; Multi needs effects **and** tracks.
  - All five ticked: Func 50 + 68 (`X5DR_bank.syx`). Fewer: 4C, 4D, 55 + 68, 52, 51 in that order, named after the selection.
  - With nothing loaded: a "No data loaded" box.
- The Help "Back up first" line now names Save → Data File….

**Behaviour change to note:** with data already loaded, an All Data file now *merges* type by type, where Load → All Data used to `loadSnapshot` it. The loaded Programs/Combinations become the clean baseline only once written, as the old scoped loads did.

**Verification:**
- `npx vitest run`: 467/467 across 14 files. `loadFileCheck.test.js` went from 111 to 61:
  - Removed: the spec-table and wording tests for the six retired Load items.
  - Added: tests for `checkDataFile` (availability, sources, completeness, refusals, hardware captures), `isCompleteDump` and the Save helpers.
- `node --check` on the module script passes.
- **Browser pane, `src`, file pickers stubbed in the page:**
  - Save → Data File… with all five ticked, from Factory Bank A: 35,562 bytes, **SHA-256 identical** to the old Save → All Data code path (computed in Node from the same bank).
  - Each partial save gives the expected Funcs and names (4C 18,750 B; 4D 15,550; 55 + 68 285; 52 967; 51 39; 4C + 4D + 52 + 51 35,306). Save is disabled with nothing ticked. With nothing loaded, the "No data loaded" box appears.
  - Load, cold, a four-type file (4C + 4D + 52 + 51): Multi greyed ("Not in this file."), the others load. Drums/Global give the no-output box; then the Write prompt; Not Now; the Browser opens. Every tab renders, MULTI shows its placeholder, and there are no console errors.
  - Load: Multi-only file into existing data; a non-Korg file; a single program file; a truncated 4C next to a complete 51 (Programs greyed "incomplete", Global offered); All Data without 68 (Multi greyed, effects-only reason); Cancel ("Load cancelled — editor unchanged.").
  - With a PROG edit pending:
    - Drums + Global → no Unsaved Edits modal, and the edit survives.
    - Combinations → the Unsaved Edits modal appears; Stay loads nothing.
  - The Write to Device failure path with no output shows a box naming the retry items.
  - Single Program ← an All Programs file still offers the source picker. Single Combination ← a Drums file is refused, pointing to "Data File…".
- **Owner:** wording approval and the hardware checklist (sent with the built file).

**Docs:** Landmine #122 rewritten. The Project Context's File load/save paragraph is updated.

## Critical Discovery #214 — Release Plan C4: Redaction-Only Scrub of the Public Docs (the Archive's One Append-Only Exception)

**Context:** Release Plan step C4, branch `docs/public-scrub`. The docs D2 makes public are scrubbed of personal and machine references before the public cut. The owner approved the hit list, the wording and this **one-time exception to the append-only rule** on 2026-10-07, before any edit was made.

**Rules of the pass:**
- Redaction only: each change swaps a name for a neutral phrase and does not change what an entry says happened.
