## Critical Discovery #216 — Backup Policy for the Private and Public Repos (Release Plan E1, E6, G4, H1)

**Context:** 2026-10-07. The owner wants backups of both repos so GitHub isn't a single point of failure, and asked where they should live: the development Mac or the hardware-test Mac. Planning only; no code changed.

**Recommendation (written into the Release Plan; locations pending the owner's confirmation):**
- **Three copies of each repo:** GitHub; a mirror on the **hardware-test Mac**; and one off-machine `git bundle` file (external drive, or iCloud Drive as one file).
- **Why not the development Mac:** after E4 it already holds the private archive checkout (full history) and the public working copy. A backup on the same disk doesn't survive that disk failing, being lost or being wiped. The hardware-test Mac is a separate failure point.
- **Why bundles:** one self-checking file with every branch and tag (`git bundle verify`; `git clone <file>` restores it). It can be made on the development Mac and copied by AirDrop, so the hardware-test Mac needs no GitHub login to hold the private repo.
- **Never** inside the iCloud-synced project folder: sync copies deletions, and many small git files cause the Landmine #95 stall. A single bundle file in iCloud Drive is fine as the off-machine copy.
- **Not covered by git:** Issues and Release notes. A `gh issue list … --json` export is kept beside the public bundle; Release files are rebuilt from their tags.

**Schedule:**
- **E1:** private repo, once (it is frozen afterwards).
- **E6:** first public mirror on the hardware-test Mac, over HTTPS since the repo is public by then.
- **G4:** weekly `remote update` and Issues export with triage, plus a new bundle at every release (keep the last few, and always `v1.0.0` and `pre-public-cut`).
- **H1:** verify the private bundle when the private repo is archived.

**Change:** Release Plan E1 (backup steps, the policy, verification, and the location decision), E6 (first public backup), G4 (weekly and per-release refresh), H1 (verify on archive). E1's old single `--mirror` to `~/x5dr-editor-backup.git` "on a second disk" is replaced.

**Addition (same day, owner-approved):** the hardware-test Mac's existing working clone isn't the backup. At E1, once the bundle there verifies, it is checked for anything that exists only there (`git status`, `git stash list`, `git log --branches --not --remotes`). At E2 it is retired: deleted, or renamed and deleted after E6, because after E4 its `origin` would point at the unrelated new public repo. Live Server moves to the artifact folder. A fresh HTTPS clone is optional after E5. E3 adds: no commits from the hardware-test Mac, or set the noreply email there first.

## Critical Discovery #217 — Release Plan D1: Full Hardware Regression on the Built File (Mac, Chrome)

**Context:** 2026-10-08. Release Plan step D1. Build `50968b7` (`main`, version 1.0.0-rc.1, the CI artifact), served by Live Server on the hardware-test Mac in Chrome 154 (macOS 26.6.2). The session drove the editor through Claude in Chrome. A temporary in-page MIDI log (a wrapper on `MIDIOutput.prototype.send` plus an input listener) recorded every byte sent and received; reloading the page removes it. The owner did the listening, the front-panel steps, the hot-plug and the file dialogs. Device writes used A99 (program and combination) as the scratch slot; after Factory Sounds Bank B and the owner's `NewTest_All_X5DR_bank.syx`, the `file://` pass left the device on Factory Sounds Bank A (with a test program in A99).

**Results (http, Live Server):**

| Item | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Connection | Pass | "x5" auto-select; port kept by name across reload and hot-plug (Landmine #118); channel mismatch (Ch 2) gives silence, the box names Ch 2, amber pill; Ch 1 recovers. Pill states seen: Connected, Disconnected, No response, Rejected |
| 2. Import From Device | Pass, with F1/F2 | All Data (`0F`+`33` → `50`+`68`), All Programs, All Combinations, Single Program (in Prog Edit), Single Combination (in Combi Edit), Multi, Drums, Global |
| 3. PROG | Pass | Owner heard Easy (Octave), OSC (multisound), VDF (Cutoff), VDA (Level), Control (Pitch Bend Range 12 → octave bend), Effect (Dry/Wet). Type change sends offsets 0–6 + Balance; Dual-Balance (type 15) sends only PN 175; Copy Effects; Initialize (`40` push + PN 157/158) |
| 4. COMBI / MULTI / GLOBAL / DRUMS | Pass | COMBI live PNs; MULTI live PNs (−11 offset), CONFIG debounced `68` (restored byte for byte); GLOBAL debounced `51`; DRUMS "used by", free-keys-only Key list (46 options), `Func 53`. Every device-memory edit was restored |
| 5. Patch Browser | Pass | Audition (`Cn pp` only), scope switch (`4E 00`), Cancel (restore + buffer push), OK (Landmine #41 shape), Unsaved Edits → Cancel and → Discard Edits and Continue |
| 6. Writes | Pass | Write To A New Slot and Write In Place, PROG and COMBI (A99); A00 untouched (Landmine #113); Write All Data (then active-tab restore, #112/#119), All Programs, All Combinations; header and modal Discard; tab switch + live edit after writes |
| 7. FILE | Pass | Factory Sounds A and B → Write to Device; Save Single Program/Combination/Data File (Programs only, and all five); Load Data File (full, partial with four types greyed, junk refused, round trip of `t_all.syx`); Single Program/Combination (match → destination → written; combi file given to Single Program refused with guidance; All Programs file → Cancel/Choose Program; junk refused). Test files in the test Mac's `Desktop/Test Sysex` |
| 8. Failure paths | Pass | SysEx DIS: live edits silent with no ACK (by design, #115), Write In Place → "No response" box, Discard reverts locally ("device may be out of sync"), import → box, Retry after ENA recovers. Format error: front-panel OSC Mode Single → OSC-2 PN 96 gets `26`, "FORMAT ERR", Rejected pill. NAK: front panel out of Prog Edit → `24`, one box, OK → `4E 03` + 100 ms + resend, pill Connected |
| 9. Help and themes | Pass | Getting Started opens on load while unseen; Troubleshooting; Report a Problem; Copy Diagnostics; About (1.0.0-rc.1); three themes with `theme-color` following `--bg-panel` |
| `file://` (starred items) | Pass | Run by the owner from a short checklist (connection, Import All Data, live edit, Write In Place and Discard, tab switch, Factory Sounds A → device, Save/Load Single Program to A99, About and a theme change): Claude in Chrome couldn't act on the `file://` tab even with file-URL access on |

**Findings:**
- **F1 — bug: a NAK in reply to Import From Device is handled as a failed Parameter Change.** `handleSysexMessage`'s NAK branch doesn't check `awaitingDump`. Seen when Single Program (Func `10`, valid only in Program/Prog Edit) was requested after a power cycle left the device in another mode: "Parameter Change Not Received" appears while the freeze overlay stays up; 5 s later the dump watchdog's "No response… no data arrived" box replaces it (the device did answer). Both use `#modal-confirm`, so the second call overwrites the first's text but both sets of button listeners stay attached, and one click settles both (the NAK continuation then sends Prog Edit). Fix branch needed: route a NAK during `awaitingDump` to the dump flow (end the overlay, say the device refused the request in its current mode), and stop `showConfirmModal` stacking.
- **F2 — device behaviour: rapid bank imports hung the X5DR.** Import All Data, All Programs and All Combinations within about 50 s, then the X5DR answered nothing (not even Global) until power-cycled. The owner has seen this once before. With a few seconds between requests, every import worked. No editor change decided; a Troubleshooting line is proposed for D3.
- **F3 — latent race (Landmine #41 shape): Load → Single Program/Combination.** `doLoad1ProgramFlow`/`doLoad1CombiFlow` call `switchToAndEditSlot`/`switchToAndEditCombiSlot` without awaiting them and start `writeProgramToSlot`/`writeCombiToSlot` at once, so the write's Mode Change lands about 8 ms after the Program Change, followed by the switch's delayed one. On hardware the write completed and later edits were ACKed. Small fix: await the switch before writing.
- **Benign `26`s confirmed** on effect type change (offset 6 where the type has none), Copy Effects (Out 3/4 routing, unused offset 6, Balance R on single-control types). Already recorded as benign (decisions table, June 2026).
- **Observation — macOS hot-plug:** after a replug, Audio MIDI Setup left the owner's MIDI interface disconnected until MIDI Studio → Refresh MIDI Setup; Chrome then saw it and the editor reselected "Korg X5DR". Driver/OS behaviour, not the editor.
- **Unconfirmed, not reproduced:** once, right after the SysEx-disabled recovery, opening the Patch Browser sent no `4E 02` before two auditions. A repeat sent it normally.
- **Not a fault:** the page reload found at the start of item 7 (MIDI log gone, Getting Started open) was the owner accidentally clicking Home and then Back during a break.
- **Hardware, owner (front panel): leaving Prog Edit keeps the edit buffer.** In Program play mode the X5DR still plays the edited sound. It reverts to the stored program only when another program is selected (and the original reselected). Losing unsaved device-side edits therefore takes two deliberate front-panel actions: exit edit mode, then select a program.

**Owner's decisions on the open questions:**
- **F4 — OSC-mode mismatch gets a warning box.** A `26` on PN 88–154 (Landmine #21) currently shows only in the status bar and the Rejected pill, while the edits are silently lost. Rare (it needs front-panel editing during a session), but a box per the failure-box rule. The other benign `26`s stay status-only.
- **F5 — NAK recovery re-selects the slot and pushes the whole edit buffer.** Today it re-enters the scope's edit mode and resends only the last parameter (Landmine #4). If the user selected another program on the front panel, the device's buffer no longer holds the editor's unsaved edits, and if they didn't come back, the resend lands in the wrong program's buffer. For PROG and COMBI, recovery will run the same sequence as Patch Browser Cancel: play mode → Program Change to the editor's slot → 100 ms (#41) → edit mode → `40`/`49` buffer push. About 250 ms in all (a 196-byte program takes about 63 ms on the wire); not noticeable. Multi and Drums write straight to device memory, so their single-parameter resend stays. Write In Place and Write To A New Slot were already safe (they push the whole buffer before the Write Request), as are Save and Discard.

**D3 wording candidates (owner picks):**
- Copy Effects box: "This cannot be undone." — Discard Edits does undo it.
- Copy Diagnostics box: "Paste them into your GitHub issue." — email is offered too.
- "Write Programs to the X5DR?" (Data File, Programs only): the "not touched" list omits Combinations.
- After a write times out: "Write failed — could not send program data to device." — it was sent but not acknowledged.
- Success messages ("ALL DATA written to device.", Data File "written to device") are replaced by "ACK ✓" when the Patch Browser's Mode Change is ACKed straight after (`doLoadFactorySoundsFlow`, Data File load).
- The status bar keeps the previous message while a destination picker or choice box is open; "Saved." could name what was saved.
- Troubleshooting: power-cycle the X5DR if it stops answering everything (F2); refresh the interface in Audio MIDI Setup (Mac) if it doesn't reappear after reconnecting.

**Next:** fix branches for F1, F3, F4 and F5, each with its own hardware check (F1 and F5 both touch the NAK handler, so they can share one); then D2 (Edge on Mac; Windows PC); then D3.

## Critical Discovery #218 — F1 and F5: Refused Dump Requests, One Confirm Box at a Time, Buffer Reload on NAK Recovery

**Context:** fixes from the D1 regression (#217), branch `fix/nak-recovery`, commit `f676501`. F1 and F5 both live in `handleSysexMessage`'s NAK branch, so they share a branch.

**Change (`src/index.html`):**
- **F1 — a NAK to a dump request.** A NAK that arrives while `awaitingDump` goes to the new `refuseDumpRequest()`: it ends the request (watchdog and settle timer cleared, freeze overlay ended), sets the pill to Rejected, and shows "Device refused the request". For Single Program and Single Combination the box says the X5DR answers those only in Program or Combination mode and to choose one in the Browser, then try again; other requests get a generic line. Further NAKs within `DUMP_NAK_IGNORE_MS` (500) are ignored, because Chrome repeats them (Landmine #7). The Parameter Change recovery no longer runs, and the watchdog's "no data arrived" box no longer follows.
- **One confirm box at a time.** `showConfirmModal` now chains through `confirmModalQueue` to the old body, renamed `openConfirmModal`: a call made while a box is open waits for it to close. Before, a second call overwrote the first box's text and left both sets of listeners on the buttons, so one click settled both. `showAlertModal` goes through the same queue.
- **F5 — NAK recovery reloads the edit buffer.** For PROG and COMBI with data loaded, OK now runs `restoreDeviceModeForTab(scope, { resync: true })`, the same routine as Patch Browser Cancel: play mode → Program Change to the editor's slot → 100 ms (Landmine #41) → edit mode → the whole `40`/`49` buffer. Every unsaved edit returns, including when another program was selected on the front panel (where a bare resend would have gone into that program's buffer). The box says it will "select this program on the device again and resend all your unsaved edits". Drum and Multi scopes keep the Mode Change + last-parameter resend (no edit buffer, Landmine #58).

**Verification:**
- `node --check` on the module script; `npx vitest run --exclude '.claude/**'`: 474/474 across 14 files; `npm run build` succeeds (951 KB).
- Built file on port 5520 (no MIDI in the Browser pane, so the "MIDI access is blocked" box was open): two more confirm boxes triggered behind it each appeared only after the previous one closed, with no overwrite and no console errors.
- **Owner on hardware (2026-10-08), built file over `file://`, all pass:**
  1. F1: X5DR in Combination mode from the front panel, Import → Single Program → one "Device refused the request" box naming Program mode; overlay gone; Rejected pill; no second box. After choosing a program in the Browser, Single Program works.
  2. F5, PROG: two edits on A00, front panel out of Prog Edit and to another program, a third edit in the editor → box → OK → all three edits heard on A00.
  3. F5, COMBI: the same with a timbre level.
  4. Plain NAK (leave Prog Edit only) → OK → editing continues normally.

**Landmines:** #4 rewritten (recovery by scope; front-panel exit keeps the buffer), #104 notes the queue, new #126 (a NAK can answer a dump request).

**Next:** F3 (Load Single Program/Combination awaits the slot switch before writing), F4 (OSC-mode mismatch box), then D2.

## Critical Discovery #219 — F3 and F4: Load Single Write Timing; a Box for OSC-2 Format Errors

**Context:** fixes from the D1 regression (#217), branch `fix/load-single-and-osc-mismatch`, commit `76c73d0`.

**Change (`src/index.html`):**
- **F3 — Load Single Program/Combination.** The destination `onConfirm` used to call `switchToAndEditSlot`/`switchToAndEditCombiSlot` (play mode → Program Change → 100 ms timer → edit mode) and start `writeProgramToSlot`/`writeCombiToSlot` at once, so the write's own edit-mode Mode Change went out about 8 ms after the Program Change (Landmine #41 shape). Now it calls `showProgSlot`/`showCombiSlot` (editor side only), then awaits the new `selectSlotBeforeWrite(playMode, d)` (play mode → Program Change → 100 ms), then writes; the write's dump enters edit mode itself and sets `editMode`. Write To A New Slot already ran its switch after the write completed, so it is unchanged.
- **F4 — OSC-mode mismatch box.** A `26` on a PROG parameter 88–154 (Landmine #21) still sets the status line and the Rejected pill, and now also opens "Device rejected an OSC-2 setting": the X5DR's OSC Mode probably differs from the editor's and OSC-2 changes are lost until they match. **Resend to device** runs `restoreDeviceModeForTab('prog', { resync: true })`, which reloads the editor's program (OSC Mode and unsaved edits included); **Not Now** closes it. `oscMismatchBoxOpen` keeps it to one box while a drag keeps sending. Other `26` replies stay quiet, as decided in June 2026.

**Verification:**
- `node --check` on the module script; `npx vitest run --exclude '.claude/**'`: 474/474 across 14 files; `npm run build` succeeds (954 KB); the built file loads on port 5520 with no console errors.
- **Owner on hardware (2026-10-08), built file over `file://`, all pass:**
  1. F3, program: Load → Single Program → `t_prog.syx` → A99: "Loaded … into A99 and wrote to device."; a following edit is heard with no NAK.
  2. F3, combination: the same with `t_combi.syx` → A99 and a COMBI edit.
  3. F4: front-panel OSC Mode Single while the editor shows Double → OSC-2 Send C → one box; Resend to device returns the X5DR to Double and OSC-2 edits work; Not Now closes the box and sends nothing.

**Landmines:** #21 updated (the box and its scope).

**Next:** all D1 code findings are fixed (F2 is device behaviour; its Troubleshooting line is in the D3 list). Next is D2: Edge on Mac, then a Windows PC with the X5DR.

## Critical Discovery #220 — D2 Part 1 (Edge on the Test Mac) Passes; Write Caret Stays Disabled After Write In Place

**Context:** 2026-10-09. Release Plan D2, Part 1, run by the owner from `docs/X5DR_Editor_D2_Checklist.md` in Microsoft Edge on the hardware-test Mac, using the CI build of `fix/release-wording` (so the D3 wording was also checked on hardware).

**Results:** every Part 1 box ticked: connection (auto-select, Getting Started on first launch, port kept across reload), Import All Data and Single Program, live edits heard, effect type change, Discard, Write To A New Slot (A99), Write In Place, tab switch, Help menu, Copy Diagnostics, all three themes. The owner also approved the D3 wording on the same build. Part 2 (Windows PC, Chrome and Edge) waits for access to the PC.

**Bug found (owner, seen occasionally in Chrome and Edge):** after Write In Place, the ▾ caret (Write To A New Slot…) stayed greyed out and didn't work; Discard Edits, then editing again, brought it back.
- **Cause:** `doWriteFlow`/`doCombiWriteFlow` call `setProgActionButtons(true)`/`setCombiActionButtons(true)`, disabling every button in the action bar, for the write. On success they called only `updateActionButtons(scope)`, which re-enables Write In Place and Discard Edits from the dirty state. The caret and **Initialize…** stayed disabled until the bar was rebuilt (Discard, a tab switch or a slot change re-render it, hence "occasionally"). The failure paths were fine; they already call `set…ActionButtons(false)`.
- **Fix** (`fix/write-caret-after-write`, `0580bc6`): on success, `set…ActionButtons(false)` first, then `updateActionButtons(scope)`, in both flows.
- **Verification:** `node --check` passes; CI run `37979100512`: 14/14 files, 474/474 tests, build OK. **Owner on hardware (2026-10-09): passes on PROG and COMBI** — after Write In Place the caret opens Write To A New Slot and Initialize… works, with no Discard in between.

**Tooling — iCloud evicted `node_modules`:** locally, vitest ran only 12 files (368 tests). ## Critical Discovery #225 — v1.1 Brainstorm: Multisound Solo and a Random Patch Generator

**Context:** 2026-10-12, owner brainstorm of v1.1 (high level; no design decisions made, nothing scheduled). Release Plan H2 and the owner's task list ("V1.1 items for consideration") were brought into line: the task list gained the H2 items it lacked, and H2 gained the task list's rudimentary keyboard (Note On/Off) item. Claude suggested themed releases (v1.1 polish, then saved state + undo, then the librarian) and dropping the service worker; the owner hasn't decided.

**Multisound Solo (owner's proposal, Claude's notes):**
- Owner: save the oscillator's VDA level, Send C and Send D, set them to 0, restore on unmute; the sends because parallel effect configurations could let audio through C/D.
- Claude (INFERRED, not in the manual): on this family the sends are probably taken after the VDA, like the A:B pan (whose `FF` value is Off, i.e. C/D only), so Oscillator Level 0 (param 65) alone may silence every path. AMP Velocity Sense (68) and AMP KBD Track Int (67) might lift a 0 level. Hardware test before building: level 0, strong positive velocity and key tracking, a parallel placement with Sends up, play hard across the range. If anything leaks, use the three-parameter version (or also zero the modulators).
- Device only, never in the store, so the patch isn't marked edited and Write never saves zeros. Any Write clears the mute (it sends the real values). Anything that reloads the edit buffer clears it: slot change, browser audition, Discard, Import, Initialize. Editing a muted oscillator's level unmutes it. Double mode only. A lost restore is silent (Landmine #115). Probably shown as Solo on each oscillator column.

**Random patch generator (owner's idea, Claude's notes):**
- A Randomize button opening a modal with a checkbox per Easy-tab panel (rather than an icon on each panel), an Again button, and Back to previous (a snapshot before each roll) until undo exists.
- Pure randomness gives too many unusable patches, the worst being silence. Proposed: a tunable table of bounded ranges per parameter, mod depths weighted toward zero, and hard floors so the patch always sounds (oscillator level, sustain/decay, cutoff). Multisound and effect type fully random within the allowed set. Later: an intensity slider from "nudge the current patch" to "anything within bounds".
- Must respect the Symphonic exclusion (ADR-0003), the effect-type defaults reset, the Placement routing reset (ADR-0005), and the hide X5D/X5DR-only setting (#222). Oscillator mode and name stay fixed. It's an ordinary edit through `setParam`, so the patch is marked edited and Discard reverts it.
- A roll changes 40–60 parameters. Rather than a burst of live Parameter Changes (fast bank imports have hung the X5DR, #217 F2), consider one single-program dump to the edit buffer; check on hardware first.

## Critical Discovery #226 — v1.1 Brainstorm: AI Patch Generation

**Context:** 2026-10-12, owner brainstorm (high level; nothing decided or scheduled). Earlier informal discussion had centred on giving JSON files to an AI and importing the result.

**Stage 1, copy and paste with any AI chat (Claude's recommendation to build first):**
- Export/Import Patch as JSON. The store already holds programs as named values; `.syx` is packed 7-bit binary that an AI would get wrong.
- Import runs value checks like FILE → Load's (Landmine #122): unknown fields and out-of-range values are refused or clamped, and a box lists what changed. The result reaches the device as one dump, not a burst of Parameter Changes (see #225).
- An "AI patch kit" (e.g. a Help menu download) to attach to the chat: the JSON format with ranges and value meanings; what each section does musically in X5DR terms; the multisound list with categories, short sound descriptions (names alone are cryptic) and the X5D/X5DR-only marks (#222); effect types and their parameters; about a dozen labelled factory patches as examples (the strongest ingredient); the traps (Symphonic exclusion, Single/Double mode, settings that cause silence).
- The AI can't hear, so it gives plausible starting points; the user iterates ("brighter", "less vibrato").

**Stage 2, a chat tab in the editor (later, if at all):**
- A chat window, a connection to an AI service, and tools the AI may call (read the patch, set a parameter, list multisounds) that go through `setParam`, so edits are live and the patch is marked edited. The AI can never Write; undo becomes much more valuable.
- Keys and cost need an owner decision: bring-your-own-key (no server, but a secret stored in the page), an owner-run server (owner pays, needs abuse limits, ends "static file, no backend"), or a local model (free and private, weaker, fiddly setup).
- The build fails today on `fetch(` (Landmine #123), so that rule would need relaxing; also a privacy note and offline behaviour.
- Stage 1's JSON format, checks and patch kit are all prerequisites for Stage 2.

## Critical Discovery #227 — D2 Part 2 (Windows PC, Chrome and Edge) Passes; Windows Added to the Verified Platforms

**Context:** 2026-10-14. Release Plan D2, Part 2, run by the owner from `docs/X5DR_Editor_D2_Checklist.md` (private archive) on a Windows 11 PC with the X5DR, in Chrome 155 and Edge 155, from the CI artifact of `main` over `file://`. The interface's machine details stay in the checklist, not here (public-doc scrub, #214).

**Results:** every Part 2 box ticked in both browsers, with no problems: connection, Import From Device (All Data, Single Program), writes (Write To A New Slot to A99, Write In Place, Write All Programs, Discard, COMBI → PROG), FILE (Factory Bank A, Save/Load Single Program to A99, Data File… with `t_all.syx`, `t_junk.syx` refused), failure paths (EX: DIS → "No response" box and amber pill, Retry after EX: ENA; Ch 2 → "No response" box naming Ch 2), Help (About 1.0.0-rc.1, themes, Getting Started and Troubleshooting text).

**Windows facts (the D2 questions):**
- **Port name:** the interface's own name, with no "x5", so auto-select picks nothing and the port is chosen by hand, as Getting Started and the README already say. The manual choice is kept across reload (Landmine #118).
- **Hot-plug:** unplugging the interface's USB cleared the port; plugging it back in, Windows found the port again and the editor reselected it on its own. The Mac needed Audio MIDI Setup → Refresh.
- **DAW sharing:** Reason 12 open with the same port enabled worked alongside the editor, in both browsers, with no error message or reconfiguration. The Help text's "Some MIDI drivers let only one program use a port at a time…" stays: it is hedged, and other drivers may still behave that way. This answers C2's "verify the current Windows MIDI Services behaviour" for this setup.
- **`file://`:** MIDI with SysEx works, and both browsers ask for MIDI permission on every load, as on the Mac (Landmine #103) and as Getting Started says.

**Changes (`docs/d2-part2-results`):**
- Getting Started section 1 (`src/index.html`) and the README Requirements line: "**Chrome** and **Edge** have been verified on macOS and Windows, and **Brave** on Linux." (Release Plan D2, amended in #223.) No other Help or README text needed patching.
- D2 Checklist: Part 2 per-browser boxes ticked, hot-plug and DAW notes, owner's summary.
- Release Plan D2 marked done; Progress Log: next step E1.

**Still open:** Chrome/Edge on Linux are unreported; the X5, X5D and 05R/W remain untested (Progress Log, Known Outliers).

## Decision #228 — Stage F (RC Beta) Complete; the First Public Release Is v1.0.0

**Context:** 2026-10-15, owner decision. The plan was an unannounced `v1.0.0-rc.1` pre-release at E6, a beta (F1 invitations, F2 triage, rc.2 if needed), then `v1.0.0` at G1. The owner considers the rc.1 testing complete: the RC tester's pre-release feedback was triaged and folded into the code by D4 (#223), and D2 Part 2 covered Windows (#227).

**Decision:**
- No `rc` is released publicly. The public cut (Stage E) ships **`v1.0.0`**: E6 now tags and publishes `v1.0.0` (not a pre-release) and closes the Project Plan's Phase 4 checkboxes; G1 is folded into it. The release stays unannounced until E7 passes and G2–G3 are done.
- F1 (invitations) is dropped: other-model owners are reached through the announcement and the device-report template (G3, G4). The identified user's fixture permission stays in H2. F2 becomes the post-release routine (G4); fixes ship as `v1.0.x` (E7 friction as `v1.0.1`, before the announcement).

**Changes (`docs/v1.0.0-release`):**
- Version `1.0.0` in `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `APP_VERSION` (the build checks they match, Landmine #123). `IS_PRERELEASE` is now false, so Help → About drops its "pre-release (beta)" line; About and Copy Diagnostics show `1.0.0`. No other Help text named the version.
- README: the "Beta: version 1.0.0-rc.1 is a pre-release" banner removed. CHANGELOG: the entry is now `[1.0.0] — unreleased`, "First public release", with the `v1.0.0` tag link; E6 adds the date.
- The hash note in `CLAUDE.md`, the Project Context and this file's header now says "before v1.0.0" (the first public commit is the v1.0.0 commit). The header line is not an entry; no past entry was edited.
- Release Plan: D7 amended; overview; E4's commit message; E6 rewritten (owner publishes); E7's fix version; Stage F and G1 replaced by short notes; G2/G3 dependencies; §9 table. Completed C2/C3/C4 steps keep their rc.1 text with a note. Project Plan's v1.0 tag checkbox points at E6. Progress Log updated.

**Owner's task list:** the PHASE 4 Stage F tasks (F1, F2) and G1 should be dropped or ticked there to match (§9: the plan changes first, then the task list).

## Decision #229 — Release Plan E1: Freeze and Back Up the Private Repo

**Context:** 2026-10-15. First step of the public cut (Stage E). This entry is committed *before* the `pre-public-cut` tag, so the frozen private repo contains it; the backup checks are recorded in the public repo after E4.

**Checks before the freeze:**
- Every local and remote branch is merged into `main`; `main` equals `origin/main`; CI on `main` passed; no stashes.
- Two untracked private notes were committed first (owner's choice), so the backup holds them: `Setup Instructions/Claude Prompts/Donations/add-support-links.md` and `Setup Instructions/X5DR_Editor_YouTube_Demo_Script.md`. They are not on the §10 publish list, so E4 doesn't copy them.
- iCloud had evicted 5,568 of 6,908 `.git` objects and `node_modules` (Landmine #95). A local `git bundle` stalled; after Finder "Download Now" and `brctl download` both counts were 0 and all 16 test files passed (510 tests). E4's `git archive` reads this folder's objects, so re-check `find .git -flags +dataless | wc -l` before E4.
- The hardware-test Mac's old working clone: clean working tree, no stashes, no unpushed commits (`git log --branches --not --remotes` empty). Nothing to rescue; it is retired in E2.

**Backup locations (E1 Decision, owner):** the hardware-test Mac (`~/Backups/x5dr-editor-private.git`, a mirror unpacked from the bundle) and **iCloud Drive** for the off-machine copy, as the single bundle file `x5dr-editor-private-pre-public-cut.bundle`, outside the project folder. GitHub is the third copy.

**Sizes (for planning):** GitHub reports the private repo at ~127 MB packed (mostly `Reference Images/`), so the bundle and each mirror are ~130 MB. The public allowlist (§10) is 97 files, 4.3 MB.

**E1 — freeze and backup (finished):**
- Private repo frozen at `main` `9709139`, tag `pre-public-cut` (tag object `122d463`), pushed; CI green.
- Bundle `x5dr-editor-private-pre-public-cut.bundle`: 125 MB, 69 refs (66 branches, the tags `pre-audit-2026-09-30` and `pre-public-cut`, and HEAD). `git bundle verify` passed on every copy.
- Three copies, as the backup policy asks: iCloud Drive (the single bundle file, in an "X5DR Backups" folder outside the project folder); the hardware-test Mac (`~/Backups/`: the bundle plus the mirror `x5dr-editor-private.git`, whose log starts at `9709139`, both tags present); GitHub.

**E3 — email privacy:** GitHub "Keep my email addresses private" and "Block command line pushes that expose my email" are on. Global `user.email` is the noreply address, checked with a test commit.

**E4 — public repo:**
- Working copy (E4 Decision, owner): `~/Developer/x5dr-editor`, outside iCloud. Landmine #95 is retired as a result (below). The Claude Code project memory was carried over to the new path.
- Extracted with §10's two `git archive` commands: 94 files (the §10 dry run on 2026-10-07 had 90; files added since).

- `npm ci`; all 16 test files ran, 510 tests passed; `npm run build` produced a 978 KB `dist/index.html`.
- Leak checks: the scrub-term grep lists only the four expected files; no PDFs or third-party `.syx` files; `Setup Instructions/` and `Reference Images/` absent. gitleaks: one false positive (ADR-0006 line 87, the prose "Velocity/After Touch Curve", rule `generic-api-key`).
- Single commit `ffe1ec8` ("X5DR Editor v1.0.0 — initial public commit"), author and committer the noreply address. `gh repo create Baylo1/x5dr-editor --private`; CI green on `main` (run 38795427190).
- `npm audit` reports 6 vulnerabilities (4 high) in `undici`, pulled in by the dev/test tooling only (nothing ships in `dist/`). Fixed on its own branch, `chore/npm-audit-fix`.

**Landmine #95 retired (owner, 2026-10-15).** Release Plan H1 said to retire it once the working copy left iCloud, and E4 moved it. The entry keeps one line for the frozen Desktop archive checkout, which is still in iCloud. Progress Log: the iCloud notes under Testing and Toolchain removed. Project Context: the GitHub row now describes the public repo and the private archive.

**Next:** E5 — configure the repo and flip it to public (owner's go/no-go).

## Decision #231 — Release Plan E5: Repo Configured and Public

**Context:** 2026-10-15. E4 (#230) created `Baylo1/x5dr-editor` private from one commit. E5 configures it and flips it public, the point of no return.

**Before the flip (Claude, via `gh`):** description and homepage (`https://baylo1.github.io/x5dr-editor/`); Issues on, Discussions/Wiki/Projects off (Projects had been on by default); the seven topics; labels `device-report`, `needs-info`, `v1.1` added beside the defaults (`bug` and `enhancement` already existed); Dependabot alerts on.

**Device report label fix (`fix/device-report-label`):** `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/device_report.md` asked for `labels: device report` (a space), while the label E5 creates is `device-report`, so device reports would have arrived unlabelled. The template now uses `device-report`.

**The flip and after (owner):** visibility → public; social preview uploaded (`src/icons/social-preview-1280x640.png`); ruleset `main` (default branch: no deletion, no force-push; PRs not required); secret scanning and push protection on; private vulnerability reporting on; Pages source → GitHub Actions; a `v*` tag rule on the `github-pages` environment.

**Two plan gaps found, Release Plan E5 amended:**
- **Social preview only after the flip.** GitHub shows the Social preview setting on a private repo only if an image was uploaded before, so it can't be done first.
- **`github-pages` needs a `v*` tag rule.** Turning Pages on creates the environment with a deployment rule for `main` only. `deploy.yml` runs on a published Release, i.e. from the tag, so without the rule E6's deploy job would most likely be refused. The environment now allows `main` and `v*`.
- Also noted in E5: on the free plan the ruleset, secret scanning and private vulnerability reporting are public-repo features, so they come after the flip too.

**Verified (2026-10-15):** visibility PUBLIC; an unauthenticated API request sees the repo and 94 files on `main`; custom social preview set; ruleset active with `deletion` and `non_fast_forward` on `~DEFAULT_BRANCH`; secret scanning and push protection enabled; private vulnerability reporting enabled; Pages `build_type` = `workflow`; environment policies `main` (branch) and `v*` (tag). README/CONTRIBUTING links resolve, except the Pages URL, which is 404 until E6's first deploy. CI green on the public repo: a re-run of `main` (attempt 2) and a manual `workflow_dispatch` run (38805267507), both at `27200ea`. A re-run reuses the same row in Actions → CI, so it doesn't appear as a new entry.

**Next:** E6 — release `v1.0.0` (owner publishes; first deploy; first public-repo backup).
